## BODY-CONEXIONES-T1-1 -- close the last two unclosed connections in Tier 1: shift_import and vida_export's
own `main()` (2026-11-07)

Carrying out BODY-CONEXIONES-T1-OBS-1's plan (OBSERVED at `f625ac0`): of the four connection-opening sites left
in Tier 1 modules, `db.py`'s is a factory (returns the connection, never owns it), `identity.py`'s two already
close in a `finally`, and `shift_import.main()` / `vida_export.main()` never closed theirs. This slice closes
both, and widens `pull.py`'s existing `try/finally` to cover `db.init(conn)` too (identity.py's pattern: open,
then `try: init + work finally: close`, so a failure in `init()` itself still closes the connection).

**The three sites.**

1. `body/shift_import.py` `main()`: `conn = db.connect()` through the final `print(line)` now sits inside
   `try: ... finally: conn.close()`, with `db.init(conn)` moved inside the `try`. Every commit point
   (`propose()`'s own `with conn:`) and every printed line are byte-for-byte unchanged -- the new wrapping
   only widens what runs under `finally`, it does not touch what runs.
2. `body/vida_export.py` `main()`: the same shape, from `conn = db.connect()` through the write and `return 0`.
   The early `return 1` for hosted mode and the early `return 1` for a non-Monday `--week` both happen before
   `conn = db.connect()` and stay exactly where they were -- hosted mode never opens a connection at all, so
   `tests/test_dispositivo.py`'s `VidaExportHostedRefusalTest` (asserting `BODY_HOME/vida` stays absent) needed
   no change.
3. `body/pull.py` `main()`: `db.init(conn)` moved from before the `try` to its first line, so a migration
   failure inside `init()` -- not just a failure inside `_run()` -- now also closes the connection.

**Tests**, `tests/test_conexiones_cerradas.py` (the existing guard module), one new `MainClosesConnectionTest`
with two tests per module (six total): a happy-path run of each `main()` against the isolated test home,
wrapped in `warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)` + `warnings.simplefilter("always", ResourceWarning)` +
`gc.collect()`, asserting no `sqlite3.Connection` `ResourceWarning`; and a run where `db.init` is patched to
raise, with `db.connect` patched to return a `_CloseRecorder` wrapper, asserting `.closed` is `True` even
though the exception propagates out of `main()` uncaught. `shift_import.main()` is driven with
`["--dir", <tmp folder with the existing turnos-demo-a.json fixture>, "--person-id", "1"]` (the same minimum
arguments `ShiftImportCliTest` already uses); `vida_export.main()` with `["--week", "2026-11-02"]` (a Monday,
local/non-hosted mode, no existing CLI test to copy from); `pull.main()` with `["--date", "2026-11-01"]` and
`body.pull.garmin_adapter.fetch_day` stubbed to return an empty `DayData` (no network), the same stubbing style
`test_garmin_host.py`'s hosted-pull tests already use. The existing `shift_import` and `vida_export` tests
(output files, rows, printed counts) were not touched and still pass unchanged.

**A gate ran red first, from this slice's own test, not from the three sites.** The first full-suite run
failed one pre-existing test, `tests.test_dispositivo.VidaExportHostedRefusalTest.test_main_refuses_and_writes_
nothing`, which asserts `config.BODY_HOME / "vida"` does not exist after a hosted-mode refusal. `BODY_HOME` is
one directory shared by every test module in a single `unittest discover` process (set once, at import, by
`tests/_isolate.py`), and the new `vida_export` happy-path test ran earlier in file order and had just created
that same `vida/` directory by writing a real weekly file into it -- a test-isolation gap in the new test, not
a defect in the three sites or in the refusal test. Fixed by giving that one test its own `config.BODY_HOME`
for its duration (`tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=TMP)`, restored via `addCleanup`, the same pattern `test_pc_cliente.py`
and `test_backup.py` already use for the same directory). The gate was then run once more on the corrected tree
and not re-run again.

**Gate**, run (twice, for the reason above) with the plain command: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest
discover tests -t .` -- first run: 756 tests, one failure (`VidaExportHostedRefusalTest`, above), `skipped=1`;
second run, final tree: 756 tests, `OK (skipped=1)`.

## BODY-PULIDO-1 -- 44px tap targets, Dia's cards and Como lo calculo's part rows join Turnos' way-back
mechanism to Tendencias (2026-11-07)

The first round from BODY-DISENO-CENSO-1's read-only audit: tap targets under 44px, and DESIGN rule 3 ("every
figure opens what made it, with a way back") not yet reaching Dia or Como lo calculo the way it already reaches
Turnos (BODY-TURNOS-ENLACES-1).

**Decisions taken.**

1. **One way-back mechanism for all three origins.** `/trends`'s `desde` query parameter now accepts `turnos`,
   `dia` or `como` (anything else is dropped, as before); `dia` and `como` also take `dia=<YYYY-MM-DD>`
   (`web.py`'s `trends()`, validated the same way `_parse_day` validates -- `date.fromisoformat` -- but an
   invalid or missing `dia` drops `desde` too, rather than 404ing the page). Tendencias shows one back link at
   the top (`<a class="taplink">`): `desde=turnos` -> `/shifts` (unchanged), `desde=dia` -> `/day/<dia>`,
   `desde=como` -> `/how/<dia>`. Range links keep both `desde` and `dia` when present. The new helper
   `_tendencias_href(key, desde, dia)` (next to `_es_extra_metric`) builds the `/trends?r=30&desde=...&dia=...
   [&todas=1]#<key>` href from a metric key, returning `None` when the key has no card on Tendencias (checked
   against `TREND_KEYS` and `TREND_GROUPS`, the same lookups `_es_extra_metric` already uses) -- the single
   place both Dia and Como lo calculo call into.
2. **Dia's cards.** `day_view()` now sets `href` on each card via `_tendencias_href(k, "dia", key)` when the
   day has a value for that metric; `day.html`'s card loop renders the card as `<a class="card">` when `href`
   is set, a plain `<div class="card">` otherwise (the same `<a class="card">`/`<div class="card">` choice
   Hoy's own cards already make, in `today.html`). A card with no value, or whose metric has no Tendencias
   card (e.g. `sleep_need_min`, deliberately absent from Tendencias per `TREND_GROUPS`'s own comment), stays a
   plain div. The whole card is the link, so no extra sizing was needed for 44px.
3. **Como lo calculo's part rows.** `readiness.Part` carries no metric key of its own (its keys are `hrv`,
   `sleep`, `battery`, `resting_hr`, `stress`), so a small dict, `PART_METRIC`, sits next to `how()` and maps
   each to its Tendencias metric key (`hrv_last_night`, `sleep_minutes`, `body_battery_wake`, `resting_hr`,
   `stress_avg`). `how()` builds each part's `href` via `_tendencias_href(metric_key, "como", day)` when the
   part has a value and maps to a metric with a card; `how.html` links only the row's first-cell label
   (`<a class="taplink">`), the row stays a `<tr>`. A part with no value, or no mapping, is not a link; the
   missing-part rows (already rendered separately, for parts readiness couldn't compute at all) are untouched.
4. **44px tap targets.** `.taplink` already matched the target shape (`display:inline-flex;align-items:
   center;min-height:44px`), so only its reach widened: `base.html`'s `hoy_turno_card` macro's three
   `<a class="note" href="/shifts" style="...">` links (shown on Hoy and on `soon.html` before any data has
   synced) are now `<a class="note taplink" href="/shifts">`, with the inline `margin`/`text-decoration` moved
   to a new CSS rule, `.shift .note{margin:0 0 0 4px}` (the two non-link `.note` divs in the same macro keep
   that margin too, unstyled otherwise); `ayuda.html`'s recorrido list links are `<a class="taplink"
   href="#...">`; `sin_acceso.html`'s two links (switch account, log out) both carry `taplink`. `.asis-icon-
   btn` (the assistant panel's icon buttons, on every screen) went from `min-width:40px;min-height:40px` to
   `44px;44px`. The Turnos strip was not touched, per the spec.

**New strings**, `trends.back_dia` / `trends.back_como`, next to the existing `trends.back_turnos`:
es: "‹ Volver al día" / "‹ Volver a cómo lo calculo"; en: "‹ Back to the day" / "‹ Back to how it's calculated".

**Part -> metric mapping used** (`web.py`'s `PART_METRIC`, added for this slice -- no such mapping existed
before): `hrv` -> `hrv_last_night`, `sleep` -> `sleep_minutes`, `battery` -> `body_battery_wake`, `resting_hr`
-> `resting_hr`, `stress` -> `stress_avg`. All five already have a Tendencias card (the first four are
`TREND_KEYS` defaults; `stress_avg` lives behind "Ver todas las medidas" in `TREND_GROUPS`'s `stress` group,
so a Como lo calculo link to it carries `todas=1`).

**Tests**, `tests/test_pulido_1.py` (22 tests): Dia's cards (default-metric link with no `todas`, extra-group
link with `todas=1`, a valued metric with no Tendencias card staying a div, a dash card having no link); Como's
rows (a valued part linking with `desde=como`, a valueless part never linking, English); Tendencias' back link
for each of the three `desde` values, an invalid or missing `dia` and an unknown `desde` showing none, and
range links keeping `desde` and `dia` together; person-scope isolation across Dia and Como; the CSS/markup
checks for `.asis-icon-btn`, `hoy_turno_card`'s three links, Ayuda's recorrido links and sin_acceso.html's
links. `tests/test_turnos_enlaces.py` needed no change -- none of its assertions pinned the markup this slice
touched (its `desde=turnos` tests don't exercise `dia`, and its text-content and CSS-class assertions still
hold against the new `_tendencias_href`-based implementation).

**Gate**, run once on the final tree with the plain command: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover
tests -t .` -- `Ran 778 tests ... OK (skipped=1)`.

**Merge: AWAITING_APPROVAL, stopped on customer-bytes.** This diff changes what a person reads and taps: two
new strings (`trends.back_dia`, `trends.back_como`) in both languages, Dia's metric cards and Como lo calculo's
part-row labels becoming links, and the assistant's icon buttons and the three shift-card/Ayuda/sin-acceso
links growing to 44px. Merge policy A's customer-bytes condition fails, so this slice stops before merging, on
the branch, for the orchestrator to measure in a browser against the demo home, per the spec's own instruction.

## BODY-PULIDO-1-M -- Ayuda's per-task link reaches 44px, Dia/Como open the Tendencias range that contains the
day; lands BODY-PULIDO-1 (2026-11-07)

The orchestrator measured BODY-PULIDO-1 in a real browser at 375 px against the demo home (per that entry's
`AWAITING_APPROVAL`) and found two defects, both fixed here before the merge:

**Ayuda's per-task link.** `ayuda.html`'s "Ir a la pantalla →" link (`{{ tarea.pantalla_link }}`, shown only
when a task names a concrete screen) carried `style="text-decoration:underline"` alone -- no `.taplink`, so
it measured well under 44px, unlike the chapter's own `recorrido` links which already had the class. It now
carries `class="taplink"` in place of the inline style; `.taplink` already includes the underline, so the
visible rendering is unchanged.

**The Tendencias range now contains the day.** Dia's cards and Como lo calculo's part rows built their own
measure's Tendencias link with a fixed `r=30`, so a day older than 30 days opened a 30-day window that did not
contain it -- a dead-looking anchor jump. `web.py` gained `_rango_que_contiene(dia, today_local)`, used by both
callers through `_tendencias_href` (now taking `today_local`): within the last 30 days of the person's own
today -> `r=30`; within 90 -> `r=90`; older -> no `r` at all (Tendencias' monthly/all-time view, which reaches
any day). `how()` and `day_view()` each compute `today_local` via the existing `_today_local(person)` helper
and pass it through; no new helper for "today" was needed.

**Tests**, `tests/test_pulido_1.py` (30 tests, up from 22): the three existing classes that built hrefs from a
fixed calendar date now use a date 10 days before `date.today()` instead, so they keep exercising the `r=30`
branch regardless of when the suite runs. Added `TapTargetsTest.test_ayuda_ir_a_pantalla_link_carries_taplink`
and a new `TendenciasRangeContainsDayTest` (Dia and Como, each at 10/60/200 days old -> `r=30`/`r=90`/no `r`;
`desde` and `dia` survive in the href across all three ranges).

**Gate**, run once on the final tree with the plain command: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover
tests -t .` -- `Ran 786 tests ... OK (skipped=1)`.

**Merge: this spec is its own approval.** The diff touches customer-facing bytes (Ayuda's link class, the
Tendencias hrefs Dia and Como build), which trips merge policy A's customer-bytes condition on its own: but
this spec's body says in words to merge after the gate, carrying BODY-PULIDO-1's approval forward along with
its own. Merged `--no-ff` into `main`; `main` left checked out, clean. Branch `feat/body-pulido-1` kept.

## BODY-PULIDO-2 -- value on tap for Tendencias' and Metas' charts, soon.html's way back (2026-11-07)

DESIGN rule 9 ("charts explain themselves: legend, scale, value on tap, «Toca un día…»") and rule 11 (44px): a
90-day Tendencias chart gave each day ~3.5px of tap width on a phone, so "value on tap" was not reachable
without a mouse; Metas' goal chart had no accessible name, no legend and no value on tap at all; and the "aún
no hay suficientes días" page (`soon.html`, `trends()`'s no-cards branch) dropped the way back that `desde`
already computed, just never passed through.

**One small script, `body/static/charts.js`** (loaded from `base.html`, same `static_url()` versioning as
`assistant.js`, no dependencies, no network call). It enhances every `<figure class="chart" data-points="...">`:
a tap or drag anywhere on the figure selects the nearest point by x and shows a readout (a `<figcaption
aria-live="polite">`) below the chart -- the point's label as the server wrote it, and, when the point carries
a day or a month, a taplink to it. A thin marker (`.chart-marker`) shows the selected x. The figure is made
focusable only once JS enhances it (`tabIndex`); ←/→ move the selection. Without JS nothing changes: the
existing per-day/per-month `<a><title><rect>` hit regions in `body/profile.py` stay exactly as they were --
they are the no-JS path BODY-EJES-FECHAS-1 already pinned.

**The server writes the points, never the script.** `profile.py` gained `chart_figure()` (wraps a chart's
existing svg+range markup in `<figure class="chart">`, adding `data-points` only when a `valor_fmt` is given)
and `_points_attr()` (one html-escaped JSON array). `window_svg()` and `month_svg()` each take new `valor_fmt`
and `link_label` keyword args (default `None`, so every existing caller is unaffected -- pinned by
`BuildersBackwardCompatTest`); `_trend_card` in `web.py` now passes `valor_fmt=lambda v: _fig_unit(t, k, v,
defs)` and the matching `trends.chart_open_day`/`trends.chart_open_month` link label. A daily point carries
`{x, label, day}` (href becomes `/day/<day>`, built by charts.js); a monthly point carries `{x, label, m}`
(href becomes `/trends?m=<m>#<key>`, `<key>` read from the figure's own `data-key`, `MetricProfile.key` --
never a second parameter). No URL charts.js builds carries anything but a day or a month; no raw figure
reaches an attribute that didn't already carry one (the per-day/-month `<title>`s already did, via dates
only).

**The goal chart** (`_goal_line_svg` in `web.py`, shown by `goal.html` -- `goals.html` holds the list, not the
chart): now takes `t` and `defs` to build an aria-label naming the goal and both dates (`goals.chart_aria`,
built by string concatenation, never `.format()`, since a goal's title is free text Carlos typed and must
never be run through `str.format`'s `{}` substitution) and a three-item legend (`goals.legend_plan/_avg/_today`)
drawn with the dashed/solid/thin-vertical strokes the svg itself uses. Its weekly points carry `{x, label}`
only -- no `day`, no `m` -- so charts.js shows no link for them, a week not being a day.

**Hint text**, one key each: `trends.chart_hint` ("Toca o desliza sobre la gráfica para ver cada día" / "Tap or
drag on the chart to see each day"), rendered under every Tendencias chart (daily and monthly alike), and
`goals.chart_hint` ("... cada semana" / "... each week") under the goal chart.

**soon.html's way back.** `trends()` already computed `back_href`/`back_label` from `desde`/`dia` before its
no-cards branch, but the two `_render("soon.html", ...)` calls in that branch never passed them through --
BODY-PULIDO-1 added the mechanism for the cards page and this gap went unnoticed until the orchestrator found
it measuring BODY-PULIDO-1. Both calls now pass `back_href=back_href, back_label=back_label`; `soon.html`
renders the same `<a class="taplink">` block `trends.html` already used, guarded by `{% if back_href %}` so
every other `soon.html` caller (Hoy, History) is unaffected by the undefined default.

**Strings as written** -- es / en:
- `trends.chart_hint`: "Toca o desliza sobre la gráfica para ver cada día" / "Tap or drag on the chart to see
  each day"
- `trends.chart_open_day`: "Abrir el día ›" / "Open the day ›"
- `trends.chart_open_month`: "Abrir el mes ›" / "Open the month ›"
- `goals.chart_hint`: "Toca o desliza sobre la gráfica para ver cada semana" / "Tap or drag on the chart to see
  each week"
- `goals.chart_aria`: "plan desde {start} hasta {end}" / "plan from {start} to {end}" (prefixed with the
  goal's own title by string concatenation)
- `goals.chart_week_label`: "Semana del {date}: {value}" / "Week of {date}: {value}"
- `goals.legend_plan` / `_avg` / `_today`: "Plan" / "Tu promedio semanal" / "Hoy" -- "Plan" / "Your weekly
  average" / "Today"

**Tests**, `tests/test_pulido_2.py` (9 new tests): r=30 and r=90 daily charts carry one `data-points` entry
per day (ISO day, localised non-ISO label), the per-day hit regions and the hint text stay; English labels are
not bare ISO; the all-time monthly view's points carry a month key and no day, with `data-key`/`data-link-label`
on the figure; the goal chart's svg has `role="img"` and an aria-label naming the goal and both dates with
neither the baseline nor the target value present, its three legend labels render, and its weekly points carry
neither `day` nor `m`; `soon.html` shows "‹ Volver al día" when reached via `desde=dia` and shows no back link
without it; `charts.js` contains no `fetch(` and no literal URL other than `/day/` and `/trends?m=`; and a
second person's chart values never reach the first person's page. `tests/test_ejes_fechas.py` needed no edit
-- nothing it pins moved (its `_strip_attrs` already drops whole attributes, so the new `data-points` content
is invisible to it; `BuildersBackwardCompatTest` calls the builders without the new keyword args and still
gets the unwrapped-looking body it asserts on, now inside a plain `<figure class="chart">` it never checks for).

**Gate**, run once on the final tree with the plain command: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover
tests -t .` -- `Ran 795 tests in 82.793s ... OK (skipped=1)` (786 before this slice, +9 new).

**Merge: AWAITING_APPROVAL, stopped on customer-bytes.** This diff changes what a person reads and taps: two
new hint strings under every Tendencias and goal chart, a new legend and accessible name on the goal chart,
new "Abrir el día/mes ›" taplinks in the tap/drag readout, and the restored "‹ Volver al día" link on
`soon.html`. Merge policy A's customer-bytes condition fails and the spec says to stop here, so this slice
stops before merging, on the branch, for the orchestrator to judge the script in a browser.

## BODY-PULIDO-2-M -- a real tap reads instead of navigating, charts stop blocking vertical scroll, weekly
labels name the Monday, the focusable chart gets a visible focus ring; lands BODY-PULIDO-2 (2026-11-07)

The orchestrator measured BODY-PULIDO-2 in a real browser at 375 px against the demo home (per that entry's
`AWAITING_APPROVAL`) and found four defects, all fixed here before the merge:

**A tap reads, it does not leave.** A real click on the per-day hit-region `<a>` inside an enhanced figure's
svg navigated straight to `/day/<day>`, before the reader ever saw the readout -- only a synthetic pointer
event had been exercised before. `charts.js` now adds a capture-phase `click` listener on the figure that,
when the click's target is an anchor inside the svg (`svg.contains(a)`), calls `preventDefault()` and selects
the nearest point instead; the readout's own "Abrir el día ›" link lives in the `figcaption` outside the svg
and is never touched by this listener, so it still navigates. Without JavaScript the hit-region markup and its
links are unchanged.

**The page still scrolls.** `figure.chart{touch-action:none}` blocked every vertical drag that started on a
stacked chart. It is now `touch-action:pan-y` (native vertical scroll stays; a horizontal drag scrubs the
chart), and `charts.js`'s `pointermove` handler now waits for the first few pixels of a drag to decide its
direction -- a drag that resolves mostly vertical sets `dragging = false` and lets the browser's own pan take
over, instead of calling `show()` on every move.

**Week labels name the Monday.** The goal chart's weekly `data-points` label (`goals.chart_week_label`,
"Semana del {date}") was built from the same date the point is plotted on -- `week_start + 6` days, the
Sunday the check's average week ends on -- so every label named a Sunday. `_goal_line_svg` now carries each
check's `week_start` (the Monday) alongside its plotted day; the plotted x/y are unchanged, only the label's
date now reads the Monday.

**Visible focus.** `figure.chart` is `tabIndex = 0` (charts.js) but had no focus style of its own; the page's
global `:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus)}` rule turned out not to render visibly on it in the
browser the orchestrator measured in. Added `figure.chart:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);
outline-offset:4px;border-radius:8px}`, reusing the app's existing `--focus` token rather than introducing one.

**Tests**, `tests/test_pulido_2.py` (4 new tests, 9 -> 13): `ChartsJsSourceTest` gained a test that the
capture-phase click listener exists, calls `preventDefault`, is scoped via `svg.contains`, and never
references the readout's `caption`; a test that `body.css` declares `touch-action:pan-y` and not `:none`; and
a test that `figure.chart:focus-visible` declares an outline. A new `GoalChartWeekLabelTest` seeds a goal and
a weekly check at `week_start = "2026-08-10"` (a Monday) and asserts the rendered label carries "10 ago" and
not "16 ago" (the Sunday six days later).

**Gate**, run once on the final tree with the plain command: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover
tests -t .` -- `Ran 799 tests in 61.113s ... OK (skipped=1)` (795 before this slice, +4 new).

**Merge: this spec is its own approval.** The diff touches customer-facing bytes (the click-cancelling
behaviour, the scroll behaviour, the weekly label's date, the focus ring) -- merge policy A's customer-bytes
condition trips on its own, but this spec's body says in words to merge after the gate, carrying BODY-PULIDO-2's
approval forward along with its own. Merged `--no-ff` into `main`; `main` left checked out, clean. Branch
`feat/body-pulido-2` kept.

## BODY-PRIMER-DIA-1 -- three first-day fixes from the first-day census (2026-11-07)

BODY-PRIMER-DIA-CENSO-1 (OBSERVED, 2026-11-07) found three quality defects on a hosted person's very first day.
This slice fixes the three that are quality, not product shape.

**1. Sign-in refused was the only plain-English dead end on the whole sign-in path.** The Cuenta callback's
`except cuenta.FlowRefused:` in `body/web.py` returned `Response("Sign-in refused", status_code=400,
media_type="text/plain")`. It now renders a new template, `body/templates/acceso_rechazado.html` (built like
`sin_acceso.html`'s shape: one card, one `taplink`), with new i18n keys `acceso_rechazado.title/text/retry`,
still at 400, with one `taplink` to `/login`. One generic message either way -- it never exposes which
cuenta-duna-v1 check failed. **Deviation:** the spec's decision said to pick the page's language "the way the
other pre-sign-in pages do (re-find `sin_acceso`'s route and copy its choice)," naming the request's

Cuenta-down page both always render with `T(DEFAULT_LANG)` regardless of request headers, because the person
is not known yet and Body has no other way to guess their language pre-sign-in. The new page follows that
same, actual pattern (`T(DEFAULT_LANG)`), not an Accept-Language mechanism that does not exist in this
codebase.

**2. The empty-state sync text never said WHEN data would arrive.** `_sync_status_text` in `body/web.py`, used
by Hoy/Día/Tendencias/Historial's empty states, always said only "the sync runs on its own" plus "it hasn't

autoescape skips re-escaping a value that is already `Markup`. Local mode is unchanged (the docstring's
original reason -- Body cannot read a per-install schedule time -- still holds there, and only there).

**3. «Primera mirada a Hoy» silently required a PC.** `tutoriales.primeros_pasos` ticked it only when every
earlier item was done, including `vincular-este-pc` -- so a hosted person with no PC, who had signed in,

stays its own item, ticked exactly as before (`bool(vinculado)`), and no longer gates it.

## BODY-PRIMER-PULL-1 -- bounded hosted backfill, a second timer, serialised with a lock (2026-11-07)

Carrying out BODY-PRIMER-PULL-OBS-1's recommendation (OBSERVED at `7700590`): the hosted pull only ever fetched
a rolling 2-day window, so a newly connected person's Tendencias, baselines and readiness stayed empty for
weeks. `body/pull.py` gets `python -m body.pull --backfill` (hosted only) plus a second systemd timer that
calls it every 10 minutes.

**1. The marker.** `garmin_cuenta` gets one new nullable column, `backfill_hasta` (a `db.py` migration in the
existing style, same pattern as `ajuste_agente.proveedor`): the oldest day (YYYY-MM-DD) this person's backfill
has already attempted, with or without data. `NULL` = not started. Two new `garmin_cuenta.py` functions,
`marcador_backfill` (read) and `avanzar_backfill` (write), named like its existing `leer`/`guardar`.

**2. The window and the batch.** `BACKFILL_DIAS = 90`, `BACKFILL_PASO = 15` in `pull.py`. Per run, per
connected person: `_dias_pendientes_backfill` computes up to 15 days older than the marker (or older than
yesterday, if the marker is still `NULL`) down to `today - 90`, newest first; `[]` once the marker has reached
that limit -- zero Garmin calls, zero cost. `_backfill_one_person` fetches that batch day by day (newest
first, so recent figures land first), advancing `avanzar_backfill` after each day -- including an empty one --
so it is never asked again, re-encrypting a refreshed token exactly as `_pull_one_person` does (re-used, not
copied). `pull_backfill_hosted` loops every connected person the same way `pull_hosted` does: one person's
`NotSignedIn` or any other exception is recorded with `registrar_error` and costs that person's progress for
this run only; the rest still progress. Only counts and dates are ever printed.

**3. The lock.** A new non-blocking exclusive lock under `BODY_HOME` (`pull.lock`), taken by `_run` around
both the daily hosted pull and `--backfill` (never around the raw `pull_hosted`/`pull_backfill_hosted`
functions themselves, so the existing direct-call tests in `test_garmin_host.py` needed no changes). POSIX:
`fcntl.flock(f, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)`. Windows (dev/test only -- the host is Linux): `msvcrt.locking(fd,
LK_NBLCK, 1)` on a 1-byte region at offset 0, confirmed by hand first (two separate handles to the same path in
the same process: the second genuinely blocks) and then by the gate's own `LockTest`. Held lock -> the run
prints "another pull is already running; skipping this run." and exits 0; the timer tries again in 10 minutes.
Local mode never takes it (unchanged local behaviour, as the spec required).

**4. `--backfill` in local mode refuses.** Local mode has `--all` for the same job; `--backfill` prints a
one-line refusal and exits 2, without touching the lock or Garmin.

**5. Units.** `deploy/host/body-backfill.service` (oneshot, `ExecStart=... python -m body.pull --backfill`,
every other directive copied from `body-pull.service` unchanged) and `body-backfill.timer`
(`OnBootSec=2min`, `OnUnitActiveSec=10min`). `body-deploy.sh`'s `UNITS` array and its `systemctl enable` line
both gained the two new files, the same way `body-pull`'s own entries read. `body-pull.service` itself needed
no edit -- the lock lives in application code, not the unit.

**6. Text.** `sync.hosted_connected` (hosted, connected, no data yet) changed from "once a day, in the
morning" (no longer true -- the backfill timer runs every 10 minutes) to, in Spanish: "Tu reloj ya está
conectado. Body está trayendo tus últimos 90 días; las primeras cifras aparecen en unos minutos."; in English:
"Your watch is connected. Body is bringing in your last 90 days; your first figures appear within minutes."
Still names no clock time. `tests/test_primer_dia_1.py` needed no textual edit (its assertions read the key
dynamically via `_t()`), only its one test method's name, which had baked in the old "once a day" wording.

**Tests**, `tests/test_primer_pull_1.py` (new, 12 tests, no network -- every Garmin call stubbed through
`body.pull.garmin_adapter.fetch_day`, patched the same way `test_garmin_host.py` does): one run fetches 15 days
newest-first and moves the marker; 6 repeated runs exhaust the 90-day window, a 7th makes zero adapter calls; a
day fetched once (empty or not) is never asked again; one person's adapter error is recorded and the other
person still progresses; a refreshed token is re-saved; an unconnected person costs no call; a held lock makes
both `--backfill` and the daily hosted pull exit 0 with zero adapter calls, and the daily pull is proven to
hold the lock from the inside (a nested lock attempt during its own in-flight call fails) and to release it
again once it finishes; local mode refuses `--backfill` without any adapter call; the printed backfill line is
asserted character-for-character, proving no health figure reaches stdout. `tests/test_host_deploy.py` gained
two tests (`BackfillUnitTest`-style) for the new unit files' directives and `body-deploy.sh`'s wiring of them;
nothing existing there was weakened. `tests/test_garmin_host.py` needed no change -- it calls `pull_hosted`
directly, never through the now-locked `_run`.

**Deviation, found and fixed inside this slice, recorded rather than hidden.** The first `_try_lock()` draft
read one byte of the lock file before taking the OS lock, to decide whether to write a seed byte first. On
Windows that read itself raised `PermissionError` whenever the byte it tried to read fell inside a region
another handle already held locked -- so a *held* lock made the second `_try_lock()` crash instead of
returning `None`. Confirmed by hand (`msvcrt.locking` on a zero-length file works with no pre-write needed) and
fixed by dropping the read/write entirely; `_try_lock` now only seeks to offset 0 and locks. The gate's first
run on this slice's tree was RED on that bug (1 failure, 2 errors, in the two held-lock tests and the
from-the-inside daily-pull test) -- `Ran 826 tests in 256.956s ... FAILED (failures=1, errors=2, skipped=1)`.
Fixed, then run once more as this slice's recorded gate (below); no other change was needed.

**Gate**, run once on the final tree with the plain command: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover
tests -t .` -- `Ran 826 tests in 98.921s ... OK (skipped=1)` (812 before this slice, +14: 12 in
`test_primer_pull_1.py`, 2 in `test_host_deploy.py`).

**Merge: stopped before it.** The diff changes the schema (`garmin_cuenta.backfill_hasta`, a new column) and
customer-facing bytes (`sync.hosted_connected`'s es/en text) -- merge policy A's schema and customer-bytes
conditions both trip, and this spec's approval authorises the build, not the merge. Committed on
`feat/body-primer-pull-1`, gate green, nothing merged.

## BODY-PRIMER-PULL-1-M -- lands BODY-PRIMER-PULL-1 with two fixes from the orchestrator's review (2026-11-07)

ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1 approved BODY-PRIMER-PULL-1's diff (the `backfill_hasta` column and its
migration, the marker/window walk, the lock, the units, the hosted empty-state text) but required two fixes
before landing, both inside `body/pull.py`:

**1. The daily hosted pull now waits for the lock instead of skipping.** `_run` used the same non-blocking
`_try_lock()` for both the daily hosted pull (`deploy/host/body-pull.service`, `OnCalendar` 09:30 once a day)
and `--backfill` (every 10 minutes). Skipping on a held lock is right for the backfill timer -- it tries again
in 10 minutes -- but wrong for the daily pull, which would simply lose that day's run. A new `_esperar_lock
(max_s)` polls `_try_lock()` every `LOCK_SONDEO_S` (5s) until it succeeds or `max_s` elapses, and the daily
pull calls it with the new module constant `LOCK_ESPERA_S = 1800` (30 minutes); only past that bound does it
print the existing skip line and exit 0. `--backfill` keeps calling `_try_lock()` directly, unchanged. One
lock implementation throughout; no new dependency. Local mode is untouched -- it never takes the lock.

**2. The backfill now skips a person whose last pull recorded an error.** `pull_backfill_hosted` retried
every connected person every run, so a person with a rejected or expired token (`garmin_cuenta.ultimo_error`
set by `registrar_error`) would be hit every 10 minutes indefinitely -- a real risk of Garmin rate-limiting or
locking the account. It now checks `garmin_cuenta.ultimo_error(conn, person_id)` (the accessor already
existed; `body/garmin_cuenta.py` was not in this slice's `touches:`, so nothing there changed) and skips such a
person before any adapter call, without counting them as failed and without moving their backfill marker.
Nothing else changes: the daily pull still tries everyone once a day and calls `limpiar_error` on success, and
a reconnect (`garmin_cuenta.guardar`) already clears `ultimo_error` too -- either path lets the backfill
resume on its own, with no new wiring needed.

**Tests**, `tests/test_primer_pull_1.py` (+3 over BODY-PRIMER-PULL-1's 12): the existing held-lock daily-pull
test was rewritten to patch `LOCK_ESPERA_S`/`LOCK_SONDEO_S` short and assert the same exit-0-with-skip-line
behaviour now happens only once that bound elapses; a new test holds the lock, releases it from a
`threading.Timer` shortly after, and proves the daily pull waits then completes (an adapter call happens) in
real time but on a patched short bound, not a 30-minute sleep; two new `BackfillWindowTest` cases prove a
person with a recorded error gets zero adapter calls and an unmoved marker while another connected person in
the same run still backfills, and that a reconnect's `guardar` (clearing `ultimo_error`) lets the next run
resume. `--backfill`'s own held-lock test was unaffected -- it still calls `_try_lock()` directly, unchanged.

**Pre-flight.** Branch tip measured at `309a012e02c590a3619f104ea22492f5d3a0a6f5`, matching the spec. `git
merge-base feat/body-primer-pull-1 main` equalled `main`'s own tip (`77005906f11107b7c90a2c35db1115c24595552e`),
so `main` had not moved since the branch was cut; no merge-in-first step was needed.

**Gate**, run once on the branch tip with the fixes committed: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover
tests -t .` -- `Ran 829 tests in 80.131s ... OK (skipped=1)` (826 before this slice, +3: the two new
backfill-skip tests plus the one new waits-then-completes lock test; one existing test was rewritten, not
added). Merged `--no-ff` into `main`; since `main` had not moved, the merge tree
(`7f410873b6efc470d97bb77ec555ba364271ed08`) is identical to the branch tip's tree, so the gate was not re-run
after the merge.

**Merge.** This spec's approval said "Then merge." in words, and the actual diff (`body/pull.py`,
`tests/test_primer_pull_1.py`) carries no schema change, no customer-facing bytes and no cross-repo contract --
merge policy A's three conditions all pass. Merged `--no-ff` into `main`, which is left checked out, clean.

## BODY-ENV-LOCAL-1 -- a local `.env` so Carlos can paste the assistant's API key once (2026-11-07)

Relayed by Main 2026-11-07, Carlos's words: "He have to create an [env] file local to put that, because right now
that is the single value that I'm still having here ready to paste." Measured on `main` at `fb16ee9`: no dotenv
loader existed; every assistant setting was read straight from `os.environ`; `.env` was already in `.gitignore`.

**1. `body/entorno.py` (new).** A ~30-line, dependency-free parser. `RUTA_DEFECTO` is `<repo root>/.env`, found
from this module's own path (`Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]`), never from the current directory. `cargar
(ruta=None, entorno=os.environ) -> (cargados, ignorados)`: missing file returns `(0, 0)` silently; otherwise reads
UTF-8 with BOM tolerance (`utf-8-sig`), skips blank/`#` lines, strips one `export ` prefix, splits on the first
`=`, strips surrounding whitespace and one matching pair of quotes from the value. A name not starting with
`BODY_AGENTE_` or not matching `[A-Z0-9_]+` is **ignored and counted** -- the allowlist decision: `body/cuenta.py`
decides hosted mode from `bool(os.environ.get(ISSUER_ENV))`, so a stray Cuenta line in a local file would
silently flip the PC into hosted mode, and host secrets belong in the server's own env file
(`deploy/host/body.env.example`), never here. A name already present in `entorno` is left alone and not counted
as loaded -- **the real environment wins**: the host's systemd `EnvironmentFile` and Carlos's own Windows user
variables keep precedence over this file. An empty value is never loaded. Never logs or returns a value.

**2. `body/web.py`.** `main()` calls `entorno.cargar()` as its first line, before `_ensure_streams()` or anything
else -- never at module import, so no test or other module ever touches a real file just by importing `body.web`.
If any line was ignored, it prints exactly one line naming the count and the rule (".env: N line(s) ignored --
only BODY_AGENTE_* names are read from this file."), placed after `_ensure_streams()` so it can never crash
against a `None` stdout under `pythonw`. No new dependency -- a plain stdlib parser, no install step.

**3. `.env.example` (new, committed; `.env` stays in `.gitignore`).** A header pointing at the local workflow
(copy to `.env`, paste keys, restart "Body app web") and naming the hosted file
(`deploy/host/body.env.example` -> `/srv/duna/env/body.env`) as the separate, unrelated path for the server. The
seven keys match `body/agente/cliente.py`'s `_FABRICAS` and `deploy/host/body.env.example` exactly (re-checked
against both; no name differs), with Duna's model standard filled in and every API key left empty:
`BODY_AGENTE_PROVEEDOR=anthropic`, `BODY_AGENTE_MODELO_ANTHROPIC=claude-sonnet-5-5`,
`BODY_AGENTE_MODELO_OPENAI=gpt-6.1-sol`, `BODY_AGENTE_MODELO_GEMINI=gemini-3.8-flash`.

**4. `README.md`.** A new "Asistente: tu clave de IA" section makes `.env.example` -> `.env` the normal PC way to
set a key, and keeps the `$env:BODY_AGENTE_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "..."` form as the documented alternative for one
PowerShell session, stating that the real environment always wins over the file.

**Tests**, `tests/test_env_local_1.py` (new, 11 tests, `tests/_isolate.py` imported first, every case on a temp
directory and a plain dict as `entorno`, never the real repo `.env`): a `BODY_AGENTE_` line loads; `BODY_CUENTA_
ISSUER`, `BODY_HOME`, `PATH` and a lowercase name are ignored and counted (4 in one file); a name already in
`entorno` is left untouched and not counted; double and single surrounding quotes are stripped; `export ` is
accepted; a UTF-8 BOM is tolerated; comments and blank lines are skipped; an empty value is not loaded; a missing
file returns `(0, 0)`; `RUTA_DEFECTO` equals the test file's own repo root's `.env`. The eleventh test proves a
fresh import of `body.web` never calls `entorno.cargar` -- it pops `body.web` out of `sys.modules`, imports it
fresh under a patched `entorno.cargar`, asserts not-called, then restores the *original* module object into
`sys.modules` rather than reloading the shared one in place.

**A caught regression, not shipped.** The first draft of that eleventh test used `importlib.reload(web)` on the
real, shared module object. A full-suite run on that draft came back **RED**, 5 failures, all in
`tests/test_person_scope.py` and `tests/test_pulido_1.py` -- neither file is in this slice's `touches:` and
neither has anything to do with environment loading. Running those two files alone (`python -m unittest
tests.test_person_scope tests.test_pulido_1`) passed clean (42 tests, OK), proving the failures were cross-module
pollution, not a real defect in those files. Disabling only the reload-based test and re-running the full suite
confirmed it: green, 840 tests. The reload mutated `body.web`'s module object in place -- same identity every
other already-imported test module holds a reference to -- rebuilding its FastAPI `app`, routes and context vars
out from under tests that ran afterward in the same process. Rewritten as the pop/restore-into-a-throwaway-import
shown above, which confines the fresh module execution to an object nothing else ever looks up. This was caught
and fixed before the gate counted below; it never reached a committed tree.

**Pre-flight.** Branch tip (this slice's own commit) measured at `cb6e8bac7f3194a3d65062507bd9072234ae1aee`. `git
merge-base feat/body-env-local-1 main` equalled `main`'s own tip (`fb16ee9d4be8046f59f7db54776946d4dfe5c1ca`), so
`main` had not moved since the branch was cut; no merge-in-first step was needed.

**Gate**, run once on the final branch tree, exact command `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests
-t .`: `Ran 840 tests in 134.586s ... OK (skipped=1)` (one pre-existing POSIX-only skip, unrelated to this
slice).

**Merge.** This spec's approval said to merge "if your merge policy allows it (no customer-facing bytes; no
schema)" -- conditional, not an override, so merge policy A's own three conditions govern. No schema or
migration change (`body/db.py` untouched); no cross-repo contract or DTO change. The diff does touch `README.md`
and adds one new printed line in `body/web.py`'s `main()` -- bytes Carlos reads as this app's own local operator
-- so this slice classified them against this ledger's own precedent rather than guessing: `BODY-WEB-AUTOSTART-1`
("no customer-facing bytes (nothing a browser ever renders changed -- this is a startup-only fix for a server
that has no console to show anything on)") and the installer slice at this ledger's line 340-341 ("the
installer's console output and the README are not customer-facing application bytes (no screen, no i18n
string)") both hold, in this Tier 2 repository, that console text and README wording are not customer-facing
bytes unless they are a template or an i18n string a browser renders. Neither is true of this diff -- no
`templates/`, no `i18n/` file changed. (A different ledger entry, `BODY-HOST-ENTRY-2`, called a console refusal
message and a README change customer-facing bytes, but that slice was Tier 1 `deploy/` work read by Carlos as
the host's own operator during a live deploy; the distinction is the surface, not a contradiction of the rule
applied here.) All three of merge policy A's conditions clear, so this merges on green without waiting. Merged
`--no-ff` into `main`, which is left checked out, clean.

## BODY-TURNOS-ESQUEMA-1 -- the schema for the optional shift-work setting, nothing that reads it yet (2026-11-07)

Carries out `BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-OBS-1`'s slice 1 of five, under `ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`, with three
orchestrator decisions bounding this slice (quoted from the approval): **(a)** three states, not the census's
`NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` -- `person.trabaja_turnos` is `NULL` (not answered yet), `0` (no) or `1` (yes), so onboarding
can ask once and a screen can tell "never asked" from "said no"; Turnos shows only when the value is `1`
(`trabaja_turnos_si`), so `NULL` and `0` both hide it. **(b)** the backfill to `1` runs ONCE, inside the same
`_migrate` branch that adds the column (guarded by `"trabaja_turnos" not in pcols`), so a person who later
answers "no" is never flipped back by a restart; it sets `1` for every person id found in `shift` or
`shift_batch`, which is Carlos's own Turnos exactly as today. A fresh database gets the column from `CREATE
TABLE person` itself, so the guard is already false and no backfill runs on it (it has no rows regardless).
**(c)** the three accessors (`get_trabaja_turnos`, `set_trabaja_turnos`, `trabaja_turnos_si`) live in
`body/db.py` (Tier 1) in this slice, so slices 2-5 (the screens) stay Tier 2.

**Shape added.** `person.trabaja_turnos INTEGER CHECK (trabaja_turnos IN (0, 1))`, nullable, no default, in both
`CREATE TABLE person` and a guarded `_migrate` ALTER (SQLite accepts a CHECK on `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` when
the default/NULL satisfies it for existing rows). `shift_batch.kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'import' CHECK (kind IN
('import', 'pattern'))`, in the CREATE and a guarded ALTER (SQLite fills the literal default into every existing
row, which is why `kind` reads back `'import'` for a shift_batch row that predates this slice). `shift_pattern`
(new table): `person_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES person(id)`, `start_day TEXT NOT NULL`, `cycle TEXT NOT
NULL CHECK (json_valid(cycle))` (a JSON array of `{"kind", "start_local", "end_local"}` entries; no
parser/validator for its contents here -- slice 5 owns that), `horizon_weeks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 8 CHECK
(horizon_weeks BETWEEN 1 AND 26)`, `updated_at TEXT NOT NULL`. The `shift.kind` vocabulary `kind` draws from,
re-found verbatim in `body/shift_import.py`'s `VALID_KINDS` and the existing `shift`/`shift_batch_item` CHECK
constraints: `{'morning', 'afternoon', 'night', 'day', 'off', 'other'}`.

**Privacy.** `shift_pattern` has a `person_id` column, so `tests/test_privacidad.py`'s coverage test (every
`person_id`-keyed table is in exactly one of `FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES` / `PARTIAL_EXPORT_TABLES` /
`NEVER_EXPORTED_TABLES`) would fail without it; added to `FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES`, exported as the person's own
row under `vida.shift_pattern` (or `null`), and deleted in `delete_person`. `person.trabaja_turnos` is exported
in `persona`, alongside `language`.

**Tests**, `tests/test_turnos_esquema_1.py` (new, 10 tests, `tests/_isolate.py` imported first, invented demo
data only): an old-shape database (person without the column, shift rows for A, a shift_batch for B, nothing
for C) migrates to A=1, B=1, C=NULL; setting C=0 and A=0 then re-running `db.init` leaves both unchanged (the

## BODY-MODELOS-ESTANDAR-1 -- Duna's AI model standard (modelos-ia-v1) (2026-11-07)

Carries out `BODY-MODELOS-ESTANDAR-OBS-1` (OBSERVED at `fb16ee9`) under `ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`, putting
Body's assistant on Duna's one set of AI models (`modelos-ia-v1`, decided by Main on Carlos's own ask "make a
standard of what model will be used, check the difference and solve them").

**Decision 1 -- code defaults for all three providers.** `MODELO_DEFAULT_OPENAI = "gpt-6.1-sol"` and
`MODELO_DEFAULT_GEMINI = "gemini-3.8-flash"` added beside `MODELO_DEFAULT = "claude-sonnet-5-5"` in
`body/agente/cliente.py`; `_modelo_openai()`/`_modelo_gemini()` now mirror `_modelo_anthropic()`'s fallback
chain (`BODY_AGENTE_MODELO_<X>` -> `BODY_AGENTE_MODELO` -> the provider's standard default). The live gate in
`proveedores_configurados()` is unchanged code (`if api_key and modelo`) -- with every provider's model function
now always returning a default, the key alone decides whether a provider turns on, at the standard model. A
provider with no key still stays off.

**Decision 2 -- dated prices as `desde` only.** `precio_modelo` (`body/db.py`) gains `desde TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT
'2000-01-01'`; its primary key becomes `(proveedor, modelo, tipo, desde)`. A row applies from its date until the
next row's date for the same (proveedor, modelo, tipo) -- one column, so it can never leave a gap or an overlap
the way a `desde`/`hasta` pair could. SQLite cannot `ALTER` a primary key, so `_migrate_precios` (new, called
from `init()` BEFORE `executescript(SCHEMA)`, the same ordering as `_migrate_metas`/`_migrate_cuenta`) rebuilds
the table in one transaction (`_rebuild_precio_modelo_table`, reusing `_rebuild_with_fk_off`) when an existing
table lacks `desde`: every row, including an operator's own hand-set price, is copied with `desde = '2000-01-01'`,
never lost. The `DEFAULT '2000-01-01'` on the column (not asked for by the spec, found necessary by the gate --
see Measured, below) keeps a raw `INSERT INTO precio_modelo (proveedor, modelo, tipo, micro_usd_por_millon)
VALUES (...)` with no `desde` column working exactly as before, for the pre-existing tests outside `touches:`
that write that table directly. `body/agente/uso.py`'s `_precios(conn, proveedor, modelo, fecha)` now takes a
date and picks, per tipo, the row with the greatest `desde <= fecha` (a correlated-subquery `MAX(desde)`, all
four tipos still required or the model is reported unpriced); `_gasto_hoy_micro_usd` prices each usage row by the
date of its OWN `creado_en` (`row["creado_en"][:10]`), not "today", since a price can step between rows on the
same day's boundary. A new `_hoy_local()` gives `verificar_tope` the person's own local calendar day for its
"is the live model priced right now" check.

**Decision 3 -- cached input per modelos-ia-v1.1** (Main, 2026-11-07, asked by Body): `body/agente/precios.json`
now seeds all three standard models, each row carrying its `desde`: Anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5` (desde
`2000-01-01`, unchanged from the prior seed); OpenAI `gpt-6.1-sol` (desde `2000-01-01`, cached input 10 cents =
100_000 micro-USD/million, OpenAI's own published price); Gemini `gemini-3.8-flash` TWICE -- desde `2000-01-01`
at 75/375/75/75 cents (in/out/cache-in/cache-write) and desde `2027-01-01` at 150/750/150/150 cents, Gemini's own
cache price being NOT KNOWN so priced at the full input rate both before and after the step (conservative: the
spend ceiling trips early, never late, never under-counts). `cache_escritura` for OpenAI and Gemini is seeded at
the input price for the same reason: both adapters report 0 such tokens today (`cache_escritura=0` in
`_desde_openai`/`_desde_gemini`), so it is a placeholder price that can never under-count a real charge.
`body/agente/precios.py` validates `desde` as a `YYYY-MM-DD` string; `sembrar()`'s `INSERT OR IGNORE` is now keyed
on all four columns, so an operator's own price for one tipo on one date is still never overwritten.

**Decision 4 -- the dead fallback in `body/web.py`.** The census's `os.environ.get('BODY_AGENTE_MODELO',
agente_cliente.MODELO_DEFAULT)` read a SECOND copy of the same env var `_modelo_anthropic()` already folds into
its own fallback chain, reached only when nothing is configured (`resuelto is None`) -- at which point
`proveedor_configurado()` is also `None` and `generar()` returns on the `no_configurado` error before `modelo` is
read, in production. Measured (see below) that `tests/test_agente_propuestas.py` patches `proveedor_configurado`
ALONE, independently of `proveedores_configurados()`/`nombre_elegido()`, which breaks that invariant under test
and DOES reach this line with a `FakeProveedor` that has no `.modelo` attribute -- so the fix is `modelo =
configurados[resuelto].modelo if resuelto else agente_cliente.MODELO_DEFAULT`, reading the client's own default
CONSTANT (removing the redundant env lookup) rather than an object attribute that not every test double carries.
No customer-facing text changed.

**Contract copy.** `docs/contracts/modelos-ia-v1.md` copied byte for byte from
`C:/Duna/body/dev-protocol/contracts/modelos-ia-v1.md` via `shutil.copyfile`; sha256
`77422651a7d0e1704ea6d854740273ee0fbc603bc8375b36831637088ece0862` verified against the spec's figure. Added to
`docs/contracts/README.md` in alphabetical order (between `host-deploy-v1-amendment-sensitive-data.md` and
`tutoriales-v1.md`), file count corrected eight -> nine.

**Host env, README.** `deploy/host/body.env.example`'s three `BODY_AGENTE_MODELO_*` lines now carry the standard
values as their default text (keys stay blank); the surrounding comment explains the key-alone-turns-it-on
behavior and names `modelos-ia-v1`. `README.md`'s «Asistente: precios del modelo» section now names the three
standard models, the `desde` dating, and Gemini's cached-input-at-full-price caveat.

**Tests.** `tests/test_host_deploy.py`'s `EnvExampleTest.FIXED` gained the three `BODY_AGENTE_MODELO_*` names at
their standard values (the three API key names stay in the blank-required set). `tests/test_agente_cliente.py`'s
`test_openai_selected_by_env_needs_its_own_key_and_model` renamed/rewritten
(`..._configures_at_the_standard_model_once_keyed`): key alone now configures OpenAI at
`MODELO_DEFAULT_OPENAI`, an explicit `BODY_AGENTE_MODELO_OPENAI` still overrides it.
`tests/test_agente_proveedores.py`'s `test_key_alone_does_not_configure_openai_or_gemini` renamed/rewritten
(`..._configures_openai_and_gemini_at_the_standard_model`) to assert the opposite of its old name, now that
decision 1 is code, not env; `test_model_alone_does_not_configure_openai_or_gemini` (model set, no key -> `{}`)
needed no change. `tests/test_agente_precios.py` updated for the 16-row seed (4 price entries x 4 tipos) and the
`(proveedor, modelo, tipo, desde)` key throughout (`uso._precios` now takes a date; the operator-row and
missing-tipo/negative-value fixtures now carry `desde`), plus a new `test_a_file_with_a_bad_desde_...` case.
New `tests/test_modelos_estandar_1.py` (4 tests): an old-shape `precio_modelo` with an operator row survives
`db.init()`'s rebuild at `desde = '2000-01-01'` and is not overwritten by `sembrar()`; a Gemini usage date of
`2026-12-31` prices at the first seed row, `2027-01-01` at the second.

**Measured, against the spec.** First full gate run (`Ran 855 tests in 115.268s ... FAILED (failures=2, errors=8,
skipped=1)`, before the fixes below) surfaced two faults the census and spec text did not anticipate, both
outside `touches:` and fixed without widening it: (1) `tests/test_agente_bucle.py`'s `RowByRowPricingTest`/`SpendCeilingTest` insert into
`precio_modelo` with the OLD four-column shape directly (no `desde`) -- fixed by giving the column `DEFAULT
'2000-01-01'` rather than editing that test file; (2) placing the `desde`-rebuild check inside `_migrate()`
itself (after its own `UPDATE person SET timezone = ...` line, which opens an implicit DML transaction in
Python's legacy sqlite3 transaction handling) raised `sqlite3.OperationalError: cannot start a transaction within
a transaction` inside `_rebuild_with_fk_off`'s own `BEGIN` -- fixed by moving the check into a new
`_migrate_precios()`, called from `init()` BEFORE `executescript(SCHEMA)`, the same position
`_migrate_metas`/`_migrate_cuenta` already use for exactly this reason. A third fault, also outside `touches:`
and fixed inside `body/web.py` itself: the spec's "point the dead fallback at the client's own resolution" read
as `proveedor.modelo`, which 500'd four tests in `tests/test_agente_propuestas.py` whose `FakeProveedor` mock has
no `.modelo` attribute (decision 4, above, has the actual fix).

**Gate**, exact command `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`, run once (after all three
fixes above) on the final tree, foreground: `Ran 855 tests in 164.163s ... OK (skipped=1)` (5 more tests than
`BODY-TURNOS-ESQUEMA-1`'s last-recorded 850: the new `test_modelos_estandar_1.py`'s 4, plus
`test_a_file_with_a_bad_desde_inserts_nothing_and_raises` in `test_agente_precios.py`).

**Merge.** `body/db.py`'s `precio_modelo` table changed shape (new `desde` column, new primary key, a rebuild
migration) -- a schema change, failing merge policy A's first condition outright regardless of the other two
(no customer-facing bytes changed; no cross-repo contract changed). Stopping `AWAITING_APPROVAL` on
`feat/body-modelos-estandar-1` without merging, per this slice's own approval ("Schema and deploy are Tier 1:
stop AWAITING_APPROVAL on the branch if your merge policy says so"). Slice commit

## BODY-MODELOS-ESTANDAR-1-M -- two fixes to the AI model standard, then merged (2026-11-07)

The orchestrator's review (`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`) approved `feat/body-modelos-estandar-1` (commit
`6e512c6`) with two fixes to be made inside the slice's own files before landing.

**Fix 1 -- one date basis for a dated price.** `body/agente/uso.py`'s `verificar_tope` asked `_precios(...,
hoy)` for the person's own local calendar day (`_hoy_local`), while `_gasto_hoy_micro_usd` prices each usage row
at the UTC date of its own `creado_en` -- the two could disagree near a person's local midnight (e.g. on
2026-12-31 after 19:00 in Bogota, once the UTC day has already stepped to 2027-01-01 and Gemini's price with
it). `verificar_tope` now computes `hoy` from `_ahora_utc().date()`, the same UTC date basis, with a comment
saying why: a vendor's price step takes effect on a UTC date, so the two checks must agree. `uso.py`'s
`_hoy_local` is now unused and removed (`body/agente/herramientas.py`'s `_hoy_local` is a separate function, for
a goal's `start_day`, and is untouched). The day RANGE that bounds which rows count as "today"
(`_rango_dia_local_utc`, the person's own local midnight) is a separate question from which date prices a row,
and stays exactly as it was.

**Fix 2 -- the price note.** `body/agente/precios.json`'s `fuente` called Anthropic's cache-write row (2_500_000,
1.25x its input price, modelos-ia-v1.1's own cited figure) "the input price" -- it is not; only OpenAI's
cache-write and Gemini's whole cache column fall back to the full input price, because no vendor figure is known
for them. Rewrote the sentence to say that, and to say Anthropic's four figures and OpenAI's cached input are
cited vendor prices from modelos-ia-v1.1. No number in the file changed.

**Test.** `tests/test_modelos_estandar_1.py` gained `UtcDateBasisTest`: with the clock patched to
`2027-01-01T03:00Z` (Bogota local `2026-12-31 22:00`) and a stored usage row at that same UTC instant, a spy on
`uso._precios` shows `verificar_tope`'s priced check and `_gasto_hoy_micro_usd`'s row pricing both ask for
`2027-01-01` -- the Gemini row that just stepped -- never `2026-12-31`. Run against the pre-fix code (by hand,
not committed), this test fails: the priced check asked for `2026-12-31` instead, discriminating the fix.

**Measured, against the spec.** `main` had not moved since the branch was cut (`git merge-base` equalled
`main`'s tip, `7735200`); no merge of `main` into the branch was needed, and nothing was resolved by guessing.

**Gate**, exact command `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`, run once on the branch after
both fixes, foreground: `Ran 856 tests in 121.396s ... OK (skipped=1)` (one more than BODY-MODELOS-ESTANDAR-1's
855: the new `UtcDateBasisTest`).

**Merge.** The diff touches no schema or migration, no customer-facing bytes (`precios.json`'s `fuente` is a
documentation field, never read by any code path, let alone shown to a person), and no cross-repo contract --
merge policy A's three conditions all pass, and this spec's body says to merge. Fix commit
`126c0b16b5936cc91b036ba96ba5ffd98fca0d65` on `feat/body-modelos-estandar-1`, merged `--no-ff` into `main` at
`40d5534f38daca65eda7f6454008443b5cbebae3`. The merge commit's tree (`e156978c04647a52a51467db0f46f55d25d7d430`)
is identical to the branch tip's tree (`git diff` between them is empty), so the gate above still describes the
tree that landed; it was not re-run after the merge.

## BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-2 -- the one-time «¿Trabajas por turnos?» question, answered in place

Slice 2 of BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-OBS-1's plan under Carlos's ruling A (`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`, Carlos
chose option A on 2026-11-07). This slice only RECORDS the answer through the accessors
`BODY-TURNOS-ESQUEMA-1` merged (`db.get_trabaja_turnos`, `db.set_trabaja_turnos`, `db.trabaja_turnos_si`);
hiding Turnos when the answer is not yes is slice 3, and the PC-link rule is slice 4.

**The orchestrator's four decisions, as built:**
1. The question is answered IN PLACE on the Primeros pasos card (two 44 px buttons posting
   `valor=si|no` and `volver=/`), not by sending the person to Ajustes -- `body/templates/base.html`'s
   `primeros_pasos_card` macro renders the question and the two buttons in place of the plain link for the
   `trabajas-por-turnos` item while it is unanswered, and renders it ticked like every other item once
   answered.
2. Its item (`trabajas-por-turnos`) sits in `ONBOARDING_ORDEN` and in `tutoriales/catalogo.json`'s `orden`
   right after `conectar-garmin` and right before `vincular-este-pc` (renumbered `vincular-este-pc` to 4 and
   `primera-mirada-a-hoy` to 5), because slice 4 makes the PC step depend on this answer.
3. It ticks from data: `tutoriales.primeros_pasos()` computes its `hecho` as
   `db.get_trabaja_turnos(conn, person_id) is not None`, never a stored flag, exactly like every other
   Primeros pasos item. It is not skipped in local mode (only `vincular-este-pc` is local-mode-skipped).
4. `POST /settings/trabaja_turnos` (`body/web.py`, written like `set_language`: the
   `_cierra_conexion_async` decorator, `parse_qs` of the raw body) takes `volver` from an allowlist of
   exactly `"/"` or `"/settings"`; anything else (`https://example.com`, `//evil`, missing) falls back to
   `"/settings"`. `valor` must be `si` or `no`; anything else changes nothing.

**Ajustes.** `body/templates/settings.html` gained a card right after the language card: the question, a
two-button `seg` form identical in shape to the language one (the stored answer's button carries `btn on`;
neither does when the value is NULL), and one description line under it. `GET /settings` now also passes
`trabaja_turnos` (`db.get_trabaja_turnos(conn, person_id)`) to the template.

**i18n**, added to both `body/i18n/es.json` and `body/i18n/en.json` (verbatim in this slice's structured
report's `customer_bytes`): `settings.turnos.pregunta`, `settings.turnos.si`, `settings.turnos.no`,
`settings.turnos.desc`. No hard-coded text was added to any template.

**Tests.** New `tests/test_turnos_opcional_2.py` (imports `tests/_isolate.py` first): the route stores
1/0 and redirects to the allowlisted target, a foreign or missing `volver` falls back to `/settings`, a bad
or missing `valor` changes nothing; Ajustes marks the stored answer `on` and neither when NULL; the item's
position in `ONBOARDING_ORDEN` and in the catalog's `orden`; `primeros_pasos()`'s `hecho` for NULL/si/no and
that it shows in local mode too; the Hoy card renders two buttons while unanswered and a ticked link once
answered, in hosted and local mode; both languages render the question on Ajustes and on Hoy. Updated
`tests/test_tutoriales_puertas.py`'s onboarding-id-set assertions (`PrimerosPasosFunctionTest`) and its
"everything done" / "card disappears" cases to include `trabajas-por-turnos`, and its
`LeerTutorialesToolTest.test_consulta_filters_by_title_or_chapter_case_insensitively` case to include the new
task (its catalog title contains "turnos", so the existing "TURNO" query now also matches it) --
restoring each case's subject, not deleting it. `tests/test_primer_dia_1.py` needed no change: nothing in it
pins the full onboarding id set or count.

**Measured, not assumed.** The in-context "¿Cómo se hace?" door on `/settings` (`tarea_en_ruta`, first
catalog match by `pantalla`) now resolves to `trabajas-por-turnos` instead of `pagarle-a-duna`, because the
new task's `pantalla` is also `/settings` and it now sits earlier in the catalog's `tareas` array. No test
pinned the previous behaviour; this is a side effect of two tasks sharing one `pantalla`, not a defect this
spec asked to avoid, and the new door is arguably the more relevant one for a page that now carries this
exact question.

**Gate**, exact command `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`, run once on the branch,
foreground: `Ran 880 tests in 131.133s ... OK (skipped=1)` (the 24 new tests in
`tests/test_turnos_opcional_2.py`, over BODY-MODELOS-ESTANDAR-1-M's prior count).

**Merge.** The diff adds new customer-facing bytes (the question, its two answers and its description line,
on both Ajustes and Hoy, in two languages) -- merge policy A's customer-bytes condition fails, and the

## BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-3 -- Turnos disappears for a person who has not said they work shifts; gate red
outside `touches:` (2026-11-07)

Slice 3 of BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-OBS-1's plan (OBSERVED at `fb16ee9`), under Carlos's ruling A (orchestrator
ledger BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-1: "a screen whose data cannot arrive for this person is not shown to them").
Branch `feat/body-turnos-opcional-3` from `main`.

**Decision 1 -- one predicate.** Every shift surface the OBS-1 census found is gated on the single
`db.trabaja_turnos_si(conn, person_id)` (merged in BODY-TURNOS-ESQUEMA-1): NULL (not answered) and False
both hide it, only True shows exactly what shows today. No screen re-derives it -- `body/web.py` adds one
helper, `_turnos_on(conn, person_id)`, that calls it, computed once per request and passed to the template
the same way `tab` already is. `base.html`'s Turnos nav tab is now `{% if turnos %}`-wrapped, and since that
nav is unconditional on every page, every one of `web.py`'s ~26 `_render()` calls that extends `base.html`
now passes `turnos=` -- not only the shift-specific routes. `today.html`'s `hoy_turno_card`, `day.html`'s
«Tus turnos» block (including the "Noche N de M" / "N.º día después" line) and `history.html`'s «Tus turnos
por tipo» card are each wrapped in `{% if turnos %}` so nothing -- no heading, no gap -- is left in their
place. `trends.html` needed no template change: `web.py`'s `trends()` now computes the `nights` set (night-
shift shading) only `if start and turnos_on`, which already empties both the SVG shading and the
`nights=bool(nights)` flag the legend is gated on.

**Decision 2 -- 404s.** `/shifts`, `/shifts/como`, and the three shift POST routes (`/shifts/confirm`,
`/shifts/confirm-all`, `/shifts/dismiss`) now 404 when the predicate is False, the same
`raise HTTPException(404)` pattern `SOLO_EN_LINEA` already uses for local mode -- a bookmark cannot reach a
screen whose data cannot arrive.

**Ayuda.** `tutoriales.capitulos_con_tareas()` gained `incluir_turnos: bool = True` (the default keeps every
existing caller's behaviour, including the one test calling it with no arguments); `/ayuda` passes
`incluir_turnos=turnos_on` and leaves the `turnos` chapter out of the list entirely when False, rather than
rendering an empty one.

**Decision 3 -- the assistant.** `herramientas.disponibles(nivel)` is the one place the tool list offered to
the model is assembled (`body/agente/bucle.py`'s `_tool_specs`), and `bucle.py` is Tier 2 but outside this
slice's `touches:`, so the signal reaches it through a module-level contextvar (`_TURNOS_ACTUAL`, default
`True`, the same pattern `web.py` already uses for `_RUTA_ACTUAL`) instead of a new parameter on
`disponibles()` that would have required editing `bucle.py`'s call site. `web.py`'s `asistente_preguntar`
sets it once per request (`agente_herramientas.fijar_turnos_actual(_turnos_on(conn, person_id))`) before
calling into `agente_bucle.ejecutar`, and `disponibles()` leaves `leer_turnos`, `leer_costo_turnos` and
`proponer_confirmar_turnos` off the list it returns when the contextvar reads False -- a person who has not
said they work shifts is never offered them, so the assistant never talks about shifts nobody has.
`_leer_historia`'s `por_turno` key is left out of its result (not offered then failing) when the predicate is
False, read directly from the `conn`/`person_id` the tool already has -- no contextvar needed there.
`ejecutar()` itself is unchanged: the orchestrator's decision was "not offered", not "refused if called
anyway", and widening it to a hard refusal would have been scope this slice was not asked for.

**Decision 4, unchanged by this slice.** Shift data already stored is not deleted when a person answers no
(hiding is reversible, deleting is not -- privacy's delete-all still removes it); `body/vida_export.py` is
untouched (Tier 1, data-driven: no confirmed shift, no shift fields); a proposal already created stays as
it is.

**Tests.** `tests/test_turnos_opcional_3.py` (new -- `tests/test_agente_herramientas.py` named in the spec
did not exist, so its cases live here instead, as the spec allowed): three fixtures (the setting NULL, False,
True) sharing the IDENTICAL stored shift rows (a night today, a 5-night block 20 days back, 140 days of
steady metrics) prove the hiding comes from the setting, never from missing data -- the nav link, Hoy's
card, Día's block line, Historial's por-tipo card, Tendencias' night shading, `/shifts`, `/shifts/como`,
Ayuda's chapter, the assistant's tool list and the history tool's `por_turno`, each checked present for True
and absent for both NULL and False. Updated `tests/test_hoy_turno.py` (`WebRenderTest._reset_db`),
`tests/test_turnos_enlaces.py` (four `setUp`s: `CostRowLinksTest`, `CostRowNoDataTest`,
`DiaRendersContextTest`, `DiaShiftVocabularyTest`), and `tests/test_tutoriales_puertas.py` (`_fresh_client`,
shared by every `_LocalModeTestCase`/`_HostedModeTestCase`) to call `db.set_trabaja_turnos(conn, True, 1)`
for their subject -- restoring what each already tested, never deleting a case.

**Measured, not assumed: `touches:` was narrower than the behaviour change.** The full gate (below) failed
20 pre-existing tests, every one in a file the spec did not list in `touches:` -- `tests/test_dispositivo.py`,
`tests/test_person_scope.py`, `tests/test_pipeline.py`, `tests/test_shift_import.py`,
`tests/test_sin_friccion.py`, `tests/test_turnos_costo.py`. Each builds a fresh test database whose default
person has a NULL `trabaja_turnos` (the one-time backfill to 1 in `body/db.py`'s `_migrate()` only runs when
the `trabaja_turnos` column is first ADDED to an EXISTING database -- a brand-new database's schema already
has the column, so the backfill branch never runs for it) with stored shift rows, and expects `/shifts`,
`/shifts/como`, or a shift-bearing Hoy/Historial page to render at 200 -- exactly the behaviour decision 2
now changes to 404/hidden. This is the predictable consequence of the predicate being honoured everywhere it
now is, not an incidental break, and it cannot be fixed without writing to files outside this slice's
`touches:`, so it stops here rather than widening its own scope. A follow-up slice naming those six files in
`touches:` and adding one `db.set_trabaja_turnos(conn, True, <their person>)` line to each affected `setUp`
(the same fix already applied four times above, to the files this slice could touch) would turn the gate
green.

**Gate**, exact command `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`, run on the branch,
foreground, twice (the second run only to read which one test is skipped, for this entry -- both runs gave
the identical count): `Ran 913 tests in 135.612s ... FAILED (failures=20, skipped=1)`. 913 = main's prior
883 (BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-2-M's own count) plus the 30 new cases in `tests/test_turnos_opcional_3.py`. Not
merged: **GATE_RED**, stays on `feat/body-turnos-opcional-3`.

## BODY-TURNOS-INFERIR-1 -- the predicate infers Turnos from shift data on a fresh database (2026-11-07)

Under `ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`, against `BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-OBS-1` (which named read-time inference
as the alternative to a migration-only default). Fixes the previous entry's GATE_RED: `_migrate()`'s
backfill-to-1 for `person.trabaja_turnos` runs only when that column is ADDED to an EXISTING database, so a
database CREATED fresh -- every test, and the hosted Body, which starts empty and receives shift files from
the PC uploader -- never runs it, leaving a person with shift data at NULL, and Turnos hiding from the very
person whose shifts are arriving.

**The rule.** `db.trabaja_turnos_si(conn, person_id)`: stored 1 -> True. Stored 0 -> False, always (an
explicit "no" is never overridden). Stored NULL -> True when the person has at least one row in `shift` or
`shift_batch` (one `SELECT EXISTS(... UNION ...)` query, evaluated only when the stored value is NULL),
False otherwise. This is read-time inference, never a write -- `get_trabaja_turnos` is unchanged, so Primeros
pasos keeps asking «¿Trabajas por turnos?» while the stored value is NULL regardless of what
`trabaja_turnos_si` infers.

**Tests.** `tests/test_turnos_esquema_1.py`'s `AccessorTest` gained
`test_trabaja_turnos_si_infers_from_shift_data_when_null`: NULL + a `shift` row -> True, NULL + a
`shift_batch` row only -> True, NULL + nothing -> False, then an explicit 0 on the same person with the
`shift` row still present -> False. `tests/test_turnos_opcional_3.py`'s `NullSettingTest` (SETTING=None,
sharing the three fixtures' identical shift rows) now shows exactly what `SiSettingTest` shows, since the
stored shift rows make it infer True; a new `NullSettingNoShiftsTest` (SETTING=None, `WITH_SHIFTS=False`,
built by giving `_seed` a `with_shifts` flag that skips every `_insert_shift` call) proves the NULL-with-
nothing-to-infer-from case still hides everything -- nav, Hoy/Día/Historial/Tendencias cards, `/shifts` and
`/shifts/como` 404, Ayuda's chapter, the assistant's tool list and `leer_historia`'s `por_turno`.

**Measured: the previous entry's "every one... builds a person WITH shift rows" does not hold for all 20.**
The one gate run below still fails 7 tests, and none of them has shift data at all:
`test_dispositivo.ApiTurnosTest.test_valid_file_proposes_a_batch_for_the_keys_person_only` (its person 2,
0 `shift_batch` rows by its own assertion), `test_shift_import.ShiftWebTest.test_shifts_page_without_proposed_batch_es`
(fresh `db.init`, no shift insert), `test_sin_friccion.HistorySectionsAlreadyGoodCensusTest.test_patterns_and_shift_empty_link_turnos`
and `test_sin_friccion.TurnosEmptyCensusTest.test_empty_both_languages` (both state "no watch data at all" in
their own docstrings), and `test_turnos_costo.StripBandsTest.test_day_without_readiness_shows_em_dash_and_a_label`
and `test_turnos_costo.WebAndToolTest.test_empty_state_with_no_shifts` (both comment "no shifts, no metrics at
all"). These 6 are the same honest-empty-state design gap the previous entry's own ruling already flagged for
the orchestrator's browser check (BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-OBS-1's hide slice stays AWAITING_APPROVAL for exactly
this); inference has nothing to infer from when there is no shift data, so they are unaffected by this fix and
`touches:` does not cover the route/template files that would change their outcome. Not widened.

**New finding, inside this slice's own touched test file:** the 7th failure is
`test_turnos_opcional_3.NullSettingTest.test_nav_shifts_link`. Every other check in that fixture (Hoy's card,
Día's block, Historial's card, Tendencias' shading, `/shifts`, `/shifts/como`, Ayuda's chapter, the assistant's
tool list, `leer_historia`'s `por_turno`) now correctly shows for NULL-with-shift-rows, because each of those
routes computes its `turnos` context through the shared `_turnos_on(conn, person_id)` helper (`body/web.py`),
which calls `db.trabaja_turnos_si` and so picks up this fix immediately. `/settings` does not: its handler
(`body/web.py` lines ~1577-1580) reads `trabaja_turnos = db.get_trabaja_turnos(conn, person_id)` and passes
`turnos=trabaja_turnos is True` straight into the template, bypassing `_turnos_on`/`trabaja_turnos_si`
entirely -- a one-line omission from BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-3's own implementation (it updated every other
route to the shared helper but not this one), invisible until a NULL value needed to be inferred as True,
which only became possible with this slice. `body/web.py` is Tier 2 but outside this slice's `touches:`, so
it was not edited; a one-line follow-up (`turnos=_turnos_on(conn, person_id)` in the `/settings` handler)
would close it.

**Gate**, exact command `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`, run once, foreground:
`Ran 924 tests in 123.529s ... FAILED (failures=7, skipped=1)`. 924 = the previous entry's 913 plus the 11
new/changed cases across `tests/test_turnos_esquema_1.py` and `tests/test_turnos_opcional_3.py`. All 7
failures are accounted for above; none is fixable inside this slice's `touches:`. Not merged:
**AWAITING_APPROVAL**, stays on `feat/body-turnos-opcional-3` -- the hide slice's customer-facing bytes still
need the orchestrator's browser check, and this slice's own predicate change is customer-bytes-adjacent in
the same way (it changes which already-written screens render for a given person), so it stops at the same
gate rather than merging itself.

## BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-3-M -- the bottom bar's fixed four columns, and landing the branch (2026-11-07)

Lands `feat/body-turnos-opcional-3` on `main`: BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-3 (Turnos disappears for a person who has
not said they work shifts), BODY-TURNOS-INFERIR-1 (`trabaja_turnos_si` infers True from existing shift data
when the setting is NULL), and BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-3-FIX (the `/settings` bypass and six empty-state test
fixes), after the orchestrator's `ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1` browser measurement found one remaining
defect and approved a fix for it.

**The defect.** The phone bottom bar is a fixed four-column grid
(`.tabs{...grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr)...}` in `body/static/body.css`). With Turnos hidden, the three
remaining tabs sat in the left three quarters of the bar with an empty slot on the right (measured by the
orchestrator at 375 px: three 94 px tabs at x 0/94/188 in a 375 px bar), instead of sharing the bar's full
width.

**The fix.** `grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr)` became `grid-auto-flow:column;grid-auto-columns:1fr`, so
the bar's columns are however many tab links it holds, each getting an equal share of the width -- three tabs
split it into thirds, four into quarters. The `>=1024px` left-rail media query (`DESIGN.md` rule 11) already
switches `.tabs` to `display:flex;flex-direction:column` and never referenced `grid-template-columns`, so the
rail needed no change. Static URLs carry a content hash (`BODY-STATIC-VERSION-1`), so nothing else is needed
for browsers to pick up the new rule. Added `TabsBarSharesWidthTest` to `tests/test_turnos_opcional_3.py`: a
regression pin reading `body/static/body.css` and asserting the `.tabs` rule has no fixed `repeat(4` column
count; the visual check at 375 px was the orchestrator's own measurement, not this slice's.

**Gate**, exact command `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`, run once, foreground:
`Ran 925 tests in 105.956s ... OK (skipped=1)`. 925 = the previous entry's 924 plus this slice's one new
test.

**Merged.** `main` had not moved since the branch was cut (still at `f4e964d`), so no rebase was needed. Fix
commit `4a98a70`, merged `--no-ff` into `main` at `d4445ba` (merge tree equal to the branch tip's tree, diff
empty). `main` is left checked out, clean.
