## BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-5 -- a hand-typed shift pattern, proposed through the same propose-then-confirm
flow a file import uses (GATE_RED, not landed)

Slice 5 of 5 of `BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-OBS-1`'s plan under Carlos's ruling A (orchestrator ledger
`BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-1`: "if on, the person can enter a pattern by hand, through the same
propose-then-confirm flow"), against the schema `BODY-TURNOS-ESQUEMA-1` already merged. New module
`body/patron_turnos.py` owns the cycle's parsing, validation, storage and expansion; `body/shift_import.py`
(Tier 1) gains a `kind` parameter on `propose_data` and widens `confirm()`'s replaceable-row predicate;
`GET/POST /shifts/patron` and `POST /shifts/patron/quitar` in `body/web.py` are the screen.

**The two rulings in the approval, carried out as written.** (1) A pattern is expanded only from the
person's own TODAY forward, never into the past: `patron_turnos.expandir(pattern, desde)` starts at
`max(desde, start_day)`, so a later edit never rewrites history, and a dedicated test
(`test_never_emits_a_day_before_hoy_even_when_start_day_is_in_the_past`) confirms no day before `desde`
is ever produced even when `start_day` sits years in the past. (2) `confirm()`'s replaceable-row predicate
(the precedence lookup and the DELETE) widens from `source LIKE 'personal:%'` to `(source LIKE
'personal:%' OR source LIKE 'patron:%')`; a pattern batch's rows are stamped `source =
'patron:<file_name>'` (`file_name` is the literal `"patron-manual"`), an import batch's keep
`'personal:<file_name>'`; a `'manual'` row is untouched either way (the `source = 'manual'` check is a
separate, unchanged branch). Two tests confirm precedence both ways on an overlapping day: a pattern
confirmed after an import (later `received`) replaces the import's row, and an import confirmed after a
pattern (later `received`) replaces the pattern's row.

**Formats matched, not invented.** FORMATO.md does not exist in this repository (only referenced in
comments); the format was read from `tests/fixtures/turnos-demo-a.json` and `body/demo.py`'s own seeding
instead. `start_local`/`end_local` in the expanded `shifts` list: `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM"`, matching the
fixture exactly. `source.received`: a plain `"YYYY-MM-DD"` date string, matching the existing precedent at
`body/demo.py:233` (`received=confirmed_days[0].isoformat()`) -- not a full datetime with a UTC offset
like the fixture's `source.received`, because that precedent already establishes a bare date as a valid
`received` value, and `hoy` (the day the pattern was proposed) has no time component of its own to invent.
`source.extracted_at`: `datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")`, matching `shift_import.py`'s own
repeated use of that exact expression for a batch's own timestamps.

**One correction to BODY-TURNOS-ESQUEMA-1's own schema comment, not to the approval.** That slice's
`CREATE TABLE shift_pattern` comment describes `cycle` entries as `{"kind", "start_local", "end_local"}`,
but this slice's approval spells the cycle entry as `{"kind", "start", "end"}` -- a different field name
for the same purpose. Since `shift_pattern`'s own comment says "no parser/validator for its contents here
-- slice 5 owns that", and `db.py` is explicitly out of this slice's `touches:` (no schema change), this
slice follows the approval's own spelling (`"start"`/`"end"`) rather than editing a comment it cannot
touch. The two names describe the same two fields; no behavior is at stake, only which key a dict uses
internally to `patron_turnos.py`.

**`shift.source` / `'personal:'` readers found by grep, outside `shift_import.py` itself:** none. Checked
`body/web.py`, `body/turnos_costo.py`, `body/history.py`, `body/readiness.py`, `body/profile.py` and
`body/db.py` for any other reader of the `shift` table's `source` column or a `'personal:'` literal;
`body/db.py:747`'s `"source"` key belongs to the unrelated `activity` table (Garmin's own source field),
not `shift`. Nothing outside `touches:` needed a change.

**Screen** (`body/templates/shift_pattern.html`, `body/templates/shifts.html`). Cycle length first:
`GET /shifts/patron?dias=N` (a plain GET form, no JavaScript) re-renders N rows, prefilling from the saved
pattern only when its length equals N; a row's label reuses `t.long_date` (no new date-formatting code).
The six kinds reuse the existing `shift.kind.*` labels; no new CSS class was needed (`.field`, `.btn`,
`.bad`, `.taplink`, `.k`, `.card` already carry everything, including the 44px targets). On a bad row,
`patron_turnos.validar()` collects every invalid row (not just the first) into a list of `{"index",
"code"}`, so the web layer can show a message on each one at once, with every other field's input kept
exactly as submitted. An `off` row's leftover times are zeroed server-side before validation (`kind ==
"off"` forces `start`/`end` to `None`), so the library's own "off day with a time" refusal is reachable
only by calling `patron_turnos.validar()` directly (tested), never through the screen. `/shifts`: a

## BODY-HOGAR-MIEMBRO-1 -- a household goal reaches every member, not only its creator
(AWAITING_APPROVAL, not merged)

Carries out orchestrator ledger `BODY-HOGAR-PLAN-1` rulings 1-2 against `BODY-HOGAR-OBS-1`: every goal
read path gated on `goal.person_id = viewer`, so `visibility = 'household'` reached nobody and wave 7c's
done-when did not hold. ROADMAP's Hogar plan (Carlos, 2026-11-06) already defines what a member gets --
shared goal, plan items per member, each member's own weekly check against their own baseline, health
figures private -- so this slice builds that, and keeps creator-only editing as a reversible v1 choice.
No Tier 1 path touched: `db.py`, `household.py`'s source, `identity.py`, `cuenta.py`, `vida_export.py`
stay as they are.

**One shared access helper, in `body/goals.py` (not `web.py`, so the assistant can reach it too) without
a circular import:** `goal_access(conn, goal_id, person_id) -> 'creator' | 'member' | None`, and a sibling
`goal_scope_sql(person_id, hh) -> (sql, params)` for the listing queries, both reading membership through
`household.household_of` only, never a direct query of its table. Sites moved onto `goal_access`:
`body/web.py`'s `goal_detail` (view gating, the shared-with-household line, and `is_creator` for the
template), the new `_require_creator` (replacing `_owned_goal_or_404`, deleted) used by `goal_activate`,
`goal_pause`, `goal_finish`, `goal_drop`, `goal_add_habit`, and `habit_check`; `body/agente/herramientas
.py`'s `_leer_meta`. Sites moved onto `goal_scope_sql`: `web.py`'s `goals_list` and `_today_due_habits`;
`herramientas.py`'s `_leer_metas`. `web.py`'s `_habits_for_goal` dropped its own `person_id` filter (it
used to silently exclude a habit assigned to someone else); it now returns every active habit of G and
`goal_detail` decides per row whether it is this viewer's (own checkbox, own progress) or another
member's (name only, via the new `goals.habit_assignee` string, no checkbox, no progress count).

**Rules 1-6, each against the three-way fixture (creator, member, a stranger or a person who left):**
(1) a member sees G in Metas, in the same status sections as their own goals, and on G's page with
«Compartida con tu hogar · la creó {name}» / "Shared with your household · created by {name}" (the
creator sees the line without "la creó"/"created by"); a stranger or a person whose `hogar_local` row was
removed (simulating leaving, since the local mirror carries no "left" state of its own, only presence or
absence of the row) gets 404, same as an unknown goal. (2) a member checks off a habit whose
`assignee_person_id` is NULL or themselves; `habit_check` now 404s a habit assigned to someone else
instead of the old blanket `g.person_id = viewer`; `_today_due_habits` lists a household goal's due
habits for a member the same way it already did for their own. (3) `goal_detail`'s chart, history and
`goal_check` upsert were already keyed by the VIEWER's `person_id`, so the only change was opening the
page to a member at all; the members block (unchanged logic, `goals.household_title`) lists every other
member, the creator included, by verdict word only. (4) the add-habit form grows a «Para mí» / «Para los
dos» ("For me" / "For both of us") radio pair, shown only when `goal.visibility == 'household'`; the
adder -- creator or member -- picks their own assignment, defaulting to "both" (NULL) when the field is
missing. (5) `_require_creator` 404s a member on all four status routes exactly like a stranger; `goal
.html`'s `<div class="confirm-actions">` block is now wrapped in `{% if is_creator %}`, so a member never
sees the buttons at all. (6) a dedicated test seeds the two members with resting-hr/steps averages ~40
apart and asserts neither figure, nor the other's habit-check count ("1 de 7"), appears on the other's
render of G; the chart and history were already per-viewer (rule 3), so nothing new leaks there.

**Rule 7, the assistant.** `_leer_metas` and `_leer_meta` (`body/agente/herramientas.py`) now read through
`goals.goal_scope_sql` / `goals.goal_access` instead of `person_id = ?`, so a member's household goals
appear in `leer_metas` (with a new `"compartida"` flag) and `leer_meta` answers for a member exactly as it
does for the creator -- `verificaciones` stays keyed by the caller's own `person_id`, never another
member's. `leer_meta`'s `habitos` entries gained `"asignado_a"`: `"ambos"`, `"tú"`, or the other member's
`display_name` -- never a figure, only who a habit is for, the same thing the page already shows.
`body/agente/propuestas.py` needed no change: `_proponer_cambio_meta`'s `WHERE id = ? AND person_id = ?`
was already creator-only (`goal.person_id` IS the creator), so that half of rule 7 already held. The
other half -- "a proposal to add a habit follows rule 4" -- is vacuous today: no `proponer_agregar_habito`
tool exists in the registry, and the WORK section asked for no new one, so this is recorded as a note for
whoever adds that tool later, not a change made here.

**Rule 8, the demo (`body/demo.py`).** A second invented person, "Ana" (id 2, never a real person's
data), one household (`hogar_local`, id `demo-hogar-1`) linking the demo person and Ana, and one shared
milestone goal CREATED BY ANA -- «Preparar el ascenso» / "Prepare for the climb" -- with a habit for both
(«Entrenar piernas» / "Train legs") and one for Ana only («Revisar el equipo» / "Check the gear"), plus a
three-week history of Ana's own habit checks and weekly `goal_check` rows so her checks exist. The demo
person's own three goals are untouched. `tests/test_demo.py` counts updated: two persons ("Demo", "Ana"),
four active goals, three habits, plus a new assertion that the one `visibility = 'household'` goal's
creator is Ana.

**Strings, es/en:** `goals.shared_by_you` ("Compartida con tu hogar" / "Shared with your household"),
`goals.shared_by` ("Compartida con tu hogar · la creó {name}" / "Shared with your household · created by
{name}"), `goals.habit_for_both` ("Para los dos" / "For both of us"), `goals.habit_for_me` ("Para mí" /
"For me"), `goals.habit_assignee` ("De {name}" / "{name}'s").

**Tests.** New `tests/test_hogar_miembro_1.py`, 23 tests: `VisibilityTest`, `SharedLineTest` (both
languages), `HabitCheckTest`, `OwnWeeklyCheckTest`, `AddHabitChoiceTest`, `CreatorOnlyTest`,
`PrivacyTest` (rule 6), `AssistantReadToolTest` (rule 7) -- a creator, a member, a stranger, and a person
who left, throughout. `tests/test_goals_web.py`'s `HouseholdGoalDetailTest.test_member_check_shown` was
left exactly as it stood (its subject -- the creator viewing their own shared goal with a member's
verdict shown -- never changed); no case anywhere was deleted.

**Gate, run once, foreground, exact command** `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`:

    Ran 999 tests in 130.963s
    OK (skipped=1)

999 = the prior entry's 975 plus this slice's 23 new tests in `tests/test_hogar_miembro_1.py` plus one
new test in `tests/test_demo.py` (`test_has_one_household_goal_created_by_ana`); its other three renamed
tests (`test_has_two_demo_persons`, `test_has_four_active_goals_with_checks`, `test_has_three_habits`)
keep the same one-test-each shape they always had, just updated counts and names. The same pre-existing
POSIX-only skip is untouched.

**Stopped AWAITING_APPROVAL, not merged.** The diff changes customer-facing bytes (templates, i18n
strings, a new "for me"/"for both" radio, the shared-with-household line, the members block now reachable
by a second person) -- merge policy A's customer-bytes condition -- and this spec's approval-reason says
in words to stop here for the orchestrator's 375 px browser check on the demo. Branch `feat/body-hogar
-miembro-1` left as is, gate green, nothing merged into `main`.

## BODY-HOGAR-MIEMBRO-1-M -- three fixes from the orchestrator's review and browser measurement of
BODY-HOGAR-MIEMBRO-1 (2026-11-07) (GATE_RED, not merged)

Carries the three fixes the orchestrator's AWAITING_APPROVAL review of `BODY-HOGAR-MIEMBRO-1` asked for,
on top of that slice's unchanged tip (`2c588cb`). `main` had not moved from the branch's base (`c72dc09`),
so no merge-in was needed before starting.

**Fix 1 -- a household goal is a milestone in v1.** A metric goal's verdict and chart are judged on its
own `baseline_value`, which only its creator has (orchestrator ledger `BODY-HOGAR-PLAN-1` (cont.)): a
member reading a shared metric goal would be judged on the creator's numbers without knowing it. Rather
than carry per-member baselines (a v2 question), this slice closes the hole by making a household goal a
milestone, always: `goals.propose(...)` now raises `ValueError` (writing nothing) for `kind='metric'` with
`visibility='household'`. `POST /goals/new` no longer trusts the form's `visibility` field for a metric
goal -- the server always stores `visibility='private'`, `hogar_id=NULL` for `kind='metric'`, whatever the
form sent (so a tampered or JavaScript-less submission still can't create a shared metric goal).
`goal_new.html`'s visibility card now sits inside `<fieldset class="milestone-only">`, the same CSS
`:has()` mechanism `metric-only`/`milestone-only` already used (no JavaScript) -- so the household choice
is only ever shown while "Hito / aventura" is selected -- with one new line under the select,
`goals.visibility_milestone_note` ("Las metas compartidas son hitos: cada quien lleva sus propios
números." / "Shared goals are milestones: each person keeps their own numbers."). `goals.goal_access` and
`goals.goal_scope_sql`'s 'member' branch now additionally require `kind = 'milestone'`, so a goal that was
already marked `visibility='household'` with `kind='metric'` before this slice (the only way one can still
exist, since `propose` now refuses to create one) stays creator-only on every surface -- Metas' list, the
goal page (404), Hoy's habits, and habit check-off (404) -- forever. Both functions' docstrings cite
`BODY-HOGAR-PLAN-1 (cont.)` for the reason. Grepped `body/agente/` for any path that creates or edits a
goal's `visibility` or `kind`: only `herramientas._proponer_meta` -> `propuestas._escribir_aplicacion`'s
`proponer_meta` branch creates a goal, and it never passes `visibility` (stays the default `'private'`) or
a `kind` other than the default `'metric'` -- so no assistant path could ever hit the refusal, and none
needed changing.

**Fix 2 -- the list card.** Metas' list card for a household goal (active, proposed, and inside the
archive `<details>`) now carries the same quiet line the goal page already showed: `goals.shared_by_you`
for the creator, `goals.shared_by` (names the creator) for a member. Computed in the route -- a new
`web._shared_line(conn, t, g, person_id)` -- not the template; `goal_detail` was refactored to call the
same helper instead of repeating the creator/member branch inline.

**Fix 3 -- another member's habit row.** `goal.html`'s "not mine" branch used to draw a `<span
class="box">` styled `opacity:.3;border-style:dashed` -- still the same 20×20, bordered, rounded-corner
shape as a real checkbox, just faint, which reads as a disabled control rather than "not yours to check".
It is now an empty `<span class="boxbtn-spacer">` (new rule in `body.css`: same `width:28px;min-height:44px`
as `.boxbtn` for row alignment, no border, no background, no `cursor:pointer`) -- the row stays aligned
with the others, "De Ana" still names whose habit it is, and nothing checkbox- or button-shaped remains.

**Strings, es/en:** one new key, `goals.visibility_milestone_note` ("Las metas compartidas son hitos: cada
quien lleva sus propios números." / "Shared goals are milestones: each person keeps their own numbers.").
No existing string's text changed.

**Tests.** `tests/test_goals.py`: `HouseholdMetricRefusedTest` (propose refuses metric+household and
writes nothing; milestone+household still allowed), `LegacyMetricHouseholdRowTest` (a goal updated to
`visibility='household'` after creation, bypassing `propose`, stays creator-only via `goal_access` and
`goal_scope_sql`). `tests/test_goals_web.py`: `MetricHouseholdFormTest` (`POST /goals/new` with
`kind=metric&visibility=household` stores private; `kind=milestone&visibility=household` still stores
household), `GoalNewFormMilestoneOnlyVisibilityTest` (the visibility card sits in `milestone-only`, with
its note), `ListCardSharedLineTest` (the list card's shared line for creator and member, es and en),
`LegacyMetricHouseholdRowWebTest` (a legacy metric household row is unreachable on `/goals`, `/goals/<id>`,
`/` (Hoy), and `/habits/<id>/check`), `OtherMemberHabitRowTest` (no `type="checkbox"` or `<button` near
another member's habit row). **Restored subjects, no case deleted:** four existing tests whose subject was
a metric household goal were changed to a milestone household goal, keeping the same thing under test --
`tests/test_hogar_miembro_1.py::OwnWeeklyCheckTest.test_viewer_sees_their_own_history_not_the_creators`
(the viewer's own weekly figure vs. the creator's, now habits_done/due instead of metric_avg),
`tests/test_hogar_miembro_1.py::PrivacyTest.test_other_members_figures_are_absent` (no other member's
figure leaks, now habit-check counts instead of metric averages),
`tests/test_goals.py::HouseholdGoalCheckTest.test_two_members_each_get_their_own_goal_check` (two members,
two independent `goal_check` rows, now from habit checks instead of metric readings),
`tests/test_goals_web.py::HouseholdGoalDetailTest.test_member_check_shown` (unchanged in substance, just
`kind='milestone'` instead of the implicit metric default).

**Found, not fixed: two more tests outside this spec's `touches` have the same subject (tracked as

`tests/test_privacidad.py::DeleteAllTest.test_right_word_deletes_every_row_of_a_and_takes_bs_check_on_as_

## BODY-HABITO-VECES-1 -- a habit's cadence `times` is now read when counting what is due (2026-11-07)

Measured on `BODY-HOGAR-MIEMBRO-1`'s demo (orchestrator ledger `BODY-HOGAR-PLAN-1 (cont.)`): a habit cadence
`{"per": "week", "times": 2}` with no context counted all 7 days of the week as due, in two separate places
that both ignored `times` -- `body/goals.py`'s `_habits_progress` (the weekly check, which also feeds every
milestone's on-track verdict) and `body/web.py`'s `_habit_progress` / `_is_due_today` (the goal page and
Hoy). A twice-a-week habit read "0 de 7 esta semana", stayed listed as due on Hoy after both of the week's
checks were done, and a milestone goal built on such habits could never reach `MILESTONE_ON_TRACK_PCT`
(70%) -- its verdict was wrong by construction.

**The rule** (the orchestrator's, recorded in the spec): for habit H, person P and the week starting
`monday`, let `days` = the week's days H can be done on (its shift `context` days via
`goals._context_due_days`, or all seven via `goals._week_days`), and `checked` = P's `done = 1` checks of H
on those days.

* `per = "day"`: due = `len(days)`; done = `min(checked, due)`. `times` > 1 a day cannot be told apart by
  one check a day, so the count stays per day (unchanged from before this fix).
* `per = "week"`: due = `min(times, len(days))`; done = `min(checked, due)`.
* `per = "month"`: it does not enter the weekly due count (due 0 for the week); the goal page shows its own
  calendar-month figure instead -- done = P's checks so far this month, due = `times`.
* Due today (Hoy): H is due today when today is in `days` AND -- for `week`/`month` only -- H is not
  already satisfied for its own period (`checked < due` this week, or this month's checks `< times`).
  `per = "day"` has no extra gate: each day is its own due instance, so a habit already checked today
  stays listed, ticked, as today.

**One function, every call site.** `body/goals.py` gains `habit_progress(conn, habit, person_id, monday,
today=None) -> (done, due, period)` and `habit_due_today(conn, habit, person_id, today) -> bool`, the one
place `times` is read. Call sites, all now going through it:

* `goals._habits_progress` (the weekly check, `goals.weekly_check`'s milestone branch) -- sums `done`/`due`
  across a goal's habits, skipping a `period == "month"` habit (it contributes nothing to the weekly
  tally, by the rule above).
* `body/web.py::_habit_progress` -- thin wrapper over `goals.habit_progress`, called from the goal-detail
  page's habit rows.
* `body/web.py::_is_due_today` -- thin wrapper over `goals.habit_due_today`, called from the goal-detail
  page (`due_today`) and `_today_due_habits` (Hoy's plan card).
* `body/web.py`'s old `_due_days_for` wrapper is gone -- its shift-context logic is now only inside
  `goals.habit_progress` / `goals.habit_due_today`.
* `body/agente/herramientas.py`: grepped for every habit-reporting tool before touching it. `_leer_meta`
  returns a habit's raw `cadencia` dict and the viewer's own `goal_check` rows (`habits_done`/`habits_due`
  columns), which are already written by `weekly_check` through the shared rule; no second copy of the
  rule existed there to fix, so this file has no diff in this slice (the spec listed it defensively under
  "any assistant tool ... that reports habit progress" -- measured none does, independent of the fix).

`RULE_VERSION` moves `"metas-v1"` -> `"metas-v2"`; past `goal_check` rows are not recomputed (unchanged
rows from before this fix keep reading `"metas-v1"`, an honest record of which rule judged them).

New i18n strings, `goals.habit.progress_month` (both locales): es "{done} de {due} este mes", en "{done} of
{due} this month" -- shown on the goal page for a monthly habit in place of the existing "{done} de {due}
esta semana" line, which is unchanged for day/week habits.

**Tests**, new file `tests/test_habito_veces_1.py`: per='day' (due unaffected by `times`), per='week' with
times 1/2/7 (due = 1/2/7), a `before_night` context with one shift so only 1 day is due against
times=3 (due = 1, not 3), per='month' (done/due = this month's checks capped at `times`, and a month habit
contributing (0, 0) to the weekly tally so a milestone with only a month habit stays `on_track = NULL`
rather than a false verdict), done capped at due for an over-checked week, due-today turning false once a
twice-a-week habit has two checks, and a milestone with only a twice-a-week habit, done twice, reading
`on_track = True` (2 of 2 = 100% >= 70%).

**Existing test updated** (its subject restored, not deleted): `tests/test_hogar_miembro_1.py`'s
`OwnWeeklyCheckTest.test_viewer_sees_their_own_history_not_the_creators` seeds a `per='week', times=1`
habit checked on all 7 days of the week. Under `metas-v1` that read `(habits_done, habits_due) = (7, 7)`;
under the fix, due = `min(1, 7) = 1` and done is capped at it, so the pair is now `(1, 1)`. The test's
subject -- the viewer's own weekly check is upserted and distinct from the creator's -- is unchanged; only
the two numbers moved, and the comment above the assertion now says so.

Every other habit-cadence test read for count-breaking numbers (`tests/test_goals.py`,
`tests/test_goals_web.py`, the rest of `tests/test_hogar_miembro_1.py`, `tests/test_agente_registro.py`):
none asserted a `habits_done`/`habits_due` pair, a progress string, or a due-today boolean on a cadence
where the old and new rule disagree (every `per='day'` case; every `per='week', times=1` case whose
`days` already equalled 1 or whose assertion didn't touch the count; the context test whose single due day
already capped due at 1 under the old rule too).

    Ran 1020 tests in 175.986s
    OK (skipped=1)

1020 is 1008 (the prior entry's count) + 12 new cases in `tests/test_habito_veces_1.py`; no test removed.

## BODY-HABITO-VECES-1-M -- due-today now stays listed, ticked, on the quota-completing day for `per='week'`/`per='month'` too (2026-11-07)

Lands `BODY-HABITO-VECES-1` with one fix, approved by the orchestrator (spec `body-habito-veces-1-m.md`,
approval-reason `ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`): `goals.habit_due_today` returned `False` for a
per='week' or per='month' habit the instant its quota was met, including on the day the quota-completing
check happened. A 2-a-week habit ticked for the second time on Hoy vanished from Hoy at once -- no visible
tick, no way to untick it that day. The prior entry's rule ("A habit already checked today stays listed,
ticked, as today") had been applied to `per='day'` only; `per='week'`/`per='month'` fell straight through
to `done < due`, which is `False` the moment `done` reaches `due`.

**The fix**, `body/goals.py::habit_due_today`: for `per='week'`/`per='month'`, H is due today when today
is one of H's due days AND (the period's `done < due`, OR P has a `done = 1` check of H dated today). The
second half is new -- a direct query for a check on today's date, rather than reading it off
`habit_progress`'s period totals, since a period that is already satisfied gives no way to tell "satisfied
before today" apart from "satisfied today" from the totals alone. `per='day'` is unchanged (no extra gate
at all). Docstring updated to state the exception.

**Tests added**, `tests/test_habito_veces_1.py`: a 2-a-week habit checked Monday and again Tuesday stays
due on Tuesday (the quota-completing day) and is not due Wednesday; a monthly habit (times=2) whose second
check lands on the 15th stays due on the 15th and is not due on the 16th. The existing due-today test
(quota met on an earlier day, checked on a later day) was left as is -- it never exercised the
quota-completing day itself, which is exactly the gap this fix closes.

**Merge of `main`**: not needed before the fix. `main`'s tip at dispatch (`32d3f30`,
`BODY-HOGAR-MIEMBRO-1-M2`'s ledger entry) was already an ancestor of the branch's pre-fix tip `30892aa`
(the branch was cut after that commit landed on `main`), measured by `git merge-base HEAD main` returning
`32d3f30` before any change -- the spec's warning that `main` had moved did not apply here.

**Gate, run once, foreground, exact command** `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`,
on the branch before the merge into `main`:

    Ran 1022 tests in 165.245s
    OK (skipped=1)

1022 is 1020 (the prior entry's measured count, not the spec's rounded "1019 + 1 skipped") + 2 new tests.
The one skip is pre-existing and unrelated.

**Merged.** The diff beyond the already-approved `BODY-HABITO-VECES-1` work is confined to one function's
extra query and docstring in `body/goals.py`, plus its test file -- no schema or migration change, no
cross-repo contract. Customer-facing counts (Hoy's due-today list) are the one merge-policy-A condition
this diff trips, and it is exactly what this spec's approval-reason classified and approved. Merged
`--no-ff` into `main`.

## BODY-HOGAR-COMPARTIR-1 -- a person can share one figure at a time with their household, and withdraw it (2026-11-07)

Roadmap wave 7c and the hogar-v1 contract promise it ("health numbers stay private to their person; sharing is per
figure, chosen by its owner, and can be withdrawn"; "Body keeps health figures private unless a person shares a
specific one"). BODY-HOGAR-OBS-1 found nothing of it built -- no table, no route, no screen. Orchestrator ledger
BODY-HOGAR-PLAN-1 ruling 3 (against BODY-HOGAR-OBS-1's proposed shape: person, metric key, household, since,
withdrawn) rules: a share is a ROW per (person, metric_key, household) with shared_at/withdrawn_at -- withdrawing
sets withdrawn_at (history kept), re-sharing inserts a new row; at most one ACTIVE row per (person, metric_key,
household), enforced by a partial unique index.

**Schema** (`body/db.py`, Tier 1), created by `db.init` the same `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` way every table is --
nothing to backfill:

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS figura_compartida (
        id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
        person_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES person(id),
        metric_key   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES metric_def(key),
        hogar_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
        shared_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
        withdrawn_at TEXT
    );
    CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_figura_compartida_activa
        ON figura_compartida (person_id, metric_key, hogar_id) WHERE withdrawn_at IS NULL;

`hogar_id` is `TEXT`, matching `goal.hogar_id` (`TEXT`, nullable) and `hogar_local.hogar_id` (`TEXT NOT NULL`);
`body/household.py`'s `Household.id` is likewise typed `str`.

**`body/compartir.py` (new) -- the only module that reads or writes the table.** `compartir(conn, person_id,
metric_key)` refuses (`ValueError`, nothing written) with no active household (`household.household_of`) or an
unknown metric key; sharing an already-active figure is a no-op (the existing `shared_at` is kept). `retirar(conn,
person_id, metric_key)` sets `withdrawn_at` on every currently active row for that person/metric (a no-op when
nothing is active); the row stays, as history. `mis_compartidas(conn, person_id)` lists this person's own active
shares with `since`, for the Ajustes card. `visibles_para(conn, viewer_id)` returns `{name, metric_key, value, day}`
for every OTHER member of the viewer's active household with an active share in THAT SAME household (membership
read only through `household.household_of`, so a stranger, a different household, a person who left, or an owner
who withdrew all drop out on their own, with no extra filtering needed); `value`/`day` are the owner's LATEST
`daily_metric` row for the key, or `(None, None)` when they have none yet -- never a series, a baseline, a history,
or a guess. `export_rows`/`delete_rows` exist so `body/privacidad.py` never queries the table itself.

**`body/privacidad.py`**: `figura_compartida` added to `FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES`; `export_person` adds a
`figuras_compartidas` key (this person's own rows, including withdrawn ones, via `compartir.export_rows`);
`delete_person` calls `compartir.delete_rows` from inside its existing single `with conn:` block (that function
does its own `DELETE` with no transaction of its own, so nesting it never commits the outer transaction early).

**Ajustes** (`body/templates/settings.html`, `body/web.py`'s `settings` route): shown only when
`household.household_of` is not None, a card «Compartir con tu hogar» / "Share with your household" lists every
`metric_def` metric (the catalogue is data -- none filtered out) with its label and a Compartir/Dejar de compartir
("Share"/"Stop sharing") button, 44 px (the existing `.btn` class already is), POSTing to the new
`POST /settings/compartir` route (`metric_key`, `accion` in `{compartir, retirar}`) and redirecting back to
`/settings`; a closing line "Solo ven el último valor y su fecha..." / "They only see the latest value...". Without
a household, one line says sharing becomes available with one, nothing else. No new GET route.

**Hoy** (`body/templates/today.html`, the `today` route): when `compartir.visibles_para` is non-empty, a quiet card
«Tu hogar» / "Your household" lists each shared figure: name · metric label · value with unit (the app's existing
`_fig_unit` formatting) · its day, as «hoy»/«ayer» (new helper `_dia_relativo`, relative to the viewer's own
`today_local`) or the short date -- or a plain "no data yet" line when the owner has none. Absent otherwise, and
only on Hoy (not wired into `soon.html`, which is not in this slice's `touches`, so a viewer with no Garmin day yet
never sees the card even if a figure is shared).

**`body/demo.py`**: Ana (BODY-HOGAR-MIEMBRO-1's invented partner) shares `resting_hr` with the demo household, so
the demo person's own Hoy shows the card.

**i18n**, both languages (`body/i18n/es.json`, `en.json`): `settings.compartir.*` (titulo, sin_hogar, accion.compartir,
accion.retirar, nota), `hogar.dia_hoy`/`hogar.dia_ayer`, `today.hogar.titulo`/`today.hogar.sin_dato`. Metric labels
and units reuse the existing `metric.*`/`unit.*` keys.

**Tests added** (`tests/test_hogar_compartir_1.py`, 25; `tests/test_privacidad.py`'s new `CompartidoExportDeleteTest`,
3; `tests/test_demo.py`, 1): share/withdraw/re-share with history kept; the partial unique index refuses a second
active row and allows a withdrawn one to coexist with a new active one; refusal with no household and with an
unknown metric key; `visibles_para` for a viewer sees only an active household member's active share, and sees
nothing for a stranger in a different household, a stranger with no household, a member who left (both directions),
or an owner after withdrawal, or a viewer with no household; only the latest day's value is ever returned or
rendered on Hoy (seeded three days, asserted the older two never appear, and a "no data yet" owner renders that
line); the Ajustes card in both languages, including the share/withdraw round trip through the route; demo seeds
exactly one active share for Ana; export and delete-all include the table.

## BODY-HOGAR-COMPARTIR-1-M -- four fixes from the orchestrator's review and browser measurement, then merged (2026-11-07)

Lands BODY-HOGAR-COMPARTIR-1 (reviewed above) with four defects it shipped with fixed first.

**Fix 1 -- `compartir.mis_compartidas(conn, person_id)` now reads the person's CURRENT active household only.**
It calls `household.household_of` itself and filters `WHERE hogar_id = ?` on that household's id (empty list with
no active household), the same `hogar_id` `visibles_para` already reads. Before this fix it read every active row
for the person regardless of which household recorded it, so after moving households Ajustes kept marking a figure
"shared" that nobody in the new household -- or the old one -- could actually see. `retirar` is unchanged: it still
withdraws every active row for the person regardless of household, which stays the safe direction (a person who
moves away should not keep broadcasting into a household they already left, by accident of forgetting which one
holds the stale share).

**Fix 2 -- Hoy's «Tu hogar» card moved to last.** It now renders after the viewer's own readiness card, the
first-steps card (when present), the plan-habits card (when present), the metric grid, and the "see the whole day"
link -- the last card on the page, directly before `base.html`'s footer. Before this fix it sat third, between the
first-steps card and the person's own plan/metrics, so another person's figure could outrank the viewer's own day.

**Fix 3 -- the Ajustes card no longer lists all 24 metrics flat.** Figures the person currently shares render first,
each with "Dejar de compartir" (unchanged markup/button). The remaining metrics sit inside a `<details class="files">`
(the app's existing collapsed-section pattern, `goal.html`/`trends.html`/etc., 44 px `summary`, closed by default)
whose summary reads `settings.compartir.elegir` -- "Elegir qué compartir" / "Choose what to share" (new i18n key,
both languages) -- each with "Compartir". With nothing shared, the summary row is the only row besides the privacy
note. No JavaScript: `<details>` is native. Buttons are still the existing 44 px `.btn`.

**Fix 4 -- the demo's Ana now has her own short history of the figure she shares.** `body/demo.py` writes `resting_hr`
for Ana over the last 5 days of the seeded span, each value drawn from the same `RANGES["resting_hr"]` the demo
already uses for the main person (via the existing `_value` helper, factor 0 -- not a copy of the demo person's own
numbers). Before this fix Ana shared a figure she had never recorded, so the demo's Hoy card could only ever render
"sin dato" and the value-rendering path was never exercised by anyone looking at the demo tenant.

**Tests added** (`tests/test_hogar_compartir_1.py`, 5; `tests/test_demo.py`, 1 -- 6 total): fix 1 -- a share recorded
under an old household is absent from `mis_compartidas` after the person moves to a new one, and the new household's
other member cannot see it via `visibles_para` either; fix 2 -- the rendered Hoy page orders "Ver todo el día" (the
last of the person's own content) before "Tu hogar" before the page footer's "No es consejo médico"; fix 3 -- with
nothing shared, `<details class="files" style="margin-top:6px">` (no `open` attribute) and "Elegir qué compartir"
are present and "Dejar de compartir" is not; with one active share, "Dejar de compartir" sits before the `<details`
tag and the unshared metrics' "Compartir" buttons sit after it; the English summary string renders; fix 4 -- Ana's
`daily_metric` rows for `resting_hr` exist and every value is non-null.

## BODY-HOGAR-CUENTA-1 -- household membership comes from Cuenta's `duna_hogar` claim, not a table only tests and the demo wrote (2026-11-07)

Carries out orchestrator ledger BODY-HOGAR-PLAN-1 (cont. 2) against BODY-HOGAR-CUENTA-OBS-1: `hogar_local` was never
written by production code, only by tests and `body/demo.py`, so two real hosted accounts could never link a
household, and a person who left one kept seeing shared goals and figures until their session ended (up to 30 days).
Branch `feat/body-hogar-cuenta-1` from `main`. Tier 1 (`body/cuenta.py`, `body/db.py`); approved to build, not to
merge -- this slice is a schema change and stops `AWAITING_APPROVAL`.

**Pre-flight.** `git grep -l hogar_local` before editing found every hit inside this spec's `touches`: `DECISIONS.md`,
`body/db.py`, `body/demo.py`, `body/household.py`, `body/privacidad.py`, and six test files. No widening needed.

**Schema** (`body/db.py`'s migration, `body/household.py`'s `SCHEMA` -- the ONE definition of the table's shape,
built from `household._COLUMNS` so `body/db.py`'s migration references the same text rather than a second copy):

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hogar_miembro (
        person_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES person(id),
        hogar_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
        member_sub     TEXT,
        fuente         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'local' CHECK (fuente IN ('local', 'cuenta')),
        actualizado_at TEXT NOT NULL
    );

`body/db.py`'s new `_migrate_hogar`, called from `init()` right after `_migrate_precios` and before `SCHEMA` fresh
installs never see: when `hogar_local` exists it creates `hogar_miembro` (via `household._COLUMNS`, inside the same
guarded `_rebuild_with_fk_off` transaction every other rebuild in this file uses), copies every row with
`fuente='local'` and `actualizado_at`=now, checks the copied count against the old table's row count, then drops
`hogar_local` -- once; a database with no `hogar_local` (fresh, or already migrated) is untouched. A fresh install
never creates `hogar_miembro` through `init()` at all -- exactly as `hogar_local` never was -- it is created lazily
wherever `household.SCHEMA` is first applied (`household_of`, `sincronizar_desde_claim`, `privacidad.export_person`/
`delete_person`, `demo.py`), the same pattern the table already followed.

**`body/household.py`.** The `LocalSource`/`ClaimSource` switch is gone (nothing else needed it); `household_of`
reads `hogar_miembro` directly, whatever wrote it. New `sincronizar_desde_claim(conn, person_id, claims) -> str`,
the ONLY writer of `fuente='cuenta'` rows:

* `"duna_hogar"` absent from `claims` -> `'sin_dato'`, nothing changes.
* `claims["duna_hogar"] is None` -> deletes THIS person's own row only -> `'sin_hogar'`.
* malformed (`valor` not a dict, `id` not a `str`, `miembros` not a `list[str]`) -> `'sin_dato'`, nothing changes --
  checked, and nothing written, before any row is touched.
* a value `{id, miembros}`: first checks THIS person's own `person.cuenta_sub` against `miembros` -- absent is
  "malformed claim, treated like `None`" per the spec, so only this person's row is deleted and the rest of the
  household is left alone (deciding this BEFORE touching any other row, so a bad claim about the asker can never
  wipe a partner's own membership). Otherwise, in one transaction: every Body person whose `cuenta_sub` is in
  `miembros` is upserted (`hogar_id`, `member_sub`, `fuente='cuenta'`, `actualizado_at`=now, replacing any row they
  had via `ON CONFLICT(person_id)`); every row under this `hogar_id` whose person's sub is NOT in `miembros` is
  deleted. A member with no Body person yet is silently skipped (they join when they first sign in) -- confirmed by
  a test. "Moving hogar" works for free from the same upsert (a person's single `hogar_id` just changes); an old
  partner's own row in the PREVIOUS `hogar_id` is left alone until their own next sign-in or refresh touches it --
  hogar-v1's documented v1 gap, not new here.

**`body/cuenta.py`.** (a) `handle_callback` calls `household.sincronizar_desde_claim(conn, person_id, claims)` right
after `resolve_person`, wrapped in a new `_sincronizar_hogar_sin_fallar` that catches any exception and logs one
count-only line (`"cuenta: hogar sync failed for 1 person (<ExceptionType>)"`, no sub, no hogar id) -- sign-in always
proceeds to `create_session` regardless. (b) New `refrescar_hogar(conn, person_id)`: reads the person's
`cuenta_sub`, calls the new optional `auth` parameter on `_get_json` (mirroring `_post_form`'s existing one) against
`GET {issuer()}/servicio/cuentas/{sub}` with `client_secret_basic` (`(CLIENT_ID, client_secret())`, the same pair
`_exchange_code` already uses), then `sincronizar_desde_claim`s the response. A network error, a bad answer, or a
failure inside the sync is caught and logged as a count-only line; the existing mirror is left untouched -- nothing
in this function may raise into its caller. Per `cuenta-duna-v1.md` section 9, `GET /servicio/cuentas/{sub}` answers
"the current claims", the same claim set the ID token carries, so `duna_hogar` arrives in it the same shape. (c) New
`_debe_refrescar_hogar(conn, person_id)`: `True` when the person has no `hogar_miembro` row, or their row is
`fuente='cuenta'` and `actualizado_at` is at least `LAST_SEEN_UPDATE_SECONDS` (one hour) old; `False` for a
`fuente='local'` row regardless of age. Wired into `resolve_session`'s existing hourly last-seen branch, guarded by
`hosted()` so local mode never calls Cuenta (confirmed by a test calling `resolve_session` directly with
`BODY_CUENTA_ISSUER` unset).

**`body/privacidad.py`**: `FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES`'s `"hogar_local"` renamed to `"hogar_miembro"`; `export_person`'s
`hogar` key now also carries `fuente`; `delete_person`'s `DELETE` retargeted to `hogar_miembro`.

**`body/demo.py`**: the demo household insert now targets `hogar_miembro` and supplies `actualizado_at` (the new
column has no default), `fuente` left at its column default `'local'`.

**Tests.** New `tests/test_hogar_cuenta_1.py` (18): every `sincronizar_desde_claim` outcome including the two
malformed-claim branches; a partner who left disappears from the hogar whichever member's claim arrives next
(both directions); a member with no Body person is skipped then joins on their own first sign-in; a person moving
hogar leaves their old partner's row stale under the old id; sign-in still returns its 303 and sets the session
cookie when the sync is mocked to raise; the hourly refresh calls `_get_json` with the exact URL and
`client_secret_basic` auth only when stale or absent, never for a `fuente='local'` row, never when
`BODY_CUENTA_ISSUER` is unset, and keeps the existing mirror on a mocked `httpx.ConnectError`; the migration from a
hand-built `hogar_local` database (rows copied with `fuente='local'`, old table gone, a second `db.init()` changes
nothing further); export and delete-all cover `hogar_miembro`. Six existing test files (`tests/test_household.py`,
`tests/test_hogar_compartir_1.py`, `tests/test_hogar_miembro_1.py`, `tests/test_goals.py`, `tests/test_goals_web.py`,
`tests/test_privacidad.py`, `tests/test_vida_export.py`) keep their subjects, every `hogar_local` reference renamed
to `hogar_miembro` with an explicit `actualizado_at` added (the column has no default).

**Gate, run once, foreground, exact command** `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`:

    Ran 1075 tests in 125.390s
    OK (skipped=1)

1075 is 1057 (BODY-HOGAR-COMPARTIR-1-M's measured count, `main` unmoved at `e77c575` since this branch was cut) + 18
new tests above; no test removed; the one skip is pre-existing and unrelated.

**Not merged.** This slice's own spec says to stop `AWAITING_APPROVAL` on the branch regardless of merge policy A, and
the diff would fail policy A's schema condition on its own merits too (`hogar_local` -> `hogar_miembro`, a real
migration in `body/db.py`). Left on `feat/body-hogar-cuenta-1`, gate green, nothing further attempted.

## BODY-HOGAR-CUENTA-1-M -- four fixes from the orchestrator's diff review of BODY-HOGAR-CUENTA-1, then merged (2026-11-07)

ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1, against BODY-HOGAR-CUENTA-OBS-1. Four code fixes against `feat/body-hogar-cuenta-1`
(tip `137467b`), plus deleting two untracked commit-message scratch files the prior worker left in the repository
root.

**Fix 1 (the premature-commit bug).** `household.sincronizar_desde_claim`, `cuenta._debe_refrescar_hogar`, and
`household.household_of` (same request path, found by the grep the spec asked for) each ran
`conn.executescript(household.SCHEMA)` to lazily create `hogar_miembro`. In Python's `sqlite3` module,
`executescript` COMMITs any transaction already open on `conn` before it runs -- measured directly (`BEGIN`, an
`UPDATE`, `executescript('CREATE TABLE ...')`, `rollback()`: the `UPDATE` survives). A sign-in (`handle_callback`) or
the hourly session-touch (`resolve_session`, right after its own last-seen `UPDATE`) calling into these functions
could therefore commit the caller's write early. All three call sites now use a plain `conn.execute(SCHEMA)` instead
-- `SCHEMA` is a single `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` statement, and a single `execute()` of DDL does NOT have the
COMMIT-first behavior (measured the same way: the `UPDATE` is gone after `rollback()`). Two new tests
(`TransactionSafetyTest`) cover both functions directly: begin a write, call the function with an absent claim,
roll back, confirm the write is gone.

Deviation from the spec text: it asked to "remove" the call "so nothing needs it", on the premise that `db.init`
already creates `hogar_miembro` on a fresh database. Measured directly (`db.init` against a fresh in-memory
connection, then checked `sqlite_master`): it does not -- `body/db.py`'s `SCHEMA` constant has no `hogar_miembro`
table, and `_migrate_hogar` only creates it when a pre-existing `hogar_local` table is found to migrate from.
Removing the call outright, with nothing creating the table on a genuinely fresh install before the first sign-in,
would have broken every one of this file's existing tests and the real first-sign-in path. `body/db.py` is Tier 1
and outside this slice's `touches`, so instead of widening the diff, the table stays lazily created by
`household.py`/`cuenta.py`'s own `execute(SCHEMA)` calls -- now safe, since they no longer use `executescript`.
Recorded here rather than guessed past; a new test (`LazyTableCreationTest`) documents the measured gap directly
against the repository. `BODY-HOGAR-CUENTA-DB-INIT-1` (open follow-up): have `db.init` create `hogar_miembro`
unconditionally, so the lazy creation in `household.py`/`cuenta.py` becomes redundant rather than load-bearing.

**Fix 2.** `refrescar_hogar` now percent-escapes the sub with `urllib.parse.quote(sub, safe="")` before building the
`GET /servicio/cuentas/{sub}` path, instead of interpolating it raw. New test checks the exact URL called for a sub
containing `/` and a space.

**Fix 3.** A service-API answer that parses as JSON but is not an object (a list, a string, ...) now keeps the
mirror untouched: `refrescar_hogar` only forwards the answer to the sync when `isinstance(claims, dict)`, logging a
count-only line otherwise; `sincronizar_desde_claim` itself now also returns `'sin_dato'` for a non-dict `claims`
argument (previously `"duna_hogar" not in claims` / `claims["duna_hogar"]` could raise `TypeError` for some non-dict
shapes, e.g. a list containing the string `"duna_hogar"`). New tests cover both: four non-dict `claims` shapes
against `sincronizar_desde_claim` directly, and a mocked list answer through `refrescar_hogar` that leaves an
existing `'cuenta'` row untouched.

**Fix 4.** The upsert in `sincronizar_desde_claim` now selects `SELECT id, cuenta_sub FROM person WHERE cuenta_sub IN
(<miembros>)` instead of reading every person row with any `cuenta_sub` and filtering the match in Python -- a query
on the claim's own `miembros` is enough; the `DELETE`'s own subquery already did this correctly, only the upsert's
`SELECT` changes. Logically equivalent to the prior filtering, so existing outcome tests already cover correctness;
one new test (`UnrelatedPersonTest`) adds an unrelated third person with a `cuenta_sub` not in `miembros` and
confirms they are never touched.

**Cleanup.** Deleted `.commit_msg_body_hogar_cuenta_1.txt` and `.commit_msg_body_hogar_cuenta_1_ledger.txt`
(untracked, left by the worker that landed `BODY-HOGAR-CUENTA-1`).

**Tests.** `tests/test_hogar_cuenta_1.py` grew from 17 to 25 (8 new: two `TransactionSafetyTest`, one
`LazyTableCreationTest`, two `NonDictClaimsTest`, one `UrlEscapingTest`, one `UnrelatedPersonTest`, and the existing
count already included `MigrationTest`/`ExportDeleteTest` etc.). `main` had not moved (tip still `e77c575` since the
branch was cut, confirmed with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`), so no merge into the feature branch was needed first.

**Gate, run once, foreground, exact command** `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`:

    Ran 1082 tests in 190.446s
    OK (skipped=1)

1082 is 1074 (this spec's supplied floor for `BODY-HOGAR-CUENTA-1`'s tip `137467b`) + 8 new tests above; the one skip
is pre-existing and unrelated.

**Merged.** The diff touches no schema or migration, no customer-facing bytes, and no cross-repo contract or DTO
shape -- merge policy A holds, and this spec's body says explicitly to merge after the fixes. Fix commit `e890a2c`
on `feat/body-hogar-cuenta-1`, merged `--no-ff` into `main`.

## BODY-HOGAR-CUENTA-DB-INIT-1 -- db.init creates hogar_miembro unconditionally (2026-11-07)

`BODY-HOGAR-CUENTA-1-M` measured that `db.init` on a FRESH database never created `hogar_miembro` -- `_migrate_hogar`
created it only when migrating from a pre-existing `hogar_local` -- so three request-path functions
(`household.household_of`, `household.sincronizar_desde_claim`, `cuenta._debe_refrescar_hogar`) ran
`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` on every call, DDL on the sign-in and session-touch path, to make the table exist. Every
other table is created by `db.init`; this was the one exception.

**`body/db.py`.** New `_ensure_hogar_miembro`, called from `init()` before `_migrate_hogar`, creates `hogar_miembro`
unconditionally from `household._COLUMNS` -- the same column text `_migrate_hogar` already used, via a function-local
`from . import household` (the same way `_migrate_hogar` already avoided the circular import: `household.py` has no
module-level import of `db`). `_migrate_hogar`'s own `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is removed from its `step`; it now
only copies rows from `hogar_local` into the already-existing table and drops it. Its idempotency and row-count check
are unchanged.

**Removed the three lazy creates** and their docstring paragraphs about `execute()` vs `executescript()` (no longer
needed: nothing here opens a transaction before the table is created, since `db.init` already made it exist).
`household.SCHEMA` stays -- `git grep -n "SCHEMA)" body/` after the change:

    body/db.py:755:    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    body/demo.py:299:    conn.executescript(household.SCHEMA)
    body/privacidad.py:70:    conn.executescript(household.SCHEMA)
    body/privacidad.py:169:    conn.executescript(household.SCHEMA)

`body/demo.py` and `body/privacidad.py` still call `household.SCHEMA` directly; both are outside this slice's
`touches`, so `SCHEMA` (and its lazy-create pattern there) is left alone.

**Tests.** `LazyTableCreationTest` (which documented the gap) became `DbInitCreatesHogarMiembroTest`: `db.init` on a
fresh database creates `hogar_miembro` with exactly `_COLUMNS`'s five columns, and calling `db.init` twice on a fresh
database is idempotent. `MigrationTest` (unchanged) already covered a database with `hogar_local` migrating with
rows copied and `hogar_local` dropped, idempotently. `TransactionSafetyTest` gained a case for a malformed-but-present
`duna_hogar` value (`{"duna_hogar": "not-a-dict"}`, a "value claim" as opposed to the existing absent-key `{}` case),
confirming `sincronizar_desde_claim` still does not commit a caller's open transaction. Checked every other test
module calling `household.household_of`, `household.sincronizar_desde_claim` or `cuenta._debe_refrescar_hogar`
(`test_goals.py`, `test_household.py`, `test_person_scope.py`): each calls `db.init` (or `executescript(household.SCHEMA)`
directly) before relying on the table, so none depended on the removed lazy creates.

**Gate, run once, foreground, exact command** `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`:

    Ran 1084 tests in 149.404s
    OK (skipped=1)

**Merged.** The diff touches `body/db.py` (DDL moved, not a schema shape change: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` on an
existing database that already has the table changes nothing; a fresh database gets the same empty table it would
otherwise get lazily), no customer-facing bytes, and no cross-repo contract or DTO shape -- merge policy A holds, and
this spec's approval-reason says explicitly that it approves the merge too. Fix commit `1f3e942` on
`feat/body-hogar-cuenta-db-init-1`, merged `--no-ff` into `main`.

## BODY-HOGAR-ENLACE-1 -- a goal can link to the place where the rest of its plan lives in another Duna app (2026-11-07)

Under `ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`, against BODY-HOGAR-OBS-1's follow-up BODY-HOGAR-LINK-OUT-1, ruled by the
orchestrator ledger BODY-HOGAR-PLAN-1 ruling 5 and (cont. 4): links are ROWS (a goal may have several, one per app at
most in v1), `app` is a key into one code registry of known apps and their URL shape, and Body stores only the app key
and that app's own opaque `ref` -- never a title copied from the other app, never a URL typed by the person (the URL
is always BUILT from the registry, so no arbitrary link can be planted on a shared goal). Lugares' trip is `viaje`,
integer id, opened at `https://lugares.duna.solutions/viajes/{id}`, access is Lugares' own lista membership. Finanzas
has no goal/budget entity with a stable id today (Finanzas orchestrator, 2026-11-07), so it is left out of the
registry until it has one.

**Schema (`body/db.py`), verbatim:**

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS goal_enlace (
        id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
        goal_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES goal(id),
        app        TEXT NOT NULL,
        ref        TEXT NOT NULL,
        creado_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
        UNIQUE (goal_id, app)
    );

`app` is deliberately not CHECK-constrained: the registry in code is the authority, and an app key no longer known
there is simply not rendered. Created by `db.init`'s `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` on fresh and existing databases
alike -- nothing to backfill.

**`body/enlaces.py` (new) -- the only module that reads or writes the table, and the registry.** `APPS` has one entry
in v1:

    "lugares": {
        "label_key": "goals.enlace.app.lugares",
        "origin_env": "DUNA_LUGARES_ORIGEN",
        "origin_default": "https://lugares.duna.solutions",
        "path": "/viajes/{ref}",
        "ref_pattern": re.compile(r"^[1-9][0-9]{0,11}$"),
    }

`url_de(app, ref)` builds the URL from the registry (`urllib.parse.quote`), None for an unknown app or an invalid ref.
`ref_desde_entrada(app, texto)` accepts what a person actually pastes -- the bare id, or a full trip URL on the
registry's own origin and path, with or without a trailing slash, query or fragment -- and returns the id; a URL on
any other host or path, or junk, returns None. `enlazar` upserts on `(goal_id, app)` (one link per app); `quitar`
deletes one; `enlaces_de` returns only registry apps whose stored ref still builds a valid URL -- an unknown app key
already stored is silently skipped, never rendered.

**Access.** Adding or removing a link stays with the goal's creator (`goals.goal_access(...) == 'creator'`, ruling 1
of BODY-HOGAR-MIEMBRO-1) -- a member or a stranger gets 404, the same as every other creator-only goal action. Seeing
it: anyone `goals.goal_access` lets see the goal.

**`body/web.py`.** Two POST routes, `/goals/{goal_id}/enlaces` (form fields `app`, `entrada`) and
`/goals/{goal_id}/enlaces/{app}/quitar`, both redirecting back to the goal page; an entry `ref_desde_entrada` rejects
redirects to `/goals/{goal_id}?enlace=invalido`, which `goal_detail` reads into an inline error. Neither route is a
GET, so `tests/test_agente_registro.py`'s GET-route-to-tool guard (`ROUTE_TOOL`) is unaffected -- it enumerates GET
routes only, confirmed by reading that test before writing the routes.

**`body/templates/goal.html`.** A quiet "Enlaces" card: each link as "Viaje en Lugares ↗" / "Lugares trip ↗"
(`target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`, `.taplink`'s 44 px tap target); for the creator a "Quitar"/"Remove" per
link and, collapsed in a `<details>`, "Enlazar un viaje de Lugares" / "Link a Lugares trip" with a text field and a
button; a note line "Se abre en Lugares; solo lo ven quienes tienen acceso allí." / "Opens in Lugares; only people
with access there can see it." Members see the link and that line, no form. Without links and not the creator, the
block is absent. Both languages, 8 new keys each in `body/i18n/es.json` / `en.json`.

**`body/privacidad.py`** and **`body/agente/herramientas.py`.** `goal_enlace` carries no literal `person_id` column
(its only foreign key is `goal_id`), so it is handled the same way `habit` already is: exported and deleted through a
join on `goal.person_id`, via `enlaces.export_rows` / `enlaces.delete_rows_for_person`, OUTSIDE
`privacidad.FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES` -- that set is checked by `person_tables()`, which looks for a literal `person_id`
column, so adding `goal_enlace` to it would have made `test_every_person_table_is_exported_or_excepted` fail (`found`
missing the table, `accounted` claiming it). This is a deviation from the spec's literal "add `goal_enlace` to
`FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES`" -- measured against the existing test and the `habit` precedent, not followed literally.
`_leer_meta`'s `meta` dict gains `"enlaces": [{app, url}]`.

**Demo.** Ana's shared household goal gets a Lugares link with invented ref `"4821"`. `tests/test_demo.py`'s
determinism checksum gained `goal_enlace` to its table list and `creado_at` to its excluded (wall-clock) columns --
without the latter, two demo runs would disagree on that column's value.

**Tests (`tests/test_hogar_enlace_1.py`, 30 tests):** `ref_desde_entrada` (bare id, full URL, trailing slash, query,
fragment, another host, another path, `0`, negative, letters, over-long number, empty, unknown app), `url_de` (env
origin, default origin, unknown app, invalid ref), unknown app stored not rendered, creator adds/replaces/removes, a
member sees the link and gets 404 on add/remove, a stranger sees neither the goal nor the link, the rendered `<a>`
has `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and the BUILT url never the pasted string (pasted a full URL with a query string,
confirmed the query string is absent from the page), es and en strings, export and delete-all.

**Gate, run once, foreground, exact command** `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`:

    Ran 1115 tests in 176.780s
    OK (skipped=1)

**AWAITING_APPROVAL, not merged.** The diff touches `body/db.py` with a new table (schema change) and customer-facing
bytes (`body/templates/goal.html`, `body/i18n/es.json`, `body/i18n/en.json`) -- merge policy A fails on two of its
three conditions, and this spec's approval-reason says explicitly to stop before merge on the goal page. Commit
`64bfc00` on `feat/body-hogar-enlace-1`, left unmerged for review.

## BODY-HOGAR-ENLACE-1-M -- four fixes from the AWAITING_APPROVAL review, then merged (2026-11-07)

ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1's review of BODY-HOGAR-ENLACE-1 (tip `c0b4538`) measured four defects in the goal
page's "Enlaces" card and accepted everything else -- the schema, `enlaces.py`'s URL building and ref validation,
creator-only access, export/delete-all. This slice fixes the four and merges.

**Fix 1 -- the error was off-screen and the field hidden.** A rejected paste redirected to
`/goals/{id}?enlace=invalido`, which rendered a top-of-page error with the matching `<details>` fold still closed --
at 375 px the error sat below the fold that held the field it was about. Now the "Enlaces" card carries `id="enlaces"`;
a rejected paste redirects to `/goals/{goal_id}?enlace=invalido&app=<app>#enlaces` (`app` only when it is a known
registry key -- never the pasted text), and that render opens the matching fold with its error line directly above
its field. A successful add or remove now redirects to `/goals/{goal_id}#enlaces` instead of the bare goal URL, so
the browser lands on the card either way.

**Fix 2 -- the fold stayed offered after the goal already had its one link per app.** `goal_enlace` is
`UNIQUE (goal_id, app)`, so posting the form again after a link exists would silently replace it rather than warn.
The fold is now the correct remedy for that shape: a goal with a link for an app shows no fold for that app (Quitar,
then link again, is the only way to change it). The privacy note now renders once, whenever there is a link or a
fold to offer; a creator with no links and nothing left to link sees no "Enlaces" block at all, same as before.

**Fix 3 -- the template hard-coded Lugares, so the registry in `body/enlaces.py` was not the authority the ruling
says it is.** Each `APPS` entry now also carries `add_summary_key`, `field_key` and `error_key` (Lugares keeps the
existing `goals.enlace.add_summary` / `goals.enlace.field_entrada` / `goals.enlace.error`). A new
`enlaces.apps_por_enlazar(conn, goal_id) -> list[{app, add_summary_key, field_key, error_key}]` returns registry
apps this goal has no link for yet, in registry order (a plain `[app for app, spec in APPS.items() if app not in
linked]`, since `APPS` is a dict and Python 3.7+ keeps insertion order). `body/templates/goal.html` loops over it --
one fold per unlinked app, the hidden `app` input carrying `{{ a.app }}`, every word looked up through `t(a.*_key)`
-- and no longer contains `value="lugares"` or any other literal app key or app-specific wording. A second app would
be one registry entry; the template would not change.

**Fix 4 -- `privacidad.delete_person` ran `conn.executescript(household.SCHEMA)`, now redundant and risky.**
BODY-HOGAR-CUENTA-DB-INIT-1 made `db.init` create `hogar_miembro` unconditionally, so `delete_person` no longer needs
to create that table itself before deleting from it -- and `executescript` commits whatever transaction happens to
be open, which the function's own docstring says it does not do (`with conn:`, one transaction, all-or-nothing). The
call is removed from `delete_person`. `privacidad.export_person`'s own `conn.executescript(household.SCHEMA)` call
(line 74) is untouched -- outside this spec's `touches:`, not part of the defect, and `household.py` itself is
untouched throughout.

    $ git grep -n "household.SCHEMA\|executescript" body/
    body/db.py:769:    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    body/demo.py:299:    conn.executescript(household.SCHEMA)
    body/privacidad.py:74:    conn.executescript(household.SCHEMA)

`household.SCHEMA` still has two users in `body/` (`demo.py` and `privacidad.py`'s `export_person`) -- not an unused
symbol to queue for removal.

Adopting Lotes' hub principle (hit_01m6w6cn8x, LOTES-API-FECHA-FUTURA-1): a record of something that already
happened refuses a date past the person's local today plus one day of tolerance; the future lives in plans.

## BODY-FECHA-FUTURA-1-M -- the opt-in `hoy` becomes required, landing BODY-FECHA-FUTURA-1 (2026-11-08)

**Ruling, from the orchestrator, applied verbatim.** BODY-FECHA-FUTURA-1 made `goals.check_habit`'s `hoy` optional
(`hoy: date | None = None`) to keep ~30 pre-existing calls with fixture dates working without touching them. A rule
a caller can forget to pass is not enforced in the single writer, which is what the hub principle (hit_01m6w6cn8x)
asks for. So `hoy` becomes a required, keyword-only argument with no default: `check_habit(conn, habit_id,

person's real local today, the demo its own scenario day, each test its fixture's today. `check_habit` still reads
no clock itself (the worker's original, sound reason for the opt-in shape) -- omitting `hoy` is simply a
`TypeError` now, so the rule cannot be bypassed by a caller forgetting it.

## BODY-LIVE-CHECKOUT-1 -- every scheduled task runs from a refreshed sibling worktree (2026-11-08)

Carlos's PC runs scheduled tasks (the web app at logon, the daily Garmin pull, the weekly file) out of this same
repository. A dispatched worker's unmerged branch lives in this repo's own working tree -- so without a fix,
"restart the web task" or "run the daily pull" mid-slice would serve or read whatever branch a worker happened to
have checked out at that moment, not `main`. This slice adds a second, sibling checkout on disk (`-LiveDir`,
default `"$repo-live"`) that holds nothing but `main`, refreshed to `main`'s latest commit at the start of every
task run, and routes every scheduled task's action through it instead of through `$repo` directly.

`body/vivo.py` is the new allowlisted launcher (`python -m body.vivo <task>`), added to `TAREAS`: `pull`,
`shift_import`, `vida_export`, `subir_turnos`, `traer_semana`, `web`.

* `refrescar(vivo)` moves `vivo` to `main`'s current commit. It REFUSES to touch anything that is not a linked
  worktree (compares `--git-dir` with `--git-common-dir`; equal means this is the repo's own main working tree,
  never to be moved), refuses a `vivo` that is not clean (`git status --porcelain` non-empty), and always
  `git checkout --detach main` -- never a branch checkout, so `vivo` is never left on a ref a later `git worktree`
  operation could conflict with. A refresh that cannot proceed (dirty, not a worktree, git failure, timeout) is a
  fail-safe, not an abort: the result is one of the `sin_cambio:<reason>` words, logged, and `main()` still runs
  the task against whatever commit is already on disk -- always a `main` commit from some earlier, successful
  refresh, never a branch, because `refrescar` never leaves `vivo` on anything else.
* `repo_principal(vivo)` resolves the parent of `vivo`'s `--git-common-dir` -- the main repository that owns the
  worktree -- so the launcher can find `$repo\.env` even though the live checkout has none of its own.
* `main()` refreshes, logs one line (`<resultado> <vivo.name> <sha>`), sets `BODY_ENV_FILE` (via
  `os.environ.setdefault`, so an already-set value is never overridden) to `repo_principal(vivo)/.env`, then runs
  the task.
* `body/entorno.py`'s `cargar()` now prefers `BODY_ENV_FILE` over `RUTA_DEFECTO` when no `ruta` is given, since the
  live checkout has no `.env` of its own and must read the main repo's.

`scripts/install-daily-sync.ps1` gains `-LiveDir` (default `"$repo-live"`), creates that worktree with
`git worktree add --detach $LiveDir main` if missing, and routes every scheduled task's action through
`-m body.vivo <task>` with `-WorkingDirectory $LiveDir` instead of `$repo`.

**Stopped GATE_RED, not merged.** The worker's own gate (`.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t
.`) came back red on two tests outside this slice's `touches:` -- `tests/test_pc_cliente.py` and
`tests/test_shift_import.py` still asserted the pre-existing direct module names (`body.subir_turnos`,
`body.shift_import`) that this slice's own script no longer contains, since every action now reads
`-m body.vivo <task>` instead. The worker stopped on the branch (`feat/body-live-checkout-1`, tip `cc74f6a`)
without merging and without writing this ledger entry -- both done now, by the orchestrator's review and its
continuation BODY-LIVE-CHECKOUT-1-M below, which also fixed two further defects the review found in the design
above: `web`'s `os.execve` on Windows, and the installer's text-matched worktree-reuse check. See that entry for
what changed and why.

## BODY-LIVE-CHECKOUT-1-M -- land it with three fixes: in-process tasks, a real worktree check, the drifted tests (2026-11-08)

Continuation of BODY-LIVE-CHECKOUT-1 above, after the orchestrator's review (`BODY-LIVE-CHECKOUT-OBS-1`). Three
defects, fixed on the same branch before merging.

**(1) `body/vivo.py`: `web` no longer uses `os.execve`.** On Windows, CPython's `os.execve` does not replace the
process image -- it starts a NEW process and the calling process then exits. So the PID Task Scheduler's "Body app
web" action launched was gone the moment `os.execve` ran: the task read as finished, its restart policy
(`-RestartCount`/`-RestartInterval`) never watched the real server, `Stop-ScheduledTask` no longer stopped it, and
the next `Start-ScheduledTask` would launch a second server on the same port. Fixed per the orchestrator's ruling:
every task, `web` included, now runs IN-PROCESS, right after the refresh, via
`runpy.run_module(TAREAS[tarea], run_name="__main__", alter_sys=True)` -- the same PID throughout, no child
process, no console. Before that call: `os.environ.setdefault("BODY_ENV_FILE", ...)`, `os.chdir(vivo)`, and
`vivo`'s path is moved to `sys.path[0]` (removed if already present, then inserted at the front) so the task
module resolves against the just-refreshed tree. `sys.argv` is set to `[TAREAS[tarea], *resto]` before the call.
A `SystemExit` the task raises propagates as this launcher's exit code (`int` codes returned as-is; `None` is 0;
anything else is printed to stderr, when `sys.stdout` is not `None`, and returns 1); a normal return is 0. The
`_despachar` function and the `subprocess` spawn of a python interpreter are gone; `subprocess` remains only for
the `git` calls `refrescar`/`repo_principal` already made.

A guard runs before the refresh: if any `body*` entry in `sys.modules` is not `body` or `body.vivo` -- a module a
wrapper or a previous task in the same process could have left cached with code the refresh is about to replace
on disk -- the refresh is skipped, the logged word is `sin_cambio:modulos_previos`, and the task still runs (never
aborted). In production this never trips: a freshly started `python -m body.vivo <task>` process has imported
only `body` and `body.vivo` by the time `main()` runs. The module's docstring's `web` paragraph is rewritten to
describe the in-process design and why `os.execve` was wrong on Windows. The one log line is now printed only
when `sys.stdout is not None`, so a `pythonw`-launched task (no stdout) cannot fail on it.

**(2) `scripts/install-daily-sync.ps1`: the worktree-reuse check now asks git, not a text match.** The script
decided whether `$LiveDir` was already a worktree of `$repo` by matching `$LiveDir` (or its `Resolve-Path`) as
text against `git -C $repo worktree list --porcelain`. `--porcelain` prints forward slashes
(`worktree C:/Duna/body-app-live`) while `$LiveDir` and `Resolve-Path` carry backslashes on Windows, so the
`-match [regex]::Escape(...)` comparison never succeeded -- a SECOND run of the installer always tried
`git worktree add --detach $LiveDir main` again, which exits 1 because the worktree already exists. Fixed: if
`Test-Path $LiveDir`, the script runs `git -C $LiveDir rev-parse --git-common-dir`, resolves that (relative to
`$LiveDir` when git prints a relative path) with `Resolve-Path`, and compares it case-insensitively against
`(Resolve-Path "$repo\.git")` -- `Resolve-Path` on both sides normalises the separators, so the comparison is
exact rather than textual. Equal -> reuse the existing tree (no `worktree add`). `$LiveDir` exists and is NOT a
worktree of `$repo` (not a git repo at all, or a worktree of a different repo) -> prints a Spanish message naming
`$LiveDir` and `$repo`, and `exit 1` without touching it. `$LiveDir` absent -> `git -C $repo worktree add --detach
$LiveDir main`, unchanged.

**(3) The two drifting tests, now fixed instead of deferred.** `tests/test_pc_cliente.py`'s
`test_hosted_registers_shift_upload_and_weekly_fetch` asserted `"body.subir_turnos"` and `"body.traer_semana"` as
literal substrings of the hosted block; `tests/test_shift_import.py`'s
`test_shiftsdir_param_used_only_inside_its_own_branch_and_no_personal_path` asserted `"body.shift_import"` inside
the `-ShiftsDir` branch. Both strings stopped appearing once BODY-LIVE-CHECKOUT-1 routed every action through
`-m body.vivo <task>` (`"body.vivo subir_turnos"`, `"body.vivo traer_semana"`, `"body.vivo shift_import"` --
`body.subir_turnos` and the others are never substrings of those). Both assertions now check the `body.vivo
<task>` form instead, each still inside the same block/branch the original test checked, so each test's subject
is unchanged: the hosted block still proves it registers the shift-upload and weekly-fetch tasks; the
`-ShiftsDir` test still proves shift import appears only inside its own branch.

**New tests**, `tests/test_vivo.py::MainTest`: `main` is asserted to call `runpy.run_module("body.<task>",
run_name="__main__", alter_sys=True)` with `os.chdir(vivo)` and `sys.argv` set beforehand and `BODY_ENV_FILE`
pointing at the main repo's `.env`; a `SystemExit` from the task propagates its code, a normal return is 0; a
dedicated test patches both `os.execve` (to raise if called) and `subprocess.run` (to fail if invoked with
`sys.executable` as the command) and confirms `main(["web", ...])` returns 0 without tripping either; another
injects an extra `body.*` module into `sys.modules` and confirms `refrescar` is skipped, the task still runs, and
the log line reads `sin_cambio:modulos_previos`; another sets `sys.stdout` to `None` and confirms `main` does not
raise. `tests/test_installer.py::InstallerWorktreeReuseTest`: the script no longer contains
`worktree list --porcelain` or the `-match [regex]::Escape($LiveDir)` text match; it contains
`git -C $LiveDir rev-parse --git-common-dir` and compares against `Resolve-Path -LiteralPath "$repo\.git"`; the
`Test-Path $LiveDir` branch contains an `exit 1` and the `worktree add` call is outside it (in the `else`).

**Gate, run once, foreground, exact command:**

    .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .

    Ran 1161 tests in 249.284s
    OK (skipped=1)

Green. (1161 vs. the first slice's own 1139-test floor from the sibling BODY-FECHA-FUTURA-1-M entry above is not a
comparable figure -- that floor was a different slice's tree; this slice added tests of its own, counted in the
`figures` of its STOP report.)

**Merge.** Diff: `body/vivo.py`, `scripts/install-daily-sync.ps1`, `tests/test_vivo.py`,
`tests/test_installer.py`, `tests/test_pc_cliente.py`, `tests/test_shift_import.py`, `README.md` (unchanged --
nothing in it named the fixed internals), `DECISIONS.md`. No schema or migration change, no customer-facing byte
(every change is to an internal launcher, an install script run by Carlos's own hand, and tests), no cross-repo
contract change. Merge policy A's three conditions are clear and this spec's body explicitly authorises the merge
("Then merge."). `--no-ff` into `main`.

**Hand steps for Carlos.** Nothing runs on its own: re-run the installer once, from an elevated PowerShell, with
whatever flags you used before (for example `.\scripts\install-daily-sync.ps1` or with `-ShiftsDir`/`-Lan`/
`-Hosted` as before) -- it re-registers the three scheduled tasks pointing at the fixed `body.vivo`, and reuses
the existing `-LiveDir` worktree rather than failing on it (fix 2 above is exactly what makes that reuse work now).
No `-LiveDir` worktree exists yet on this PC as of this merge, so the very first run still creates it fresh either
way. To undo: `Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName "Body app daily sync"; Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName "Body
app weekly file"; Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName "Body app web"`, then `git -C <repo> worktree remove
<LiveDir>` (as the script's own header comment already says).
