## BODY-PULIDO-3 -- the BODY-DISENO-CENSO-2 round's 7 candidate slices, built together (2026-11-08)

Each site re-found in the code (static census words below are what the code actually held, not a restatement):

**1. NAV-GLOBAL-2 (rule 11, 44px tap targets).** Five sites, none reaching 44px before this slice:
- `base.html`'s in-context help door: `<a class="ayuda-ctx" href="/ayuda#{{ tarea_ctx.id }}">{{ t('ayuda.como_se_hace') }}</a>` -- a `display:block;text-align:right` row with no `min-height`.
- `base.html`'s two `.foot` links (Ayuda, Ajustes): `<a href="/ayuda" style="text-decoration:underline">...</a>` / `<a href="/settings" style="text-decoration:underline">...</a>` -- plain inline anchors, no tap-target sizing.
- `trends.html`'s back-to-Tendencias link (shown inside a month drill-down): `<a href="/trends">{{ t('trends.back_hist') }}</a>` -- no class at all.
- `history.html`'s shift-empty link: `<a href="/shifts" style="text-decoration:underline">{{ t('nav.shifts') }}</a>`.

Fix: one shared rule per layout shape, reusing the existing `.taplink` class (`display:inline-flex;align-items:center;min-height:44px;text-decoration:underline`, unchanged) for the two inline-flow sites (`trends.html`'s back link and `history.html`'s shift-empty link now carry `class="taplink"`, their redundant inline underline style dropped); `.ayuda-ctx` changed from `display:block;text-align:right` to `display:flex;justify-content:flex-end;align-items:center;min-height:44px` (same right-aligned, full-width look, now 44px tall); a new `.foot a{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;min-height:44px;text-decoration:underline}` rule picks up both `.foot` links without a template change beyond dropping their now-redundant inline style. `body/static/body.css`, `body/templates/base.html`, `trends.html`, `history.html`.

**2. TURNOS-SCORE-1 (rule 4, measured ≠ estimated).** `shifts.html`'s strip cell: `{% if c.score is not none %}{{ c.score }}{% else %}—{% endif %}` -- Body's own estimated readiness score, printed as a bare number, no «≈». Fix: `<span class="approx">≈</span>{{ c.score }}` in the scored branch, reusing the plain `.approx` class `day.html` already uses for its own estimated metric cards (no size modifier needed at the strip's 11px cell text) -- the same marker Hoy's hero, Como lo calculo and the strip's own hero (`shifts.hero_dias`) already carry. `body/templates/shifts.html`.

**3. DIA-ACTIVIDAD-1 (rule 10, plain language).** `body/web.py`'s `day_view`: `acts.append({"name": a["name"] or a["type"] or "—", "detail": ...})` -- an unnamed activity fell back to Garmin's raw `type` code verbatim (e.g. a code with no `activity.type.*` entry would print the code itself). Fix: new `_activity_name(t, a)` helper -- a known type (`history.KNOWN_ACTIVITY_TYPES`) reads its existing `activity.type.<key>` label (the same i18n map `_kind_label` already reads for History); an unknown or missing type reads the new `activity.generic` key ("Actividad" / "Activity") instead of the code. `body/web.py`, `body/i18n/es.json`, `body/i18n/en.json`.

**4. HOGAR-ENLACE-HOY-1 (rule 3's one exception, ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1).** `today.html`'s «Tu hogar» row already had no `<a>` (rule 3 was not literally violated -- nothing of the owner's sat behind the row), but it also carried no provenance: `<div class="k">{{ item.name }} · {{ item.metric_label }}</div>` followed by the figure and a bare day word, with no mention that the figure came from someone else's watch. Fix: `_hogar_compartido_ctx` in `body/web.py` now builds a `procedencia` sentence (new key `today.hogar.procedencia`: es "{name} compartió esto · su reloj · {day}", en "Shared by {name} · their watch · {day}") in place of the old bare `day_text`, reusing the existing `_dia_relativo` hoy/ayer/short-date helper for `{day}`; `today.html`'s row now shows the metric label, the figure, and this sentence -- still no `<a>` anywhere in the card. `docs/DESIGN.md` rule 3 gained one sentence recording the exception. `body/web.py`, `body/templates/today.html`, `body/i18n/es.json`, `body/i18n/en.json`, `docs/DESIGN.md`.

**5. HABITO-CONTEXTO-1 (rule 7, shifts are the axis).** `today.html` and `goal.html` both hardcoded `<span class="chip night">{{ h.context }}</span>` for every habit context chip, including `off_days` -- a day off is not a night, but it read with the night tint. Fix: new `_context_chip_cls(context)` in `body/web.py` returns `"off"` for `off_days` and `"night"` otherwise (before_night/after_night keep the night family, per the spec); `_today_due_habits` and `goal_detail`'s habit rows now carry `context_cls` alongside the existing translated `context` label; both templates render `class="chip {{ h.context_cls }}"`. New CSS `.chip.off{background:var(--wash);color:var(--ink2)}`, reusing the same off-day family `.shift.off`/`.strip-cell.off` already use. `body/web.py`, `body/templates/today.html`, `body/templates/goal.html`, `body/static/body.css`.

**6. METAS-MIEMBROS-1.** `goal_detail` in `body/web.py`: `_, verdict = _verdict(t, crow["on_track"] if crow else None)` -- the class `_verdict` returns alongside the verdict word was thrown away, so `goal.html`'s members block rendered `{{ m.name }}<span>{{ m.verdict }}</span>`, a bare uncoloured span, while the viewer's own verdict two cards above kept its `<span class="chip {{ cls }}">`. Fix: keep the class as `member_cls`, pass it through as `cls` on each member dict; `goal.html` now renders `<span class="chip {{ m.cls }}">{{ m.verdict }}</span>`, the same shape the viewer's own verdict already used. `body/web.py`, `body/templates/goal.html`.

**7. AJUSTES-1 (rule 11, 44px tap targets).** Five rows in `settings.html` (Ayuda, Privacidad, Asistente, and, when hosted, Garmin and Dispositivos) wrapped a `<div class="card">` around an inner `<a class="q" style="display:block;...">` -- only the text's own line box was the link, not the card's padding around it. Fix: the `<a>` IS the card now (`<a href="/ayuda" class="card" style="display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:8px;min-height:44px;...">`), the whole row tappable at a guaranteed 44px, the existing "→" arrow kept as the affordance, no JavaScript. `body/templates/settings.html`.

**Tests**, `tests/test_pulido_3.py` (18 new): the shared CSS rules read straight from `body.css`; the five NAV-GLOBAL-2 sites rendered end to end (`.ayuda-ctx` and the two `.foot` links on an ordinary `/trends` page, the back-to-Tendencias `taplink` on a month view, the shift-empty `taplink` on History); the strip's scored cell carries `<span class="approx">≈</span>` and an unscored cell still shows a plain dash; Día's activity fallback reads a known type's translated label, never a raw unknown code, in both languages; the «Tu hogar» row states its provenance in both languages and is never inside an `<a>`; a habit's `off_days` chip gets `chip off` never `chip night`, while `before_night` keeps `chip night`; a household goal's other-member verdict renders `<span class="chip ok">En camino</span>`, never the bare `<span>` shape; the three always-visible Ajustes rows are each one `<a class="card">` carrying `min-height:44px`.

**Gate**, run once on the final tree with the plain command: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t
.` -- `Ran 1179 tests in 203.230s ... FAILED (failures=1, skipped=1)` (1161 before this slice, +18 new; 1 pre-existing
test now fails as a direct, correct consequence of fix 2 above).

**GATE_RED, not fixable inside `touches:`.** `tests/test_turnos_costo.py::HeroQuestionsTest::
test_hero_question_differs_from_rows_question_and_number_shown_once` asserts `r.text.count("≈") == 1` on the whole
`/shifts` page, with the comment "the big figure, not repeated in the sentence below it" -- written when the strip

estimada" / "Your readiness · estimated") --
- es: `"shifts.strip_cell"`: `"{fecha} · {turno} · preparación {n}"` → `"{fecha} · {turno} · preparación ≈ {n} (estimada)"`
- en: `"shifts.strip_cell"`: `"{fecha} · {turno} · readiness {n}"` → `"{fecha} · {turno} · readiness ≈ {n} (estimated)"`

No change was needed in `body/web.py`: `_strip` already calls `t("shifts.strip_cell", fecha=fecha, turno=turno,

## BODY-I18N-GUARD-1 -- a test that notices when es.json and en.json drift apart (2026-11-08)

DESIGN rule 10/15 ("every es string has an en twin") had no test behind it -- `body/i18n/__init__.py`'s
`T.__call__` falls back to Spanish on a missing English key, and to the raw key on a missing both, silently, so a
gap would only ever surface as a wrong-language sentence or a literal key on Carlos's screen (BODY-DISENO-CENSO-2's
unknown). Added `tests/test_i18n_paridad.py`.

**What the first run (alone) found: nothing.** `body/i18n/es.json` and `body/i18n/en.json` already carry the exact
same 566 keys, with matching `{placeholder}` names, matching list lengths (`date.days`, `date.months`), and no
empty or whitespace-only value. Checked with a throwaway script before writing the test (deleted, never committed):
`set(es) - set(en)` and `set(en) - set(es)` both empty; a `string.Formatter().parse()` pass over every shared key
found zero placeholder mismatches. **No string was added to either file; this slice's only change is the new test
module.**

**Literal keys.** Scanned every `t('…')` / `t("…")` call with a string-literal first argument across
`body/templates/**/*.html` and `body/**/*.py` (a regex over source, not an import) -- 375 distinct literal keys,
every one present in `es.json`.

**Dynamic keys (`prefix + variable` / `prefix ~ variable`).** 22 distinct dynamic prefixes found across templates
and code, every one checked against the fixed list its value actually comes from, read from source (not re-typed
by hand):
`metric.` (`body.db.METRIC_DEFS`, 24 keys), `part.` (`readiness.py`'s `WEIGHTS` keys: hrv/sleep/battery/
resting_hr/stress), `shift.kind.` (`web._STRIP_KIND_ORDER`, 7), `shifts.cost_sub.` (`turnos_costo.MODELO
["metricas"]`, 5), `shifts.word.` (`diferencia_y_palabra()`'s 3 return words), `shifts.reason.` (`_motivo()`'s 4
return codes), `patron.error.` (`patron_turnos.validar()`'s per-row codes, 4 -- its whole-cycle `largo_invalido` is
filtered out by index before reaching `t()`, so it needs no i18n string and is not asserted), `trends.q.`
(`TREND_KEYS` ∪ `TREND_GROUPS` values, 22), `trends.plain.` (`TREND_GROUPS` values, 13), `trends.group.`

## BODY-PATRON-ERROR-CICLO-1 -- a whole-cycle patron error now renders, instead of a silent re-render (2026-11-08)

Worker follow-up from `BODY-PATRON-LARGO-INVALIDO-SILENT-1` (noted in `BODY-I18N-GUARD-1`): `patron_turnos.validar()`
can raise a whole-cycle error (`{"index": None, "code": "largo_invalido"}`), and `web.shifts_patron_save` kept only
per-row errors (`if err["index"] is not None`), so a whole-cycle refusal re-rendered the form with no message at
all -- and there was no `patron.error.largo_invalido` string. Latent today (`_patron_dias` clamps the cycle to
1..56, so today's form cannot produce it), but DESIGN's "anything off the normal flow raises a flag" means a
refusal must never be silent, and the next caller of `validar` (an API, the assistant) will not clamp.

- `web.shifts_patron_save`: splits `PatronInvalido.errors` into per-row (`index` not `None`, as before, keyed to
  each row) and whole-cycle (`index is None`), translating the whole-cycle codes with the same
  `t("patron.error." + code)` call the per-row path already used, into `errores_ciclo` (a list of already-translated
  strings, not codes) passed to the template.
- `shift_pattern.html`: when `errores_ciclo` is non-empty, a form-level error line at the top of `<form>`, one `<p
  class="k bad">` per message -- the same class the per-row errors already use.
- `body/i18n/es.json` / `en.json`: `patron.error.largo_invalido` -- es "El ciclo debe tener entre 1 y 56 días.", en
  "The cycle must be between 1 and 56 days." (the bound read from `validar()`'s own check, not re-typed). The
  missing twin of the existing `patron.error.*` family, same voice.
- `tests/test_patron_error_ciclo_1.py` (4 tests, new module, `tests/_isolate.py` imported first): patches
  `body.patron_turnos.validar` to raise the whole-cycle error and asserts the message renders in es and en and
  nothing is saved; a per-row error still renders on its row and the whole-cycle string does not leak in; a valid
  form still saves and redirects. `tests/test_turnos_opcional_5.py` needed no change -- its 39 tests still pass
  unchanged, confirmed by running that module alone before the full gate.

Because the whole-cycle message is now built in Python with the same `t("patron.error." + code)` call the per-row
path already used (not a new `t(...)` call inside the template), the i18n parity guard's dynamic-prefix scan
(`tests/test_i18n_paridad.py`) sees no new prefix -- `patron.error.+` was already in its fixed list. That guard file
is outside this slice's `touches:`, so its stale comment ("its whole-cycle `largo_invalido` is filtered out by
index before reaching `t()`, so it never needs an i18n string") was left as written; `largo_invalido` now does
reach `t()`, by index `None`'s own path rather than the per-row one the comment describes. Left for the next slice
that touches that file.

## BODY-TESTS-VELOCIDAD-1 -- the order dependency in test_garmin_host, and a faster test_vivo/test_primer_pull_1 (2026-11-08)

**The order dependency, root cause.** Reproduced exactly as specified: in one process, imported `tests._isolate`,
then loaded and ran `tests.test_agente_bucle` through `tests.test_fecha_futura_1` (sorted) each with
`unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromName` + a fresh `TextTestRunner`, then `tests.test_garmin_host` --
`MfaFlowTest.test_expired_mfa_state_is_refused` raised `KeyError` on a key it had itself just inserted, and
`test_old_mfa_state_is_pruned_on_the_next_write` found its own stale entry never pruned. Bisected by instrumenting
`web._mfa_key`, `web._prune_mfa_state` and `web._MFA_STATE` directly: both failures trace to `tests.test_garmin_host`
binding its own `web` name to a **different module object** than the one `web.app`'s route handlers actually run
against -- confirmed by `tests.test_garmin_host.web is web: False` where the right-hand `web` is the module every
earlier-imported test file (e.g. `tests.test_cuenta_rp`, whose `TestClient(web.app, ...)` IS the real app) already
holds.

The leak is in `tests/test_env_local_1.py`'s `ImportarWebTest.test_importar_body_web_no_llama_cargar`: it does
`del sys.modules["body.web"]`, re-imports it (building a second, throwaway module object with its own empty
`_MFA_STATE`), then `finally: sys.modules["body.web"] = original` -- restoring the `sys.modules` dict entry, but
**not** the `body` package's own cached `web` attribute, which Python's import machinery also pointed at the
throwaway copy during the re-import and never un-sets. Confirmed empirically (`tests/test_import_semantics.py` in
scratchpad, not committed) that both `from body import web` and `import body.web as web` resolve through
`getattr(sys.modules["body"], "web")`, never through `sys.modules["body.web"]` directly -- so any module whose
*first* `body.web` import happens after that test has run binds to the orphaned copy. `unittest discover` imports
every test module during collection, before any test runs, so the production gate never hits this window; the
spec's own prescribed reproduction (load-then-run-immediately, one module at a time) does, because it imports
`tests.test_garmin_host` for the first time only when the loader reaches it -- after `test_env_local_1` has already
corrupted the attribute.

The true fix belongs in `tests/test_env_local_1.py` (also restore `sys.modules["body"].web = original`), but that
file is outside this slice's `touches:`. Fixed within `tests/test_garmin_host.py` instead: rebind `web =
sys.modules["body.web"]` right after the normal import, bypassing the stale attribute entirely, and cleared
`web._MFA_STATE` in `MfaFlowTest.setUp`/`addCleanup` for defense in depth against any other process-wide leak into
that dict. Re-ran the same 19-module sequence: all green (`tests.test_garmin_host: OK (ran 36, failures=0,
errors=0)`). **Open follow-up** (`BODY-TEST-ENV-LOCAL-WEB-ATTR-RESTORE-1`): `tests/test_env_local_1.py`'s restore is
still incomplete and will corrupt the `body.web` attribute for any future test module first imported after it runs
outside a `discover`-style collection -- a later slice touching that file should add the attribute restore too.
No code in `body/web.py` was at fault -- `/garmin/conectar`'s prune-then-insert order was already correct -- so no
production change.

**`tests/test_vivo.py`** (27.6 s -> 12.86 s for its 13 tests, alone). Built the throwaway git repo + worktree once
for the whole module (`setUpModule`/`tearDownModule`) instead of once per test. Only `RefrescarTest` mutates the
trees (commits on main, dirties the live checkout), so only its own `setUp` resets them (`git reset --hard
<initial-sha>` on the repo, `git checkout --force --detach <initial-sha>` on the live tree -- no test here ever
creates an untracked file, so no separate `clean` is needed); `MainTest` and `RepoPrincipalTest` never mutate
either tree and no longer pay for a reset they don't need. Also patched `vivo.refrescar` in the `MainTest` cases
whose subject is the `runpy`/`chdir`/`sys.argv` wiring, not `refrescar`'s own correctness (which `RefrescarTest`
already owns) -- though profiling showed this call was already short-circuited by `_modulos_body_inesperados()`,
since `tests/_isolate.py` always has `body.config` imported first, so the mock is for clarity and future-proofing,
not where the time went. Target was under 8 s; not reached. Profiled with `cProfile` per-test: the remaining ~9 s is
`RefrescarTest`'s 4 tests calling `vivo.refrescar()` for real, which itself makes ~6 git subprocess calls (measured
at 125-350 ms per spawn on this machine) -- unavoidable without weakening `RefrescarTest`'s own assertions or
touching `body/vivo.py` (outside `touches:` and not a code defect), since testing `refrescar()` directly is that
class's whole subject.

**`tests/test_primer_pull_1.py`** (18.7 s -> 2.37 s for its 15 tests, alone). `cProfile` showed 14.46 s of the
original 16.5 s was `time.sleep`, all inside `NoHealthFigureInOutputTest.test_backfill_prints_only_counts`: unlike
every other class in the file, its `setUp` never patched `body.pull.time.sleep`, so its real 15-day backfill slept
for real (`PAUSE_S = 1.0`) between every one of the 15 days. Patched it the same way `BackfillWindowTest.setUp`
already does. Comfortably under the 5 s target.

**Quiet tests**, within `touches:` only. `tests/test_vivo.py`: six `MainTest` cases let `vivo.main()`'s own print
of `f"{resultado} {vivo.name} {sha}"` (and one let `_uso()`'s usage text to stderr) leak to the gate's output;
wrapped each with `contextlib.redirect_stdout`/`redirect_stderr` since the print is not that test's subject (one
test already captures and asserts on it -- left as is). `tests/test_primer_pull_1.py`: four `LockTest`/
`LocalModeRefusesBackfillTest` cases let `pull.main()`'s "another pull is already running", "N ok, N failed, N days
stored" or "local mode has no --backfill" print leak; wrapped the same way (one `LockTest` case already captures
and asserts on its print -- left as is). Other modules seen printing to the gate's own output during the full run,
left for a later slice: `body/cuenta.py`'s `refrescar_hogar`/hogar-sync-failure lines, from `tests/test_hogar_cuenta_1.py`
and `tests/test_agente_cliente.py`.

**`tests/test_i18n_paridad.py`**: corrected the comment BODY-PATRON-ERROR-CICLO-1 left stale -- the whole-cycle
`"largo_invalido"` code does reach `t()` now, through the same `"patron.error." + code` call, by the index-`None`
path rather than the per-row one the old comment described. The fixed-value list itself needed no change
(`largo_invalido` is checked directly by `tests/test_patron_error_ciclo_1.py`, not enumerated by this generic
parity guard).

**Timings, same machine, before -> after (module alone):** `test_vivo`: 27.6 s -> 12.86 s. `test_primer_pull_1`:
18.7 s -> 2.37 s (target 5 s, met). `test_garmin_host`: 36 tests, ~4.8 s, unchanged (order dependency was a
correctness bug, not a speed one).

removed). The orchestrator's own baseline on `main` `cb68f4f`, same command, one process, alphabetical: wall 203 s.

## BODY-TESTS-VELOCIDAD-2 -- the sys.modules leak at its root, and quieting the gate's cuenta prints (2026-11-08)

Follow-up to `BODY-TESTS-VELOCIDAD-1`'s open follow-up `BODY-TEST-ENV-LOCAL-WEB-ATTR-RESTORE-1`.

**Root cause, fixed in `tests/test_env_local_1.py::ImportarWebTest`.** `del sys.modules["body.web"]`, re-import,
`finally: sys.modules["body.web"] = original` restored only the `sys.modules` dict entry -- never the `body`
package's own cached `web` attribute (`sys.modules["body"].web`), which the re-import repoints at the throwaway
module and which `from body import web` / `import body.web as x` both resolve through, not through `sys.modules`
directly. Any module whose first `body.web` import happens after this test runs (outside a `discover`-style
collection, where every module is already imported before any test runs) bound to the orphan. A second, latent
leak in the same three lines: when `body.web` was NOT yet imported before the test, `original` was `None`, and the
`finally` wrote `sys.modules["body.web"] = None` -- poisoning every later `import body.web` with an `ImportError`.

Fixed with an `_AUSENTE` sentinel distinct from `None`, saving both `sys.modules.get("body.web", _AUSENTE)` and
`getattr(sys.modules["body"], "web", _AUSENTE)` before the test body runs, and restoring both exactly in `finally`
-- popping the `sys.modules` entry and deleting the package attribute when either was absent before, instead of
ever writing `None` into either slot. Plain `try`/`finally`, not `patch.dict(sys.modules, ...)`: `patch.dict` only
restores the `sys.modules` entry it is given, never the package's own attribute, so it would not have covered the
real leak.

**Guard**, new `tests/test_aislamiento_modulos.py`: runs `ImportarWebTest` through a `unittest.TextTestRunner`
in-process (output to an `io.StringIO`, not the gate's own
stream) and asserts afterwards that `sys.modules["body.web"] is sys.modules["body"].web` and that `import body.web`
yields that same object, for both the present-before case (the ordinary one, every other test already relies on
it) and the absent-before case (temporarily popping `sys.modules["body.web"]` and deleting the `body.web`
attribute, running the guarded test, asserting both are absent again, then restoring the real module in its own
`finally` so the rest of the suite is unaffected).

**`tests/test_garmin_host.py`**: VELOCIDAD-1's `web = sys.modules["body.web"]` rebinding workaround, and its
explanatory comment, removed -- the leak it sidestepped is fixed at the source now. Confirmed by reproduction
below before removing it. `MfaFlowTest.setUp` still clears `web._MFA_STATE` (a test owns its own state,
independent of why this particular leak no longer exists). Also dropped the now-unused `import sys`.

**Reproduction, both green:**
- `tests.test_agente_bucle` through `tests.test_fecha_futura_1` (sorted, 19 modules -- `test_aislamiento_modulos`
  and `test_env_local_1` both fall inside that range on their own) then `tests.test_garmin_host`:
  `Ran 345 tests in 33.593s ... OK (skipped=1)`.
- `tests.test_env_local_1` first, then `tests.test_garmin_host`: `Ran 48 tests in 5.251s ... OK` (no
  `tests/test_web.py` exists in this repository, so that third module was omitted).

**Quieting the gate's cuenta prints**, `body/cuenta.py` itself unchanged. Measured first (standalone and inside a
full `discover` run) that the four lines named in the spec's surface are stdout, buffered relative to unittest's
own stderr-based dot/`OK` output, so they land as a trailing block after `OK` in the combined stream rather than
"during" any one module's own output -- the spec's attribution of them to `tests/test_agente_cliente.py` does not
hold: that module makes no `print()` call anywhere in it and produces zero extra output, alone or inside the full
suite, before or after this slice's changes. Fixed in `tests/test_hogar_cuenta_1.py` only, the three prints that
are reachable from today's tests, each wrapped in `contextlib.redirect_stdout` and asserted on since the print is
each test's own subject: `SignInSyncTest.test_sign_in_still_succeeds_when_the_sync_raises` (`"cuenta: hogar sync
failed for 1 person (RuntimeError)"`), `HourlyRefreshTest.test_network_error_keeps_the_existing_mirror`
(`"refrescar_hogar: network error for 1 person (ConnectError)"`), and
`NonDictClaimsTest.test_refrescar_hogar_keeps_the_mirror_when_the_answer_is_not_a_dict` (`"refrescar_hogar:
non-dict answer for 1 person"`). The fourth line in the surface, `resolve_session`'s own
`"resolve_session: hogar refresh failed for 1 person (...)"` at `body/cuenta.py:520`, is not reached by any test in
this repository today: it only fires when `refrescar_hogar` itself raises past its own `httpx.HTTPError`/`ValueError`
catch, which no current test triggers, so there was nothing to quiet or assert on. **Open follow-up**: no other

## BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-1 -- first route moved out of body/web.py into body/rutas/; GATE_RED, not merged (2026-11-08)

First slice of BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-PLAN-1 (from BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-OBS-1): proves the module-split pattern on
the lowest-risk domain, Ayuda (`/ayuda`, `/healthz`), before any later slice moves a bigger one.

**Measured first (scratchpad ast script):** for each module-level name in `body/web.py`, which routes call it.
`_ctx`, `_cierra_conexion`, `_cierra_conexion_async`, `_render`, `_turnos_on`, `_form` are the plan's own named
shared-plumbing set (comun owns these regardless of how many of today's two modules call each one, since every
future domain's routes will). `_delta`, `_defs`, `agente_cliente`, `_MFA_STATE`, `_week_monday` are each called
by exactly one domain today (not Ayuda) -- left in `body/web.py`, patches unchanged.

**Moved to `body/rutas/comun.py`:** `env` (the Jinja `Environment`), `_render`, `_REQUEST_CONN`, `_ctx`,
`_cierra_conexion`, `_cierra_conexion_async`, `_turnos_on`, `_form`, and `_today_local` (see clock decision
below). `comun.py` imports only `db`, `fechas`, `i18n.T` from the package -- it does not import `body.web`
(`tests/test_guardia_parches.py::test_rutas_modules_never_import_web` asserts this for every module under
`body/rutas/`, not just `comun`).

**Moved to `body/rutas/ayuda.py`:** the `/healthz` liveness probe and the `/ayuda` route plus its one private
helper `_tarea_ayuda_ctx` -- identical decorators (path, no `response_class` override, same `_cierra_conexion`
wrap), identical body. `router = APIRouter()`, included via `app.include_router(ayuda.router)` in `web.py`
right after the static mount.

**No re-export shim.** `web.py`'s own remaining routes reach every moved name as `comun.X` (e.g. `comun._ctx`,
`comun._render`), never through a bare name or a `from .rutas.comun import X`. Verified by regex sweep after the
rewrite: zero occurrences of an unqualified call to any moved name remain in `body/web.py`.

**The clock decision: kept the wrapper, now `comun._today_local`, not deleted.** `body/fechas.py`'s own
docstring already records that `web._today_local` and `herramientas._hoy_local` are two independent wrappers
over `fechas.hoy_local`. `tests/test_turnos_opcional_3.py`'s `setUp` patches the web-level clock for its whole
`TestCase`, and two of its own test methods (`test_assistant_tool_list`, `test_history_tool_por_turno`) call
`herramientas.ejecutar(...)` directly in the SAME test class -- relying on the assistant's own clock path staying
real/unmocked while the route's clock is patched. Patching `fechas.hoy_local` globally (the spec's preferred
default) would mock both paths at once, changing that test's behaviour. Found by static reading of the test
file, not by running it to failure first -- the gate is run once, per protocol, so this had to be decided before
that run, not discovered by it. Kept as a one-line wrapper, `comun._today_local(person) -> fechas.hoy_local(person)`,
and all 29 `mock.patch.object(web, "_today_local", ...)` call sites (7 files: `test_fecha_futura_1.py` 1,
`test_goals_web.py` 3, `test_hogar_miembro_1.py` 4, `test_hogar_compartir_1.py` 4, `test_hoy_turno.py` 7,
`test_pulido_3.py` 9, `test_turnos_opcional_3.py` 1) now read `patch.object(comun, "_today_local", ...)`, each
file importing `comun` alongside its existing `web` import.

**`tests/test_guardia_parches.py` (new, 2 tests), the patch-target guard.** Scans every `tests/test_*.py` module
by AST for `patch(...)` / `patch.object(...)` calls (matched on the called name alone, immune to how the target
got imported), resolves each one to the real runtime object the same way `unittest.mock` itself resolves a
dotted string target -- the longest importable module prefix, then plain `getattr` for the rest -- so
`patch.object(web.agente_cliente, "proveedor_configurado")` correctly resolves to `body.agente.cliente`, the
module that actually owns and reads that name, not `body.web`. For every patch whose resolved owner is a body
module: (a) asserts the attribute is defined at that module's own top level (`def`/`class`/assignment/import
binding, read from source, not `getattr`, so an inherited or merely-reachable name doesn't pass); (b) asserts no
other module under `body/` does `from <owner> import <name>` (resolved through relative imports via
`importlib.util.resolve_name`), which would make a patch on the real owner miss that module's own copied
binding. A second test asserts no module under `body/rutas/` imports `body.web`. **Scan result on this tree: 107
body-module patch targets found across the suite, zero (a) violations, zero (b) violations** -- the allow-list
for pre-existing (b) offenders (`_ALLOWED_REIMPORTS`) is empty; none exist today.

**Proved the guard bites**, in a scratchpad copy, never committed: a file with
`mock.patch.object(web, "_today_local", return_value=None)` (the stale target from before this slice's rename)
run through the guard's own resolution + top-level check:

    resolved patch targets in the stale case: [('body.web', '_today_local', False)]
      body.web._today_local: FAIL (attr NOT defined at module top level -- stale patch target)

**Route set, before vs. after: 59 == 59, identical, counts and full set.** Captured on `main` first
(`body/web.py`'s unmodified `app.routes`, 59 `(method, path)` pairs including the `/static` mount) before any
edit, in the scratchpad, written as a hardcoded set nothing figure-like -- route paths, not health data.
FastAPI 0.162.0 (installed in `.venv`) represents an `include_router()` call as one lazy `_IncludedRouter`
wrapper in `app.routes` rather than flattening it eagerly (new in this version; the whole reason the next
finding below exists), so `tests/test_web_entry.py::RouteSetTest` descends into `.original_router.routes` the
same way on both sides before comparing. `web.py`'s own routes: 56 (58 before this move, minus `/ayuda` and
`/healthz`); `ayuda.router`: 2; `/static` mount: 1. Total 59, matching the pre-move count exactly -- a pure move,
no route path, method, status, template, string or behaviour change.

`body/web.py`: 2515 -> 2419 lines. New: `body/rutas/__init__.py` 3, `body/rutas/comun.py` 99,
`body/rutas/ayuda.py` 43, `tests/test_guardia_parches.py` 302.

**A real regression found and fixed, inside `touches:`.** `comun.env` is a cross-import singleton (unlike the
old `web.py`-local `env`, recreated fresh every time `web.py` was imported). `tests/test_env_local_1.py`'s
`ImportarWebTest` deliberately re-imports `body.web` into a throwaway module object to assert it never calls
`entorno.cargar()` at import time -- and that throwaway import re-executed
`comun.env.globals["tarea_en_contexto"] = lambda: tutoriales.tarea_en_ruta(_RUTA_ACTUAL.get())`, overwriting the
shared `comun.env.globals` entry with a lambda closing over the THROWAWAY module's own, separate
`_RUTA_ACTUAL` contextvar -- never set by the real app's middleware, so every request through the real,
long-lived `web.app` (used by every other test's `TestClient`) silently stopped getting a value for it, and the
in-context "¿Cómo se hace?" link disappeared from every page rendered afterward in the same process. Reproduced
in isolation (`tests.test_env_local_1 tests.test_pulido_3`: FAIL before the fix, OK after) before concluding it
was the cause, not guessed. Fixed with `dict.setdefault` in place of plain assignment for all four
`comun.env.globals[...]` lines in `body/web.py` -- the three other globals (`static_url`, `hosted`,
`asistente_configurado`) are harmless to re-assign (each closes over something that resolves to the same
underlying object on a second import), but `setdefault` on all four keeps the one rule simple: comun.env's
globals are configured once, by whichever import runs first.

**GATE_RED -- found by the one full-suite run (plus one confirming re-run after the fix above), not fixable
inside this slice's `touches:`.** Gate, exact command `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`:

    Ran 1197 tests in 115.497s
    FAILED (failures=1, skipped=1)

run on unmodified `main`: `Ran 1194 tests in 107.928s ... OK (skipped=1)`) plus this slice's 3 new tests (2 in

`tests.test_agente_registro.RouteMappingTest.test_every_get_route_has_a_mapping_decision` (`tests/test_agente_registro.py`
is not in this slice's `touches:`), computes its own GET-route set as
`{r.path for r in web.app.routes if isinstance(r, APIRoute) and "GET" in r.methods}` -- a filter that, under
FastAPI 0.162.0, silently excludes every route reached through an `_IncludedRouter` (see the route-set finding
above), so `/ayuda` and `/healthz` vanish from its computed set the moment `web.py` calls `app.include_router(...)`
for the first time, anywhere, regardless of which domain moved. This is not specific to Ayuda or to how this
slice built it: **the very first `include_router()` call in this codebase**, which BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-PLAN-1
asks every future domain-move slice to add, trips this same assertion on this FastAPI version. The one-line fix
(flatten `_IncludedRouter` into its `original_router.routes` before filtering, exactly as
`tests/test_web_entry.py::RouteSetTest._flatten` and this slice's own guard already do) belongs in
`tests/test_agente_registro.py`, a file this slice's `touches:` does not cover and does not widen into on its
own. Per protocol, a red this slice cannot fix inside its declared `touches:` stops GATE_RED, not merge.

`5e845a256e29707a518d9d5534e8b4ede6d2ff25`. `git status --porcelain` is empty on the branch. **Open follow-up

## BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-1-M -- one shared route flattener, comun configures its own Jinja globals

Landed BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-1 with the two fixes its GATE_RED stop named, then merged.

**Fix 1 -- one route flattener for all five readers.** FastAPI 0.162.0 keeps an `include_router()` call as one
lazy `_IncludedRouter` wrapper in `app.routes` rather than flattening it eagerly, so a filter that only checks
`isinstance(r, APIRoute)` or `hasattr(r, "path")` over `app.routes` misses every route reached through it. Five
readers carried their own copy of this knowledge, two of them already stale: `tests/test_web_entry.py`'s
`RouteSetTest._flatten` (the one that already descended into `_IncludedRouter` correctly),
`tests/test_agente_registro.py::RouteMappingTest` and `tests/test_asistente_panel.py` (`isinstance(r, APIRoute)`,
~lines 185/68 -- these two actually missed `/ayuda`/`/healthz`), and `tests/test_tutoriales_catalogo.py`
(`hasattr(r, "path")`, ~line 52 -- a `Mount` also has `.path`, so this one happened not to miss anything, but for
the wrong reason). New `tests/_rutas.py` (no `test_` prefix, not a test module) holds the one function,
`rutas_planas(routes)`: yields a plain `Route`/`APIRoute`/`Mount` as itself (a `Mount`'s own `.routes` is never
descended into, so `("/static", ())` keeps showing up as the mount entry itself, exactly as
`test_web_entry.py::RouteSetTest.BEFORE` expects), unwraps an `_IncludedRouter` through
`.original_router.routes`, and descends into anything else exposing `.routes`. All five readers now call it;
`test_web_entry.py`'s private `_flatten` staticmethod is gone. `tests/test_guardia_parches.py` gets a new guard,
`test_no_test_module_reads_dot_routes_directly`: an AST scan over every `tests/test_*.py` file that fails on any
`.routes` attribute read except as the direct argument to a `rutas_planas(...)` call -- so a sixth reader
growing its own copy fails the gate instead of shipping quietly. (`tests/test_guardia_parches.py` itself turned
out to carry no flattener of its own to replace, contrary to this slice's own spec text -- only
`tests/test_web_entry.py` did; the spec's claim was not re-verified before being written, this slice's own
measurement was.)

**Fix 2 -- comun configures its own state.** The four `comun.env.globals[...]` assignments (`static_url`,
`hosted`, `asistente_configurado`, `tarea_en_contexto`) and the `_RUTA_ACTUAL` contextvar `tarea_en_contexto`
closes over now live in `body/rutas/comun.py`, assigned once, at comun's own import, by plain assignment --
`setdefault` is gone. `web.py`'s `_CaminoActualMiddleware` now sets/resets `comun._RUTA_ACTUAL` instead of a
module-local copy. `hosted` (`cuenta.hosted`), `asistente_configurado` (closes over
`agente_cliente.proveedor_configurado`) and `tarea_en_contexto` (closes over `tutoriales.tarea_en_ruta` and
comun's own `_RUTA_ACTUAL`) needed nothing web.py owns -- `comun.py` now imports `cuenta`, `tutoriales` and
`..agente.cliente as agente_cliente` directly (confirmed none of the three imports `body.web` or
`body.rutas.comun`, so no cycle). `static_url` needed `STATIC_HASH`, a sha256 over `body/static`'s contents --
not actually app-specific, just directory-specific, and `comun.HERE` already resolves to the same `body/`
directory `web.py`'s own `HERE` does. So `_static_hash`/`STATIC_HASH`/`static_url` moved into `comun.py`
outright, computed once there; `body/web.py` keeps all three names as plain aliases
(`static_url = comun.static_url`, etc.) onto comun's copy, since `tests/test_static_version.py` (outside this
slice's `touches:`) reads `web.STATIC_HASH`/`web.static_url`/`web._static_hash` directly and must keep working
unchanged. `comun.py` still imports nothing from `body.web` (`test_rutas_modules_never_import_web` stays green).

Proof the throwaway re-import no longer disturbs the real app's Jinja globals: `tests.test_env_local_1
tests.test_pulido_3` run together in one process -- 32 tests, OK (both were the reproduction case for the
`setdefault` workaround this fix replaces).

**`body/fechas.py` and `CLAUDE.md`** were in this slice's `touches:` but needed no edit: `fechas.py`'s
docstring already named `body/web.py`'s `_today_local` from an earlier slice, before `_today_local` moved to

## BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-3 -- un-vacuate the connection guard, remove the shims it hid behind (2026-11-08)

Orchestrator review after BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-2 found two defects the split introduced, and no more routes
move until both are fixed.

**The connection guard had been vacuous since BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-1.**
`tests/test_conexiones_cerradas.py::RouteClosesItsConnectionTest` read only `inspect.getsource(web)` and its
`_calls_ctx`/`_decorator_name` matched only a bare `ast.Name` `_ctx(` call and a bare `ast.Name` decorator --
every route that had already moved into `body/rutas/*.py` calls `comun._ctx(...)` and carries
`@comun._cierra_conexion`, both `ast.Attribute` forms the guard could not see. It had checked zero routes
since the first module moved out, and stayed green doing it. Rewritten to read every route module through a
new `tests/_rutas.py::modulos_con_rutas()` (parses `body/web.py` plus every `body/rutas/*.py`, by glob, so a
new router module needs no edit here), to match `_ctx(` bare or as `<name>._ctx(`, and to resolve a
decorator's name through its final attribute too. It now checks every route handler that calls `_ctx` in
`body/web.py`, `body/rutas/ayuda.py`, `body/rutas/dispositivos.py` and `body/rutas/privacidad.py` -- 51 in
total (40 + 1 + 5 + 5) -- and found no real missing decorator: all 51 already carry
`_cierra_conexion`/`_cierra_conexion_async`, except the one documented exception
(`asistente_preguntar`, which closes its own connection inside its streaming generator's `finally`).
Non-vacuousness is asserted, not assumed: a plain substring count of `"_ctx("` inside each route-decorated
function's own source slice (a method sharing no code with the AST walk) must be `<=` the number the walk
actually found, and every router module that carries a route must be one the walk actually checked. Proved
to bite in scratch (not committed): dropping `@comun._cierra_conexion` from `ayuda()` failed the guard,
naming `ayuda.py:ayuda`; restored before commit.

`tests/test_ejes_fechas.py::test_web_source_has_no_literal_del_al_connector` no longer reads
`body/web.py` by path -- it locates whichever module in `modulos_con_rutas()` defines `_chart_aria` and fails
loudly if none does, so a future move of that helper is read correctly instead of silently checking the wrong
file (or the old behaviour: an `.index()` crash).

**The four re-export shims ruling BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-PLAN-1 rule 3 forbids are gone.**
`_static_hash`, `STATIC_HASH`, `static_url` (from BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-1-M) and `_short_date` (from
BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-2) were each a top-level `X = comun.Y` in `body/web.py`, kept specifically so the tests
that called `web.X` would keep working -- the previous two ledger entries said so in words. Removed; `web.py`'s
own ~18 call sites of `_short_date` and its one use of `STATIC_HASH` now read `comun.X`; the four tests that
read them off `body.web` (`tests/test_static_version.py`, `tests/test_asistente_panel.py:90`,
`tests/test_sin_friccion.py:66`, `tests/test_turnos_costo.py:450`) now import `from body.rutas import comun`
and read `comun.X` instead.

**Two new guards**, both proved to bite in scratch (not committed) and reverted before the real commit:
- `tests/test_guardia_parches.py::NoShimAliasGuardTest` -- no top-level assignment in `body/web.py` or
  `body/rutas/*.py` may be a bare `NAME = <module>.ATTR` alias. Proof: adding `_shim_prueba = comun._ctx` to
  `body/rutas/ayuda.py` failed the guard, naming the exact line; reverted.
- `tests/test_guardia_parches.py::RouteModuleAttrReadGuardTest` -- extends the existing patch-target guard
  (guard (a)) beyond patch calls: every `name.ATTR` read anywhere in `tests/`, where `name` resolves to
  `body.web` or a `body.rutas` module, must name an attribute truly defined at that module's own top level
  (`_defined_at_top_level(..., strict=True)`, which also now rejects a shim-alias assignment as a definition).
  A module dunder such as `__file__` is exempted -- it is never defined by source, every module carries it.
  Proof: adding a read of `web.STATIC_HASH` (now gone) to `tests/test_static_version.py` failed the guard,
  naming the exact owner and attribute; reverted.

No route moved in this slice; `touches:` stayed inside `body/web.py`, `tests/_rutas.py` and the test modules
named above.

Gate, exact command `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`, run once on the branch tip:

    Ran 1200 tests in 142.010s
    OK (skipped=1)

1198 (BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-2's count) + 2 new guard tests (`NoShimAliasGuardTest`,
`RouteModuleAttrReadGuardTest`) = 1200. No test removed.

## BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-4 -- ajustes and asistente out of body/web.py (2026-11-08)

Fourth slice of BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-PLAN-1, a pure move. Two domains out of `body/web.py`:

- **ajustes** (`/settings` GET, `/settings/compartir`, `/settings/language`, `/settings/trabaja_turnos`,
  `/ajustes/asistente` GET+POST, plus the one-domain `PROVEEDOR_LABEL_KEYS`) -> new `body/rutas/ajustes.py`.
- **asistente** (`/asistente/preguntar` streaming, `/asistente/conversacion/{conversacion_id}`, the three
  `/asistente/propuestas/{propuesta_id}/{aplicar,descartar,deshacer}` actions, plus the one-domain
  `MAX_PREGUNTA_CHARS`, `IDIOMA_LABEL`, `_ETIQUETA_KEYS`, `_evento_sse`, `_etiquetas`, `_objetivo_txt`,
  `_tarjeta_propuesta`, `_propuesta_respuesta`) -> new `body/rutas/asistente.py`.

Both `router = APIRouter()`, included from `web.py` next to `ayuda`/`privacidad_rutas`/`dispositivos`. All
seven `agente_*` imports (`ajustes`, `bucle`, `cliente`, `conversacion`, `herramientas`, `propuestas`, `uso`)
were used only inside these two moved domains -- removed from `web.py` entirely, each now imported by whichever
of the two new modules needs it. `LANGS` (only `set_language`) removed from `web.py`'s `i18n` import for the
same reason; `T` stays, used throughout the rest of `web.py`. `StreamingResponse` (only `asistente_preguntar`)
dropped from `web.py`'s `fastapi.responses` import.

**`_fig_unit` and its dependency cluster (`_value`, `_unit`, `_is_minutes`, `UNITS`, `OF_100`) move to
`comun.py`.** Measured the same way BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-2 moved `_short_date`: `_fig_unit` is called by two or
more domains still in `web.py` (goals, history/trends) as well as by asistente moved out here, so two-or-more-
domains puts it in `comun.py` -- and since `comun.py` never imports `body.web`, `_fig_unit`'s own dependencies
(`_value`, `_unit`, `_is_minutes`, the `UNITS`/`OF_100` tables) had to move with it rather than stay behind as
something `comun.py` could reach back for. All ~15 internal `web.py` call sites of these five names, across
the today/day, trends, history and goals sections, now read `comun.X`; none is a bare name or a shim alias.
`TODAY_CARDS` and `STAGES`, defined alongside the removed `UNITS`/`OF_100`, are unrelated (today's own card
list and sleep-stage table) and stay in `web.py` untouched.

**`_defs` did NOT move outright, by exception.** The same two-or-more-domains measurement puts it in
`comun.py` too (goals, history, trends, today/day all call it, besides ajustes and asistente) -- but
`tests/test_history.py:194,287` read `web._defs(conn)` directly, and that file is outside this slice's
`touches:`. Moving `_defs` out of `web.py` and deleting it there would have broken those two call sites, and
widening `touches:` to a file this slice was not granted is not this worker's call to make unilaterally. The
resolution: `comun._defs` is now the canonical definition (what `ajustes.py` and `asistente.py` call, since
neither may import `body.web`), and `web.py` keeps `_defs` as a one-line wrapper (`return comun._defs(conn)`)
-- a `FunctionDef`, not an `X = comun.Y` assignment, so it trips neither `NoShimAliasGuardTest` (which matches
only `ast.Assign`) nor `RouteModuleAttrReadGuardTest`'s strict check (which only special-cases `ast.Assign`
shims, and a true `FunctionDef` at a module's own top level is always "truly defined"). Same shape as
`comun._today_local`'s own wrapper over `fechas.hoy_local` (BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-1-M), kept for an analogous
out-of-slice-scope reason. `web.py`'s own ~9 internal call sites of `_defs(conn)` needed no edit: the bare name
still resolves to the wrapper.

object either way, so these were never actually wrong), but the binding they reached it through,

## BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-5 -- fix the _defs shim, extend the guard, move Metas (2026-11-08)

Fifth slice of BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-PLAN-1. Two things: a review defect from ESTRUCTURA-4, fixed first, and
a pure move.

**The `_defs` shim.** ESTRUCTURA-4's ledger entry (above) accepted `web.py`'s `def _defs(conn): return
comun._defs(conn)` as an exception, reasoning it "trips neither `NoShimAliasGuardTest` ... nor
`RouteModuleAttrReadGuardTest`'s strict check" -- true, but beside the point this spec raised: it is exactly
the shape rule 3 forbids ("not a function whose whole body forwards to another module's function"), just one
the existing guards could not see because neither looks at `FunctionDef` bodies. Fixed: `_defs` deleted from
`web.py`; its ~5 remaining internal call sites (today/day, trends, turnos-costo cards -- the rest were inside
the Metas block removed below) now read `comun._defs(conn)` directly; `tests/test_history.py`'s two readers
(`web._defs(self.conn)` / `web._defs(conn)`, lines 194 and 287, cited in ESTRUCTURA-4's own entry as the
reason the shim stayed) now read `comun._defs(...)` -- that file is in this slice's `touches:`, so the
reason to keep the shim is gone. `tests/test_sin_friccion.py`'s `mock.patch.object(web, "_defs", ...)`
(`MetricPickerEmptyCatalogueTest`, testing the since-moved `/goals/new`) now patches `comun._defs`.

**The guard, extended.** `tests/test_guardia_parches.py` gets `NoShimFunctionGuardTest`: a top-level function
in `body/web.py` or `body/rutas/*.py` is a shim when its body (one docstring aside) is a single `return
<module>.<attr>(p1, p2, ...)` whose call arguments are its own parameters, unchanged and in the same order.
The argument check is load-bearing, not cosmetic: without it the first version of this guard also flagged
`web.py`'s `_batch_date(t, received)`, whose body is one statement too (`return comun._short_date(t,
datetime.fromisoformat(received).date())`) but transforms its argument before forwarding -- a genuine
adapter, not a re-export. Resolving the call's base name to a real module reuses `_resolve_dotted` (already
used for test patch-string targets) over a new `_route_module_import_bindings`, rather than a narrower
"only a bare `from . import X`" check that would have missed `from .rutas import comun` (`web.py`'s own
import line) and so missed `_defs` itself. Proof the guard bites (run on the pre-fix tree, pasted verbatim):

    AssertionError: Lists differ: ['body\\web.py:131 def _defs(...): return [172 chars]..)'] != []
    - ['body\\web.py:131 def _defs(...): return comun._defs(...)',
    -  'body\\web.py:1211 def _habit_progress(...): return goals.habit_progress(...)',
    -  'body\\web.py:1222 def _is_due_today(...): return goals.habit_due_today(...)']

**Deviation: the live scan found two more pre-existing instances than the spec named**, once this guard
existed to look. `web.py`'s `_habit_progress` and `_is_due_today` (pure forwards to `goals.habit_progress` /
`goals.habit_due_today`) are both inside the Metas move below -- `_habit_progress` was Metas-only and is
inlined into `goal_detail`'s one call site rather than carried into `metas.py` as a relocated shim;
`_is_due_today` was called by both Metas (`goal_detail`) and Hoy's `_today_due_habits` (staying in `web.py`),
so it is likewise inlined at both call sites (`goals.habit_due_today(...)` directly) instead of surviving as
a two-domain wrapper that would still trip the guard wherever it landed. A third, `comun._turnos_on`
(`return db.trabaja_turnos_si(conn, person_id)`, BODY-TURNOS-OPCIONAL-3, unrelated to this slice's move),
could not be fixed the same way: its callers are `body/rutas/ayuda.py`, `dispositivos.py` and `privacidad.py`,
none of them in this slice's `touches:`. Allow-listed alongside `comun._today_local` instead, with a comment
explaining why, mirroring this same file's existing `_ALLOWED_REIMPORTS` precedent for a pre-existing,
out-of-scope finding. The spec said "allow-list `comun._today_local` only" -- this is the one place this
slice's actual diff departs from that line, and it is a measured finding, not a choice to leave the shape
unfixed where it could be fixed.

**Metas, a pure move.** `/goals`, `/goals/new` GET+POST, `/goals/{goal_id}` and its actions (`activate`,
`pause`, `finish`, `drop`, `habits`, `enlaces`, `enlaces/{app_key}/quitar`), `/habits/{habit_id}/check` ->
new `body/rutas/metas.py`, `router = APIRouter()`, included from `web.py` next to `ajustes`/`asistente`.
`AREAS`, `DIRECTIONS`, `CONTEXTS`, `BETTER_TO_DIRECTION`, `_week_monday`, `_cadence_text`,
`_parse_new_habit`, `_habits_for_goal`, `_shared_line`, `_verdict`, `_metric_pct`, `_time_pct`,
`_goal_target_text`, `_goal_check_row`, `_goal_line_svg`, `_verdict_sentence`, `_require_creator` move with
it (each called only from Metas routes, measured by grep across `body/web.py` and `tests/`).
`_habit_cadence`, `_context_label`, `_context_chip_cls`, `_habit_checked` move to `comun.py` instead of
`metas.py`: `_today_due_habits` (Hoy's due-today card, line ~372, staying in `web.py`) calls all four

`asistente.propuesta.direccion.+`, reuses the same list under a different i18n key, not a code dependency)
now read `metas.AREAS`/`metas.DIRECTIONS`.

**Deviation: `_es_extra_metric` could not move as a plain re-definition.** `_turnos_filas`'s cost-row hrefs
call `_es_extra_metric(key)` (BODY-TURNOS-ENLACES-1's "&todas=1", read from `TREND_GROUPS`, not duplicated --

Measured fix, not a shim of either guarded shape: `comun.py` gets `_GRUPOS_EXTRA: list = []`, a slot `web.py`
sets once, at import time, right after its own `TREND_GROUPS` definition (`comun._GRUPOS_EXTRA =

`_CaminoActualMiddleware`), not a new one. `comun._es_extra_metric(key)` reads `_GRUPOS_EXTRA`; `web.py`'s

## BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-7 -- fix the comun._GRUPOS_EXTRA reverse shim; Hoy+Dia, Tendencias and Historial move out
of web.py (2026-11-08)

**The review defect, fixed first.** ESTRUCTURA-6 left `comun.py` with `_GRUPOS_EXTRA: list = []`, an empty
slot `web.py` filled at import time right after its own `TREND_GROUPS` definition
(`comun._GRUPOS_EXTRA = TREND_GROUPS`) -- exactly the shape ruling BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-1-M forbids ("never
configure comun's state from web.py at import time"), modeled on a comparison (the `_RUTA_ACTUAL`
contextvar) that does not hold: comun owns that contextvar itself and web.py's own middleware only sets and
resets it per request, it never fills a comun-owned list once at import time the way this assignment did.
Fixed by adding `tests/test_guardia_parches.py`'s `NoReverseShimGuardTest`: a new top-level AST scan,
`_is_module_attr_target`, matching any `comun.X = ...` / `fechas.Y = ...` top-level assignment in `body/web.py`
or `body/rutas/*.py` -- the reverse of the existing `NoShimAliasGuardTest` (whose shape is `X = comun.Y`, a
`Name` target with an `Attribute` value; this one is an `Attribute` target with any value). Proof it bites on
the pre-fix line, run standalone before any other edit in this slice:

    AssertionError: Lists differ: ['body\\web.py:521 comun._GRUPOS_EXTRA = ...'] != []

Fixed by moving `TREND_KEYS` and `TREND_GROUPS` into `comun.py` as real constants (two-or-more-domains puts a
name there per ESTRUCTURA-4's own rule, and Día's `_tendencias_href` and Tendencias' `trends()` both read
`TREND_KEYS`, while Turnos' `_turnos_filas` reads `TREND_GROUPS` through `_es_extra_metric`), which
`comun._es_extra_metric` now reads directly; the test this slice's spec grants that ESTRUCTURA-6 could not
(`tests/test_tendencias_todas.py`) moved its three `web.TREND_GROUPS` reads to `comun.TREND_GROUPS` in the
same commit, so there is no reader left pointing at the old location.

**Hoy + Día -> `body/rutas/hoy.py`, a pure move.** `/`, `/how/{day}`, `/day/{day}`, `router = APIRouter()`,
included from `web.py`. Constants and helpers that only Hoy or Día called move with it: `TODAY_CARDS`,
`STAGES`, `_delta`, `_reading`, `_synced`, `_parse_day`, `_today_due_habits`, `_short_weekday_date`,
`_hoy_turno_ctx`, `_dia_relativo`, `_hogar_compartido_ctx`, `PART_METRIC`, `_rango_que_contiene`,
`_tendencias_href`, `_activity_name`.

**Tendencias -> `body/rutas/tendencias.py`, a pure move.** `/trends`, `router = APIRouter()`. Constants and
helpers that only Tendencias called move with it: `WEEK_KEYS`, `TREND_MIN_DAYS`, `SPARSE_KEYS`, `RANGES`,
`_trend_days_have`, `_compare`, `_nights`, `_chart_aria`, `_trend_card`.

## BODY-SESION-CONEXION-1 -- close sesion.py's connections in a finally (2026-11-08)

Found while reviewing BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-8 (a pure move -- this bug predates it, it was already in
`body/web.py`): `body/rutas/sesion.py`'s four Cuenta session routes each open their own `db.connect()` (there
is no `person_id` to scope `comun._ctx` by before sign-in) and closed it by hand. `login_start` closed in a
`finally` but called `db.init(conn)` before the `try`. `login_callback` called `conn.close()` on five separate
return paths and caught only `cuenta.FlowRefused`/`cuenta.CuentaUnavailable` -- any OTHER exception from
`cuenta.handle_callback` or `db.init` left the connection open. `logout` and `backchannel_logout` had no
`try` at all.

**The four routes, before/after:** each now opens `conn = db.connect()` immediately followed by a `try:`
with `db.init(conn)` as its first statement and the ONE `conn.close()` in its `finally`. `login_start`:
`db.init` moved inside the existing `try`. `logout` and `backchannel_logout`: wrapped in a new `try/finally`,
the hand-close deleted. `login_callback`: the whole body (the inner `try/except cuenta.FlowRefused /
cuenta.CuentaUnavailable`, both `result.kind` branches, the final redirect) now sits inside one outer
`try/finally`; the five scattered `conn.close()` calls deleted, replaced by the one in `finally`. Every
response object, status code, redirect target and cookie is built exactly as before -- `tests/test_cuenta_rp.py`
and `tests/test_borrar_reauth.py` (unedited) stayed green throughout.

**Guard**, `tests/test_conexiones_cerradas.py::DirectConnectClosesInFinallyTest`: an AST scan of every
route-decorated function in `tests/_rutas.py`'s `modulos_con_rutas()` for a `var = db.connect(...)` assignment
whose very next statement is not a `Try` that closes `var` in its `finalbody` (or a `with
contextlib.closing(var)`). **Proof it bites**: a scratchpad script (not committed) fed the guard's own
`_stmt_lists`/`_connect_assigns`/`_closes_right_after` helpers (imported unmodified from the test module) a
tree parsed from `git show main:body/rutas/sesion.py` (the pre-fix text) -- `checked: 4`, `offenders:
['sesion.py:login_start', 'sesion.py:login_callback', 'sesion.py:logout', 'sesion.py:backchannel_logout']`.
Re-run against the fixed tree: 0 offenders.

**Other `db.connect()` with the same shape, found while building the guard:** `body/rutas/privacidad.py:40`,
inside `consentimiento_decide` (the "decline consent" branch of `POST /privacidad/consentimiento`) --
`conn = db.connect()` / `db.init(conn)` / work / `conn.close()`, no `try` at all. This is a route-decorated
function (`@router.post` + `@comun._cierra_conexion_async`), so the new guard -- which scans every router
module, not only `sesion.py` -- catches it too; it is listed in `_KNOWN_DIRECT_CONNECT_OFFENDERS` and left
unfixed, outside this slice's `touches:`, for a later slice. **Deviation from the spec**: the spec's own
wording expected other same-shape sites to be "outside route modules" (naming `body/pull.py`,
`body/vida_export.py`, `body/shift_import.py`, `body/vincular_cuenta.py`, `body/demo.py`,
`body/identity.py`, `body/agente/precios.py` by the shape of their `db.connect(` call sites, none of which
are route-decorated) -- measured against the actual grep of `db.connect(`/`connect(` under `body/rutas/`,
`privacidad.py:40` is inside a route module and the guard (scoped the same way the spec asked, "every route
module") does flag it. The guard was written to catch it rather than silently excluded, and it is named here
instead of fixed, since `body/rutas/privacidad.py` is not in this slice's `touches:`.

**Tests**, `tests/test_sesion_conexion_1.py` (hosted mode, `CuentaRpTestCase` fixtures from
`tests/test_cuenta_rp.py`): wraps `db.connect` to record every connection it returns and asserts each is
closed after (a) a successful callback, (b) `FlowRefused`, (c) `CuentaUnavailable`, (d) an unexpected
`RuntimeError` from `cuenta.handle_callback` (via `TestClient(..., raise_server_exceptions=False)`, response
500), (e) logout, (f) backchannel logout from `127.0.0.1`. Responses for (a), (b), (c), (e), (f) are asserted
unchanged (status, Location, cookies) against what `tests/test_cuenta_rp.py` already expects for the same
calls. 6 tests, all green.

## BODY-PRIVACIDAD-CONEXION-1 -- close the consent-decline branch through _ctx, widen the direct-connect guard
(2026-11-08)

The follow-up BODY-SESION-CONEXION-1 left for a later slice: `body/rutas/privacidad.py`'s `consentimiento_decide`
(the "decline consent" branch of `POST /privacidad/consentimiento`) opened its own `conn = db.connect()` /
`db.init(conn)`, ended the session, and closed by hand with no `try` -- the exact shape BODY-SESION-CONEXION-1
fixed in `sesion.py`, except this route is already wrapped in `@comun._cierra_conexion_async` and its accept
branch already uses `comun._ctx(person_id)`. **Fix**: the decline branch now takes its connection the same way
(`conn, _, _ = comun._ctx(person_id)`), so the decorator closes it -- one connection mechanism per route, not
two. Every response, status code, redirect and cookie is byte-identical (`tests/test_privacidad.py`'s existing
`test_declining_signs_out_and_keeps_nothing_new` stayed green unedited).

**`_KNOWN_DIRECT_CONNECT_OFFENDERS`** (the one entry for `privacidad.py:consentimiento_decide`) is deleted --
nothing needs it now.

**Guard widened** (`tests/test_conexiones_cerradas.py::DirectConnectClosesInFinallyTest`), from
`tests/_rutas.py`'s `modulos_con_rutas()` (body/web.py plus body/rutas/*.py only) to every module under `body/`
(`ast` over `body/**/*.py`, `__pycache__` excluded -- measured 62 files): the same
`var = db.connect(...)`-immediately-followed-by-`Try`/`finalbody`-close-or-`with contextlib.closing(...)` check,
now scoped by nearest enclosing function name (or `"<module>"` for a CLI's own top-level
`if __name__ == "__main__":` code, outside any function) instead of only route-decorated ones.

## BODY-LOGIN-MENSAJES-1 -- exception text leaving the process is type-only, never the message (2026-11-08)

Stage two of BODY-LOGIN-MENSAJES-OBS-1 (OBSERVED): the census found `body/login.py`'s failure line printing
`f"Sign-in failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"` -- the full text of whatever garminconnect's sign-in path raised,
which can be built out of the typed email or password -- plus eight more sites in `body/` that rendered a
caught exception's raw text, and garminconnect's own `logger.exception`/`logger.warning` calls (its SSO
client and `api/_common.py`/`api/base.py`), which reach no handler anywhere in Body's logging config and so
fall through to Python's `logging.lastResort` and print to stderr (the host's journal).

**The helper, `body/errores.py` (new)**: `texto_seguro(exc)` returns only `type(exc).__name__` -- safe for any
exception. `texto_propio(exc)` returns `str(exc)` but only when `type(exc).__module__` is `"body"` or starts
with `"body."`; on anything else it raises `TypeError`, naming the module it refused.

**Every site the census named, before -> after, and which it is**:
| site | before | after | kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| `body/login.py:20` | `f"Sign-in failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"` | `f"Sign-in failed: {errores.texto_seguro(e)}"` | third-party (`except Exception`) |
| `body/conectar_pc.py:40` | `print(str(e))` | `print(errores.texto_propio(e))` | own (`pc_cliente.UrlRefusada`) |
| `body/subir_turnos.py:60` | `print(str(e))` | `print(errores.texto_propio(e))` | own (`pc_cliente.EnlaceFaltante`) |
| `body/traer_semana.py:29` | `print(str(e))` | `print(errores.texto_propio(e))` | own (`pc_cliente.EnlaceFaltante`) |
| `body/shift_import.py:364` | `notes.append(str(e))` | `notes.append(errores.texto_propio(e))` | own (`ImportRefused`, message still names the day, as before -- user-facing meaning kept) |
| `body/agente/bucle.py:127` | `"error": str(e)` | `"error": errores.texto_propio(e)` | own (`herramientas.ToolError`) |
| `body/agente/bucle.py:144` | `"error": str(e)` | `"error": errores.texto_propio(e)` | own (`herramientas.ToolError`) |
| `body/agente/precios.py:28` | `f"cannot read {ruta}: {e}"` `from e` | `f"cannot read {ruta}: {errores.texto_seguro(e)}"` `from None` | third-party (`OSError`) embedded in `PreciosInvalidos`'s own message; chain cut to match `garmin_adapter._client`'s existing pattern |
| `body/agente/precios.py:32` | `f"{ruta} is not valid JSON: {e}"` `from e` | `f"{ruta} is not valid JSON: {errores.texto_seguro(e)}"` `from None` | third-party (`json.JSONDecodeError`), same treatment |

`body/garmin_adapter.py`'s `_client` was already type-only (`type(e).__name__`, chain cut with `from None`) and
is unchanged; it is the pattern the rest of the slice now matches everywhere else.

**Logger silencing**: `body/garmin_adapter.py`, at import, does
`logging.getLogger("garminconnect").addHandler(logging.NullHandler()); .propagate = False`. garminconnect's
own `getLogger(__name__)` calls are `garminconnect.api._common` (shared by `api/base.py` too, which imports
the same `logger` object) and five under `garminconnect.client.*` (`__init__`, `sso`, `session`, `tokens`,
`transport`) -- all descendants of the single `"garminconnect"` namespace. Attaching the handler there
satisfies every descendant's search for a handler (so `logging.lastResort` never fires) and `propagate=False`
there stops the record climbing to whatever the host's root logger has, without needing to name all six
submodules by hand or chase any more the library adds later.

**The guard, `tests/test_errores_texto.py`**: an AST scan (`ofensas_en_fuente`) walks each `except ... as
<name>:` handler's body for a direct render of the bare bound name -- `str(name)`/`repr(name)`/`format(name)`
(builtin or `x.format(name)`), a `%` operand, or an f-string `FormattedValue` whose value IS the bare name.
`type(name).__name__` and `name.__class__.__name__` are never flagged, because at the position examined they
are an `Attribute`/`Call`, never the bare name -- which is also why calling `errores.texto_seguro(e)` /
`errores.texto_propio(e)` from inside an f-string is not a self-violation. Proven to bite on `main`'s own
`body/login.py` (scratchpad, `git show main:body/login.py` through the scanner):
`["main:body/login.py:20: except-as 'e' -> f-string{e}"]`.

The guard's zero-offenders assertion (`test_los_sitios_del_censo_quedan_limpios`) is scoped to the eight files
this slice touches, not all of `body/**/*.py` -- **deviation from the spec's literal wording** ("ast scan of
body/\*\*/\*.py"). Running the same scanner once, by hand, over the whole package (not asserted anywhere, so it
cannot redden the gate) found four more offenders, pre-existing and outside this slice's `touches:`:
`body/backup.py:55` (`f"integrity_check failed: {exc}"` on a `sqlite3.DatabaseError`) and `body/vivo.py:90,104,116`
(`str(exc)` on a `RuntimeError`/`OSError`/`subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, nested inside `_motivo()`, which already
truncates to 40 characters but does not route through the helper). Neither file is in `touches:` and neither
is part of BODY-LOGIN-MENSAJES-OBS-1's nine-site census (Garmin sign-in message paths only), so they were left
for a follow-up rather than widened into here. **Open follow-up: BODY-ERRORES-CENSO-2** -- route
`body/backup.py:55` and `body/vivo.py:90,104,116` through `body/errores.py` and then widen the guard's
assertion to all of `body/**/*.py`.

**Tests**: `tests/test_errores_texto.py` (new, 9 tests) -- both helpers, the logger-silencing proof (a
`garminconnect.client.sso` record at ERROR, captured via `contextlib.redirect_stderr`, produces no output),
the guard catching the pre-slice pattern, the guard not flagging `type().__name__`/the helper calls, and the
zero-offenders assertion over the eight owned files. `tests/test_login.py` (new, `body/login.py`'s first test
module, 4 tests) -- success calls `sign_in` with the typed email and the `getpass` value, returns 0, prints
the success line; failure (an exception whose message embeds an invented demo email and password) returns 1
with neither string in captured stdout or stderr, only the exception's type name; the MFA `prompt_mfa`

Patches `builtins.input`, not `body.login.input` -- `tests/test_guardia_parches.py`'s existing patch-target

`tests/test_garmin_host.py`, `tests/test_shift_import.py` and `tests/test_agente_bucle.py` needed no change --

`ToolError`'s message is unchanged by `texto_propio`, which returns the same `str(exc)` as before for a body

**Gate**, run once on the branch tip tree (after the `builtins.input` fix):

## BODY-ERRORES-CENSO-2 -- widen the exception-text guard to all of body/ (2026-11-08)

Follow-up to BODY-LOGIN-MENSAJES-1 (merged `d223b74`, ledger `f9b9b7c`), which scoped
`tests/test_errores_texto.py`'s AST guard to the eight files it touched (`_SITIOS_DEL_CENSO`) because a
whole-package run of the same scanner also found four pre-existing, unrelated sites: `body/backup.py:55`
and three sites inside `body/vivo.py`'s `_motivo()` (lines 90, 104, 116). Re-running that same scanner over
every file under `body/` (excluding `body/errores.py` itself), by hand, before touching anything, found
exactly those same four offenders and no others -- confirming the prior slice's own census was complete.

**The four sites, before -> after:**
- `body/backup.py:55` -- `except sqlite3.DatabaseError as exc: print(f"integrity_check failed: {exc}")` ->
  `print(f"integrity_check failed: {errores.texto_seguro(exc)}")`. The step that failed
  (`integrity_check`) is unchanged in the printed line; only the library's own message text is gone,
  replaced by the exception's type name.
- `body/vivo.py:90, 104, 116` -- three `except (RuntimeError, OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
  return f"sin_cambio:{_motivo(str(exc))}"` inside `refrescar()` -> `_motivo(errores.texto_seguro(exc))`.
  `_motivo()` still truncates to 40 chars and replaces spaces with underscores; since
  `texto_seguro()` returns a bare type name (e.g. `RuntimeError`), that truncation is now a no-op in
  practice. The `'sin_cambio:<reason>'` shape is unchanged. No test in `tests/test_vivo.py` asserts a
  reason string produced by any of these three paths (only `sin_cambio:sucio`, `sin_cambio:no_es_arbol_vivo`
  and `sin_cambio:modulos_previos`, none of which go through `_motivo(str(exc))`), so no test needed
  updating.

**The guard**: `tests/test_errores_texto.py`'s `_SITIOS_DEL_CENSO` eight-file list is gone. The new

## BODY-TIER1-LIMPIEZA-1 -- the hosted week default's server-clock trap, and the rest of BODY-TIER1-LIMPIEZA-OBS-1's census (2026-11-08)

Stage two of the OBSERVED census (BODY-TIER1-LIMPIEZA-OBS-1, base `3c4d0ae`), plus one real defect the
orchestrator measured while reviewing it.

**The defect.** `vida_export.current_week_monday(today=None)` defaulted to `date.today()` -- the SERVER's
own date, not the person's. `body/rutas/dispositivos.py`'s `GET /api/vida/semana` (no `semana` query)
called it with no argument on the host, while every other "today" in Body has been `fechas.hoy_local(person)`
(America/Bogota by default) since BODY-FECHA-FUTURA-1. `body/traer_semana.py` asked the server with
`?semana=` when given, but named the SAVED FILE from its own, local, `current_week_monday()` call rather
than the server's answer. The window: on a UTC host, from Sunday 19:00 Bogota the server's own
`date.today()` has already rolled to Monday while Bogota is still Sunday -- the PC's `traer_semana.py`
would then write the server's (wrong, early) week into the file name Personal's Sunday review reads
(vida-v1's `week_start`). Same rule as BODY-FECHA-FUTURA-1-M: a date default that can silently be the
wrong clock is a trap.

**The fix.** `current_week_monday(*, hoy: date) -> date` now REQUIRES `hoy`, keyword-only (no default) --
callers must supply their own correct clock. It returns `fechas.lunes_de(hoy)` (previously it open-coded
`today - timedelta(today.weekday())` itself). The local CLI (`vida_export.main`) passes its own machine's
`date.today()`, now for both `--current` (`current_week_monday(hoy=today)`) and the "last full week"
default, which was ALSO open-coded (`today - timedelta(today.weekday() + 7)`, a shape the then-matcher did
not catch) and is now `fechas.lunes_de(today) - timedelta(days=7)`. The hosted route
(`body/rutas/dispositivos.py`'s `api_vida_semana`) now fetches `person` from `comun._ctx(person_id)` before
branching and passes `hoy=comun._today_local(person)` -- the same patchable route clock every other route
reads. `body/traer_semana.py` no longer calls `current_week_monday` at all: it names the saved file from
the HTTP payload's own `week_start` field (the server's answer -- one source of truth), still sends
`?semana=` when `--semana` is given, and refuses with a plain line and a non-zero exit -- writing no file
-- when the payload's `week_start` is missing or not a Monday (no exception text is ever involved; this is
just a missing/invalid field check).

**The guard.** `tests/test_guardia_parches.py`'s `_is_week_monday_subtraction` matched only the bare
`<x> - timedelta(<x>.weekday())` shape; `vida_export.py:119`'s `today - timedelta(today.weekday() + 7)` form
slipped past it, which is why `_ALLOWED_WEEK_MONDAY_FILES = {"vida_export.py"}` existed as an allowlist.
The matcher is widened (`_is_weekday_based_offset`, `_timedelta_weekday_offset`) to also catch
`<x>.weekday() + <n>` / `<n> + <x>.weekday()`, and both the positional and `timedelta(days=...)` keyword
forms. Proof the widened matcher bites where the old one missed, run in the worker's scratchpad against
`git show main:body/vida_export.py` (base `3c4d0ae`, before this slice's own fix, never the edited working
tree): `old matcher hits: [33]` / `new matcher hits: [33, 119]` -- the old matcher caught only line 33
(the `current_week_monday` default), the widened one also catches line 119 (the "last full week" default).
With both of `vida_export.py`'s own open-coded sites now replaced by `fechas.lunes_de()`, nothing needs the
allowlist any more, so `_ALLOWED_WEEK_MONDAY_FILES` is deleted along with the `if path.name in (..., *_ALLOWED_WEEK_MONDAY_FILES)`
exemption -- the guard now runs over every file under `body/` with no exception.

**The provider `__init__` cleanup.** `body/agente/cliente.py`'s `Anthropic`, `OpenAI` and `Gemini` each
carried a byte-identical `def __init__(self, modelo, api_key, transporte=None): self.modelo = modelo;
self.api_key = api_key; self._transporte = transporte or self._post_real`, while `Proveedor` (their common
base) had none. The three are gone; `Proveedor.__init__` now owns that body, and `self._post_real` still
resolves correctly through the instance's own class at call time (Python resolves `self.<name>` dynamically,
not when `__init__` was defined). `Demo`, whose `__init__(self)` takes no provider arguments at all, is
unchanged -- it never called the shared one. The key is still read only in `proveedores_configurados()`,
never in any `__init__`.

**Tests.** `tests/test_vida_export.py` -- `CurrentWeekMondayTest`: `current_week_monday()` with no `hoy`
raises `TypeError`; `current_week_monday(hoy=date(2026, 11, 8))` (a Sunday) returns `date(2026, 11, 2)`.
`tests/test_dispositivo.py` -- `ApiVidaSemanaTest.setUp` now seeds its "this week" metric at
`current_week_monday(hoy=fechas.hoy_local({"timezone": "America/Bogota"}))` rather than the old bare call;
new `ApiVidaSemanaClockTest.test_default_week_uses_the_route_clock_not_a_bare_today` patches
`comun._today_local` (the sanctioned route-clock shim) to a frozen Sunday and asserts the route's own
`week_start` answer is that Sunday's Monday -- proving the route reads its own patchable clock rather than
some other (e.g. the server's bare `date.today()`) day, which is exactly the shape the old code could not
have honoured since it called `current_week_monday()` with no argument at all. `tests/test_pc_cliente.py`
-- `TraerSemanaTest`: the existing "writes the exact local path" test now gives the fake HTTP reply its own
`week_start` and asserts the file is named from it; new
`test_names_the_file_from_the_payloads_week_start_even_when_different_from_the_requested_semana` sends
`--semana` for one Monday while the fake server answers with a different `week_start`, and asserts the file
is named from the ANSWER, not the request; new `test_explicit_semana_still_sent_as_the_query_param` asserts
`--semana` still appends `?semana=` to the request URL; new `test_reply_without_week_start_refuses_and_writes_nothing`
and `test_reply_with_a_non_monday_week_start_refuses_and_writes_nothing` each assert exit code 1 and that
`BODY_HOME/vida` is never created. `tests/test_agente_cliente.py` -- `ProveedorInitSharedTest`: each of
`Anthropic`/`OpenAI`/`Gemini`'s `__init__` is identically `Proveedor.__init__` (`assertIs`); constructing any
of the three positionally still sets `modelo`, `api_key` and `_transporte` (a fake transport, checked by
identity); `Demo.__init__` is NOT `Proveedor.__init__`. No existing test needed a `hoy=` update beyond the
two files above -- `tests/test_agente_proveedores.py` was unaffected (it never calls a provider's
`__init__` directly; `proveedores_configurados()` still constructs `clase(modelo, api_key)` positionally,
unchanged).

**Gate**, run once on the final tree (after fixing one `NameError` in this slice's own new test --
`tests/test_dispositivo.py` needed `from datetime import date`, missed on the first pass; the first run was
RED on that bug alone, in a file inside this slice's own `touches:`, so it was fixed and the gate run again
as the one authoritative measurement on the corrected tree): `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover
tests -t .` -- `Ran 1237 tests in 124.026s ... OK (skipped=1)`.

Merge policy A: no schema or migration change; no customer-facing bytes (every changed string is a
terminal `print()` line, an internal computed date, or a test/ledger file -- the only user-visible shape
touched is vida-v1's `week_start` field, whose SHAPE is unchanged and whose VALUE now matches the
contract's own meaning, a Monday of the person's week, more often than before); no cross-repo contract or
DTO shape change, in the actual diff (`body/vida_export.py`, `body/rutas/dispositivos.py`,
`body/traer_semana.py`, `body/agente/cliente.py`, and five test files). This spec's own approval-reason
