## BODY-SEGURIDAD-1 -- same-origin check for unsafe methods, fixed security headers, the referrer trap, safe_return_to's backslash defect (2026-11-08)

First fix slice from BODY-SEGURIDAD-CENSO-1 (an OBSERVED census run in a separate read-only Tier 1 session,
reported COMPLETE against this repository's `32a806d` -- it wrote nothing here, so there is no earlier ledger
entry for it to point to; its findings are quoted in this slice's own spec instead): 58 routes, zero CSRF/Origin
checks anywhere, zero response security headers, one open-redirect site. This slice bundles the census's ranked
items 1 (cross-site POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), 2 (fixed response headers, deliberately WITHOUT a script/style
Content-Security-Policy -- that needs the app's 7 inline `<script>` blocks moved to files first, BODY-SEGURIDAD-2)
and 6 (open redirects), plus a defect the orchestrator found while reviewing the census: `cuenta.safe_return_to`
accepted `/\evil.example` (it starts with `/`, not `//`) -- a browser reads a backslash as a forward slash, so
that value is a protocol-relative redirect off this site exactly like `//evil.example` already was refused.

**The Origin rule** (`body/seguridad.py`, new: one ASGI middleware, `SeguridadMiddleware`; `body/web.py` only
adds it with `app.add_middleware(SeguridadMiddleware)`, after `_CaminoActualMiddleware` and
`RequestLogMiddleware` -- web.py stays the pure assembler, BODY-WEB-ESTRUCTURA-PLAN-1). For
POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE only: `Origin` present and not the literal string `"null"` -> allowed iff its
`host[:port]` (lower-cased, default port 80/443 dropped) equals the request's own `Host` header, normalised
the same way, OR (hosted mode only) the host of `cuenta.public_url()`; `Origin` absent and `Referer` present
-> the same host check against `Referer`'s own URL; BOTH absent -> allowed unconditionally, because a browser
always sends `Origin` on a cross-site unsafe request and a request with neither is therefore never a browser
(the PC client authenticating with its device key, `/login/cuenta/logout-token`'s own server-to-server call from
Cuenta Duna, curl, a test) -- the session cookie is never ambient on a request like that, so there is nothing
for an Origin check to protect; `Origin: null` -> always refused. HOST is compared, never scheme: behind Caddy
(`deploy/host/Caddyfile.body`'s `reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8770`, read, not changed) the proxy preserves the
inbound `Host` header unchanged while terminating TLS itself, so `request.url.scheme` can read `http` on the
very same request whose browser-sent `Origin` reads `https` -- comparing scheme as well would refuse every
real hosted request. No exemption list was needed: every one of the app's device-key and server-to-server POST
routes already sends neither header, so the "both absent" rule covers them without naming a single one.

**The referrer trap**, measured by the orchestrator before this slice started. `base.html`,
`acceso_rechazado.html`, `consentimiento.html` and `sin_acceso.html` all set
`<meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer">`. Per the Fetch standard, a non-CORS POST sent from a page whose
referrer policy is `no-referrer` carries `Origin: null` -- so the Origin rule above, left alone, would have
refused every one of Body's own form submissions (the habit checkbox, goal actions, settings, sign-out, ...),
not just a cross-site one. All four now say `content="same-origin"` instead: a cross-site request still arrives
with no `Referer` and `Origin: null` (still refused), while Body's own forms now send a same-origin `Origin`
the rule allows. `base.html` carries a one-line comment explaining why, next to the meta tag.

**The refusal page.** `body/templates/origen_rechazado.html` (new): standalone like `sin_acceso.html` and
`acceso_rechazado.html` -- no nav, the theme-before-paint script, one sentence, one link home (`/`) -- served
at 403 by the middleware above through `comun.env.get_template(...)`. New i18n keys, es + en, in both
`body/i18n/es.json` and `body/i18n/en.json`: `origen_rechazado.title` ("Esto no se hizo" / "This wasn't done"),
`origen_rechazado.text` ("Esta acción vino de otra página y no se hizo. Vuelve a Body e inténtalo desde aquí." /
"This action came from another page and was not done. Go back to Body and try it from here."),
`origen_rechazado.volver` ("Volver a Body" / "Back to Body").

**Fixed response headers**, the same middleware, on every response -- grepped `body/` first for every route
that sets any header by name (`dispositivos.py`, `ajustes.py`, `pwa.py`, `privacidad.py`, `web.py`'s own
`WWW-Authenticate`): only `Cache-Control`, `Content-Disposition` and `WWW-Authenticate` appear, none of the
five below, so nothing is overwritten: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`,
`X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'` (`frame-ancestors` only, by design --
no `script-src`/`style-src` until BODY-SEGURIDAD-2 moves the inline scripts out), `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy:
same-origin`. Added by wrapping ASGI `send` on the `http.response.start` message, so they land on a 200, a 404,
a 403, a redirect and a `/static` file alike; each header is added only if a route has not already set that
exact name (`setdefault`-style), so a future route-level override still wins.

**The redirect fix.** `cuenta.safe_return_to(raw)` now refuses: anything not starting with `/`, or equal to `/`
followed by `/` or `\` (the backslash defect above); any value containing a literal `\` anywhere else; any
value containing `://`; any value containing a control character (`ord(c) < 0x20` or `0x7f`). `/%5Cx`
(percent-encoded backslash) is deliberately ALLOWED: it is the two characters `%`, `5`, `C`, never a literal
backslash, so a browser resolves it as an ordinary same-origin path segment and it cannot affect how the
authority is parsed -- refusing it would only reject a harmless path. `body/rutas/metas.py`'s `habit_check`
(`POST /habits/{habit_id}/check`) now reads its `back` field through `cuenta.safe_return_to` (previously
`f.get("back") or "/"`, unchecked). `body/rutas/ajustes.py`'s `set_trabaja_turnos`'s `volver` allow-list
(narrowed to exactly `{"/", "/settings"}`) is left exactly as it was -- it is already stricter than
`safe_return_to`, so there is nothing to tighten there.

**Guards**, `tests/test_seguridad.py` (new). (a) Every one of the app's unsafe-method routes -- read from the
live app via `tests/_rutas.rutas_planas`, filtered to the methods `seguridad.UNSAFE_METHODS` names, never
typed by hand -- refuses a `https://evil.example` Origin with 403 and the `origen_rechazado.html` text, before
any handler, auth check or database write; asserts the checked count equals the route count found and that it
is greater than zero (measured: 32, all POST, no PUT/PATCH/DELETE route exists in the app). (b) a same-origin
`Origin`, a same-origin-only `Referer` (no `Origin`), and neither header present, each reach the handler
(`POST /settings/language`, which always answers 303). (c) `Origin: null` -> 403. (d) the five headers are
present on a 200 page, a 404, a 303 redirect and a `/static` file. (e) no template under `body/templates`
still sets `<meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer">`. (f) an `ast` scan over every `RedirectResponse(...)`
call under `body/`: its target must be a fixed string literal, an f-string whose literal LEADING chunk already
fixes the string as `/` followed by a non-`/`-non-`\` character (nothing a later substitution inserts can
rewind characters the fixed prefix already determined), a direct `cuenta.safe_return_to(...)` or
`cuenta.logout_url(...)` call, or a bare variable assigned from `cuenta.safe_return_to(...)` earlier in the same
function -- or else named in a small, reasoned `ALLOWLIST` the test also checks for staleness (an entry that no
longer matches any call site fails the test): `body/rutas/sesion.py:50` (`url` is `cuenta.start_login()`'s own
externally-built authorize URL, on Cuenta Duna's domain by design, never request data), `sesion.py:76`
(`result.return_to` was already passed through `safe_return_to` at write time, in the same module's
`login_start`, before being stored in the row `handle_callback` reads it back from), `body/rutas/ajustes.py:72`
(its own stricter `{"/", "/settings"}` allow-list, left as is per this slice's own instruction above). The scan
found no other call site outside these two generic rules and this three-entry allowlist, across every
`RedirectResponse(` call in `body/` (43 call sites in total, counted by the same `ast` walk the guard test
itself runs, after this slice's one fix to `metas.py`'s `habit_check`).

**Proof that (a) bites on `main`**, run once in the worker's own scratchpad, never committed: `main`'s own
`body/web.py` at `32a806d` (this slice's base, confirmed by `git rev-parse main`) was loaded, byte for byte via
`git show main:body/web.py`, as a module inside the real `body` package (so its relative imports resolve
against the current, otherwise-unrelated `body.cuenta`/`body.rutas.*` on disk), against a throwaway
`BODY_HOME`. Posting `POST /settings/trabaja_turnos` with `Origin: https://evil.example` and no cookie answered
`303 /` -- the handler ran and set `trabaja_turnos`, with no Origin check of any kind standing in the way.
The same request against this slice's own `body/web.py` is exactly guard (a)'s own first case, and answers 403
with the `origen_rechazado.html` page instead.

**Noticed, not fixed here (BODY-SEGURIDAD-CADDY-HEADER-DUPE-1):** `deploy/host/Caddyfile.body`'s own `header`
block already sets `X-Content-Type-Options` and `Referrer-Policy` for hosted traffic -- reading it (required by
this slice's own spec, for the Origin rule's scheme reasoning above) shows those two now duplicate
`body/seguridad.py`'s own app-level headers on every hosted response. Both sides agree on the exact value, so
this is harmless, not a defect; tidying it is a `deploy/` change, Tier 1 and outside this slice's `touches:`, so
it is left for its own slice rather than touched here.

**`docs/DESIGN.md`**, rule 13 ("Health data stays home"), three lines added: unsafe methods are same-origin
only, checked by one middleware (`body/seguridad.py`); every response carries the fixed header set named above;
every redirect built from request data goes through `cuenta.safe_return_to`.

**Gate**, run once on the final tree: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .` --
`Ran 1251 tests in 128.537s ... OK (skipped=1)`.

Merge policy A, judged against the actual diff: no schema or migration change (nothing in `body/db.py` or any
migration touched). No cross-repo contract or DTO shape change (every touched file is `body/seguridad.py`

## BODY-SEGURIDAD-1-M -- lands BODY-SEGURIDAD-1 after two review fixes (2026-11-08)

The merge slice for BODY-SEGURIDAD-1, held `AWAITING_APPROVAL` above. ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1 approved
the merge against BODY-SEGURIDAD-CENSO-1, after the orchestrator's own diff review and a browser measurement,
on condition of two review fixes made here first.

**Fix 1 -- the refusal page answers in the request's own language.** `body/seguridad.py`'s `_origen_rechazado`
used to render `T(DEFAULT_LANG)` unconditionally -- always Spanish, even for an English-speaking caller --
because `SeguridadMiddleware` runs ahead of `identity.current_person_id`, before any person (and their saved
language) is resolved. A new small helper, `body/i18n/pick(accept_language: str | None) -> str`: the first tag
in a raw `Accept-Language` header value (everything before the first comma, `;q=...` stripped away by the
comma split) picks `"en"` when it starts with `"en"` (case-insensitive); anything else -- `es-CO`, a different
language, a header with no first tag, or no header at all -- picks `DEFAULT` (`"es"`). `_origen_rechazado` now
reads `scope["headers"]` for `accept-language` itself (the ASGI scope, not a `Request`, since the middleware
sees raw ASGI) and renders `T(i18n.pick(...))`. `Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9` now answers "This action came
from another page and was not done."; `es-CO`, no header, and `fr-FR,fr;q=0.9` all answer the Spanish text
unchanged -- no new i18n keys needed, both strings already existed from BODY-SEGURIDAD-1 itself, just
unreachable until now.

**Fix 2 -- a refused request now reaches the request log.** `body/web.py` added `SeguridadMiddleware` as the
LAST `app.add_middleware(...)` call, and Starlette's `add_middleware` inserts each new middleware at index 0
of its internal list, so the LAST call ends up OUTERMOST. That made `SeguridadMiddleware` the outermost of the
two, short-circuiting a cross-site 403 before `RequestLogMiddleware` ever saw the request -- an attack attempt
was invisible in the log, the opposite of Carlos's rule that anything off the normal flow raises a flag.
Execution order, outermost first, before this fix: `ServerErrorMiddleware`, `SeguridadMiddleware`,
`RequestLogMiddleware`, `_CaminoActualMiddleware`, `ExceptionMiddleware`, the router. The fix swaps the last two
`app.add_middleware(...)` lines, so the call order is now `_CaminoActualMiddleware`, `SeguridadMiddleware`,
`RequestLogMiddleware` -- `RequestLogMiddleware` added last puts it outermost of the two. Execution order,
outermost first, after: `ServerErrorMiddleware`, `RequestLogMiddleware`, `SeguridadMiddleware`,
`_CaminoActualMiddleware`, `ExceptionMiddleware`, the router. `_CaminoActualMiddleware` keeps its own position
relative to the router unchanged -- only the relative order of the two outer layers moved. Every response still
carries the fixed security-header set (`SeguridadMiddleware` wraps `send` on every request it lets through, and
`RequestLogMiddleware` does not touch headers), and `RequestLogMiddleware`'s own behaviour for an allowed
request is unchanged -- it still reads `request.scope["route"]` for the path template after `call_next`
returns. For a refused request, routing never runs (`SeguridadMiddleware` returns its 403 directly, without
calling `self.app`), so `_route_template` finds no `"route"` key in scope and logs its existing `"-"` marker,
not a path template. A refused cross-site `POST` now logs exactly one `body.request` record:
`"POST - 403 <N>ms"` -- method, the no-route marker, status, duration; never the `Origin` value (`evil.example`
does not appear), never the query string. New guard,
`tests/test_request_log.py::RefusedCrossSiteRequestLogsOnceTest`: `POST /settings/language?x=<secret>` with
`Origin: https://evil.example` logs one record, `fields[0] == "POST"`, `fields[1] == "-"`, `fields[2] == "403"`,
and asserts neither `"evil.example"` nor the query value appears in the message. New guard,
`tests/test_seguridad.py::RefusalPageLanguageTest`: English `Accept-Language` gets the English sentence; `es-CO`,
absent, and `fr-FR` each get the Spanish sentence -- all four cases go through the live middleware stack via
`TestClient`, exercising `i18n.pick`'s both branches, not called directly. Every existing BODY-SEGURIDAD-1 guard
in `tests/test_seguridad.py` stayed green through both fixes, unmodified except for the new test class added
alongside them.

**BODY-SEGURIDAD-CADDY-HEADER-DUPE-1, closed as not-a-defect.** The worker's follow-up, opened above, called
the Caddy-side and app-side headers a duplication. They are not a duplicate on the wire: Caddy's `header`
directive with a value SETS that response field -- it replaces whatever the upstream (this app) already sent,
it does not append a second occurrence -- and the two sides agree on the exact value for both headers
(`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`). A client sees each header exactly once,
with the value both layers happen to agree on. Nothing to fix; closed.

## BODY-SEGURIDAD-4 -- per-person attempt limits on the Garmin sign-in relay

Against BODY-SEGURIDAD-CENSO-1's item 4: `body/rutas/garmin.py` let a signed-in person submit
`/garmin/conectar` (a Garmin email + password) and `/garmin/codigo` (the MFA code) without any limit. The real
harm was never only guessing a code -- any Body account could use Body's own server as a relay to try many
Garmin email/password pairs, and Garmin answers that by rate-limiting or blocking the host's address, which
breaks the daily pull for every person on that host. The limit has to key on the signed-in `person_id`, not the
session cookie, so signing out and back in (a fresh cookie) does not reset it.

**Two limits, in the route module, no schema change:**

1. **Sign-in attempts** (`/garmin/conectar`): at most 5 failed attempts per `person_id` in a sliding hour, kept
   in a new module-level `_SIGNIN_FAILURES: dict[int, list[float]]` next to the existing `_MFA_STATE`, read
   through `time.monotonic()` and pruned on every call. A failure is the adapter raising (today's `error=garmin`
   redirect); an empty form (`error=datos`) does not count and is checked first, before the limit; `needs_mfa`
   does not count either way; a direct success clears the person's failures. The 6th attempt inside the window
   is refused with `/garmin?error=demasiados` *before* `garmin_adapter.start_sign_in` is called -- the password
   never reaches Garmin, and Garmin never sees the 6th failed attempt from this host on this person's behalf.
2. **MFA code attempts** (`/garmin/codigo`): at most 5 wrong codes per MFA state. The `_MFA_STATE` tuple grew a
   third field, `wrong_codes` (`(client_state_json, started_at, wrong_codes)`), incremented on each wrong code.
   The 5th wrong code pops the state and redirects to `/garmin?error=demasiados` instead of letting the code be
   retried for the rest of the 10-minute TTL window; the person starts again from the email form, which is a
   fresh sign-in attempt under limit 1. `_prune_mfa_state` keeps pruning by `started_at`, unchanged in shape.

**Why per person, not per session:** a new session (sign out, sign back in, a different browser) must not reset
either counter, or the limit would only ever slow down the honest case and never the relay abuse it exists for.
Both counters are plain in-process dicts, exactly like the existing `_MFA_STATE`, acceptable because the host
runs a single process: `deploy/host/body-web.service`'s `ExecStart` is `.../python -m body.web --port 8770`
with no `--workers` flag, and `body/web.py`'s `main()` calls `uvicorn.run(app, ...)` with no `workers=` argument
either -- `uvicorn.run` defaults to one worker when the argument is omitted, so one process holds both dicts for
the whole host.

**Message**, new key `garmin.error.demasiados` (es + en), reused for both limits -- the same plain sentence
reads correctly for a code lockout too, since neither limit names a number of seconds:
- es: «Demasiados intentos seguidos. Espera una hora e inténtalo de nuevo.»
- en: "Too many attempts in a row. Wait an hour and try again."

`garmin.html` needed no change -- its existing `{% if form_error %}` card at the top of the page already
renders whatever string `garmin_view` resolves for `error=demasiados`, exactly as it does for the other
`_GARMIN_FORM_ERROR_KEYS` entries.

**Tests**, `tests/test_garmin_host.py` (the adapter patched throughout, no network): `SignInAttemptLimitTest` --
5 failures then the 6th refused with `garmin_adapter.start_sign_in` asserted never called; the window slides
(stale timestamps past the hour let a 6th attempt through); a direct success clears the person's failure list;
an empty form does not add to it; a second, independently signed-in person is unaffected; the new message
renders in both es and en (via `/settings/language`). `MfaAttemptLimitTest` -- 4 wrong codes keep re-rendering
the code form (state kept), the 5th drops the state and answers `error=demasiados`; a further POST after that
drop gets `error=mfa_expired`, because the state is simply gone and that is the existing no-pending-state case,
not a separate code path; a right code on the 3rd try still connects and stores the token. Two existing tests
that read or wrote `_MFA_STATE` entries directly (`test_old_mfa_state_is_pruned_on_the_next_write`,
`test_expired_mfa_state_is_refused`) were updated for the tuple's new third field; neither test's own assertion
changed. No test wrote a real-looking secret anywhere.

the merge commit's own tree before merging, so not re-run after the merge): `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m
unittest discover tests -t .` -- `Ran 1265 tests in 114.209s ... OK (skipped=1)`.

## BODY-SEGURIDAD-4-B -- closing the MFA-cycling gap and the false wait-an-hour message

Orchestrator review of BODY-SEGURIDAD-4 (merged `2786eb3`, ledger `9d736d8`, gate 1265) found two defects in
`body/rutas/garmin.py`. (1) **The limit could be cycled.** `_SIGNIN_FAILURES` (as it was named) counted only an
outright adapter exception. A `needs_mfa` start was never counted, and dropping the MFA state after 5 wrong
codes cleared nothing counted either -- so someone who knew (or was testing) the password could loop
`conectar` -> 5 wrong codes -> `conectar` -> 5 wrong codes without ever reaching the hourly limit, and each
`conectar` makes Garmin send a fresh code to the account owner. (2) **The drop message lied.** After the MFA
state was dropped the page said "Demasiados intentos seguidos. Espera una hora..." (`garmin.error.demasiados`),
but nothing made that person wait an hour -- a fresh email+password start was accepted immediately, so the
sentence was false in that case.

**One rule now governs the hourly limit: every sign-in start counts unless it ends with a token stored.** In
`garmin_conectar`, an attempt is recorded both when the adapter raises (as before) and, now, when it answers
`needs_mfa` -- the start is counted the moment it happens, not deferred to however the MFA state later resolves.
The person's attempts are cleared only when a token is actually stored: a direct success in `garmin_conectar`,
or a right code in `garmin_codigo`. An MFA state that is later dropped (5 wrong codes) or left to expire
therefore stays counted, because nothing clears it on either path. Consequence: at most 5 starts per person
per hour, so at most 25 code guesses per hour, and at most 5 codes Garmin sends to the account owner per hour
through Body. The dict is renamed `_SIGNIN_ATTEMPTS` (was `_SIGNIN_FAILURES`) since it now counts starts, not
only failures; `_prune_signin_failures` is renamed `_prune_signin_attempts` to match, and the comments at each
use site were rewritten for the new meaning.

**Message**, new key `garmin.error.mfa_demasiados` (es + en), used only by the wrong-code drop redirect
(`/garmin?error=mfa_demasiados`, added to `_GARMIN_FORM_ERROR_KEYS`) -- a true sentence that tells the person
to start over, instead of the false "wait an hour":
- es: «Demasiados códigos equivocados. Vuelve a empezar con tu correo y tu contraseña.»
- en: "Too many wrong codes. Start again with your email and password."

`garmin.error.demasiados` is unchanged and stays for the hourly limit itself; `garmin.html` needed no change,
reusing the same `form_error` card.

**Tests**, `tests/test_garmin_host.py` (the adapter patched throughout, no network), all renamed references
from `_SIGNIN_FAILURES` to `_SIGNIN_ATTEMPTS`: `SignInAttemptLimitTest` gained
`test_completing_mfa_clears_the_person_so_a_later_start_is_allowed` (an MFA start is counted, a right code
clears it, five more failed starts afterwards are still allowed) and
`test_mfa_cycle_does_not_evade_the_hourly_limit` (five rounds of `conectar` (needs_mfa) + 5 wrong codes each,
then the 6th `conectar` is refused with `garmin_adapter.start_sign_in` asserted never called -- the cycle this
slice closes). `MfaAttemptLimitTest` gained `test_mfa_demasiados_message_renders_in_es_and_en` and
`test_expired_mfa_state_stays_counted_in_signin_attempts` (an MFA state aged past its TTL still answers
`error=mfa_expired`, and the person's earlier counted start is still in `_SIGNIN_ATTEMPTS` afterwards). The
existing `test_five_wrong_codes_drop_the_state_and_redirect_to_demasiados` was renamed
`..._redirect_to_mfa_demasiados` and its assertion changed from `error=demasiados` to `error=mfa_demasiados`,
since that is now the true redirect for a dropped MFA state; `test_success_clears_failures` was renamed
`test_success_clears_attempts` (same body, new dict name) with no behaviour change.

124.632s ... OK (skipped=1)` (1265 + the 4 new tests above).

## BODY-SEGURIDAD-2 -- script-src 'self': every inline script and handler moved to /static (2026-11-08)

Second half of `BODY-SEGURIDAD-CENSO-1`'s item 2 (the first half, `frame-ancestors 'none'` alone, shipped as
`BODY-SEGURIDAD-1`). A `script-src` policy needs the inline code out first, so this slice moves every
executable inline `<script>` block and the one inline `onchange=` attribute into `body/static/*.js`, loaded
through `static_url(...)` (`BODY-STATIC-VERSION-1`'s cache-busting), then turns `script-src 'self'` on.

**What moved where**, behaviour-identical:
- **`tema.js`** -- theme-before-paint (`base.html:58` and the four standalone pages' copy:
  `acceso_rechazado.html:9`, `consentimiento.html:9`, `sin_acceso.html:9`, `origen_rechazado.html:9`). Loaded
  as a plain blocking `<script src>` in `<head>`, no `defer`/`async`, so it still runs before first paint.
- **`pagina.js`** -- scroll restore + service-worker registration (`base.html:156`). Loaded with `defer`:
  scroll restore still works, because a deferred script runs after the document is parsed (just before
  `DOMContentLoaded`), the same relative timing it had at the bottom of `<body>` before, and
  `location.pathname` plus the `pagehide` listener never depended on `DOMContentLoaded` having fired.
- **`ajustes_tema.js`** -- settings.html's theme buttons (`settings.html:84`). Loaded with `defer`, so
  `#theme`'s buttons already exist when it runs.
- **`meta_nueva.js`** -- `goal_new.html`'s `bodyMetricChange` (`goal_new.html:97`), plus the inline
  `onchange="bodyMetricChange()"` attribute (`goal_new.html:33`), now an
  `addEventListener('change', bodyMetricChange)` call inside the file; it still runs once on load as before.

`base.html:150`'s `<script id="asis-i18n" type="application/json">` data block is untouched -- CSP's
`script-src` never executes a `type="application/json"` block, so it was never the problem.

**The policy**, `body/seguridad.py`'s `content_security_policy()`, built from `_CSP_FIXED_DIRECTIVES` plus a
`form-action` computed per request, so a test reads named parts instead of re-parsing one long literal:

| Directive | Value | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `default-src` | `'self'` | floor for anything not named below |
| `script-src` | `'self'` | the point of this slice -- no inline script left to need `'unsafe-inline'` |
| `style-src` | `'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com` | **remaining gap, not closed here** -- 22 templates carry `style="..."` attributes, and server-built SVG (Tendencias/charts) does too; `'unsafe-inline'` stays until those are moved |
| `font-src` | `'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com` | Hanken Grotesk's font files |
| `img-src` | `'self' data:` | the `data:` SVG icon and any inline-data image |
| `connect-src` | `'self'` | `assistant.js`'s `fetch` calls are same-origin only (confirmed by reading the file) |
| `manifest-src` | `'self'` | the PWA manifest |
| `worker-src` | `'self'` | the service worker |
| `object-src` | `'none'` | no plugin content anywhere |
| `base-uri` | `'none'` | nothing sets `<base>` |
| `frame-ancestors` | `'none'` | unchanged from `BODY-SEGURIDAD-1` |
| `form-action` | `'self'` locally; `'self' <Cuenta's issuer origin>` once hosted | see census below |

**form-action census.** Grepped every `RedirectResponse(...)` under `body/rutas/` and every `method="post"`
form under `body/templates/` for a target outside Body. Three POST forms can 303-redirect off-site, all to
the same place -- Cuenta's OIDC issuer, via `cuenta.logout_url(sid)` (built from `cuenta.issuer()`):
- `/logout` (`body/rutas/sesion.py:94`) -- always redirects to `cuenta.logout_url(sid)` when hosted.
- `/privacidad/consentimiento` (`body/rutas/privacidad.py:42`) -- redirects there when the person declines
  consent.
- `/privacidad/borrar` (`body/rutas/privacidad.py:96`) -- redirects there after a hosted account deletion.
  (The re-auth branch at `privacidad.py:88` redirects to `/login/cuenta/start?...`, a Body path, not off-site.)

No other `RedirectResponse` target in `body/rutas/` leaves Body's own origin (confirmed against
`tests/test_seguridad.py`'s existing `RedirectTargetsAreSafeTest`, which already enumerates every
`RedirectResponse` call site). So the one off-site origin `form-action` needs, only when hosted, is Cuenta's
issuer origin -- scheme + host, stripped of any path, via `seguridad._origin(cuenta.issuer())`. Built at
request time from `cuenta.hosted()`/`cuenta.issuer()`, never a literal, so it tracks whichever Cuenta
environment Body is actually configured against.

**Guards**, `tests/test_seguridad.py`:
- (a) `InlineScriptGoneTest` -- no template under `body/templates` holds a `<script>` tag with neither
  `src=` nor `type="application/json"`. Proved to catch all 8 pre-slice offenders by running the exact same
  regex against `main`'s templates before writing any fix (scratchpad, not committed):
  `['body/templates/base.html:58', 'body/templates/base.html:156', 'body/templates/settings.html:84', 'body/templates/goal_new.html:97', 'body/templates/acceso_rechazado.html:9', 'body/templates/consentimiento.html:9', 'body/templates/sin_acceso.html:9', 'body/templates/origen_rechazado.html:9']`.
- (b) `InlineEventHandlerGoneTest` -- no template holds an `\bon[a-z]+="` attribute (word-boundary, so
  `viewport`/`content`/`aria-controls` false-positives from a looser pattern are excluded); only
  `goal_new.html:33`'s `onchange=` existed, now gone.
- (c) `SecurityHeadersTest` -- every response's `Content-Security-Policy` header equals
  `seguridad.content_security_policy()` exactly, and its `script-src` directive carries neither
  `'unsafe-inline'` nor `'unsafe-eval'`.
- (d) `StaticUrlScriptsExistTest` -- every `static_url('...js')` a template references (including the four
  new files) names a file that exists under `body/static`.
- (e) `FormActionOriginTest` / `HostedResponseCarriesFormActionTest` -- `form-action` is `'self'` alone
  locally (`os.environ` has no `BODY_CUENTA_ISSUER`) and `'self' https://fake-cuenta.test` once
  `cuenta.ISSUER_ENV` is patched the way the existing hosted tests do (e.g. `tests/test_dispositivo.py`),
  checked at the function level and once more end to end through a real `TestClient` response.

**docs/DESIGN.md** (rule 13) now records the full policy, names the `style-src` gap and why it stays, and
names Google Fonts as the one third-party origin the policy allows -- self-hosting it instead is open as
**BODY-FUENTES-PROPIAS-1**, a follow-up, not done here.

**Gate**, run once on the branch's final tree before this entry's own commit:
`.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .` -- `Ran 1276 tests in 176.752s ... OK (skipped=1)`
(1269 before this slice, +7 new guard tests: `InlineScriptGoneTest`, `InlineEventHandlerGoneTest`,
`StaticUrlScriptsExistTest`, `FormActionOriginTest`'s 3 methods, `HostedResponseCarriesFormActionTest`).

## BODY-SEGURIDAD-3 -- GET routes stop writing `goal_check`; the daily pull becomes the one writer
(2026-11-08)

`tests/test_get_sin_escritura.py`'s own sweep (new in this slice) states the defect plainly: `/goals` and
`/goals/{goal_id}` both called `body/rutas/metas.py`'s `_goal_check_row`, which upserted a `goal_check` row
through `goals.weekly_check` the first time anyone viewed a goal in a given week -- freezing that week's
verdict at whoever opened the page first, for every viewer, for the rest of the week. Read from the diff
this slice inherited and built on (the previous worker stopped BLOCKED on an unrelated red, with this fix
itself complete and reviewed):

(a) **`/goals` and `/goals/{goal_id}` wrote on a GET.** Fixed by splitting `goals.weekly_check` in two:
`goals.evaluar_semana` computes a goal_check body (same fields, same `rule_version`) WITHOUT writing
anything; `weekly_check` keeps the upsert, calling `evaluar_semana` for the numbers. Both GET routes now
call `evaluar_semana` for the viewer's current week, live, every time -- never a stored row for that week,
which would go stale the moment any habit or metric changes for the rest of the week.

(b) **Showing the current week twice.** Once (a) made the current week always computed live, a *stored*
`goal_check` row for that same week (written by an earlier day's daily pull, before the week ended) would
otherwise still show up in `/goals/{goal_id}`'s 8-week history and its metric chart alongside the fresh
live value. Both queries now exclude `week_start = <this Monday>` and splice the live `evaluar_semana`
value in instead, so the current week is shown exactly once, always fresh.

(c) **No writer left.** With `weekly_check`'s write-path reserved for closing a finished week, nothing
called it any more. `goals.cerrar_semanas(conn, person_id, *, hoy)` is the new one writer: it writes this
week's AND last week's `goal_check` row for every ACTIVE goal `person_id` can see (own goals plus shared
household milestones, the same `goal_scope_sql` scope `/goals` itself uses) -- last week too, so data that
lands late (a Sunday's Garmin numbers pulled on Monday) still lands in the week it belongs to.
`body/pull.py` is the one caller: a new `_cerrar_semanas_seguro` wraps it so a failure there is caught,
printed as a counts-only line naming the exception TYPE (`body/errores.py`'s `texto_seguro`, never its
message -- no health figure, no token, nothing but a class name), and never counted as a Garmin failure or
allowed to stop the next person. Wired into the hosted daily pull (`pull_hosted`), hosted `--backfill`
(`pull_backfill_hosted`), and the local sync (`_run`, which previously called `goals.cerrar_semanas` bare --
a failure there would have failed the whole local sync; now it goes through the same safe wrapper).

`body/agente/herramientas.py`'s docstring is updated to name both new write paths (`weekly_check`,
`cerrar_semanas`) in its "a `lectura` tool must never write" rule (BODY-ASISTENTE-OBS-1), and to say
explicitly why `leer_metas`/`leer_meta` do NOT use the new live `evaluar_semana` either: an active goal
with no data yet would read as a computed "no verdict" dict instead of the "sin verificación aún" text
every other read tool and existing test already depends on.

**Guard**, `tests/test_get_sin_escritura.py`: seeds `body/demo.py`'s own demo database (two people, three
metric goals, a shared household milestone, habits, 30 days of data -- invented, no real figure), then
calls every one of the app's 26 GET routes (`tests/_rutas.py`'s `rutas_planas`) with a real id substituted
in, snapshotting every table's content before and after each call. Only `/login` and `/login/cuenta/start`
are allowed to write (the pre-auth sign-in start storing its PKCE/state row before any session cookie
exists -- inert in this sweep's local-mode test run, kept so the guard still holds under a hosted run).
Any other GET route that changes a single row fails the test by name.

**Open follow-up, not resolved here -- `BODY-PULL-RELOJ-1`:** `cerrar_semanas` only ever re-closes the
CURRENT and PREVIOUS week. Data that lands later than that -- a long `--backfill` run restoring Garmin
days from further back than one week, or a habit check corrected after the fact -- updates the raw
`daily_metric`/`habit_check` rows but never revisits the correspondingly older `goal_check` row, which
stays whatever it was computed as on the day it was closed. Worth a dedicated look once backfill depth or
late corrections become a real scenario; not a regression from this slice (the old `weekly_check`-on-GET
path had the same one-shot-per-week limit, just triggered differently), so not fixed here. (This follow-up
ID is reconstructed from reading the inherited diff and this slice's own build -- the previous worker's own
report, if it named this differently, was not available to this session.)

**Gate**, run once on the branch's final tree, together with BODY-SEGURIDAD-3-M's own additions (one
combined commit; see that entry): `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .` --
`Ran 1294 tests in 146.569s ... OK (skipped=1)` (1276 before this pair of slices, +18 new tests: 1 in
`test_get_sin_escritura.py`, 10 in `test_goals.py`, 1 in `test_goals_web.py`, 6 in `test_primer_pull_1.py`).

## BODY-SEGURIDAD-3-M -- every person with a goal gets their weekly check, not only the ones connected to
Garmin; merge BODY-SEGURIDAD-3 into `main` (2026-11-08)

Finished and landed BODY-SEGURIDAD-3 (above), inherited complete and uncommitted on `feat/body-seguridad-3`
and reviewed and accepted by the orchestrator (`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`, against
`BODY-SEGURIDAD-CENSO-1`), with two fixes made in this slice:

**1. The household test's SUBJECT, kept; its body, rewritten.** `tests/test_hogar_miembro_1.py`'s
`OwnWeeklyCheckTest.test_viewer_sees_their_own_history_not_the_creators` asserted that VIEWING
`/goals/{id}` had upserted the viewer's own `goal_check` row -- exactly the write-on-GET BODY-SEGURIDAD-3
removes, and the one red the previous worker's gate left (correctly BLOCKED on it rather than touching a
file outside that slice's `touches:`). Rewritten to keep rule 3 (BODY-HOGAR-MIEMBRO-1: the viewer's own
weekly check comes from the viewer's own habit checks, never the creator's) as its subject: (a) views
`/goals/{gid}` as the viewer (person 2), asserts the page shows their own live verdict ("1 de 1", the
BODY-HABITO-VECES-1 cap) and that the view wrote NOTHING (`goal_check` row count stays 0); (b) then runs
`goals.cerrar_semanas(conn, 2, hoy=...)` -- what the daily pull does -- and asserts the STORED row for
person 2 is `(1, 1)`, keyed to person 2 alone (no row for person 1, the creator). Searched the rest of
`tests/` for any other test relying on a GET writing `goal_check` (every `client.get(...)` call site in
every file that also touches `goal_check`, `weekly_check` or `_goal_check_row`): none found -- every other
`goals.weekly_check` call in the suite seeds data directly, never through a GET.

**2. The hosted pull now closes weeks for every person with a visible goal, connected to Garmin or not.**
Before this fix, `pull_hosted`/`pull_backfill_hosted` called `_cerrar_semanas_seguro` only inside the
Garmin loop, for persons whose pull succeeded that day (`garmin_cuenta.every_person_id`) -- so a household
member with no Garmin connection at all, or whose pull failed, never got a `goal_check` row stored for
their own habit goals, even though a habit goal's verdict never depends on Garmin data. Added
`goals.personas_con_meta_activa(conn)` (`body/goals.py`): every person who can see an active goal -- a
goal's own creator (any goal, any visibility), plus every member of the household behind a
`visibility='household', kind='milestone'` goal (the only kind a household can share, same rule
`goal_access`/`goal_scope_sql` already enforce) -- read from the `goal` and `hogar_miembro` tables, never
from `garmin_cuenta`. `body/pull.py` gained `_cerrar_semanas_todas(conn)`, which sweeps that list through
the existing `_cerrar_semanas_seguro` once each; the per-person call that used to sit inside the Garmin
loop was removed from both `pull_hosted` (`body/pull.py:195`, after the loop) and `pull_backfill_hosted`
(`body/pull.py:276`, after the loop) and replaced by one call to the sweep after each loop, so nobody is
closed twice. **Backfill**: chose to run the SAME sweep there too (not skip it) -- it is cheap next to the
Garmin network calls `--backfill` already makes, and a day backfilled into the current or previous week
can change that week's stored verdict, so leaving it out would mean the fresher data from a backfill run
only reaches `goal_check` on the next daily pull, up to a day later for no real saving.

**3. The local sync goes through the same safe wrapper.** `_run` called `goals.cerrar_semanas` bare, so an
exception closing weeks would have failed the whole local sync's exit code, unlike the hosted path.
Replaced with `_cerrar_semanas_seguro(conn, person_id)` (`body/pull.py:350`, right after
`readiness.recompute_all`) -- runs after every local path that stores or recomputes data: the default/
`--days`/`--date` pull, `--all`, and `--recompute` all reach this same line, since it sits after the
if/elif block that handles those three, not inside any branch of it.

**New tests** (`tests/test_primer_pull_1.py`'s `WeeklyChecksHostedTest`, rewritten from BODY-SEGURIDAD-3's
inherited version, and `tests/test_goals.py`'s new `PersonasConMetaActivaTest`): a person with an active
habit goal and no `garmin_cuenta` row at all gets swept by `pull_hosted` and by `pull_backfill_hosted`
alike; a person whose Garmin pull raised still gets theirs (the sweep runs after the loop regardless of
that loop's own ok/failed counts); nobody is swept twice (call count equals the number of distinct persons,
checked by set-equality against the call list); a raising `goals.cerrar_semanas` for one person still lets
the next person's weekly check land (`"weekly checks: 1 rows"` in stdout) and never marks either person's
Garmin pull as failed. `tests/test_primer_pull_1.py`'s existing `test_backfill_prints_only_counts` is
updated for the new scope rule: with no goal in that test's database, the sweep now closes nobody and
prints nothing (previously it printed `"weekly checks: 0 rows"` unconditionally for the one connected
person).

`docs/DESIGN.md` rule 13's BODY-SEGURIDAD-3 paragraph gained one sentence naming this: the hosted daily
pull sweeps every person who can see an active goal, not only the Garmin-connected ones.

## BODY-PULL-RELOJ-1 / BODY-SEMANAS-TARDIAS-1 -- the hosted daily pull asks each person for their
own today, not the server's; late data re-closes its own week (2026-11-08)

Two leftovers from BODY-SEGURIDAD-3-M, measured by the orchestrator on `main` at `572b3dd`:

**1. `BODY-PULL-RELOJ-1` itself: the server's date, not the person's.** `body/pull.py`'s
`pull_hosted` built the day list ONCE, from `date.today()`, and used that same list for every
person; `pull_backfill_hosted(conn, hoy=None)` defaulted `hoy = hoy or date.today()`, same
problem. The hosted daily pull's timer fires at one fixed instant (09:30 America/Bogota,
`deploy/host/body-pull.timer`): for a Bogota person the server's date already equals theirs at
that hour, so Carlos himself was never affected, but for a person in a zone far from the
server's, "today and yesterday" were the server's, not theirs -- the same clock rule
BODY-TIER1-LIMPIEZA-1 already named: a date that decides a business boundary is the PERSON's,
required, never a server default.

Fixed: `pull_hosted(conn, *, fecha=None, n_days=2)` -- `fecha` (from `--date`) stays one explicit
day for everyone, same as before; left out, EACH person's own day list is now built inside the
per-person loop from `fechas.hoy_local(db.person(conn, person_id))` and `n_days` (from `--days`).
`pull_backfill_hosted(conn, *, hoy=None)` -- `hoy`, when given (tests only), is still used for
every person alike; left out, each person's own `fechas.hoy_local` is read per person inside the
loop. No `date.today()` remains in either hosted path. `body/pull.py:364` (local mode's
`--days`/`--date` pull) and `body/pull.py:98` (`pull_all`'s starting point when nothing is
stored yet) both KEEP `date.today()` deliberately, with a comment saying why: local mode runs on
the person's own PC, so the PC's own clock already IS the person's clock -- there is no second
person's zone to get wrong, the same reasoning `vida_export`'s CLI already uses for its own
`date.today()`.

**2. A misnamed follow-up.** BODY-SEGURIDAD-3-M's own ledger entry (above, heading
`## BODY-SEGURIDAD-3-M -- ...`, its open-follow-up paragraph at `DECISIONS.md:8604`) recorded a
DIFFERENT finding under this same ID, `BODY-PULL-RELOJ-1`: "`cerrar_semanas` only re-closes the
current and previous week; data landing later than that ... never revisits that older
`goal_check` row." That finding is real, and is a distinct defect from the one above (a
one-shot-per-week limit vs. a wrong clock) -- it gets its own ID here, `BODY-SEMANAS-TARDIAS-1`,
rather than being folded into this one. (No correction is made to the inherited text at
`DECISIONS.md:8604` itself -- the ledger is append-only; this entry is the correction, pointing
at where the renaming happened.)

**`BODY-SEMANAS-TARDIAS-1` fixed.** `goals.cerrar_semanas(conn, person_id, *, hoy, desde=None)`
gained `desde`: when given, every week from `lunes_de(desde)` up to (not including) last week --
which `cerrar_semanas` already re-closes on its own -- is re-closed too. Three callers now supply
it:

- **Hosted `--backfill`** (`pull_backfill_hosted`): `_backfill_one_person` now returns `(days
  fetched, oldest day fetched this run)` instead of a bare count (and attaches `.oldest` to a
  raised exception alongside the existing `.saved`, so a mid-run failure still re-closes whatever
  it did fetch). `pull_backfill_hosted` collects these into `desde_por_persona: dict[int, date]`
  and passes it to `_cerrar_semanas_todas(conn, desde_por_persona)`, which now takes that mapping
  and passes each person's own `desde` (or `None`) to `_cerrar_semanas_seguro`. One run's 15-day
  batch (newest first) already reaches back far enough to cross into an older week than last
  week's, so this fires on ordinary backfill runs, not only a deep one.
- **Local `--all`** (`pull_all`): now also returns `(days saved, oldest day saved this run)`;
  `_run` passes that oldest as `desde` to the single `_cerrar_semanas_seguro` call shared by
  `--all`, `--recompute` and the default/`--days`/`--date` pull (the other three paths pass
  `desde=None`, since none of them can land further back than last week).
- **A late habit-check correction** (`body/rutas/metas.py`'s `habit_check` POST): after
  `check_habit` stores the day, if that day's week (`fechas.lunes_de(day)`) is older than last
  week, the route itself calls `goals.weekly_check(conn, goal_id, person_id, week_start)` for that
  one week, in the same request -- a POST, so it may write; a day in this week or last is left to
  the daily pull, which already owns both, so nothing is written for those (kept green by the
  unchanged `tests/test_get_sin_escritura.py` GET-write guard, since this route was already a POST).

## BODY-PERSONA-FUGA-1 -- a black-box guard over BODY-SEGURIDAD-CENSO-1's one recorded unknown
(2026-11-08)

BODY-SEGURIDAD-CENSO-1 named one thing it could not settle by reading: the internal row-level
person-scoping filtering inside `body/history.py`, `body/readiness.py`, `body/turnos_costo.py`,
`body/compartir.py` and `body/household.py` was read as a consistent pattern, never checked
line-by-line against what the app actually renders. This slice builds that check as a black-box
guard, `tests/test_persona_fuga.py`: two invented people (A = person 1, B = person 2), seeded in
every person-owned table with a marker or figure that cannot belong to anyone else, then every
screen, the device-key API and every assistant read tool rendered as each of them in turn. No
leak was found.

**What was seeded**, in `_seed_person`, once per person: `daily_metric` (20 days x 6 metrics,
B's figures far outside any real range -- the spec's own examples, resting HR 187, 98765 steps,
17h43 sleep), `readiness`/`baseline` via the normal `readiness.recompute_all` (never a hand-built
row), `activity`, `sleep_session`, `shift`, `shift_batch`/`shift_batch_item`, `shift_pattern` via
`patron_turnos.guardar`, four `goal` rows covering every status (active metric goal with a habit,
a habit check, a weekly goal_check and a `goal_enlace`; a proposed milestone; an archived/paused
milestone) plus `plan`, `ajuste_agente`, `consentimiento`, `conversacion_agente`/`mensaje_agente`,
a `propuesta_agente` via `agente_propuestas.crear`, `dispositivo`, `garmin_cuenta` (an
obviously-fake token string, `FAKE-TEST-TOKEN-ZZ<tag>-NOT-REAL`, encrypted with a random
per-test `BODY_TOKEN_KEY` -- no real credential anywhere), `inicio_sesion` via
`cuenta.create_session`, and one row each of `raw_payload`, `uso_agente`, `tope_agente`. That is
every table `body/privacidad.py` knows (`FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES | PARTIAL_EXPORT_TABLES |
NEVER_EXPORTED_TABLES`) plus the three reached only through another id (`habit`, `goal_enlace`,
`shift_batch_item`) -- `TableCensusTest` asserts this set is exhaustive and that every one of
those tables has a seeded row, so a new person-owned table added later and left unseeded fails
loudly instead of silently going unchecked. `hogar_miembro` and `figura_compartida` are the two
exceptions -- `compartir.compartir` and `household_of` both require an active household to exist
at all, so these are seeded only once A and B are linked, in the linked-state tests.

**Two markers turned out unusable, and are recorded rather than forced in:**
`shift_batch_item.code` (seeded as `ZZ<tag>-LOTE` for the table census) is read by no screen, API
or export today -- `turnos.py`'s preview and `shifts.html` show only counts and kept-days, and
`privacidad.export_person`'s `shift_batches` section is a plain `SELECT * FROM shift_batch`,
never joined to its items -- so it is excluded from the "must render somewhere" marker list
rather than making that half of the guard vacuous. `plan.title` and `raw_payload.payload` are
likewise seeded for table-census completeness only, read by nothing.

**A figure was tried and measured to self-collide, not assumed:** `resting_hr` was first included
in the set of "figures that must never appear for the other person." Running the suite failed
with `'55' unexpectedly found in` B's own `/privacidad/exportar` response -- A's resting_hr of 55
matched the *seconds* field of that export's own timestamp (`...T18:31:55+00:00`), nothing to do
with A at all. Any one- or two-digit figure is a hostage to every hour/minute/second/day field a
page prints, so the guard's figure set was narrowed to `("steps", "sleep_minutes")` -- both
render with a thousands separator or an "h"/"min" split (`"98.765"`, `"17 h 43"`) that cannot
occur by coincidence, and the raw export carries the same value unformatted (`98765.0`), so no

baseline/Tendencias/Historial realism) but never searched for as leak markers, for the same
reason. The one place this slice does check a `resting_hr` figure is a single targeted `assertIn`
on A's own Hoy page, confirming B's deliberately-shared figure appears there -- a presence check
on one page, where the short-number collision risk does not apply.

**Unlinked sweep** (`UnlinkedSweepTest`, `DeviceAndPropuestaCrossIdTest`): every one of the 26 GET
routes this app has (`RouteSetUnchangedTest` cross-checks that number against
`tests._rutas.rutas_planas(web.app.routes)`, so a new route added later and left off the hand
list fails instead of going unswept), substituting each id-taking route's own id and the other
person's id in turn (`/goals/{id}`, `/asistente/conversacion/{id}`, `/how/{day}`, `/day/{day}`),
the device-key `/api/vida/semana`, and all 11 assistant read tools (`leer_hoy`, `leer_dia`,
`leer_como_calculo`, `leer_tendencias`, `leer_historia`, `leer_metas`, `leer_meta`,
`leer_turnos`, `leer_costo_turnos`, `leer_ajustes`, `leer_tutoriales`) -- run as A looking for B's
markers, then as B looking for A's, well over 25 routes-plus-tools each way (asserted, not just

assistant proposal -- got the same cross-id check goals/habits already had under
BODY-PERSON-SCOPE-1: revoking or acting on the other person's row 404s (or, for device revoke, a
silent same-status no-op whose proof is the untouched `revocado_en` column, not the response
code). Not one foreign marker or figure appeared either way, and every marker/figure DID appear
somewhere for its own owner (a marker that renders nowhere would make the whole guard vacuous,
not a real result).

**Linked and shared sweep** (`LinkedSharingSweepTest`): A and B linked into one household
(`hogar_miembro`), B shares exactly `resting_hr` (`compartir.compartir`) and creates one
household-visibility milestone goal (`ZZB-META-COMPARTIDA`, `kind="milestone"` -- a metric goal

allow-list needed.)

## BODY-ESTILOS-1 -- replace every inline `style="..."` with a class, drop `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`

Every `style="..."` attribute in the 22 templates (201 attributes, measured: `git grep -o
"style=" main -- body/templates | wc -l` == 201, `git grep -o "style=" HEAD -- body/templates |
wc -l` == 0) and every inline `style=` built into server-side SVG by `body/profile.py` and
`body/rutas/metas.py` (20 attributes, same measurement, `main` 20 -> `HEAD` 0) becomes a class in
`body/static/body.css`:

- **Spacing/layout utilities** (`.mt-8`, `.mb-12`, `.gap-10`, `.text-right`, `.flex-1`,
  `.items-end`, `.w-100`, `.block`, `.hidden`, ... -- ~45 classes) for every `margin`, `padding`,
  `display`, `flex`, `gap`, `align-*`/`justify-*`, `width`, `opacity` and `text-align` value an
  inline style had set, each one a fixed value rather than an arbitrary one (a utility class, not
  an escape hatch for new values).
- **A small set of named component classes** for markup-specific shapes that recur: `.settings-row`
  (the tappable settings-list row), `.steps-col`/`.help-link` (the help walkthrough list),
  `.rail-logout-btn`/`.foot-logout-btn` (the two differently-styled logout controls, `all:unset`
  based), `.ayuda-img`, `.chart-svg` (every chart `<svg>`'s `display:block;margin-top:8px`), and
  `.legend-line`/`.legend-dash`/`.legend-today` (the three chart-legend swatch shapes).
- **A fixed data-series palette**, `.c-night`/`.c-night-light`/`.c-body`/`.c-amber`/`.c-info`/
  `.c-est`/`.c-other`/`.c-inset`, each setting `background` (HTML swatches) and `fill` (SVG shapes)
  together to the same token, plus a stroke-only `.stroke-body` (and `.stroke-muted`/`.stroke-line`
  for the two fixed-colour reference lines) for a `<polyline>`/`<line>`, since a `fill` in a `.c-*`
  class would override its own `fill="none"` attribute (an SVG presentation attribute loses to any
  CSS rule, so a stroked line gets its colour only from a `stroke-*` class). The only colours any
  template or server-built SVG ever needed were these eight tokens (sleep stages:
  `body/rutas/hoy.py`'s `STAGES`; training types and month segments: `body/rutas/historial.py`'s
  colour map; the normal-range band and chart line: `body/profile.py` and `body/rutas/metas.py`,
  always called with the one default colour) -- both now carry a palette class name instead of a
  `var(...)` string.
- **Dynamic bars become geometry, not style.** A goal's progress bar (`goals.html`), a day's sleep
  stages (`day.html`) and a month's training segments (`history.html`) were each a `<div>` with a
  `<span>`/`<i>` sized by `style="width:...%"`; each is now an inline `<svg class="bar"|"stage">`
  with `<rect>` elements sized by `width=`/`height=` geometry attributes, which CSP's `style-src`
  does not govern at all.

`body/seguridad.py`'s `content_security_policy()` drops `'unsafe-inline'` from `style-src`, which
now reads `style-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com`. `tests/test_seguridad.py` gained four
guards: no template carries `style=`, no Python-built markup carries `style=` (CSSOM property
*sets* in `body/static/*.js`, e.g. `el.style.display = ...`, are excluded on purpose -- those are
JS, not markup, and are not what `style-src` governs), no static script carries one either, and
`style-src` itself carries no `'unsafe-inline'`. `tests/test_profile.py`'s one assertion on the old
`var(--night)` string is updated to the new class name.

**Stopped BLOCKED, correctly**, on 8 tests outside this slice's `touches:` that assert literal
`style="..."` text for a subject this slice's own diff changed how it renders: `tests/
test_tendencias_todas.py:94,122,154,161`, `tests/test_hogar_compartir_1.py:393`, `tests/
test_pulido_3.py:320-322`, `tests/test_turnos_opcional_3.py:151` (both the `NullSettingTest` and
`SiSettingTest` subclasses of its shared `_SettingChecks` mixin).

**Gate** was not re-run to green past that block (per protocol: a reproducing failure outside
`touches:` is not fixed by widening scope without approval) -- 8 failures recorded, branch
committed at `419129a1b8919252a8270f492c20222bbf84c85f`, not merged.

## BODY-ESTILOS-1-M -- fix 3 measured cascade regressions, add a 4th found by systematic audit, land the 8 tests

ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1 dispatched this slice against BODY-ESTILOS-1's BLOCKED report and
the orchestrator's own browser measurement of the branch at 375px against a computed-style and
layout fingerprint of main (`61cb029df3e39bd5ad6c3d4e99df75c466ba82ad`), which found three visible
regressions -- each the same shape: an inline `style=` always wins the cascade regardless of
specificity, but the class that replaced it does not, so wherever the class it replaced was less
specific than an existing component rule, replacing the attribute with the class let the component
rule win where the attribute used to.

**The three measured fixes:**

| # | Regression | Losing rule (specificity) | Winning rule before fix (specificity) | Fix (selector) | Main value restored |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hoy plan row collapses 82px -> 69px | `.block{display:block}` (0,1,0) | `.plan li{display:flex}` (0,1,1) | `.plan li.block{display:block}` (0,2,1) | `display:block` on both `<li class="block">` in `today.html` (the sleep-score plan row and the household-shared plan row) |
| 2 | Every chart-legend line/dash/today swatch renders as a 10x10 square | `.legend-line`/`.legend-dash`/`.legend-today` (0,1,0) | `.legend i{width:10px;height:10px;...}` (0,1,1) | `.legend i.legend-line`/`.legend i.legend-dash`/`.legend i.legend-today` (0,2,1) | legend-line 10x3px, `vertical-align:3px`; legend-dash 12px wide, 0 tall, 1.6px dashed top border; legend-today 1x12px |
| 3 | `svg.bar` (`/goals`) and `svg.stage` (`/day/{date}`, `/history`) render 100px wide (their `viewBox` width) instead of the card's full width; `svg.bar` also added a ~6px line-box gap under each goal card | no rule set a width or `display:block` on the `<svg>` | (none -- missing declaration, not a losing one) | `svg.bar{display:block;width:100%}`, `svg.stage{display:block;width:100%}` (0,1,1, beats the dead `.bar`/`.stage` single-class rules those two selectors still also match) | full card width (~313px at 375px viewport), no added gap |

**A fourth, found by the audit below, that the browser measurement did not catch:** `today.html`'s
and `shifts.html`'s "no score yet" / "no hero yet" text (`<a class="card est">...<div class="fig
c-muted">`) rendered in `var(--ink)` (full ink) instead of `var(--muted)` (grey) -- main's `style=
"color:var(--muted)"` on that `<div>` beat `.est .fig{color:var(--ink);font-weight:600}` (already
present on main, confirmed: `git show main:body/static/body.css | grep -n ".est .fig"` -> line 75,
unchanged by this branch); the branch's `.c-muted{color:var(--muted)}` (0,1,0) could not, against
`.est .fig` (0,2,0). Fixed with `.est .fig.c-muted{color:var(--muted)}` (0,3,0); `font-weight:600`
was already correct (main's inline style never touched it either).

**Systematic audit.** Every one of the 70 selectors `body/static/body.css`'s BODY-ESTILOS-1 diff
added (`git diff main...feat/body-estilos-1 -- body/static/body.css | grep -cE "^\+[a-zA-Z.][^{]*
\{"` == 70, including the already-compound `table.parts td.p-0` the previous worker had already
fixed) was traced to every actual element it is applied to, across all 22 templates and
`body/profile.py`/`body/rutas/metas.py`, and checked against every pre-existing compound selector
(two classes, or a class + element/pseudo -- `.tabs a` family, `a.card,button.card`, `.grid2 .card`,
`.chip.*`, `.box.done`, `.plan li`, `.list li`, `.costrow .nw`, `.confirm-actions .btn`, `.est
.big,.est .fig`, `.shift .note`/`.shift.*`, `.foot a`, `.legend i`, `.strip-cell.*`, `.strip-legend
.dot.*`, `table.parts th/td` and its `:first-child` compounds, `.asis-* …` descendant rules,
`.tabs .rail-foot`) that could match the same element and set the same property. Beyond the four
fixes above, the only other coincidence found was `.tabs .rail-foot{margin-top:auto}` (0,2,0,
desktop-only) against the new `.mt-auto{margin-top:auto}` (0,1,0) on `base.html`'s logout form
(inside `<nav class="tabs">`): the compound always wins there regardless of the utility class, but
both set the identical value, so there is no visible difference and nothing to fix. No other class
among the 70 matches an element also reached by a higher- or equal-and-later-but-actually-losing
specificity rule setting the same property; 66 of the 70 audited classes needed no change.

**The 8 out-of-touches tests**, each rewritten to assert the class (or SVG class) that now carries
the style, never a literal `style="..."`, same subject:

| Test | Old assertion | New assertion |
|---|---|---|
| `test_tendencias_todas.py:94` | `page.index('<details class="files"')` | `page.index('<details class="files mt-10"')` |
| `test_tendencias_todas.py:122` | `page.index('class="legend"', start)` | `page.index('class="legend mt-4"', start)` |
| `test_tendencias_todas.py:154` | `assertIn('<details class="files" style="margin-top:10px" open>', page)` | `assertIn('<details class="files mt-10" open>', page)` |
| `test_tendencias_todas.py:161` | `assertIn('<details class="files" style="margin-top:10px">', page)` | `assertIn('<details class="files mt-10">', page)` |
| `test_hogar_compartir_1.py:393` | `assertIn('<details class="files" style="margin-top:6px">', r.text)` | `assertIn('<details class="files mt-6">', r.text)` |
| `test_pulido_3.py:320-322` | `assertRegex(r.text, r'<a href="/ayuda" class="card" style="[^"]*min-height:44px[^"]*">')` (x3, `/privacidad`, `/ajustes/asistente`) | `assertIn('<a href="/ayuda" class="card settings-row">', r.text)` (x3) |
| `test_turnos_opcional_3.py:151` (`NullSettingTest`, `SiSettingTest`) | `assertIn("fill:var(--night)", r.text)` / else `assertNotIn(...)` | `assertIn('class="c-night op-18"', r.text)` / else `assertNotIn(...)` |

No assertion was deleted without a replacement checking the same structural outcome; all four
files are now within `touches:` and pass.

**`docs/DESIGN.md`** (security section, rule 13): the stale "remaining gap: `style-src` still
carries `'unsafe-inline'`" note and the stale policy string (which still listed `'unsafe-inline'`)
are corrected to the landed state, and the compound-selector trap is written down as a standing
rule: spacing/layout through the named utility classes, data-series colour only through the fixed
palette classes, never a `style=` attribute anywhere; a utility or modifier class meant to override
a component rule that is itself a compound selector must be written as a compound selector too, so
it wins on specificity rather than on source order; an inline `<svg>` replacing a block `<div>`
needs its own `display:block; width:100%`.

## BODY-FUENTES-PROPIAS-1 -- self-host Hanken Grotesk, drop Google Fonts (except the font files)

Closes the open follow-up above: the served policy no longer reaches `fonts.googleapis.com` or
`fonts.gstatic.com` for the typeface, the last two third-party origins this app loaded.

**Source and hashes.** The three files -- `hanken-grotesk-latin-wght-normal.woff2`,
`hanken-grotesk-latin-ext-wght-normal.woff2`, `LICENSE` -- were copied byte-for-byte with
`shutil.copyfile` from `C:\Duna\duna-admin-ui\src\fonts\hanken-grotesk\` (the same files Duna's
console commits, `ADMIN-FUENTES-LOCALES-1`, commit `fcd45ad1`), verified on disk:
sha256 `e9201eddf1d41d0b62253295d869ce3cf65768f7102b797f02c7f8c876b4a9d5` (latin),
`768af2923e0ab1549f1dfba0a5c8ea749c4c01f01d8e77ffaf7fcd12f57a0a24` (latin-ext),
`ef8780a5a0864714268dd7b6e00de9b39605a1dd61650ed2fa0af9b79b857967` (LICENSE).

**Unicode ranges.** Each `@font-face` rule in `body/static/body.css` carries the well-known Google
Fonts `latin` / `latin-ext` `unicode-range` values (no local source states the exact ranges these
two files were built with). Spanish never triggers the latin-ext download: the latin subset's own
`U+0000-00FF` already covers every accented character Spanish uses.

**Templates changed.** `base.html` and the four standalone pages (`acceso_rechazado.html`,
`consentimiento.html`, `origen_rechazado.html`, `sin_acceso.html`) each drop the
`<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">` and the Google Fonts stylesheet
`<link>`, replaced by `<link rel="preload" href="/static/fonts/hanken-grotesk/hanken-grotesk-
latin-wght-normal.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>`, so the latin file starts
loading with the HTML, as Google's CSS used to.

**MIME registration.** `body/web.py` calls `mimetypes.add_type("font/woff2", ".woff2")` before the
`/static` mount: Python's `mimetypes` has no `.woff2` entry by default (measured
`mimetypes.guess_type("x.woff2")` == `(None, None)`), which would otherwise serve the font as a
guessed type instead of `font/woff2`.

**Policy, before and after.** `body/seguridad.py`'s `_CSP_FIXED_DIRECTIVES`:
`style-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com` / `font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com` ->
`style-src 'self'` / `font-src 'self'`, with no `https:` origin for either directive any more.

**Guards, with their bite proof.** `tests/test_fuentes_propias.py` (new): (a) each font file is
served at `/static/fonts/hanken-grotesk/<name>` as `font/woff2`, byte-identical to disk; (b) no
template and no static file names `fonts.googleapis.com` or `fonts.gstatic.com` -- non-vacuous,
proved to bite on `main` `4d7a8cc` (5 templates, 10 occurrences, before this slice's own fix); (c)
the served policy's `style-src` and `font-src` are `'self'` alone; (d) the rendered base page
carries the preload link for the latin file; (e) the OFL licence ships beside the font files,
hash-pinned. `tests/test_seguridad.py`'s CSP string pin updated to match.

**What this slice did NOT include, and why.** The three font files stayed on disk, untracked,
sha256-verified correct: this repository's global `core.autocrlf=true` plus its blanket
`.gitattributes` (`* text eol=lf`) rewrites the binary `.woff2` bytes and the CRLF `LICENSE` on
`git add` (measured 34704 -> 34702 bytes for the latin `.woff2`, 4623 -> 4530 for `LICENSE`), so
the committed blob would not match the hashes above. Fixing it needs a `.gitattributes` entry
marking these paths binary, outside this slice's `touches:`, or a git-config change, forbidden to
this slice. Stopped `BLOCKED` at commit `ad4b4532aef43e70c65377e6b373e0bb7d559c2d`, correctly --
finished by `BODY-FUENTES-PROPIAS-1-M` below.

## BODY-FUENTES-PROPIAS-1-M -- .gitattributes stops git rewriting binary font bytes

Finishes `BODY-FUENTES-PROPIAS-1`: commits the three font files it left on disk, byte-exact.

**The corruption mechanism, measured.** This machine's `core.autocrlf=true`, together with
body-app's only `.gitattributes` line (`* text eol=lf`), makes `git` treat every path -- including
binary `.woff2` files and the CRLF `LICENSE` -- as text and normalise its line endings on `git
add`. The previous worker measured 2 bytes lost from each `.woff2` and 93 from `LICENSE` in the
staged blobs (restated above in raw byte counts: 34704 -> 34702, 4623 -> 4530). These are the
first binary files this repository has ever tracked, which is why the rule never mattered before.

**Attributes added**, below the unchanged first line `* text eol=lf`: `*.woff2 binary`,
`*.woff binary`, `*.ttf binary`, `*.otf binary`, `*.png binary`, `*.jpg binary`, `*.jpeg binary`,
`*.gif binary`, `*.ico binary`, `*.webp binary`, `*.pdf binary`, `*.sqlite binary`, `*.db binary`,
and `body/static/fonts/**/LICENSE -text` (the licence is stored exactly as published, CRLF
included, so its hash matches the source) -- with a comment above explaining why. `git diff --stat
-- .gitattributes` showed only insertions (18 lines added, none removed or changed), confirming
`* text eol=lf` stayed first and no existing rule was altered.

**`git check-attr` gap.** The spec's verification step, `git check-attr -a -- <path>`, required
interactive approval this non-interactive dispatch could not grant (the verb is not in this
worker's git grant list: add, branch, cat-file, check-ignore, checkout, commit, diff, log,
ls-tree, merge, merge-base, rev-parse, rm, show, status, switch -- `check-ignore` is granted,
`check-attr` is not). Verified instead by the stronger, authoritative check the spec itself also
asks for: the staged and committed blob hashes below, which can only match if `binary`/`-text`
actually took effect -- a corrupted blob would not reproduce the exact bytes of the source files.

**Staged hashes** (`git cat-file -p :<path>`, before commit) -- all three equal the hashes above:
latin `e9201ed...b4a9d5`, latin-ext `768af29...57a0a24`, LICENSE `ef8780a...b857967`.

**Committed hashes** (`git cat-file -p HEAD:<path>`, after commit `0f813b1f7b307f85234e20345fff
d2f27afa4fd6`) and the **working-tree files** -- both equal the same three hashes, for all three
files.

**New test.** `tests/test_fuentes_propias.py` gained `TrackedBlobByteExactTest`: for each of the
three files, runs `git cat-file -p HEAD:<path>` via `subprocess` from the test process (skipped,
with a stated reason, only when `git` is not on `PATH` or the repository has no `.git` directory)
and asserts the sha256 of its stdout equals the expected value. A future `.gitattributes` change
that lets `git` rewrite these bytes again now goes red instead of silently corrupting the tracked
blob.

**Gate**, on the committed tree `0f813b1f7b307f85234e20345fffd2f27afa4fd6`, command
`.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`: `Ran 1320 tests in 178.615s ...
OK (skipped=1)` -- 1319 non-skipped against the previous worker's 1318, the +1 being the new test
method above; no other drift.

## BODY-RENDIMIENTO-1 -- the schema is made ready once per process per DB file, not on every request

Stage one of `BODY-RENDIMIENTO-OBS-1` (OBSERVED, base `cc38a840060a6d77c026734e02eb0217bbff53a9`), which measured
`db.init(conn)` running on every one of 7 per-request call sites: `identity.py:54`
(`current_person_id`), `identity.py:87` (`person_from_device`), `rutas/comun.py:87` (`_ctx`),
`rutas/sesion.py:46,61,90,116` -- the five guarded migrations, `executescript(SCHEMA)` (48
`CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS`), `_migrate`, a 48-row `METRIC_DEFS` upsert and an `INSERT OR IGNORE`
of person 1, then a `COMMIT`, on two connections, every page view.

**The fix.** `body/db.py` gained `ensure_ready(conn)`: runs `init(conn)` the first time this
process meets a DB file, a no-op after. Keyed on `(resolved_path, os.stat(path).st_ino)` -- the
file's identity, read from `PRAGMA database_list` plus `os.stat` -- not on the `Connection` object
or the path string alone, so a test that points `config.DB_PATH` at a fresh temp dir, or deletes
and recreates the file, gets a new key and is made ready again even from the same process (proven:
`os.stat().st_ino` differs after delete+recreate on this NTFS volume, measured directly). Guarded
by one `threading.Lock` held across the whole check-then-init-then-mark sequence (routes run in a
threadpool, and `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` plus the upserts are idempotent, but serializing the
rare first touch is simpler than reasoning about two concurrent `init()` runs). All 7 per-request
sites now call `ensure_ready`, never `init` directly; `init` itself is unchanged and keeps its 6
CLI callers (precios, demo, pull, shift_import, vida_export, vincular_cuenta) untouched, each
already calling it once per process.

**Before -> after, measured on this slice's own populated fixture** (`demo._seed(dias=30)` + one
assistant conversation), with `tests._rutas.contar_sql` tracing every connection the app opens:

- **Before** (proven by temporarily reverting the 3 call sites back to `db.init(conn)` and running
  `tests/test_get_sin_escritura.py`'s new statement-level assertion against that reverted tree,
  then restoring the fix -- see "the guard" below): every one of the 20 non-404 GET routes ran 86
  write statements per request (43 for the 3 routes that 404 before reaching a screen in local
  mode but still open a connection) -- `init()`'s own migrations/schema/upserts, every time,
  regardless of the route's own work.
- **After**: 0 write statements on every GET route (see the ceilings table below for the full
  per-route statement/connection count). No route opens more than 2 connections; most open 2
  (`comun._ctx`'s connection plus `identity.current_person_id`'s own), a few 404 before opening a
  second.

**busy_timeout.** `db.connect()` now sets `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000` right after
`PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`: a reader that collides with the daily pull's or the assistant's write
used to fail at once (SQLite's default busy behaviour); it now waits up to 5s for the writer to
finish. Stores nothing in the database file -- not a journal-mode change (`BODY-RENDIMIENTO-WAL-1`,
below, is the journal-mode question, deliberately not touched here).

**Local person after a deletion.** `/privacidad/borrar` (`body/rutas/privacidad.py`'s
`privacidad_borrar`) carries no `cuenta.hosted()` gate, unlike the consent routes right above it in
the same file -- local mode CAN reach it, and `privacidad.delete_person` ends with
`DELETE FROM person WHERE id = ?`. Before this slice, the NEXT request's unconditional `db.init(conn)`
silently re-created person 1 (`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO person ...`) before anything else ran, so the
gap was invisible. With `ensure_ready` making the schema ready only once, nothing would otherwise
notice person 1 is gone. Fixed in `db.local_person_id` (`body/db.py`): a `SELECT` first, an
`INSERT OR IGNORE` only when absent, so the normal path (the row already exists) writes nothing.
Pinned by `tests/test_privacidad.py`'s `LocalPersonRecreatedAfterDeleteTest`: GET `/` works, POST
`/privacidad/borrar` with the confirmation word deletes person 1, GET `/` works again and person 1
exists again. Proven to bite: reverting `local_person_id` to its old one-line body and re-running
this test gave `AssertionError: 500 != 200` on the second GET `/`; restoring the fix made it pass
again.

**The guard, widened to the statement level** (`tests/test_get_sin_escritura.py`). Content-dump
comparison alone cannot see a write that leaves every row unchanged -- `init()`'s own
`INSERT OR IGNORE`/upsert statements did exactly that on every request before this slice, invisible
to the old guard's `_dump()` compare. `tests/_rutas.py` gained `contar_sql()`: wraps
`sqlite3.connect` for its duration (the only way the app reaches it is through `body.db.connect`),
traces every connection with `set_trace_callback`, and counts statements whose verb is INSERT,
UPDATE, DELETE, REPLACE, CREATE, ALTER or DROP, plus a COMMIT that followed one. The sweep now
calls `db.ensure_ready` (not `db.init`) in its fixture, so first-touch setup is made ready BEFORE
the sweep starts and is never counted as a route's own write; each route call is wrapped in its own
`contar_sql()` so counts never leak between routes. Both the old content-dump compare and the new
statement-count assertion are kept (`before != after` and `stats["writes"]`), against the same
`_ALLOWED_WRITE_PATHS` allow-list (`/login`, `/login/cuenta/start`, inert in local mode).
**Bite proof**: with the 3 call sites temporarily reverted to `db.init(conn)` (db.py's
`ensure_ready`/`busy_timeout`/`local_person_id` left as this slice leaves them -- irrelevant to
this proof, since the reverted routes never call `ensure_ready` at all), the new assertion failed
with 20 offending routes, each showing a non-zero write count: `/ayuda`, `/privacidad/consentimiento`
(404, 43), `/privacidad`, `/privacidad/exportar`, `/ajustes/dispositivos` (404, 43), `/settings`,
`/ajustes/asistente`, `/asistente/conversacion/{conversacion_id}`, `/goals`, `/goals/new`,
`/goals/{goal_id}`, `/shifts`, `/shifts/como`, `/shifts/patron`, `/`, `/how/{day}`, `/day/{day}`,
`/trends`, `/history`, `/garmin` (404, 43) -- every other route ran 86 writes. Restoring the fix
made the assertion pass (0 writes on every route); full output of both runs is in this session's
transcript, not pasted here (no health figure in either -- these are statement counts only).

**A cost ceiling** (new file, `tests/test_rendimiento.py`). Reuses `tests._rutas.contar_sql` and
`rutas_planas`; its own `_reset_db`/`_seed`/`_fill` mirror the GET guard's fixture (same
`demo._seed(dias=30, idioma="es")` + one conversation, no real figure). For every GET route,
measured statements and connections per request on that fixture, right after this slice's fix,
then set each ceiling to the measured value plus headroom (so a small, legitimate change to a
route does not make the test flaky). Non-vacuous: asserts the app's whole GET-route path set
equals the ceiling table's key set, not just a count match.

| route | measured statements | ceiling | connections |
