## BODY-RENDIMIENTO-2 -- one in-memory reader for a person's metrics over a window

Slice 2 of BODY-RENDIMIENTO-OBS-1. After BODY-RENDIMIENTO-1, `/shifts` still ran ~307 statements
on this repo's own fixture: `body/rutas/turnos.py`'s `_turnos_strip` called `readiness.compute`
once per day for 56 strip days (6-7 queries each: the day's own values, yesterday's stress, and up
to four `baselines.baseline` calls, each a 30-day `db.series` window), and `body/turnos_costo.py`'s
`resumen` called `db.series` once per metric per block (`_costo_bloque`, 5 metrics) and
`db.day_values` once per candidate day per block (`_dia_en_banda`/`_recuperacion_bloque`, up to 20
days per block), on top of its own `referencia` (5 more `db.series` calls).

**The reader.** `body/lector.py`'s `Lector(conn, person_id, desde, hasta, metrics)` (new module,
Tier 2) loads every one of `metrics` over `[desde, hasta]` with one SELECT per metric against
`daily_metric` -- its own read-only query, the same columns `db.series` reads, so `body/lector.py`
never imports `body/db.py` (Tier 1). It answers `series(metric, start, end)` and `day_values(day)`
from that in-memory dict with EXACTLY `db.series`/`db.day_values`'s own semantics (same keys, same
inclusive bounds via plain ISO-string comparison, same missing-day behaviour, same value types);
`day_values` is restricted to the metrics the reader was built with, which every call site here
already reads through a fixed, known metric list, so the restriction changes nothing a caller sees.

**Call sites.** `readiness.compute` and `baselines.baseline` take `lector` as an optional keyword
(default `None`, the original per-call queries -- every caller that does not loop over days, e.g.
`body/rutas/hoy.py`'s single-day calls, `body/goals.py`, `body/rutas/metas.py`, is unchanged).
`readiness.METRICS` names the six metrics a `compute` call can touch (`hrv_last_night`,
`sleep_minutes`, `sleep_need_min`, `body_battery_wake`, `resting_hr`, `stress_avg`) -- the set a
caller builds a `Lector` with before looping `compute` over many days. `_turnos_strip` builds ONE
`Lector` for the whole 56-day strip, window `[start - 31, today_local]` (30 days of
`baselines.WINDOW_DAYS` plus one extra day: the stress part's baseline is computed on YESTERDAY,
so the earliest strip day's own window reaches one day further back than `WINDOW_DAYS` alone --
found by a failing equality test, not reasoned out in advance) and passes it through every
`readiness.compute` call. `turnos_costo.referencia`, `_costo_bloque`, `_dia_en_banda` and
`_recuperacion_bloque` take the same optional `lector` keyword; `resumen` builds ONE `Lector` over
`[hoy - RESUMEN_DIAS, hoy + dias_estables]` (wide enough for `referencia`'s own
`[hoy - REFERENCIA_DIAS, hoy - 1]`, since `REFERENCIA_DIAS <= RESUMEN_DIAS`, and for every block's
cost and recovery window, none of which reaches past `hoy + dias_estables`) and threads it through
all four. `body/rutas/hoy.py` needed no change: its Turnos card calls `turno_de_hoy` (which calls
`resumen`, already reader-backed) and `readiness.compute` only once per request, never in a loop --
checked directly, not assumed.

**Equality, not approximation.** Every number stays pinned to the pre-reader path:
- `tests/test_baselines.py` (new): `baseline()` with and without a `Lector`, matching and no-baseline cases.
- `tests/test_readiness.py`: `compute()` with and without a `Lector`, a normal day and a too-little-data day,
  field by field (score, version, missing, every part's value/reference/subscore/weight).
- `tests/test_turnos_costo.py`'s new `LectorEqualityTest`: `referencia`, `_costo_bloque`, `_dia_en_banda`
  and `_recuperacion_bloque`, each with and without a `Lector`.
- `tests/test_rendimiento_turnos.py` (new), a richer fixture (~220 days, three night blocks of
  different lengths, two day-shift blocks, one day in five left as a gap): every one of the 56
  strip days' `readiness.compute` matches field by field; `resumen()` matches for several `hoy`
  values, including one before any night block (`motivo == "sin_turnos"`) and ones landing inside
  the fixture's gaps; and `/shifts`' own rendered HTML is byte-identical with the reader against a
  test-only switch -- patching the `Lector` name in both `body.rutas.turnos` and `body.turnos_costo`
  (where each is imported) to a stub returning `None`, which forces every `lector=` kwarg this
  slice added back onto its original, unchanged branch.

**Statements, this repo's own fixture** (`demo._seed(dias=30, idioma="es")` + one assistant
conversation, same fixture `tests/test_rendimiento.py` already used):

| route | before | after | new ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/shifts` | 307 | 38 | 50 |
| `/shifts/como` | 35 | 19 | 25 |
| `/` | 55 | 55 (unchanged -- single day, no loop) | 75 (unchanged) |

`tests/test_rendimiento.py`'s `_CEILINGS["/shifts"]` and `["/shifts/como"]` drop from their old
400/46 (`/shifts` carried its own much-higher ceiling with a comment naming this slice) to 50/25 --
the same ~30% margin rule as every other route. `/` keeps its existing ceiling: `_hoy_turno_ctx`
and the single `readiness.compute` call there never loop over days, so this slice made no change

**docs/DESIGN.md**: a new sentence under rule 13's `(BODY-RENDIMIENTO-1)` paragraph -- a screen that

## BODY-RENDIMIENTO-3 -- the app compresses pages in transit, /static is cached forever by its hash

Surface (BODY-RENDIMIENTO-OBS-1, measured by the orchestrator on `main` `7febf4f`): the LAN gets
every page uncompressed (only the hosted copy is compressed, by Caddy); `/static` files already
carry a content hash in their own URL but the mount still answers only with ETag/Last-Modified, so
every page view makes a conditional request for `body.css`, the scripts and the font. Decision
recorded there and binding here: Tendencias' own markup is NOT changed in this slice.

**Middleware, `body/web.py`.** Starlette (installed) `1.10.0`. `GZipMiddleware` (from
`starlette.middleware.gzip`, re-exported by `fastapi.middleware.gzip`), `minimum_size=1000`, added
between `_CaminoActualMiddleware` and `SeguridadMiddleware`'s `add_middleware` calls. Starlette
prepends each `add_middleware` call so the LAST one added ends up OUTERMOST (the existing comment
on `RequestLogMiddleware` already said so); the result, outer to inner:
`RequestLogMiddleware -> SeguridadMiddleware -> GZipMiddleware -> _CaminoActualMiddleware -> routes`.
GZip sits next to the routes and the `/static` mount so it compresses the actual bytes they
produce; `SeguridadMiddleware` wraps it, so its send-wrapper appends the fixed security-header set
(`X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, the CSP, `Cross-Origin-Opener-
Policy`) onto whatever GZip already sent (`Content-Encoding`, `Vary`, a recomputed
`Content-Length`) -- different header names, no conflict, proven by
`SecurityHeadersSurviveGzipTest`. `RequestLogMiddleware` stays outermost, unchanged invariant (a
`SeguridadMiddleware` refusal still reaches the log).

**Streaming exclusion (1a).** The assistant's answer is `body/rutas/asistente.py`'s
`asistente_preguntar` (`POST /asistente/preguntar`), a `StreamingResponse` with
`media_type="text/event-stream"`. This installed Starlette version's `GZipMiddleware` already
excludes `text/event-stream` (and `font/woff2`) by default
(`DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_CONTENT_TYPES`, `starlette/middleware/gzip.py`), so no Body-specific exclusion
code was written -- the cleanest means available was to rely on the default rather than add to or
override it. Read from `starlette/middleware/gzip.py`'s `IdentityResponder.send_with_compression`:
when the content type is excluded, every `http.response.start` and `http.response.body` message is
forwarded with `await self.send(message)` immediately, one inbound chunk to one outbound message,
same as an uncompressed response -- never buffered. `AssistantStreamKeepsStreamingTest` proves this
through the real app and the `demo` provider's two-round, three-event exchange (`herramienta`,
`texto`, `fin`): the response carries no `Content-Encoding`, and the three events arrive as 3 or
more separate raw chunks (`r.iter_raw()`), not one chunk at the end.

**Compression (1b/1c), measured** (demo data built for this slice: 150 days times every
`comun.TREND_KEYS` and `TREND_GROUPS` key, invented values, no real health figure):

| route | plain | gzip | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/trends?r=90` | 555,555 B | 26,848 B | 0.048 |
| `/trends` (all) | 58,973 B | 4,811 B | 0.082 |
| `/trends?m=2026-02` | 192,495 B | 10,576 B | 0.055 |

(figures measured in-process against this slice's own fixture, not the orchestrator's surface
fixture -- same property, different data, so the absolute bytes differ from the surface's
459 KB/174 KB/45 KB; both agree the page is highly repetitive and compresses many-fold.)
`TrendsGzipRoundTripTest` proves, against the real app: a request carrying `Accept-Encoding: gzip`
gets back `Content-Encoding: gzip` and a `Vary` header naming `Accept-Encoding`, and
`gzip.decompress` of the raw response equals the plain body byte for byte; a request that sends an
empty `Accept-Encoding` gets the plain body straight, with no `Content-Encoding` at all.

**Hosted, Caddy (1d), no network -- from `encode gzip`'s documented behaviour**
(`deploy/host/Caddyfile.body:6`): Caddy's `encode` directive does not apply its own compression to
a response that already carries a `Content-Encoding` header -- it is written to avoid double-
encoding an upstream that already compressed, not to compress on top of it. Since Body's own
`GZipMiddleware` already sets `Content-Encoding: gzip` on a compressible response before Caddy
ever sees it, Caddy passes that response through unchanged; it only compresses the (rarer)
response Body left uncompressed (below `minimum_size`, or an excluded content type that Caddy's
own default exclusions do not also cover).

**BREACH oracle, decided.** The question: what secret, if any, sits in a Body page next to
attacker-reflected input, now that the page is compressed (Body has no CSRF token in forms; same-
origin checks are by Origin/Host, `body/seguridad.py`). Searched the one genuine secret any Body
page ever renders: `body/rutas/dispositivos.py`'s `dispositivos_crear` (`POST
/ajustes/dispositivos`) puts a freshly-minted device bearer key into `dispositivos.html`'s
`new_key`. It is not a BREACH target: (1) it is a brand-new, single-use secret each time the route
runs, not a stable one repeated across many probes -- BREACH needs the SAME secret present across
many requests while only the attacker-controlled part varies; (2) the route is a POST, an unsafe
method, refused cross-site before any handler runs by `SeguridadMiddleware`'s Origin/Referer check,
so an attacker cannot trigger it from another origin at all; (3) its response carries
`Cache-Control: no-store`; (4) no other part of that same response reflects open-ended attacker-
chosen text next to the key -- the only user-supplied string on the page (the device's own name)
is typed by the account holder on their own page, not a remote attacker's repeatable input. No
other Body page echoes free-form, attacker-controlled text into rendered markup at all (query
params that reach templates are dates/ids, validated and narrow, never raw text). Decision: no
route is excluded from compression for BREACH; none carries the shape BREACH needs.

**Static caching (2), `body/web.py`'s `_StaticConCache(StaticFiles)`**, the file where the `/static`
mount lives: overrides `file_response` only, which runs before the base class decides between the
full `FileResponse` and a 304 `NotModifiedResponse` -- setting `Cache-Control` there covers both,
since `NotModifiedResponse.NOT_MODIFIED_HEADERS` already carries `cache-control` through. A request
whose `v` query parameter equals the CURRENT `comun.STATIC_HASH` gets
`public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; any other `v` (absent, stale, or foreign) gets `no-cache`,
falling back to the ETag/Last-Modified revalidation the mount already did. `/sw.js` is untouched
(still `no-cache`, `body/rutas/pwa.py`) -- it is not a hashed `/static` URL. The web app manifest
(`manifest.webmanifest`) is a plain `/static` file loaded through `static_url` like any other
(`base.html`'s `<link rel="manifest">`), so it gets the same rule automatically, no special case.
`StaticCachingTest` proves all three outcomes for `body.css`, `charts.js` and the self-hosted
`.woff2` font. Every template's `static_url` output already uses the current hash by construction
(`static_url` appends `comun.STATIC_HASH` itself, pinned by `tests/test_static_version.py`'s
existing `StaticUrlTest`) -- nothing to extend there; this slice re-ran that module to confirm
(green).

**docs/DESIGN.md**: a new `(BODY-RENDIMIENTO-3)` paragraph under rule 13, next to the existing
`static_url`/CSP material -- the app compresses pages itself (so the LAN gets it too), the
streaming exclusion is Starlette's default, the `/static` caching rule, and the manifest following
the same rule with no special case.

## BODY-FUENTE-CACHE-1 -- fonts are cached forever by path, with or without `v`

BODY-RENDIMIENTO-3's `_StaticConCache` only granted the forever `Cache-Control` to a request whose
`v` matched `comun.STATIC_HASH`. The self-hosted font (BODY-FUENTES-PROPIAS-1) has no `v` and
cannot easily get one: it is referenced from `body/static/body.css`'s two `@font-face` rules
(`src:url(/static/fonts/hanken-grotesk/...woff2)`), and `body.css` is a static file, not a
template, so it cannot call `static_url`. `base.html`'s preload link (and every other template
that preloads the latin font) uses that same literal, unversioned URL -- it must stay byte-identical
to the `@font-face` URL or the preload is wasted.

**The rule, and why it is safe.** A font file is immutable by its path alone, so it does not need a
`v` to earn the forever-cache: every byte under `body/static/fonts/` is already pinned by sha256 in
`tests/test_fuentes_propias.py` (the two `.woff2` files and the LICENSE), so an in-place change to
any of them already fails the gate before this slice, and a new font version has to ship under a
new path (a new file or directory name) with its own pinned hash -- it can never silently replace
bytes an old cached copy still points at. `body/web.py`'s `_StaticConCache.file_response` now treats
any request whose resolved on-disk path falls under `body/static/fonts/` as immutable regardless of
`v`, alongside the existing `v == comun.STATIC_HASH` rule; `_FUENTES_DIR` is the one `fonts/`
directory this checks against, resolved once at import time.

**The guard.** BODY-RENDIMIENTO-3 and BODY-FUENTES-PROPIAS-1 already pinned the three files under
`body/static/fonts/hanken-grotesk/` by sha256, each in its own test. This slice adds
`EveryFontFileIsPinnedTest` (`tests/test_fuentes_propias.py`): it walks `body/static/fonts/`
recursively, compares the set of relative paths found against `_FUENTES_DIR_FILES` (the same three
pinned hashes, gathered once), and asserts they are equal -- not just that every known file is
pinned, but that nothing new on disk is UNpinned -- then re-hashes every pinned file and asserts the
count checked equals the count found on disk. A new font file added without a pinned hash fails
this test before it can reach `main`.

**Tests** (`tests/test_rendimiento_red.py`): `StaticCachingTest` is split into `VERSIONED_PATHS`
(`body.css`, `charts.js`, which still revalidate with no `v` or a stale `v`) and `FONT_PATH` (the
latin `.woff2`, which is asserted immutable in all three cases -- current `v`, no `v`, stale `v`).

**docs/DESIGN.md**: a new `(BODY-FUENTE-CACHE-1)` paragraph under rule 13, next to the existing
`(BODY-RENDIMIENTO-3)` caching material -- a font is immutable by path, which is what lets it share
the forever-cache with no `v`, and a font update arrives under a new path with its hash pinned and
`body.css` plus every preload link changed together.

**Gate**, once, foreground, on the slice commit: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover
tests -t .` -- `Ran 1344 tests in 151.375s ... OK (skipped=1)`. 1344 = BODY-RENDIMIENTO-3's own
floor of 1343 plus this slice's one new test (`StaticCachingTest`'s four methods are renamed/
rewritten in place, net zero; `EveryFontFileIsPinnedTest` adds one); reconciled, not re-derived.

**Merge.** `git merge --no-ff feat/body-fuente-cache-1` onto `main` (prior tip
`cc7139cdfc2b0290a05738a042fc1c92eb5c6eea`), producing merge commit
`56e118ef25e09c349f798ea322d899bec283cafb`. The merge tree and the branch tree are the same tree --
`HEAD^{tree}` and `feat/body-fuente-cache-1^{tree}` both equal
`ac37e92ad0877ccfddcece0bbc36ab7a7081c472`, so the diff between them is empty and the gate above,
run on the slice commit `182596fba23691d14a2183cbe7a2d4558336f8ac` whose tree is this same tree,

## BODY-ESTADOS-VACIOS-1 -- every screen swept for a sparse or brand-new person, not just
Carlos-with-871-days

The existing GET sweeps (`tests/test_get_sin_escritura.py`, `tests/test_persona_fuga.py`,
`tests/test_rendimiento.py`) all run on ONE populated fixture (`body/demo.py`'s seed, 30+ days,
every metric, shifts, goals). None of them had ever rendered the whole app for a sparse or empty
person, so a `None`, a `nan`, a crash or an empty chart frame on a fresh account would first be
seen by a real person -- this slice's own surface statement. `tests/test_estados_vacios.py` closes
that gap with a guard; it found nothing to fix.

**The seven states**, each built with the same low-level helpers the other sweeps use
(`db.set_metric`, direct `shift`/`goal`/`habit` rows, `db.set_trabaja_turnos`), each seeded TWICE
(once `language='es'`, once `'en'`) -- 14 person rows in all:

| state | shape |
|---|---|
| A | brand new: a `person` row only -- no metrics, no shifts, no goals, no devices |
| B | one day of data, today, every metric a watch can send (`body/demo.py`'s own `CORE_DENSE + SECONDARY + CARDIO_SPARSE` catalogue, one invented value per key -- the midpoint of `demo.RANGES`, never a real figure) |
| C | 20 days with ONLY `sleep_minutes` -- a watch/setting sending some metrics but not others |
| D | `trabaja_turnos = 1`, zero `shift` rows, zero metrics -- the `"sin_datos_reloj"` reason code's own path |
| D2 | `trabaja_turnos = 1`, one 3-night confirmed block 6-4 days ago, zero daily_metric rows before or after it |
| E | an active metric goal on `vo2max` (zero `daily_metric` rows for that key, ever) plus an active milestone goal with one habit and zero `habit_check` rows |
| F | 10 days of a full metric set, all of them 49-40 days before today -- the last-sync-40-days-ago state |

**The sweep**: every GET route `tests/_rutas.rutas_planas` finds on `body.web.app` (26 routes,
measured by the same `RouteSetUnchangedTest`-style assertion the other sweeps use), for each of the
14 person rows, with `/day/{day}` and `/how/{day}` parameterised on that state's own plausible days
(today, or -- for C/D2/F -- the day that actually exercises the sparse/gap shape: C's first and
last sleep day, D2's night-block start and the first data-free day after it, F's stale last-sync
day and today) and `/goals/{goal_id}` parameterised on E's two goal ids. `/asistente/conversacion/
{conversacion_id}` is excluded (needs a seeded conversation, `body/agente` is outside this slice's
`touches`) and `/api/vida/semana` always 404s in local mode before any person is resolved
(`identity.person_from_device` raises `HTTPException(404)` ahead of `cuenta.hosted()` even being
read) -- neither is a coverage gap this slice leaves silently open, both are named in the test
module's own docstring. **352** (route x state x language) calls total, measured by
`tests/_isolate`-isolated run, never re-derived by hand:

    A/es 24  A/en 24  B/es 24  B/en 24  C/es 26  C/en 26  D/es 24  D/en 24
    D2/es 26 D2/en 26 E/es 26  E/en 26  F/es 26  F/en 26

**Per call**, for a 200: no `Traceback`, `undefined`, or a bare word-boundary `None`/`nan`/`NaN`/
`inf` (checked on every response, HTML or JSON, since a computed-NaN float could leak into the
JSON export too); on an HTML response only, no literal `{{`, `}}`, `{%`, `[]` or `{}` (an empty list
or dict is an ordinary JSON value on `/privacidad/exportar`, and `/sw.js`'s own `}}` is plain
JavaScript -- both excluded by content-type, not by an allow-list: no allow-list was needed in
practice) and no `<polyline points="...">` with fewer than 2 coordinate pairs. Per route: status
200, or the route's own documented answer -- 404 for every hosted-only route in local mode
(`/garmin`, `/ajustes/dispositivos`, `/login`, `/login/cuenta/start`, `/login/cuenta/callback`,
`/privacidad/consentimiento`, `/api/vida/semana`), 404 for `/shifts`, `/shifts/como`,
`/shifts/patron` when `trabaja_turnos_si` is false (every state but D/D2), 200 otherwise.
Non-vacuous: all 14 state/language rows reach `/` with 200, asserted by name, and the total swept
count is asserted well above a token sample.

**Result: zero defects.** No crash, no raw-value leak, no short polyline turned up anywhere in the
352 calls -- confirmed by hand on three of the more exposed shapes (F's `/` with a 40-day-stale
day, D's `/shifts` with the toggle on and nothing in it, E's `/goals/{id}` with a zero-data metric
chart): each renders its own honest-gap sentence (e.g. "Aún no hay turnos... puedes escribir tu
propio patrón aquí", "Aún no hay datos de tu reloj para calcular esto", "Aún sin datos
suficientes") rather than a blank, a zero or a crash. This slice's own approval
(`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`) authorised fixing a crash or a raw leak with an existing i18n
string if the guard found one; it found none, so no route, template or domain module changes
alongside the guard, and the existing populated-fixture suite stayed green unchanged (no fix means
no risk of changing a populated person's own screens).

**Why none of the seven states crashed** -- read, not guessed, while building each seeder: this
app's "honest gaps" rule (`docs/DESIGN.md`) was already enforced call-by-call in the modules this
slice could have touched -- `profile.metric_profile` returns `None` under 14 rows and every chart
builder (`profile.window_svg`/`month_svg`, `metas._goal_line_svg`) returns `""` or a single
`<circle>` under 2 points rather than a malformed `<polyline>`; `readiness.compute` needs
`MIN_PARTS = 3` scored parts before it scores at all; `turnos_costo.resumen`/`referencia` return
`None` per metric under `min_dias_referencia` and name a `REASON_CODES` reason instead of a number;
`history.coverage`/`training`/`patterns` each return `None` or an empty structure under their own
minimums (`PATTERN_MIN_N = 4`, `len(rows) < 14`, `not rows`). This slice is the first to have
exercised that rule end-to-end, across every screen, for a person who never had 30+ days to hide
the edge in.

**Product follow-ups** (rendering is honest but could read better; reported per this slice's
approval, not built -- each needs new customer wording or a new empty-state layout, which the
approval reserves for the orchestrator to spec with a measured mock), ranked:

1. **F's Hoy shows a stale day with no "this is old" cue.** `/` for a person whose watch stopped
   syncing 40 days ago renders the readiness screen for that LAST day it has, dated in the page
   (e.g. "martes 29 de septiembre") with "Sin sincronizar hoy" in the meta line -- but nothing
   says the card itself is 40 days old, or that today's real date is something else entirely. A
   returning person could read a 40-day-old readiness card as current. Proposed: when the
   rendered day is more than a few days before the person's real local today, say so plainly next
   to the date (an existing-pattern sentence, "últimos datos de hace N días", not a new chrome
   element).
2. **D's `/shifts` repeats "sin datos del reloj" five times in a row.** With the toggle on and
   zero shift rows AND zero metrics, the top card already says the honest, useful thing ("Aún no
   hay turnos... puedes escribir tu propio patrón aquí") -- but the cost table below it still
   renders all five metric rows, each reading "sin datos del reloj", adding five lines that say
   the same thing the top card already said. Proposed: hide the cost table entirely (not just its
   rows) until there is at least one confirmed night block, the same honest-gap-at-the-section-
   level `/trends` already applies.
3. **E's zero-data goal chart shows a bare plan line with no caption.** `/goals/{id}` for a
   metric goal with zero actual readings renders the dashed plan line and a "Hoy" marker but no
   actual-progress line or dot -- technically honest (nothing invented), but a first-time viewer
   sees an almost-empty chart with no sentence explaining why. Proposed: a one-line caption under
   the chart when there is no actual-progress point yet (e.g. "aún no hay promedios semanales que
   mostrar"), reusing the same honest-gap voice as the weekly-review card right below it.

`7e00ebbb95b1122a1d14ef7bd409aac49d2ad3b5`), producing merge commit

## BODY-ESTADOS-VACIOS-2 -- the three product follow-ups BODY-ESTADOS-VACIOS-1 reported, plus
BODY-ESTADOS-VACIOS-2-M's test move that unblocks the merge

Implements the three follow-ups BODY-ESTADOS-VACIOS-1 reported above (not built there, under that
slice's own approval, since each needs new wording or layout a guard alone cannot add) and, as a
second slice (`-2-M`), moves one pinned test that the first slice's own rule change left failing on
`main`'s old behaviour -- outside the first slice's `touches:`, so it stopped BLOCKED rather than
editing it. Built on `feat/body-estados-vacios-2` at `8141e43b5a903cd6fc7d045dd713be8683d37c4f`.

**Decision 1 -- Hoy's stale-data line.** `/` gets a line above the readiness card
(`today.stale` + `today.stale_link`, reusing the existing `.note` gap style) when the latest day
with any data is 2 or more days behind the person's local today; `dias` 0 or 1 changes nothing, so
a watch that is merely a day behind (today's night not yet synced) never sees it. The link target
depends on hosting: `/garmin` when `cuenta.hosted()` (the in-app connection screen), `/settings`
when local (the nearest actionable page this app has -- the sync itself runs as a per-install Task
Scheduler job outside anything this app can read or trigger). Both branches are read, not guessed:
`body/rutas/hoy.py` reads `cuenta.hosted()` the same way every other hosted/local branch in this
app already does.

**Decision 2 -- Turnos drops the all-empty cost table, keeps the partial one.** `/shifts`'s cost
table (5 metric rows, each either a figure that links to `/trends` or an honest em-dash) is dropped
entirely (`costo_vacio`, decided once in the route: `all(f["href"] is None for f in filas)`) when
every row has no figure -- removing five identical "sin datos del reloj" lines that repeated what
the hero card above already said. A partial row (at least one metric with a figure) keeps the table
rendering exactly as before, em-dashes and all, so a person with a few days of data loses nothing.

**Decision 3 -- Metas' zero-points chart caption.** `/goals/{id}`'s chart caption reads
`goals.chart_soon` instead of `goals.chart_hint` when the plan line has zero actual weekly points
(`chart_sin_puntos`, decided once in the route). The tap layer needed no JS change: read before
touching anything, `profile.chart_figure`'s own `if not points` branch already omits the
data-point layer under zero points, so a caption mismatch was the only gap -- a zero-point chart
never carried a tap layer to begin with, caption aside.

**BODY-ESTADOS-VACIOS-2-M's move -- `tests/test_turnos_enlaces.py::CostRowNoDataTest`.** Its
`test_no_link_and_the_em_dash_row_remains` pinned the OLD rule (cost table always renders, even
all-empty) on an all-empty fixture; Decision 2 above makes that fixture's own assertion wrong on
purpose. The class's docstring subject -- "a row with no figure ('--') never links anywhere" --
still holds, and after Decision 2 it only ever shows up in the PARTIAL state (the all-empty state
has no table left to carry such a row). So the test keeps its class and its subject but moves to
the partial-data fixture `tests/test_estados_vacios_2.py::_seed_turnos_parcial` already built (one
metric, `resting_hr`, with a figure; the other four with none), imported rather than duplicated.
Its new assertion parses the rendered `<table class="parts mt-8">...</table>` into `<tr>` rows (not
a page-wide substring, since the table now carries a row that DOES link) and checks, per row, that
every em-dash row (`"—<div" in row`) contains no `<a` tag -- the property the class's name is
about -- while `shifts.sin_dato_corto` and the row with a figure both still render.

The all-empty case the moved test used to cover gets its own new test in the same class,

Built on `feat/body-estados-vacios-2` at `b9b7ae727748f6ff8b66341ed911955045adea3a` (-M's tip). The

**Decision 1 -- the stale line is a flag, not a footnote.** `body/static/body.css` gets `.aviso`,
mirroring `.shift` (rounded, padded, bordered, left-bar `::before`), with the amber tokens already
in both themes (`--amber` for the bar, `--amber-tint` for the background) and ink text at body

## BODY-ESTADOS-VACIOS-3 -- hosted mode's own sweep, before body.duna.solutions is the next deploy

Cuenta is deployed (Main, 2026-11-08) and Body's next deploy is hosted and multi-person from day
one. BODY-ESTADOS-VACIOS-1 (ledger 0776687) swept every GET route as six sparse people, but only in
LOCAL mode: every hosted-only route (`/garmin`, `/ajustes/dispositivos`, `/login`,
`/login/cuenta/start`, `/login/cuenta/callback`, `/privacidad/consentimiento`, `/api/vida/semana`)
was a documented 404 there, never actually rendered for a person. This slice sweeps hosted mode
itself, as a new person (never person 1), before that deploy.

**Mechanism**: a real Cuenta Duna session, built the exact way `tests/test_cuenta_rp.py`'s
`CuentaRpTestCase` already does (its fake issuer, its hosted env, its fresh temp db) -- the same
mechanism `tests/test_garmin_host.py` and `tests/test_hogar_cuenta_1.py` build on. This is the
faithful choice over a `dependency_overrides` swap on `identity.current_person_id`: that override
would replace the very function the consent gate (`identity.ConsentRequired`) and the
unsigned-request path (`identity.LoginRequired`) live inside, so it could never observe either one
-- and this slice exists specifically to exercise both (its new H1 state IS the consent gate).
Each person in the sweep is a brand-new `TestClient` (its own cookie jar) signed in with its own
invented `sub`, so Cuenta Duna assigns it a real, fresh person id -- never 1, exactly as a second
hosted sign-up would get one.

**People**: reused directly from `tests/test_estados_vacios.py`'s own seed builders (A, B, C, D,
D2, E, F), each now taking an optional `pid` -- the row Cuenta Duna's sign-in already created --
instead of making its own. Two states only hosted mode has: H1 (signed in, consent not yet
accepted) and H2 (signed in, consented, Garmin never connected). Each of the 9 states in both
Spanish and English, for 18 signed-in persons, plus one unsigned pass and person 1 -- populated in
the same database with a distinctive invented display name, goal title and habit name
(`ZZ1-PERSONA-UNO-MARCADOR`, `ZZ1-META-UNO-MARCADOR`, `ZZ1-HABITO-UNO-MARCADOR`) that no other
person in this sweep ever shares a household or goal with, so their appearance on anyone else's
page is unambiguously a leak.

**The sweep**: every GET route `tests/_rutas.rutas_planas` finds, including the seven hosted-only
ones, for every one of the 19 person-passes (18 signed-in + 1 unsigned) -- 342 (route, person)
calls in total (every GET route in the app times the 19 passes; some are skipped per person when a
`{day}`/`{goal_id}` parameter has no id to substitute, matching ESTADOS-VACIOS-1's own rule). Same
assertions as ESTADOS-VACIOS-1 (no 500, the documented status, the five-word leak regex plus the
four Jinja/SVG literals plus the `<polyline` under-2-points check on every 200 HTML page), plus:
no page for anyone other than person 1 ever contains one of person 1's three markers; the unsigned
pass answers its documented status on every route and never 200 with data; H1 is redirected (303)
to `/privacidad/consentimiento` on every route except that one itself (which it reaches, 200,
since the consent screen is explicitly exempt from its own gate); every one of the seven
hosted-only routes was actually exercised (never silently skipped, never still 404) and the three
whose own correct behaviour CAN be 200 (`/garmin`, `/ajustes/dispositivos`,
`/privacidad/consentimiento`) answered 200 for at least one person.

**No fix was needed.** The sweep found zero crashes and zero raw-value or cross-person leaks --
every hosted route this slice's approval (`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`) asked to guard already
answers its own GET correctly for a second, fresh, unconsented or newly-consented person.

**Deviation from the spec's literal wording** (`deviations`, recorded here too): the spec's step 3
asked to assert "each hosted-only route was rendered at least once with 200 for some person." Four
of the seven's own DOCUMENTED, correct behaviour is never 200: `/login` and `/login/cuenta/start`
always redirect (303) to the issuer regardless of who asks; `/login/cuenta/callback` with no real
authorization-code round trip is always refused (400, `cuenta.FlowRefused`); `/api/vida/semana`
with no device key is always 401. Measured directly against the running app rather than assumed:
this slice asserts those four were exercised and never 404 (proving they are no longer the LOCAL
sweep's blanket 404), and asserts 200 specifically for the three that can actually answer it
(`/garmin`, `/ajustes/dispositivos`, `/privacidad/consentimiento`).

**Isolation**: `tests/_isolate.py` imported first in the new test module, exactly as every other
test module here does; the new module writes only to its own fresh temp database (via
`CuentaRpTestCase.setUp`'s `config.DB_PATH` redirect), never to `BODY_HOME`. No real health
figure, password, token or secret appears anywhere in the new module, this entry, or any commit.

**Follow-ups reported, not built** (structure and proposed behaviour only, ranked -- no new
customer wording or layout, per the approval's own bound):
1. `/privacidad/consentimiento` for H1: the consent screen itself is the one page a newly
   signed-in, unconsented person can always reach, and this sweep confirms it renders 200 -- but
   this slice did not inspect whether its own copy gives that person enough to decide (what Body
   collects, why, and the exact two actions: accept or decline-and-sign-out). Proposed: a short,
   explicit "what this means" list above the two buttons, reusing existing privacidad.* strings
   where any already say this.
2. `/garmin` for H2 (consented, watch never connected): renders 200 with the existing "No
   conectado" + email/password form -- functionally fine, structurally a dead-end screen with no
   indication of what happens after connecting (first data arrives within minutes per
   BODY-PRIMER-PULL-1, but H2's own page never says so before they try). Proposed: reuse
   `sync.hosted_connected`'s sibling copy, or a one-line "first data arrives within minutes" hint,
   on the pre-connection form itself.
3. `/ajustes/dispositivos` for any newly-consented person with zero device keys: renders 200 with
   an empty list and the "create a key" form -- no explanation of what a device key is FOR (the PC
   sync script) before the person is asked to name one. Proposed: a one-line explainer above the
   form, likely already covered by `ayuda`'s own tutorial for this screen (`tutoriales.py`) and so
   possibly just a missing cross-link rather than new copy.

## BODY-REGISTRO-TU-1 -- two register guards, and the one ambiguous string they let through once

Adopts hub item `hit_01m6ymj1w53wcm7ghds29vpk1s` (Pedidos, `ORDERS-QUESTION-ROUTING-REGISTER-PACK-1`):
every fixed customer sentence keeps its product's register, and a link is never followed directly
by punctuation a chat client could read as part of it. Body speaks tú, in one register, to one
person; nothing guarded that until now.

**Census.** Every fixed Spanish customer sentence in the repository:
- `body/i18n/es.json`: 575 top-level keys, 573 string values (the other two, `date.days` and
  `date.months`, are lists of words with no register at all).
- `body/i18n/en.json`: the same shape, 575 keys / 573 strings (mirrored, for guard 2's scan and for
  checking English alignment on the one fixed string).
- `tutoriales/catalogo.json` (not in `touches:`, read-only): 29 titles (8 chapters + 21 tasks), all
  infinitive or noun-phrase task names ("Confirmar los turnos propuestos", "Descargar todo") --
  infinitives carry no tú/usted register, so none could be a violation; no fix needed.
- `body/**/*.py`: the orchestrator's two named files plus every other file with an accented Spanish
  character were read. `body/agente/herramientas.py`'s Spanish is tool `descripcion` text (sent to
  the model, never the person) and `ToolError` messages -- `body/agente/bucle.py`'s own docstring
  states a tool error "becomes a tool-result error text fed back to the model, never an exception
  shown to the person," confirmed by reading `bucle.py`'s loop. `body/turnos_costo.py`'s Spanish is
  internal state codes ('peor'/'mejor'/'igual', 'sin_turnos', ...) looked up through es.json/en.json
  keys elsewhere, not fixed sentences themselves. `body/agente/propuestas.py` and
  `body/agente/conversacion.py` have no Spanish customer sentence (SQL, English docstrings, and
  internal state tags like 'aplicada'/'descartada'). `body/conectar_pc.py`, `body/pc_cliente.py`,
  `body/traer_semana.py`, `body/subir_turnos.py` print CLI messages to Carlos on his own PC, already
  tú ("Corre: python -m body.conectar_pc"). `body/templates/goal.html` and every other template have
  no hardcoded Spanish sentence outside `t()` calls (`settings.html`'s one non-ASCII literal is the
  language name "Español", not a sentence). Conclusion: every fixed customer sentence in this
  repository lives in `body/i18n/es.json` / `en.json`; nothing else needed scanning by guard 1.

**Guard 1 -- register (`tests/test_registro_tu.py`, `TestRegistroTuEsJson`).** Scans every es.json
string (573, non-vacuous) for: `usted`/`ustedes`; the formal imperatives `ingrese`, `seleccione`,
`haga`, `escriba`, `elija`, `intente`, `verifique`, `revise`, `toque`, `pulse`, `presione`,
`confirme`, `agregue`, `conecte`, `descargue`; and the specific risky phrases `le recomendamos`,
`le enviamos`, `lo invitamos`, `le pedimos`, `le sugerimos` (bare `le`/`lo`/`la` are not matched --
in this app's Spanish they are almost always relative pronouns ("lo que...") or definite articles
("la hora..."), never a formal "you"). 0 hits. A second scan covers `su`/`sus`/`tiene`/`puede`
(573 strings, non-vacuous): 12 real hits, all third person about a thing, listed in the allow-list
below with the reason each is safe; 0 hits outside the allow-list. A third test asserts the
allow-list has no stale entries (every listed key still matches). Two bite-proof tests: the word
pattern matches a planted `"Ingrese su correo"`; the phrase pattern matches a planted
`"Le recomendamos revisar su conexión"`.

**Guard 2 -- no punctuation glued to a link (`TestEnlaceSinPuntuacionPegada`).** Scans es.json (573)
+ en.json (573) + every string constant in `body/agente/*.py` except Tier 1 `cliente.py`
(`herramientas.py`, `bucle.py`, `propuestas.py`, `conversacion.py`, `ajustes.py` -- 861 constants,
including docstrings and SQL, to keep the scan honestly non-vacuous rather than hand-picking which
literals count) -- 2007 strings total, non-vacuous. Checks for `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `)` or `!`
immediately after a `{...url...}`/`{link}`/`{enlace}`/`{href}`-shaped placeholder, or after a
literal `http(s)://` token where the punctuation ends the token (next character is whitespace, a
quote, a closing bracket, or end of string -- so a dot that is part of the link's own path, followed
by more path, is not a false hit). 0 hits: no link in this codebase is ever followed by punctuation.
Two bite-proof tests (planted `"Mira esto: {url}."`, planted `"Ve a https://body.app."`) and one
false-positive guard (`"Ve a https://body.app/ruta para mas info"` does not trip the raw-URL check).

**Allow-list** (`su`/`sus`/`tiene`/`puede`, each third person about a thing, never the reader):

| es.json key | string | why it is safe |
|---|---|---|
| `how.explain` | "...las demás se reparten su peso." | "su" = the other score parts' own weight |
| `soon.goals` | "Aquí vivirán tus metas, su plan..." | "su" = the goals' own plan |
| `goals.enlace.field_entrada` | "...o su número" | "su" = the trip's own number |
| `settings.compartir.nota` | "Solo ven el último valor y su fecha." | "su" = that value's own date |
| `today.hogar.procedencia` | "{name} compartió esto · su reloj..." | "su" = that household member's watch |
| `goals.visibility_milestone_note` | "...cada quien lleva sus propios números." | "sus" = each member's own figures |
| `trends.tap_month` | "Toca un mes para ver sus días." | "sus" = that month's own days |
| `sin_acceso.text` | "Tu cuenta Duna no tiene acceso..." | "tiene" subject is "tu cuenta", not a direct address |
| `goals.no_habits` | (fixed below) | "tiene" subject is "esta meta" |
| `ajustes.asistente.opcion.completo.desc` | "...el asistente puede leer..." | "puede" subject is "el asistente" |
| `dispositivos.new_key_intro` | "...Body no puede mostrarla otra vez." | "puede" subject is "Body" |
| `asistente.propuesta.sin_deshacer` | "Esto no se puede deshacer." | "se puede" is impersonal, not usted |

**String changed** (meaning and length class kept, per the approval):

| key | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `es.json` `goals.no_habits` | "Aún no tiene hábitos." | "Esta meta aún no tiene hábitos." |
| `en.json` `goals.no_habits` | "No habits yet." | "This goal doesn't have habits yet." |

Read alone, "Aún no tiene hábitos." / "No habits yet." name no subject, and in an app that
otherwise addresses the reader as tú, "tiene" without one reads as a stray formal "you have no
habits." `body/templates/goal.html:65` renders the key standalone (`{{ t('goals.no_habits') }}`)
inside the goal detail page, so naming the goal in the string itself, rather than changing the
template, fixes it without touching how or where the key is used. English did not already name the
goal either ("No habits yet."), so it was aligned the same way.

## BODY-ACCESIBILIDAD-1 -- a structural accessibility sweep over every page

A new guard, `tests/test_accesibilidad.py`, parses every HTML GET response with the standard
library's `html.parser` (no new dependency) and checks eight rules: (a) `<html lang>` matches the
person's language; (b) exactly one `<h1>`; (c) no duplicate `id`; (d) every `<a href>` and
`<button>` has an accessible name (text content, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` pointing at an id
that exists, or `title`; an `<svg>`/`<img>` child alone counts only if it carries its own name);
(e) every `<input>` (except hidden/submit/button), `<select>` and `<textarea>` is labelled (a
`<label for>`, a wrapping `<label>`, or `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`); (f) every `<img>` carries
`alt`; (g) every inline `<svg>` carries `role="img"` plus a name, or `aria-hidden="true"`; (h) no
positive `tabindex`.

**Scope swept**: the populated (demo) fixture plus ESTADOS-VACIOS-1 sparse states A, D and E (per
the spec, not every state `tests/test_estados_vacios.py` seeds), each in es and en, local mode --
106 (page, state, language) renders -- plus hosted mode for the three hosted-only pages that can
ever answer 200 (`/garmin`, `/ajustes/dispositivos`, `/privacidad/consentimiento`), reached through
`tests/test_cuenta_rp.py`'s fake-issuer session exactly as `tests/test_estados_vacios_hosted.py`
does -- 6 more renders. 112 pages checked in total, 0 violations after the fixes below.

**Violations found, before the fixes** (measured by running the new guard against the unfixed
tree): 500 `g_svg_name` (every inline `<svg>` in this codebase had neither `role="img"` nor
`aria-hidden`: the 5 bottom-nav icons and the logout icon in `base.html`, the 4 assistant-panel
icons also in `base.html`, the goal-list progress-bar `<svg class="bar">` in `goals.html`, the
training-month `<svg class="stage">` in `history.html`, the sleep-stage `<svg class="stage">` in
`day.html` -- repeated across every page/state/lang combination that renders `base.html`'s nav, so
one real defect class, 500 occurrences); 164 `e_form_label` (17 real unlabelled controls, each hit
once per populated/sparse state and per hosted state it appears in: `goal_new.html`'s title, why,
area, metric_key, direction, target_value, baseline_value, deadline, visibility, habit_title,
habit_times, habit_per, habit_context; `goal.html`'s own habit_title/habit_times/habit_per/
habit_context repeat plus its dynamic household-app-link `entrada` input; `shift_pattern.html`'s
`select name="kind_N"`; `privacidad.html`'s `confirmacion` input; `garmin.html`'s code/email/
password inputs; `dispositivos.html`'s `nombre` input); 2 `c_duplicate_id` (`/day/{day}`:
`id="sleep_minutes"` on both the sleep-detail card built by hand and the generic per-metric card
`hoy.py`'s `day_view` builds from `metric_def`, which also defines a `sleep_minutes` row). 0 for
(a), (b), (h) (none ever tripped) -- (f) and (h) stay at exactly 0 even after the fix, since no
template anywhere renders a bare `<img>` or sets `tabindex`; the guard's own non-vacuous assertion
asserts that measured zero rather than fabricating a dead element to move a counter (recorded as
this slice's one deviation, below).

**Fixes**:
- `aria-hidden="true"` added to the 13 decorative svgs named above (base.html x10, goals.html x1,
  history.html x1, day.html x1) -- each sits beside visible text or inside a labelled button, so it
  is redundant, never the only name-bearing content.
- `aria-label` added to the 17 unlabelled controls, reusing the exact text already shown beside each
  one (its sibling `div.q`, its placeholder, or the row's own dynamic label) -- no new words, an
  attribute only.
- Three fields in `goal_new.html`/`goal.html` had no visible label anywhere near them (`habit_times`,
  `habit_per`, `habit_context`): new i18n keys, `a11y.habit_times` / `a11y.habit_per` /
  `a11y.habit_context`, added to `es.json` and `en.json`, used only as `aria-label` values (never
  rendered as visible text).
- `day.html`'s generic per-metric card loop now omits `id="{{ c.key }}"` when `c.key == 'sleep_minutes'`
  (the hand-built sleep-detail card above already owns that id, and is the more useful anchor
  target for `today.html`'s `#sleep_minutes` link); no other metric card's id changed, so every
  other anchor (`hrv_last_night`, `resting_hr`, `body_battery_wake`) still resolves exactly as
  before.

**New i18n keys** (es / en, tú register, used only as accessible names):
- `a11y.habit_times`: "Cantidad de veces" / "Number of times"
- `a11y.habit_per`: "Cada cuánto" / "How often"
- `a11y.habit_context`: "Contexto del hábito" / "Habit context"

**docs/DESIGN.md** gains rule 18, "Accesibilidad estructural": states rules (a)-(h) in the same
words as the guard, says `tests/test_accesibilidad.py` guards them on every page, and says in words
that tap-target size (rule 11's 44 px) is a layout measurement made in a real browser, not something
this test can see in server-rendered HTML.

**Deviation**: the spec's own non-vacuous instruction ("assert... each rule was evaluated on more
than 0 elements") cannot hold literally for rules (f) and (h), measured: this codebase renders zero
`<img>` tags anywhere (every picture-like thing is a server-built inline `<svg>`) and sets
`tabindex` nowhere. Rather than plant a dead, invisible `<img>` purely to move a counter above zero
-- the same shape this protocol's own instructions elsewhere call out as a workaround -- the test
asserts the measured zero for exactly these two rules (`assertEqual(..., 0)`, with a comment that
either count moving off zero means the assertion itself needs updating) and keeps the stronger
`assertGreater(..., 0)` for the six rules that do have real candidates in this codebase today.

**Gate**, once, foreground, on this slice's own branch tip (before the merge; tree identity proven

`Ran 1371 tests in 317.297s ... OK (skipped=1)` (1369 before this slice, +2: the two test methods in
the new `tests/test_accesibilidad.py`).

**Merge.** The diff adds visible-nowhere `aria-hidden`/`aria-label`/`role` attributes and three new
i18n keys read only as `aria-label` values -- never rendered as visible text, but still bytes a
screen-reader user hears, so it trips merge policy A's customer-bytes condition on a literal
reading. This spec's approval-reason (`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`) says in words: "Fixes add
attributes (aria-label, aria-hidden, label for/id, role) and, where an accessible name needs words,
new i18n keys used ONLY as accessible names: they are read by screen readers and are not visible.
Nothing visible changes, so there is no layout to measure... This spec approves the merge." Merged
on that authorisation, scoped to exactly the attribute/key additions listed above, not withheld.

## BODY-TAP-44-1 -- grow four under-44px tap targets' hit area, not their drawing

**Census** (the orchestrator's, measured on `main` `720d827`, 375x812, demo data, 16 screens:
`getBoundingClientRect` of every `a[href]`, `button`, `input`, `summary`). Four kinds under 44 px:
(1) the habit check button `.boxbtn` (`body.css:109`, `width:28px`) -- 28x44 on Hoy (`base.html:39`
macro) and on a goal's habit list (`goal.html:49`); (2) the footer links "Ayuda" and "Ajustes" in
`.foot` (`body.css:165-166`; `base.html:79`) -- 35x44 and 40x44, on every screen; (3) Historia's
month rows (`<a class="block mt-10 no-underline">`, `history.html:15`) -- 313x38. Not a defect:
Tendencias r=90's per-day chart anchors (4x110, the documented no-JS path, DESIGN rule 9) and the
20x20 radios on Nueva meta / Ajustes del asistente, each inside a 313x44 `label.radio` that is the
real target.

**Decision** (`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`): grow the hit area, not the drawing. Widening
`.boxbtn` to 44 would shift every habit row's text by 16 px; padding the footer would change its
rhythm.

**The `.hit` pattern**, one reusable rule in `body.css`: `position:relative` on the target plus a
borderless, see-through `::before` (`content:"";position:absolute`, no background, no border,
`pointer-events` left on), inset per target to reach 44x44. Verified free before use: `.box.done`
already owns an `::after`, but on the inner `.box` span, not on `.boxbtn` -- `.boxbtn::before` and
`.foot a::before` were unclaimed.

**Applications** (insets, and why no overlap):
- `.boxbtn` (28x44): `left:-8px;right:-8px` -> 44x44. Free on both sides: in `today.html`/`goal.html`
  it is the lone visible child of an unstyled `<form>`, the first flex item of `.plan li`
  (`gap:10px`), so the left extension lands in the card's own 14 px padding and the right extension
  uses 8 of the 10 px gap before the title text, 2 px to spare. In `base.html`'s `primeros_pasos_card`
  it sits inside the single full-row `<a class="help-link">`, so its extension never leaves that
  link's own, already-larger hit area. Applied straight to the `.boxbtn` selector -- no template
  change.
- `.foot a` (Ayuda 35x44, Ajustes 40x44): `left:-5px;right:-5px` -> 45x44 / 50x44. `.foot` is
  12.5 px text; the " · " separator between items (space + middle dot + space) is roughly 0.8em,
  ~10 px, so each of two adjacent extended links claims half of it -- 5 px -- and they meet at the
  gap's midpoint without overlapping. Applied straight to the `.foot a` selector -- no template
  change.
- Historia month rows (313x38): `top:-3px;bottom:-3px` -> 313x44. `mt-10` gives 10 px between rows;
  3 px top + 3 px bottom per row uses 6 of it, 4 px to spare. These rows had no selector of their
  own (`class="block mt-10 no-underline"` is three reused utilities), so `history.html`'s
  `month_row` macro gets the one new class `.month-row`.

**Test** (`tests/test_tap_44.py`, 13 methods): `body.css` carries the `.hit` base rule and each of
the three `::before` insets, with the exact axes above and none of the others; the original
`.boxbtn{...}` and `.foot a{...}` rules keep every one of their `width`/`min-height`/`display`/
`padding`/`margin` declarations unchanged and gain no `position:relative` of their own (that lives
only in the separate, shared `.hit,.boxbtn,.foot a,.month-row` rule) -- the "nothing visible moves"
pin; `.box.done::after` is confirmed to be on the inner span, never `.boxbtn::after`; the rule is
non-vacuous (three extended selectors, each inset on some axis, plus the shared base rule covering
exactly four selectors). Rendered: Hoy and a goal page each render `class="boxbtn"` for a due habit;
Historia renders `class="block mt-10 no-underline month-row"`; the footer still wraps `<a
href="/ayuda">` inside `<p class="foot">`; `history.html`'s own macro source carries the new class.

**docs/DESIGN.md** rule 11 gains: a target smaller than 44 px grows its hit area, never its
drawing, with the `.hit` pattern -- `position:relative` plus an inset, see-through `::before` -- in
whatever space already surrounds it; a radio or checkbox counts as its full `label`; Tendencias'
per-day chart anchors stay exempt (the no-JS path, rule 9).

**Gate**, once, foreground, on this slice's own branch tip (before the merge; tree identity proven
below, so not re-run after merging): `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .` --
`Ran 1384 tests in 183.264s ... OK (skipped=1)` (1371 before this slice, +13: `tests/test_tap_44.py`).

**Merge.** The diff is CSS plus one new template class that moves no pixel -- pinned by the test
above -- and the spec's approval-reason (`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`) says in words: "CSS
only: hit-area extensions that draw nothing, so no visible pixel changes. That is pinned by a test,
and the orchestrator re-measures in the browser after the merge... This spec approves the merge."
Merged on that authorisation.

## BODY-ANCHO-COMPLETO-1 -- wide screens fill the panel, per device, on the theme's own mechanism

Carlos, 2026-11-08: "for wider screens we should have the option in the app to fill the whole
panel." Measured on `main` at 1440x900: the rail takes 220px, `main` takes the rest (1205px), but
`.wrap` was capped at 820px and left-aligned, leaving ~385px empty on every screen. ORCHESTRATOR
DECISIONS this slice builds to: the preference is per device (like the theme), full width is the
default at >=1024px, "lectura" is the centred-column alternative, and width becomes columns, never
wider prose.

**The mechanism, exactly the theme's.** `tema.js` gains one more `try{...}catch(e){}` line: it
reads `localStorage.getItem('body.ancho')` and sets `document.documentElement.dataset.ancho =
'lectura'` only when that value is `'lectura'` -- absent, `'completo'`, or anything else leaves the
attribute unset, so the CSS default (no attribute) IS completo, the same "unset = light" pattern
the theme itself uses. Still one blocking `<script src>` in `base.html` (no second tag).
`ajustes_tema.js` was rewritten around a small `seg(key, selector, fallback, apply)` helper shared
by both button rows, so the theme row and the new row are one small function each, not two copies
of the same click/paint logic. `settings.html` gets a second `.seg`/`.btn` card, `id="ancho"`,
shaped exactly like `#theme`'s, with a one-line note (`ancho.nota`: "Se guarda en este
dispositivo." / "Saved on this device.") and no width-gating of its own -- it renders the same at
every width, so a phone can set the preference for a tablet or monitor sharing the same browser
profile. Four new keys in both `body/i18n/es.json` and `body/i18n/en.json`:
`settings.ancho`/`ancho.completo`/`ancho.lectura`/`ancho.nota`.

**The layout, >=1024px only -- every new declaration lives inside the existing
`@media (min-width:1024px)` block in `body/static/body.css`, nothing outside it changed:**
- `[data-ancho="lectura"] .wrap{max-width:820px;margin:0 auto}` -- the only place `820px` still
  appears for `.wrap`, now centred (`margin:0 auto`), where before it was left-aligned against
  `main`'s own padding. The unscoped `.wrap{max-width:820px}` is gone: completo's `.wrap` carries
  no cap, so it fills `main`.
- `.wrap p:not(.foot),.wrap .read{max-width:70ch}` -- running prose (plain `<p>`, `.read` "why"
  lines such as a goal's `goal.why`) stays readable in both modes; `.foot`'s short nav line is
  excluded since centering it under a width cap would misalign it.

**Columns, per screen, in completo (five new auto-fill/auto-fit grid classes, one per screen that
needed one; a screen not listed gets the base rule and no columns):**
- **Hoy** (`.cols-hoy`, `today.html`): the readiness hero (`<a class="card est">`) was moved to sit
  directly beside the day's metric grid (`.grid2`) + "Ver el día" link, both now inside one
  `.cols-hoy` wrapper; Primeros pasos and the habit-plan card stay above it, full width, since they
  are onboarding/checklist content, not part of the hero+metrics pairing the spec asked for.
- **Tendencias** (`.cols-tendencias`, `trends.html`): both the main card loop and each `extra_groups`
  disclosure's card loop sit in their own `.cols-tendencias` grid (`minmax(340px,1fr)`, wide enough
  for a card's title + figure + chart + legend). Each chart's SVG keeps its own fixed `height="110"`
  attribute regardless of column width, so "each chart at least as tall as today" holds with no CSS
  change needed.
- **Metas** (`.cols-metas`, `goals.html`): the active-goals loop, the proposed-goals loop and the
  archived-goals loop (inside its `<details>`) each get their own `.cols-metas` grid
  (`minmax(280px,1fr)`). `goal.html` (one goal's own detail page) is NOT in this list -- it shows
  one goal's sections, not a list of goal cards, so it gets the base rule only; its own "why" prose
  already gets the global 70ch cap with no template change.
- **Turnos** (`.cols-turnos`, `shifts.html`): the hero (`/shifts/como`) and the cost-table card,
  already adjacent in the DOM, wrapped in one `.cols-turnos` grid. The 56-day strip and its legend
  stay outside it, full width, exactly as the spec asked.
- **Día**: no template change. Its figures grid already carries `class="grid2 grid3"`; `.grid3`
  itself gets the override `grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(150px,1fr))` inside the
  1024 block (the existing `@media(min-width:640px){.grid3{repeat(3,...)}}` rule is untouched, so
  375/768px are unaffected). `.grid3` is shared with Historia's shift-kind metrics grid
  (`history.html`), which gets the same auto-fill treatment as a side effect -- not separately
  listed by the spec, but the same "figures in columns" idea.
- **Historia** (`.cols-historia`, `history.html`): `training.months` and `training.months_older`
  (inside its `<details>`) each sit in a `.cols-historia` grid (`minmax(260px,1fr)`). The
  `.month-row`'s own 44px hit-area pseudo-element (BODY-TAP-44-1, `top:-3px;bottom:-3px`, no
  horizontal extension) is unaffected by column placement: it insets vertically within its own box
  only, so side-by-side rows in the same grid row never overlap.
- **Settings**: not listed in step 3 -- gets the new control (above) and the base rule, no columns.

**Lectura reverts every one of those to a single column** --
`[data-ancho="lectura"] .cols-hoy,...,.cols-historia{grid-template-columns:1fr}` and
`[data-ancho="lectura"] .grid3{grid-template-columns:repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr))}` (the pre-1024,
640px-and-up value), inside the same 1024 block.

**Charts need no JS change, and `charts.js` was not touched (it is not in `touches:`).** Every
chart in this app is a server-rendered inline `<svg viewBox="..." width="100%">` (or CSS
`width:100%`): the browser already rescales it to its container's current width on every resize,
with no JS caching a pixel width at load. `charts.js` itself only adds the tap/drag readout; it
reads the SVG's live `getBoundingClientRect()`/`offsetWidth` inside its event handlers (click,
pointermove), never once at script-load time, so it already "redraws" to the new width for free.
Confirmed by reading `body/profile.py`, `body/rutas/metas.py` and every `viewBox=` template site --
none caches a width in JS.

**Test** (`tests/test_ancho_completo.py`, 25 methods, 0 skipped): tema.js reads `body.ancho` and
sets `dataset.ancho` only for `'lectura'`, never `'completo'`, with one blocking script tag;
settings renders the new control's four i18n keys in both es and en (checked both at the
source-template level and by actually rendering `/settings` through a `TestClient`); the `.wrap`
820px cap exists only under `[data-ancho="lectura"]` (regex-scanned over every `.wrap{...}` rule in
`body.css`, not just a substring check); a line-by-line diff against `main`'s `body.css` (`git show
main:body/static/body.css`, read as UTF-8 explicitly -- the first run caught a real encoding bug in
this check itself, a middle-dot mangled by the platform's default locale encoding, before it was
fixed) asserts every added declaration sits inside the `min-width:1024px` block; each of the five
listed screens carries its own grid class, Día's `grid3` keeps its class name, and `grid3` carries
the auto-fill override plus the lectura 3-column fallback; the 70ch prose rule is present; none of
the nine touched templates gained a `style=` attribute or an inline `<script>` with no `src`
(CSP); a handful of sanity counts guard against the screen census or the i18n-key list being
accidentally empty.

**docs/DESIGN.md** rule 19, "Pantallas anchas": full width by default at >=1024px, the extra width
becomes columns (CSS grid, `minmax()`+`auto-fill`/`auto-fit`, no fixed breakpoint), prose capped at
70ch in both modes, "lectura" as the per-device alternative on the theme's own mechanism, phone and
the 768px band unchanged, the assistant panel still sized from the content.

**Gate**, once, foreground, on this slice's own branch tip: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest
discover tests -t .` -- first run RED on one offender inside `tests/test_ancho_completo.py` itself

## BODY-ANCHO-COMPLETO-1-M -- Hoy's phone reading order restored; branch merged

The orchestrator measured `feat/body-ancho-completo-1` (tip `773fd974e50701155163627d61eca7ab7471431e`)
in a real browser against `main` (`43666001fa45681ce0a1cdb51df82b1ac1a1db30`), both on demo data, in
the same tab, at 375/1024/1440px with the assistant panel open and closed. Every screen passed --
`.wrap` 1125px at 1440 with no horizontal scroll and 70ch prose, "Lectura" a centred 820px column,
Ajustes' "Pantallas anchas" control, Tendencias' 2-column/1-column drop at 1024 beside the open
assistant panel, Metas/Historia/Turnos/Tendencias matching `main` element for element at 375 -- with
one defect: on Hoy at 375px, `today.html` had moved the readiness hero (`a.card.est`, Hoy's
headline) *after* Primeros pasos and the habits card, opening `<div class="cols-hoy">` below them
instead of with the hero first.

**Fix, in `body/templates/today.html` only.** The DOM order is now exactly `main`'s: the readiness
hero, then Primeros pasos, then the habits card, then the figure cards. `<div class="cols-hoy">`
now opens with the hero as its first child and a second `<div>` holding Primeros pasos, the habits
card and the figure cards + "ver el día", in that order -- the same single DOM order satisfies both
the phone (identical to `main`) and the >=1024px two-column grid, so no CSS changed at all (no
`grid-template-areas`, no `order`; nothing needed inside or outside the 1024 query).

**Test**, added to `tests/test_ancho_completo.py` (`HoyPhoneOrderHeroFirstTest`): renders `/` with
demo data carrying one metric row (ticks "conectar-garmin"/"primera-mirada-a-hoy" but leaves
"trabajas-por-turnos" unanswered, so Primeros pasos renders) and one active goal with a daily habit
due today (so the habits card renders too), then asserts the hero's `class="card est"` HTML

**The red**: both failing tests in `tests/test_ancho_completo.py` compared `body.css` against

moment `main` itself carries this slice family's CSS. `test_body_css_grew` asserted the file is
longer than `main`'s, false on `main` itself after BODY-ANCHO-COMPLETO-1 merged. `test_every_
added_line_is_inside_the_1024_query` treated every line not already on `main` as "added by ANCHO",
so it would refuse ANY later slice that adds a body.css line outside the `min-width:1024px` block --
including the coming Today redesign.

**Fix, in `tests/test_ancho_completo.py` only**, restoring each test's SUBJECT as a property of the
file itself, never by deletion or weakening (per this spec's approval reason):
- `test_body_css_grew` -> `SanityCountsTest.test_1024_block_holds_every_cols_rule_and_the_lectura_
  cap`: asserts a `min-width:1024px` block exists and, using the existing `_media_1024_flags` line
  tracker, that the lines inside it contain a rule for every `cols-*` class in `_COLS_BY_SCREEN`
  plus the Lectura `.wrap` 820px cap.
- `test_every_added_line_is_inside_the_1024_query` -> `ColsAndDataAnchoStayInThe1024QueryTest`, two
  tests sharing a `_tracked_rules()` helper (every CSS rule whose selector names a `cols-` class or
  the `data-ancho` attribute, or whose selector is exactly `.grid3` with `auto-fill` in its body --
  the auto-fill test is needed because `.grid3` also carries the unrelated 640px three-column
  default and the lectura-collapsed override, neither of which this slice family added): one test
  asserts every tracked rule's line sits inside the 1024 block (`_media_1024_flags`), the other
  asserts no tracked selector has a rule at the top level, outside every `@media` at all (a new
  `_top_level_flags` helper, same brace-depth technique generalised to any nesting depth).
  `_tracked_rules()` anchors each rule's line on the position of its own `{` (`m.start(2) - 1`),
  not the regex match's start, so a rule immediately following a gap that crosses the 1024
  boundary is not mis-attributed to the wrong line.
- Durability checked directly (not by the gate, which only sees the current file): a scratch script
  outside the repository appended a bare `.cols-hoy{display:block}` line to an in-memory copy of
  `body.css` and confirmed `_is_tracked_rule` + the line-tracking flags catch it as a phone-level
  offender.

## BODY-INTRADIA-ADAPTER-1 -- intraday adapter function (heart rate, stress, Body Battery events)

Carries out BODY-INTRADIA-1-INV's first follow-up unchanged: one new on-demand adapter function,
its shape and its parsing only -- no schema, no storage, no screen.

**`body/garmin_adapter.py`**: `fetch_intraday(day, token_str=None) -> IntradayData`, following
`fetch_day`'s session/token pattern exactly (the hosted per-person token path included). Three
calls for one local day: `get_heart_rates`, `get_stress_data` (not `get_all_day_stress`, which the
installed garminconnect 0.3.20 hits at the same endpoint), `get_body_battery_events`.

`IntradayData` is a new dataclass beside `DayData`, not a change to it: `day`; `raw` (the payload
per kind, so a later slice can store them under new `raw_payload` kinds); `heart_rate` and `stress`
as tuples of `(local time, value)` in payload order; `heart_rate_interval_minutes` /
`stress_interval_minutes`, read from any key in that payload naming "interval" (case-insensitive)
and holding a number, else `None` -- never guessed from timestamp deltas; `body_battery_events` as
a tuple of the event dicts the payload carries, unchanged.

Honest gaps, same rule as `DayData`: a series Garmin returns empty, null, or with null samples
stays absent -- an empty tuple, never a zero; null samples are dropped before the tuple is built. A
call that raises does not lose the other two: `raw["_errors"]` records which kind failed, the same
pattern `fetch_day`/`DayData` already use (no separate `missing` field needed).

Sample timestamps are assumed to be epoch-ms already shifted to local wall time -- the same
convention this module already uses for Garmin's `...TimestampLocal` scalar fields (`_local_iso`)
-- unconfirmed for these specific arrays by the installed package, which types `get_heart_rates`
and `get_stress_data` no further than `dict[str, Any]`. Documented in the new helpers'
docstrings (`_interval_minutes`, `_intraday_series`), same defensive-and-documented style as the
existing `_max_metrics_entry`.

**Nothing calls `fetch_intraday` yet**: not `pull.py`, not the backfill loop, not the web app. It
is reachable only by direct call (and by the new tests), exactly as this spec required.

**Tests, `tests/test_garmin_parse.py`** (all fixtures invented, shaped from the library's call
signatures -- the installed package itself names no field keys for these three calls beyond their
type hints, so none of this is real health data): a full day parses in order
(`IntradayFullDayTest`); a stated interval key is read and an absent one stays `None`
(`IntradayStatedIntervalTest`); empty, null and missing series stay the empty tuple and null
samples are dropped rather than becoming `0` (`IntradayHonestGapsTest`); a failing `get_stress_data`
call leaves heart rate and Body Battery events intact and names `"stress"` in `raw["_errors"]`
(`FetchIntradayStressFailureTest`, same `FakeGarmin*`-class pattern as the existing VO2max failure
test). No guard elsewhere in `tests/` enforces "`body/garmin_adapter.py` is the only module that
may import garminconnect" (checked by grep before writing one), so
`OnlyGarminAdapterImportsGarminconnectTest` adds it: scans every other `.py` file under `body/` for
an `import garminconnect` / `from garminconnect` line.

## BODY-ENTRENO-SUENO-PARSE-1 -- sleep SpO2 and respiration parsed into DayData, not stored yet

BODY-ENTRENO-1-INV slice 7. Carlos named snoring and nasal breathing at night as goals
(2026-11-09, per the approved spec). The watch does not measure snoring, but the daily sleep
payload Body already pulls (`raw["sleep"]`, `dailySleepDTO`) carries `avgSpO2`,
`averageRespirationValue`, `lowestRespirationValue` and `highestRespirationValue`
(installed `garminconnect` 0.3.20, `typed.py:214-224`), and `garmin_adapter.parse_day` did not
extract them. Zero extra Garmin calls -- parsing only, of a payload already fetched and stored.

`DayData` (`body/garmin_adapter.py`) gained four fields -- `sleep_spo2_avg`, `sleep_respiration_avg`,
`sleep_respiration_low`, `sleep_respiration_high` -- read from `dailySleepDTO` in `parse_day`
alongside the other sleep fields. A new `_num_in_range(v, lo, hi)` helper treats Garmin's own `None`,
a non-numeric value, or a value outside the physiologically possible window as absent, never 0:
50..100 for `avgSpO2` (SpO2 percent), 1..60 for each respiration value (breaths/min) --
Garmin sends 0 or another sentinel when the sensor was off, and 0 is outside both windows so the
range check alone covers it. An older payload missing these keys still parses the rest of the day
(`sleep_minutes`, `sleep_score`, `resting_hr`, etc.) unchanged.

**Not stored yet, by design.** `daily_metric.metric_key` (`body/db.py`) is a foreign key on
`metric_def(key)`; adding these four values to `DayData.metrics` the way every other metric is
added would make `store_day`'s insert loop raise an integrity error the first time it ran for real,

slice's `touches:` (Tier 1, approval scoped to `body/garmin_adapter.py`,

fields above -- parsed, never written to `daily_metric`. **What a storage slice needs:** four
`METRIC_DEFS` rows, kind `"measured"`, origen `"garmin"` -- `sleep_spo2_avg` (label e.g.
"Blood oxygen (sleep avg)", unit `"%"`, direction `"higher"`); `sleep_respiration_avg` /
`sleep_respiration_low` / `sleep_respiration_high` (label e.g. "Breathing rate (sleep avg/low/high)",
unit `"brpm"`, direction `"neutral"` -- unlike `resting_hr` or `stress_avg`, there is no single
"better" direction for a breathing rate, only a normal band) -- plus a `store_day` change to read
these four `DayData` fields into the metrics insert alongside `.metrics`. Whether and how a screen
shows these figures, with the honest caveat that they are a proxy and never snoring or a diagnosis,
stays a later customer-facing slice (ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1's own scoping).

## BODY-ENTRENO-ADAPTER-1 -- a second Garmin read, for per-set strength detail, called by nobody yet (2026-11-09)

`BODY-ENTRENO-1-INV` (slice 1, an investigation) found that per-set detail for strength sessions
(exercise, reps, weight, duration, start) needs `get_activity_exercise_sets(activity_id)`
(`garminconnect` 0.3.20, `api/activities.py:613`) and that its response shape is UNDOCUMENTED in
the installed package -- the method itself is typed only `dict[str, Any]` with the docstring
"Return activity exercise sets.", no more. The only two confirmed facts about this endpoint are:
the write call in the same module, `set_activity_exercise_sets`, whose docstring says its payload
is "in the same shape as the response from `get_activity_exercise_sets`" and names
`exercises[].category` (the parent) and `exercises[].name` (the sub-category) as the fields Garmin
validates; and `exercises.py`'s static catalog of 1527 `(category, exercise)` pairs to a display
name. This slice added the read function the investigation recommended, mirroring
`fetch_intraday` (`BODY-INTRADIA-ADAPTER-1`), and nothing else -- the write call
`set_activity_exercise_sets` is not used, now or ever, by this module.

`body/garmin_adapter.py` gained: `ExerciseSet` and `ExerciseSetsData` dataclasses; `_client`-based
`fetch_exercise_sets(activity_id, token_str=None)`, one call
(`api.get_activity_exercise_sets(activity_id)`), same session/token pattern as `fetch_day` and
`fetch_intraday` including the hosted per-person token path (`token_str` given -> returns
`(ExerciseSetsData, token_after)`; a failed call records `_errors["exercise_sets"]` and leaves
`sets` empty rather than raising); and a pure `parse_exercise_sets(payload)` -> `tuple[ExerciseSet,
...]`, taking the Garmin response directly (not a day/call-keyed wrapper, since there is only one
call here).

Each `ExerciseSet` carries `set_type` ('active' | 'rest', from an assumed `setType`/`type` key,
recognised only against a fixed word list -- an unrecognised or missing value is `None`, never
guessed toward either); `category`/`exercise`, read from the first entry of an assumed `exercises`
list per the write docstring's confirmed field names; `display`, a read-only lookup of
`(category, exercise)` against `exercises.py`'s catalog (`None` when the pair is not in it -- the
catalog is read, never used to rename `category`/`exercise` themselves); `reps` (first of assumed
`reps`/`repetitionCount`/`repCount`); `weight_value`/`weight_unit` (assumed `weight`/`weightUnit`
keys -- Garmin is known to send body-composition weight in grams elsewhere, but nothing confirms
this endpoint's unit, so a present value is kept and its unit left `None` rather than guessed; no
`weight` key, or an explicit null, leaves both absent together); `duration_s` (assumed `duration`,
assumed seconds); and `start_local` (assumed `startTime`, tried first as epoch-ms local via the
existing `_local_iso` convention, then kept as a plain string if it is one). Every assumed key is
named in a docstring at the point it is read. A row that is not a dict, or any payload shape this
parser does not recognise (`None`, a bare non-list, an unrelated dict, a list under `exerciseSets`
holding junk), yields an honest gap -- an empty `sets` tuple, or a set whose unrecognised fields are
all `None` -- never a crash and never a 0.

**Nothing calls `fetch_exercise_sets` or `parse_exercise_sets` yet.** Not `pull.py`, not the
backfill loop, not `body/web.py` or any route, not the assistant. This merge adds no new Garmin
traffic: `fetch_exercise_sets` runs only when a future slice calls it, on demand, when a person
logs or corrects a session -- the same on-demand contract `BODY-INTRADIA-ADAPTER-1` set for
`fetch_intraday`.

**Tests** (`tests/test_garmin_parse.py`, invented fixtures only): `ExerciseSetsParsingTest` --
a 3-set strength fixture (active/rest/active) parses in order with `category`/`exercise`/`display`/
`reps`/`duration_s`/`start_local` correct on the active sets and absent on the rest set; a set with
no `weight` key keeps `weight_value`/`weight_unit` both absent; a stated `weightUnit` is passed
through unchanged; an unconfirmed-unit weight value is kept with `weight_unit` left `None`; an
unknown `(category, exercise)` pair not in the catalog has `display=None`; `None`/`{}`/`[]`/a bad
string/`{"exerciseSets": None}`/`{"exerciseSets": "nope"}` all give an empty tuple without raising;
a row with only unknown keys gives one `ExerciseSet` with every field `None`; a non-dict row inside
`exerciseSets` is skipped, not raised on; the bare list form (`payload` without the `exerciseSets`
wrapper) is also accepted. `FetchExerciseSetsSuccessTest`/`FetchExerciseSetsFailureTest` --
`fetch_exercise_sets` keeps `activity_id` as a string regardless of the caller's type, the hosted
token path returns `(data, token_after)`, and a raising `get_activity_exercise_sets` is recorded as
`_errors["exercise_sets"]` with `sets` empty rather than propagating. `OnlyGarminAdapterImportsGarminconnectTest`
(pre-existing) still passes unchanged -- the new `from garminconnect import exercises` import stays
inside `garmin_adapter.py`, the one module allowed to hold it.
