## BODY-ENTRENO-PULL-1 -- workout_set write helpers, sticky person correction, no job wired yet (2026-11-09)

`BODY-ENTRENO-1-INV` slice 3. With the `workout_set` table merged (`BODY-ENTRENO-SCHEMA-1`,
`135486a`) and the on-demand reader `fetch_exercise_sets` (`BODY-ENTRENO-ADAPTER-1`), this slice
adds the one place that stores a session's sets, next to `save_day`/`set_metric` in `body/db.py`,
same style, no migration.

`save_exercise_sets(conn, person_id, source, source_id, sets)`: upserts each `ExerciseSet`-shaped
item onto the UNIQUE slot `(person_id, activity_source, activity_source_id, set_order)`, 1-indexed
in the order given, writing only `garmin_*`, `set_type` and `updated_at` -- never `person_*`,
never `corrected_by_person` (the investigation's Q2 rule: a re-read from the watch rewrites the
watch's own columns and never clears a person's correction). A slot beyond `len(sets)` -- the
watch no longer reports it -- is deleted unless `corrected_by_person = 1`; a corrected slot in that
range stays, garmin_* and all, untouched by the trim. Requires the activity row to already exist,
via the table's own FK (no extra check needed). `correct_exercise_set(conn, person_id, source,
source_id, set_order, *, exercise=None, category=None, reps=None, weight_kg=None, note=None)`:
writes the given `person_*` fields and sets `corrected_by_person = 1`, via an upsert whose
`DO UPDATE` keeps a field's prior value when the matching keyword is left `None` (`COALESCE` against
the stored column) -- one correction can touch just one field without erasing another correction
already there. Creates the slot (`set_type = 'active'`, every `garmin_*` column `NULL`) when the
watch never reported it. Person-scoped by construction: the UNIQUE slot a conflict can land on
always includes `person_id`, so this can never write another person's row, and a plain `SELECT ...
WHERE person_id = ?` can never read one either -- no separate ownership check needed anywhere.
`create_manual_session(conn, person_id, day, start_local, title, duration_s=None) -> source_id`: an
`activity` row with `source = 'manual'` and a generated `source_id` (`manual-<uuid4 hex>`), filling
only columns the table already has (`title` -> `name`; no manual `type`). `exercise_sets(conn,
person_id, source, source_id)`: the sets in order, each with a display value (the person's
correction when `corrected_by_person`, else the watch's reading -- weight carries its unit:
`"kg"` for a person's correction, the watch's own stated unit otherwise, `None` with the value when
absent) plus both originals (`garmin`/`person` sub-dicts), for the assistant to read.

`body/pull.py` gained `traer_series(conn, person_id, activity_source_id, token_str=None)`: the one
call site to `garmin_adapter.fetch_exercise_sets` (the only Garmin access here), saved with
`db.save_exercise_sets`. Returns the sets-saved count, or `(count, token_after)` when `token_str` is
given -- the same dual-return shape `fetch_exercise_sets` itself already uses for the hosted
per-person token path. **Not called by `pull_all`, `pull_hosted`, `pull_backfill_hosted` or
`main`** -- Garmin traffic and the jobs' pace are unchanged; this runs only on demand, when a person
logs or corrects a session (the assistant tools, slice 4).

**Tests** (`tests/test_entreno_sets.py`, invented fixtures, no network -- every Garmin call stubbed
through `body.pull.garmin_adapter`): a first save stores the watch's sets in order; absent weight
stays `NULL` with its unit; saving against a non-existent activity raises (the FK); a correction
survives a second save with different watch values (`garmin_*` updated, `person_*` and
`corrected_by_person` intact); an uncorrected stale slot is removed while a corrected one stays,
garmin columns untouched; `correct_exercise_set` creates a missing slot, leaves an unmentioned field
at its prior correction, and never touches `garmin_*`/`set_type` on an existing slot; a manual
session with spoken sets (correct_exercise_set against `create_manual_session`'s `source_id`);
`exercise_sets` displays the watch's values when uncorrected and the person's when corrected, both
originals always present; person A cannot read or correct person B's sets (two people, same
`source_id`, scoped rows); `traer_series` saves and returns the count locally and `(count,
token_after)` hosted; and `pull_all`/`pull_hosted`/`pull_backfill_hosted` each run with
`garmin_adapter.fetch_exercise_sets` replaced by a `Mock` that must stay uncalled, proving none of
the three jobs reach it.

## BODY-ENTRENO-TOOLS-1 -- planear_entreno/registrar_entreno/leer_entreno assistant tools

Slice 4 of BODY-ENTRENO-1-INV (ROADMAP 9b): Carlos wants to speak a planned or finished workout to
the assistant instead of typing each exercise. Adds three tools on the existing propose/apply/undo
pattern (`body/agente/herramientas.py`, `body/agente/propuestas.py`), over the storage merged in
BODY-ENTRENO-SCHEMA-1/BODY-ENTRENO-PULL-1.

* `planear_entreno` (propuesta, nivel ninguno): stages one `plan` row -- day, optional time, title,
  an optional goal link, and a list of planned exercises `{ejercicio, series, reps?}`. Insert-shaped
  like `proponer_meta`: no "before". No screen writes `plan` yet, so `propuestas.py` inserts and
  deletes that one row directly (the module's docstring now names this exception) instead of
  delegating to a writer that does not exist.
* `registrar_entreno` (propuesta, nivel ninguno): "here is what I did" for a day. When that day has
  a Garmin strength activity, it maps the spoken sets onto the watch's sets by order, fetching them
  with `pull.traer_series` at BUILD time (not apply time) if not already stored, so the card can
  show the watch's value and the spoken correction per set -- that fetch only ever fills
  `workout_set`'s `garmin_*` columns (a cache of what the watch already recorded), never a `person_*`
  column, and nothing is ever sent to Garmin. With no activity, it stages a manual session instead.
  Apply writes through `db.correct_exercise_set`/`db.create_manual_session`, same as the screens
  would. Undo removes the manual session entirely, or -- for a touched Garmin set -- restores its
  exact pre-correction state (including `corrected_by_person` back to 0 when it was never corrected)
  via a direct UPDATE/DELETE on `workout_set` in `propuestas.py`, because that exact restoration
  cannot be expressed through `correct_exercise_set` (which only ever moves a set INTO "corrected")
  and `db.py` is outside this slice's `touches`.
* `leer_entreno` (lectura, nivel completo): a day's or a range's training sessions with their sets
  (display value plus whether each was corrected) and the planned session for that day, if any.
  Nivel `completo` was chosen over `resumen` (the spec offered either) because it surfaces per-day,
  per-set figures -- the same granularity `leer_dia`/`leer_como_calculo` are gated at, and the kind
  of daily value `ResumenHasNoDailyValuesTest` establishes `resumen` tools must never expose.

Both proposal tools got drift checks: `registrar_entreno`'s Garmin-matched case refuses to apply if
a later pull changed the watch's own reading for a touched set, and refuses to undo if the session
was corrected again after applying; `planear_entreno` refuses to undo if its `plan` row was already
changed or removed. A test proves person B can neither apply person A's proposal nor read person A's
sessions through `leer_entreno` (`tests/test_agente_entreno.py`), same ownership guard every other
proposal already carries.

Cards: `body/rutas/asistente.py`'s `_tarjeta_propuesta` gained a `"series"` field -- a per-set
watch-vs-you table for `registrar_entreno` (`None` for every other action) -- built from new
`_ejercicio_plan_txt`/`_serie_txt` helpers; `body/static/assistant.js`'s `crearTablaSeries` renders
it with `textContent` only (no `innerHTML`), styled by three new rules in `body/static/body.css`.
Twelve new i18n keys in `es.json`/`en.json`: two card titles ("Plan de entrenamiento"/"Training
plan", "Lo que hiciste"/"What you did"), the plan and registered-workout summary templates, and the
set-detail/column-header strings ("Reloj"/"Watch", "Tú"/"You").

Registry: lectura tools 11 -> 12, propuesta tools 4 -> 6, total 15 -> 18. Every literal a test
pinned about the old counts was updated: `tests/test_agente_registro.py` (`expected_levels`,
`PROPUESTA_NOMBRES`, the two count assertions, `_all_tool_calls()`), `tests/test_agente_bucle.py`
(`NivelDatosEnforcementTest`'s offered-at-`ninguno` set), `tests/test_agente_propuestas.py`
(`NoProponibleTest`'s set, plus two new card tests for `planear_entreno`/`registrar_entreno` on the
SSE route). `tests/test_agente_entreno.py` is new: 21 tests across `planear_entreno`,
`registrar_entreno` (Garmin-matched and manual) and `leer_entreno`.

**Deviation, noted rather than asked about:** the demo provider (`body/agente/cliente.py`) is

to see the exact antes/despues/series strings without a browser).

`body/agente/bucle.py` and `body/rutas/comun.py` were both in `touches` but needed no change: the
tool loop already dispatches by name through the registry with no per-tool code, and the card

## BODY-ENTRENO-MEDIDA-1 -- registrar_medida assistant tool + self-measured keys in Trends

Slice 6 of BODY-ENTRENO-1-INV (ROADMAP 9b): Carlos names goals that follow a number he measures
himself -- hamstring/hip flexibility as a reach toward the floor, snoring minutes from a phone app.
BODY-ENTRENO-SCHEMA-1 had already merged `metric_def.origen` ('garmin' | 'self') and the two generic
self-measured keys (`flex_alcance_cm`, `snoring_min`) with labels and demo data; `daily_metric`
already took `source='self'` through `db.set_metric`, and Trends/baselines/goal evaluation were
already source-agnostic. Missing piece: a way to SAY the number. Continues on
`feat/body-entreno-tools-1`, after BODY-ENTRENO-TOOLS-1's own commits on that branch.

* `registrar_medida` (propuesta, nivel ninguno), on the existing propose/apply/undo pattern: a
  metric key, a value and an optional day (default today in the person's zone). The key is checked
  against the LIVE `metric_def` row (`origen = 'self'`), never a hardcoded pair of names -- a future
  self-measured metric_def row is accepted the same way. The JSON-schema `enum` offered to the model
  (`herramientas.SELF_METRIC_KEYS`) is built from `db.METRIC_DEFS` -- the same source metric_def
  itself is seeded from -- rather than typed out a second time. `metric_def` carries no range
  column, so the only sanity check beyond the unit/type checks `_validar_parametros` already runs is
  rejecting a negative value, with the reason, per the spec's documented fallback.
* Apply writes through `db.set_metric(..., source='self', ...)` directly in `propuestas.py` -- a
  third exception to "applying calls the same writer the screens use" (after `planear_entreno`'s
  direct `plan` insert and `registrar_entreno`'s direct `workout_set` undo): no screen writes a
  self-measured figure yet, so this is the writer's first caller besides `body/demo.py`'s seeding
  and `body/readiness.py`'s own score. `antes` carries that day's existing value (or `None`)
  for undo to restore exactly, and drift is checked the same way as every other kind: the live
  `daily_metric` row is compared against what `antes`/`despues` captured, both at apply and at undo.
* Trends: `comun.TREND_GROUPS` gained a `"self"` group, built as `[d[0] for d in db.METRIC_DEFS if
  d[5] == "self"]` rather than a literal key list -- the same template-not-one-person approach as
  the tool's enum. A self-measured key would otherwise never clear `profile.metric_profile`'s
  14-day gate (built for the watch's own cadence), so `metric_profile` gained an optional
  `min_days` (default 14, unchanged for every existing caller); `tendencias.py`'s `_trend_card`
  passes `min_days=1` for a metric_def row with `origen == 'self'`, so a card appears from the first
  value, honestly sparse (no interpolation -- `window_svg`/`month_svg` already break a line at a
  gap rather than invent one). Each self-measured card carries a new `"self"` flag and its own note
  (`trends.self_note`, distinct from the watch's `trends.sparse_note` -- a self-measured gap has a
  different cause and deserved its own words) instead of reusing Watch-specific copy.
* A goal can already point at any metric_def key; `tests/test_agente_medida.py` proves one on
  `flex_alcance_cm` (direction `lower`) is evaluated weekly from self-measured values exactly like a
  Garmin-sourced one -- `goals.evaluar_semana` reads `db.series`/`daily_metric` with no `source`
  filter, so `body/goals.py` needed no change at all, confirming BODY-ENTRENO-1-INV's own Q4 finding.

`metric.flex_alcance_cm`/`metric.snoring_min` already existed in `es.json`/`en.json` (added by an
earlier slice, ahead of BODY-ENTRENO-SCHEMA-1's own docstring claim that this slice would add them).
New this slice: `trends.group.self`, `trends.q.flex_alcance_cm`, `trends.q.snoring_min`,
`trends.plain.flex_alcance_cm`, `trends.plain.snoring_min`, `trends.self_note`,
`asistente.propuesta.titulo.registrar_medida`, `asistente.propuesta.medida_valor`. The first wording
of `trends.self_note` used "puede haber" (impersonal "there may be") and tripped
`tests/test_registro_tu.py`'s su/sus/tiene/puede register guard, which scans es.json for that
exact word regardless of construction and is outside this slice's `touches`; reworded to "a veces
hay" instead of asking for an allow-list entry in a file this slice may not change.

Registry: propuesta tools 6 -> 7, total 18 -> 19. Every literal a test pinned about the old counts
was updated: `tests/test_agente_registro.py` (`PROPUESTA_NOMBRES`, the two count assertions, the
`test_six_propuesta_tools_at_nivel_ninguno` method renamed to `test_seven_...`),
`tests/test_agente_bucle.py` (`NivelDatosEnforcementTest`'s offered-at-`ninguno` set),
`tests/test_agente_propuestas.py` (`NoProponibleTest`'s set, plus one new SSE card test,
`test_registrar_medida_carries_a_propuesta_label`). `tests/test_agente_medida.py` is new: 17 tests
across propose/apply/undo, drift both ways, refusals (a `garmin` key, an unknown key, a negative

too), two-person isolation (each person's value and each person's undo), the goal-evaluation case,

## BODY-ENTRENO-TOOLS-1-M -- the four display-only fixes, then the merge

Continued on `feat/body-entreno-tools-1` (base `main` at `7585b54ec35eb45a8515a0d1fc166ed1ceda5c87`),
landing both `BODY-ENTRENO-TOOLS-1` (`ffb401f` + ledger `0935ed1`) and `BODY-ENTRENO-MEDIDA-1`
(`d6aea9b` + ledger `3ea7d43`), each AWAITING_APPROVAL above with a green gate. The orchestrator
measured the cards in a browser (BODY-ENTRENO-1-INV) and approved these four fixes verbatim, then
the merge (`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`).

1. **Readable watch exercise name.** The per-set table's watch column showed Garmin's raw code
   verbatim ("BARBELL_ROW · 10 rep · 40 kg"). `body/rutas/asistente.py`'s `_tarjeta_propuesta` now
   builds that cell's name from the raw `garmin_exercise`/`garmin_category` already carried in a
   `registrar_entreno` proposal's `antes_json["sets_antes"]` -- never from `despues["mapeo"][i]
   ["reloj"]["ejercicio"]`, which can already be a prior person correction -- through a new
   `_nombre_legible()` (underscores as spaces, only the first letter capital), falling back to the
   category when the exercise name is absent. Display only: the stored `garmin_exercise` is
   untouched, and `herramientas.py` (outside this slice's `touches`) needed no change because the
   raw values it already stores in `antes_json` were sufficient. Tested both the exercise-name and
   the category-fallback case (`tests/test_agente_propuestas.py`,
   `test_registrar_entreno_garmin_shows_a_readable_watch_name`,
   `test_registrar_entreno_garmin_falls_back_to_category_when_exercise_is_missing`).
2. **Manual session: no empty watch column, titulo in the line.** `body/static/assistant.js`'s
   `crearTablaSeries` now drops the "Reloj"/"Watch" column entirely when no row in `series` carries
   a watch value (the manual case), instead of a column full of "—". `_tarjeta_propuesta`'s
   `registrar_entreno` branch now reads the manual session's own `titulo` into the card's line via a
   new `asistente.propuesta.entreno_registrado_titulo` key ("{titulo} · {fecha}") when the person
   gave the tool a real title, and keeps the existing `entreno_registrado` ("Entrenamiento del
   {fecha}") wording when `titulo` is still the tool's own "Entrenamiento" default -- detected by
   that literal, the only signal available without widening `touches` into `herramientas.py`. The
   JS column drop has no Python-test coverage (no JS runner in this gate); the titulo wording is
   tested on both sides (`test_registrar_entreno_manual_carries_a_per_set_watch_vs_you_table`'s new
   assertion, `test_registrar_entreno_manual_without_a_titulo_keeps_the_dateonly_wording`).
3. **Honest self-measured card below baselines.MIN_DAYS.** With fewer self-measured values than
   `baselines.MIN_DAYS` (7), `statistics.quantiles` on 1-6 points collapses `p.low`/`p.high` toward
   a single repeated value (measured: one point gave "Tu rango normal (9–9)" and a spurious "= como
   siempre" delta). `body/rutas/tendencias.py`'s `_trend_card` now computes `pocas = d["origen"] ==
   "self" and p.days < baselines.MIN_DAYS`: when true, `delta`/`cls` are forced to `("", "flat")`,
   `profile.window_svg` is called with a new `banda=False` (skips the normal-range rect and scales
   the chart to the plotted points alone, not to the untrustworthy low/high), and the card carries a
   new `conteo` string ("{n} mediciones/measurements hasta ahora/so far", singular for n=1) built by
   a small `_medidas_count_txt` helper -- there is no plural mechanism in `body/i18n/__init__.py` to
   delegate to. `body/templates/trends.html` hides the normal-range legend span and shows `c.conteo`
   instead when `c.pocas`. `month_svg` needed no `banda` parameter: a self-measured key below
   `MIN_DAYS` can never reach 7 same-month points, so `p.months` is always empty and the chart never
   renders there regardless. From `MIN_DAYS` on, a self-measured card behaves exactly like any other
   (both sides tested in `tests/test_agente_medida.py`'s new `TrendsSelfMeasuredThresholdTest`).
4. **flex_alcance_cm wording, verbatim per the spec.** `metric.flex_alcance_cm` ("Dedos al suelo (cm
   que faltan)" / "Fingertips to floor (cm short)"), `trends.q.flex_alcance_cm` ("¿Se acercan tus
   dedos al suelo?" / "Are your fingertips getting closer to the floor?") and
   `trends.plain.flex_alcance_cm` ("cuántos cm te faltan para tocar el suelo con las rodillas
   rectas, medido por ti" / "how many cm short of the floor you stop, knees straight, measured by
   you") replaced the backwards "how far you reach" wording for this lower-is-better metric. None of
   the new or changed strings tripped `tests/test_registro_tu.py`'s register guard, so no allow-list
   entry was needed.

**New i18n keys** (both `es.json`/`en.json`, placeholders match): `trends.medidas_count_one`,
`trends.medidas_count_other` ({n}), `asistente.propuesta.entreno_registrado_titulo` ({titulo},
{fecha}).

## BODY-ENTRENO-PRIVACIDAD-1 -- the consent widens to v2: training detail, night blood oxygen and
## breathing, and self-measured figures, named before the person is asked to trust them

BODY-ENTRENO-1-INV's Q7: since `consentimiento-v1` (BODY-PRIVACIDAD-1) was written, Body started
keeping more without widening what the consent names -- night blood oxygen and breathing
(BODY-ENTRENO-SUENO-STORE-1, stored on every pull already), the per-set detail of training
sessions (BODY-ENTRENO-PULL-1 / TOOLS-1), and the numbers a person records themself
(BODY-ENTRENO-MEDIDA-1: flexibility, snoring and the rest). `ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`
carries out Q7 with wording approved verbatim.

**What changed.** `body/privacidad.py`'s `CONSENT_VERSION` moves from `"consentimiento-v1"` to
`"consentimiento-v2"`. Nothing else reads the literal `"consentimiento-v1"` in code (the two
earlier ledger entries that name it stand as history, untouched -- the ledger is append-only).
`has_consented`/`record_consent` already take `version` as a parameter, defaulting to
`CONSENT_VERSION`, so no other line in that module changed. `body/identity.py`'s gate (raises
`ConsentRequired`/403 for a person with no accepted row for the *current* `CONSENT_VERSION`) was
read, not changed -- it already re-asks on any version bump, including this one, with no code of
its own naming a version.

**Text, verbatim, both catalogs** (`body/i18n/es.json`, `body/i18n/en.json`):
`privacidad.consentimiento.que` now names sleep's night blood oxygen and breathing, the training
detail (sets, reps, weight) as always-kept, and -- "if you add them" -- shift calendar, goals,
habits and self-recorded measures (flexibility, snoring as examples). `privacidad.resumen` now
lists watch figures, training, goals, habits, shifts and self-recorded measures. Intraday figures
are named nowhere: nothing stores them yet (BODY-INTRADIA-ESQUEMA-1, not built, bumps the version
again when it does). Neither string tripped `tests/test_registro_tu.py`'s register guard (no
usted marker, no new `su/sus/tiene/puede` hit), so its allow-list needed no change.

**Tests** (`tests/test_privacidad.py`, one new method on `HostedConsentGateTest`): a person
carrying only a `consentimiento-v1` row (inserted directly via `privacidad.record_consent(conn,
person_id, "consentimiento-v1")`) is sent to `/privacidad/consentimiento` on the next request same
as a person with no row at all; accepting inserts a `consentimiento-v2` row and leaves the v1 row
in place (both counted at 1 afterward) -- the version bump's history guarantee, not just its gate.
The four existing accept/decline/language tests keep passing unchanged: none asserted the literal
version string except through `privacidad.CONSENT_VERSION` itself, which now reads v2 everywhere
they use it.

tests -t .` -- `Ran 1533 tests in 407.767s ... OK (skipped=1)`. 1 more than the prior recorded
floor (1532, `BODY-ENTRENO-TOOLS-1-M`): the one new test method above; `skipped=1` carries over
unchanged.

## BODY-ENTRENO-TITULO-1 -- absent stays absent; a spoken "Entrenamiento" is not mistaken for silence

Follow-up found in `BODY-ENTRENO-1-INV` slice 4 (TOOLS-1), per `ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`:
`body/agente/herramientas.py` `_registrar_entreno` stored the Spanish literal `"Entrenamiento"` as
the manual proposal's `titulo` whenever the person gave no title, so an English speaker got a
Spanish word stored as their session's title, and a person who actually said "Entrenamiento" was
read as one who said nothing (`body/rutas/asistente.py` `_tarjeta_propuesta` compared the stored
value against that same literal). Fixed at the source: a missing or blank spoken title now stores
`titulo: None` -- never a literal -- and the card's `!= "Entrenamiento"` comparison is gone; any
given title, including the word "Entrenamiento" itself, now gets the titled wording
(`asistente.propuesta.entreno_registrado_titulo`, "{titulo} · {fecha}"), and only `None` gets the
untitled, date-only wording (`asistente.propuesta.entreno_registrado`, already approved wording from
`BODY-ENTRENO-TOOLS-1-M`, unchanged).

**Apply** (`body/agente/propuestas.py` `_escribir_aplicacion`, the manual `registrar_entreno` case):
`db.create_manual_session` still needs a title to pass, so a `None` titulo resolves to a new
localized default -- key `entreno.titulo_por_defecto` ("Entrenamiento" / "Training") -- read in the
person's own language the same way `proponer_idioma`'s drift check already does
(`db.person(conn, person_id)["language"]`, then `i18n.T(lang)`). This is the one new customer-facing
string the approval covers; it was not possible to pass `None` through to the `activity.name` column
instead, because `db.create_manual_session`'s own signature types `title` as a plain `str` (Tier 1,
out of this slice's `touches:`), not `str | None` -- so a literal default has to be supplied at the
call site, by design, not by oversight.

**Not migrated**: proposals already stored with the literal `"Entrenamiento"` as of this slice's
dispatch stay as they are -- there are none on a real account, since the manual `registrar_entreno`
tool itself only merged into `main` today (`BODY-ENTRENO-TOOLS-1-M`, same day).

## BODY-ENTRENO-HABITO-AUTO-1 -- marcar_habito, so a habit can be checked off from the watch's own evidence

Slice 5 of `BODY-ENTRENO-1-INV` (Q5, ROADMAP 9b): a ball sport once a week is Carlos's own goal, and
he does not want to type what the watch already knows. Adds `marcar_habito` on the existing
propose/apply/undo pattern -- a generic "check habit H for day D, from this evidence" tool. Ball
sports is one use of it; the tool never carries a hardcoded activity-type list, and the model
decides which of the day's activities (`leer_entreno`) fulfils which of the person's active habits
(`leer_meta`), then proposes.

**Access, reused, never a second rule**: the habit must exist and be active; the person may check
it only through `goals.goal_access` (creator, or household member on a shared milestone) plus the
exact assignee rule `body/rutas/metas.py`'s own `habit_check` route already enforces (unassigned, or
assigned to the caller) -- a household member's own assigned habit is never another member's to
check, even when both can read the goal. The day-not-future check reuses `fechas.fecha_real_valida`
with the person's real local today, the same rule `goals.check_habit` itself enforces. An optional
`actividad` (`{source, source_id}`) is checked against the live `activity` row: it must belong to
the caller and land on the proposed day, or the tool refuses.

**antes/despues**: `antes` is that day's existing `habit_check` row for this person (done, note) or
None. Apply writes through `goals.check_habit(..., done=True, hoy=<person's local today>)`; undo
restores the prior row exactly, or deletes it when there was none -- a narrow direct DELETE on
`habit_check`, documented in `propuestas.py`'s module docstring as the same kind of exception
`registrar_entreno`'s own Garmin-set restoration already is, since `check_habit` only ever upserts
and has no "no row" shape to call back into. Drift (propose vs. apply, and apply vs. undo) is
checked against the live `habit_check` row, exactly like the other proposal tools.

**Card** (`asistente._tarjeta_propuesta`): title "Marcar hábito" / "Check off a habit"; the done line
names the habit and the day, plus -- when an activity was given -- its name and duration as evidence
(a new `_actividad_txt` helper, mirroring `body/rutas/hoy.py`'s `_activity_name` fallback and
`t.minutes`, kept local to `asistente.py` since `hoy.py` is outside this slice's `touches:`). When
the day already had a "not done" row, it shows as `antes` the same way `proponer_cambio_meta` does.
One sentence, appended at the end of `agente.sistema` in both catalogs, tells the model to offer
this when it sees a day's activity fulfilling an unchecked active habit, naming the activity, and
never to check it without the person's own approval.

**Deviation from the approval's verbatim Spanish text**: the approved sentence ends "...nunca lo
marques sin su toque." (never mark it without their tap). `tests/test_registro_tu.py` (outside this
slice's `touches:`, so it could not be edited) scans every `es.json` string for an allow-list of
formal-register ("usted") trigger words, one of which is the bare word "toque" (the formal
imperative of "tocar") -- it has no grammatical awareness, so it flags the noun "toque" ("a tap")
exactly as it would flag the verb. "su" is a second, separate trigger (third-person "su/sus/
tiene/puede", needing an allow-list entry in that same file) that this slice also has no entry for.
Reworded to "...nunca lo marques sin que la persona lo apruebe." (never mark it without the person
approving it) -- same meaning (the person's own tap on Aplicar is what "approves" it), no trigger
word. The English sentence is untouched (that guard only scans `es.json`). Flagging this rather than
silently keeping the literal text: the wording was approved verbatim, and this one clause is not
what was approved, even though it says the same thing.

**Tests** (`tests/test_agente_habito.py`, 20 new): propose writes nothing; apply marks done and
keeps the note/evidence; undo removes a row that did not exist before, or restores one that did
(not done, with its own note); drift refuses on both apply (row changed after propose) and undo (row
changed again after applying); person B cannot apply person A's proposal; a future day, an unknown
habit, an inactive habit, another person's private habit, a household member's own assigned habit,
an activity belonging to another person, and an activity on a different day are all refused; the
card text with and without evidence, in both es and en, plus the antes line for a prior not-done
row. `test_agente_bucle.py`'s nivel='ninguno' tool-name set, `test_agente_propuestas.py`'s
never-a-proposal name set, and `test_agente_registro.py`'s `PROPUESTA_NOMBRES`/tool-count/test-name
literals (seven -> eight propuesta tools, 19 -> 20 total) are updated to match, each test's own
subject unchanged.

## BODY-CUENTA-ERRORES-1 -- map callback error codes per cuenta-duna-v1 section 10

`BODY-CUENTA-1-INV` (2026-11-09) observed that `handle_callback` special-cased only
`login_required` and sent every other `error=` Cuenta's authorize redirect can return --
`access_denied`, `invalid_request`, `unauthorized_client`, `server_error`,
`temporarily_unavailable` -- into one generic `FlowRefused("error")`, rendering
`acceso_rechazado.html`'s "link expired / already used" text. That hid the real cause on
2026-11-09: a person with no `body` grant got the wrong page. `docs/contracts/cuenta-duna-v1.md`
section 10 already names what each code must show, and both pages and texts already existed, so
this slice adds no new customer-facing text.

**The mapping**, in `body/cuenta.py`'s `handle_callback`: `login_required` unchanged (still
bypasses the state check, as before -- a deliberate pre-existing special case, not touched);
`access_denied` now returns `CallbackResult(kind="sin_acceso")`, the same page and 200 status a
signed-in person with no `body` in `duna_productos` already reaches (`body/rutas/sesion.py`'s
existing `sin_acceso` branch needed no change, since it renders from `t`/`switcher_url`/
`logout_url` only, never from `claims`); `invalid_request`, `unauthorized_client`, `server_error`,
`temporarily_unavailable` now raise `CuentaUnavailable()`, so the existing `except
cuenta.CuentaUnavailable` branch in `login_callback` renders the `cuenta.down` outage sentence
(no route change needed there either); any other or unknown code still raises
`FlowRefused("error")`, keeping today's `acceso_rechazado` behaviour, with a code comment naming
this contract section. The raw `error` value is never placed in a page or a log line.

**Order**: the `state` check was moved to run before the new error-code branch (it previously ran
after the generic `"error" in params` check), so a forged callback carrying `error=access_denied`
and a wrong `state` is still refused as a state mismatch (400, `acceso_rechazado`), not shown
«Sin acceso» -- confirmed by
`test_forged_access_denied_with_bad_state_is_still_refused_as_state_mismatch`. `login_required`
keeps bypassing the state check exactly as before this slice.

**Tests added** (`tests/test_cuenta_rp.py`, `CallbackRefusalTest`): one case per code
(`test_login_required_starts_a_visible_sign_in`, `test_access_denied_shows_sin_acceso`,
`test_outage_codes_show_cuenta_down_sentence` for the four outage codes,
`test_unknown_error_code_keeps_acceso_rechazado`,
`test_forged_access_denied_with_bad_state_is_still_refused_as_state_mismatch`), each also
asserting the raw code string never appears in the rendered page.

## BODY-IDIOMA-PRIMERA-1 -- seed a hosted person's language from the browser at first sign-in

Carries out BODY-CUENTA-1-INV part B's body-only recommendation (ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1):
Cuenta's ID token and userinfo carry no locale claim and its `person` model has no column for one
either -- the `language` column lives only on Body's own `person` table (`body/db.py`), so "take
the first language from Cuenta" (BODY-IDIOMA-CARLOS-1 point 3) cannot be built here. A Cuenta
locale claim is a Cuenta change, to be asked for through the hub, not built in this slice.

**The rule**: on a hosted person's FIRST sign-in only, `body/cuenta.py`'s `resolve_person` seeds
the new row's `language` column from a `language` parameter the caller already picked -- never a
raw header read inside `resolve_person` itself. `login_callback` in `body/rutas/sesion.py` (which
already holds the request) picks it with `body/i18n`'s existing `pick(accept_language)` --
reused, not re-implemented -- from the callback request's `Accept-Language` header, and threads it
through `handle_callback` into `resolve_person`. `pick` already falls back to `i18n.DEFAULT`
("es") for a missing or unsupported header, so `resolve_person` needed no fallback of its own. An
existing person (the `SELECT ... WHERE cuenta_sub = ?` row already exists) is returned untouched;
their `language` is never written by `resolve_person`, whatever the header says on a later
sign-in -- so a person's own choice through `/settings/language` (`body/db.py`'s `set_language`)
is never overwritten by a sign-in. No new text, no new template, no new i18n key, no reworded
string.

**Tests added** (`tests/test_cuenta_rp.py`, `FirstSignInLanguageTest`, via a `headers` param added
to the existing `_sign_in` helper): first sign-in with `en-US,en;q=0.9` sets `en`; with `es-CO`
sets `es`; with an unsupported header (`fr-FR,fr;q=0.9`) or no header at all falls back to `es`; a
second sign-in with a different header leaves the stored language as it was
(`test_second_sign_in_with_different_header_leaves_language_unchanged`), including one the person
changed themself through `db.set_language`
(`test_second_sign_in_never_overwrites_a_person_chosen_language`).

**Line-number note**: `tests/test_seguridad.py`'s `RedirectTargetsAreSafeTest` keys its
`ALLOWLIST` by exact `file:line`. The new import and the extra `handle_callback` argument were
folded into existing lines in `body/rutas/sesion.py` (merged `from ..i18n import T, pick as
pick_lang` into one line; the picked language appended to the existing two-line `handle_callback`
call) so neither `RedirectResponse` call's line number moved -- that guard test was not in
`touches:` and needed no change.

**Merge policy A**: no schema/migration change (the `person.language` column and its default
already existed; only an existing `INSERT` gained one more column value), no customer-facing bytes
(no new template, no new i18n key, no reworded string -- only routing logic and tests), no
cross-repo contract or DTO change. All three conditions pass; this spec's approval reason also
says "Merge approved."

## BODY-SEGURIDAD-ALLOWLIST-1 -- re-key the redirect-target ALLOWLIST off line number (2026-11-09)

`tests/test_seguridad.py`'s `RedirectTargetsAreSafeTest` keyed its `ALLOWLIST` of reasoned
`RedirectResponse` call sites by exact `(file, line number)` -- the line-number note on
BODY-IDIOMA-PRIMERA-1 above is the cost of that: a worker had to fold an import and an argument
into existing lines in `body/rutas/sesion.py` purely to keep two unrelated redirects' line numbers
still, because any edit above one of them would have moved the line and turned the gate red with
a false alarm.

**Old key**: `(file, line)`, e.g. `("body/rutas/sesion.py", 50)`.

**New key**: `(file, enclosing function name, ast.unparse(target))`, e.g.
`("body/rutas/sesion.py", "login_start", "url")`,
`("body/rutas/sesion.py", "login_callback", "result.return_to or '/'")`,
`("body/rutas/ajustes.py", "set_trabaja_turnos", "volver")` -- the three current call sites, read
from the files rather than carried over blind. `_enclosing_function` (already in the module) finds
the function; a module-level redirect would key with function name `None`. This key survives an
unrelated edit anywhere else in the file, including one that shifts the redirect's own line number,
and still changes if the redirect moves to a different function or its target expression changes.

**Why**: the key only needs to survive edits that do not touch the redirect's own meaning. Line
number fails that; (file, enclosing function, target source) does not, because nothing about an
unrelated edit elsewhere in the module changes either of those.

Both assertions kept their subject, unchanged in scope: an unlisted unsafe target still fails the
test, naming `file:line` in the failure message (line numbers stay in the message only, never in
the key, so a failure is still easy to locate); an `ALLOWLIST` entry that no longer matches any
call site still fails as stale. The scan itself was factored out of the test method into
`_scan_redirect_targets(tree, rel, allowlist)`, a module-level helper the real test and three new
synthetic cases share -- `RedirectAllowlistKeyStrictnessTest`, built from small in-memory sources
parsed with `ast.parse`, touching nothing under `body/`:

* a listed call site moved down by ten inserted lines still passes (proves the re-key actually
  stopped tracking line number);
* the same function redirecting to a different, unsanitized target still fails (proves the key
  did not become "any redirect in this function is fine");
* the listed target text appearing in a different function still fails (proves the key did not
  become "this target string anywhere is fine").

**Merge policy A**: no schema/migration change, no customer-facing bytes (test file only, no
template, no i18n string), no cross-repo contract or DTO change -- all three pass. This spec's
approval reason says "Merge approved."

## BODY-TURNOS-PALABRA-DIRECCION-1 -- Turnos' cost rows say the direction, not a verdict

Carries out BODY-TURNOS-SUENO-DIURNO-1-INV's first recommendation (OBSERVED 2026-11-09). The Turnos
cost table ended each of its five rows with a JUDGEMENT word -- es "peor"/"mejor"/"igual", en
"worse"/"better"/"about the same" -- from `turnos_costo.diferencia_y_palabra()`. Three of the five
metrics (sleep_minutes, hrv_last_night, body_battery_wake) are keyed to one sleep session by
Garmin's own fields, and on a night-shift day that session is the person's daytime rest, not a
night comparable to the reference (the person's own day-shift weeks) -- so "better"/"worse" could
read as an artefact of WHEN the watch measures, not an honest verdict.

**The fix**: `diferencia_y_palabra` now derives the word purely from the REAL difference's own
sign -- `'mas'` (diff > 0), `'menos'` (diff < 0), `'igual'` (below `UMBRAL_IGUAL`, unchanged) --
instead of from the metric's own better-direction. A lower resting HR during a night block (which
`test_a_lower_resting_hr_during_nights_is_not_worse` already established is NOT medically worse)
now reads "menos", never "mejor": the word names which way the mean moved, not whether that move is
good. The signed `costo` (positive = worse, `_signo`'s convention), the recovery rule
(`_recuperacion_bloque`) and the reference (`referencia`) are byte-for-byte unchanged -- only the
displayed word's derivation changed. Checked (grep) that nothing besides `body/rutas/turnos.py`
reads `diferencia_y_palabra`'s word or the `shifts.word.*` keys dynamically; the assistant's
`leer_costo_turnos` tool and Hoy never touch either.

**Words, verbatim** (approved in the dispatch): `shifts.word.mas` es "más" / en "more";
`shifts.word.menos` es "menos" / en "less"; `shifts.word.igual` unchanged (es "igual" / en "about
the same"). `rutas/turnos.py` drops the `+`/`−` sign it used to prefix onto the figure, since the
word already says which way it moved ("42 min menos", not "-42 min menos") -- `t.num`/`t.minutes`
never embedded a sign themselves, so this was one `sign = ...` line and its use removed, nothing in
the number formatters.

**Deviation from the spec's "remove the old keys if nothing else reads them"**: the old
`shifts.word.peor`/`shifts.word.mejor` keys were kept (unused) in `body/i18n/es.json` and
`en.json` instead of being removed. `tests/test_i18n_paridad.py` -- outside this slice's
`touches:` -- hardcodes `"shifts.word.+": ["peor", "mejor", "igual"]` in its own dynamic-prefix
registry and asserts each resolved key exists in `es.json`; removing the keys would have required
editing that file, which this slice was not authorised to touch. No live code path calls `t()`
with either key any more (confirmed by grep), so the orphan keys are translated but never
rendered.

**No colour or class keyed to the old word**: checked `body/templates/shifts.html` and
`body/static/body.css` -- the row's only markup is `<span class="nw">{{ f.value }}
<strong>{{ f.palabra }}</strong>...`, no class branches on the word's value in either file.

**Tests** (`tests/test_turnos_costo.py`, `DireccionYPalabraTest`): each of the five metrics renders
`'mas'`/`'menos'`/`'igual'` by the sign of the real difference regardless of the metric's own
better-direction (`test_no_metric_ever_reads_a_judgement_word`, all five metrics, both signs); a
lower resting HR reads `'menos'` not `'mejor'` (`test_a_lower_resting_hr_reads_menos_not_mejor`); a
higher resting HR reads `'mas'` not `'peor'`. Two new end-to-end tests render `/shifts` in es and en
(a block seeded off-baseline on its own nights, not just the recovery tail, so every row clears
`UMBRAL_IGUAL`) and extract each row's value+word pair: the word is always in
`{'más','menos','igual'}` / `{'more','less','about the same'}`, never `'peor'/'mejor'`/
`'worse'/'better'`, and the figure carries no `+`/`-`/`−` now that the word follows it. These checks
are scoped to the row's own value+word span (`<span class="nw">...<strong>`), not every string on
the page: `shifts.cost_sub.resting_hr`/`hrv_last_night` (both languages) are pre-existing, unchanged,
general metric-direction text ("lower usually means better fitness") -- a timeless fact about the
metric, not a verdict on this measurement -- and were out of this slice's approved-verbatim word
list, so left as they were. The recovery result is unchanged on the existing fixtures (no test in
`ResumenTest`/`RecuperacionBloqueTest`/`LectorEqualityTest` needed a change, and all pass unmodified).

**Merge policy A**: customer-facing bytes changed (the `shifts.word.*` translations and the
dropped sign on the figure are both bytes a person reads on `/shifts`) -- fails the
customer-bytes condition. Per the dispatch's approval reason ("Customer-facing, so the slice stops
AWAITING_APPROVAL for the orchestrator's 375 px check"), this slice stops before merge.

**Gate**, once, foreground, on the branch, not merged: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest
discover tests -t .` -- `Ran 1584 tests in 364.458s ... OK (skipped=1)`.

## BODY-TURNOS-REFERENCIA-NOCHE-1 -- the last night week, against the person's own earlier ones

Carries out BODY-TURNOS-SUENO-DIURNO-1-INV's second recommendation
(`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`): the existing Turnos cost rows compare night blocks against the
person's day-shift weeks, which is not like for like for three of the five metrics (they come from
the main sleep session, a daytime rest after a night) -- BODY-TURNOS-PALABRA-DIRECCION-1 already
made those rows say only the direction, not a verdict. A verdict is honest only against the
person's OWN earlier night blocks.

**Model** (`body/turnos_costo.py`), added to `resumen()`, no second DB read -- from the same
`Lector`-backed per-block figures it already computes: a new `_medias_bloque()` reads each block's
raw per-metric window mean (same window as `_costo_bloque`, inicio..fin+dias_estables, no reference
subtracted); a new `_ultima_semana()` finds the LAST block whose window is fully on or before
`hoy`, compares its per-metric mean against the mean of the EARLIER blocks' own window means (one
value per block, so a long block never outweighs short ones), gated on a new `MIN_BLOQUES_PREVIOS =
3` earlier blocks per metric (added to `REASON_CODES` as `pocos_bloques_previos`), reusing
`diferencia_y_palabra()` for the direction word and deriving a mejor/peor/igual verdict from the
same signed-cost convention `_costo_bloque` already uses. Recovery: the last block's
`recuperacion_dias` against the median of the earlier blocks' (only those with a figure). Returned
under a new `ultima_semana` key -- `None` with no completed block at all. `MODELO`'s existing keys,
the day-week `referencia()`, the cost rows' `costo_promedio` and the hero `dias_recuperacion` are
unchanged; `VERSION` stays `turnos-v1` since no existing formula changed.

**Page** (`body/rutas/turnos.py`, `body/templates/shifts.html`): a new card after the existing cost
card, same `.card`/`table.parts` styling, no new CSS needed. `_turnos_ultima_ctx()` builds it from
`resumen()`'s own `ultima_semana`: a gap message (`shifts.ultima.faltan`) when no metric reached the
minimum; otherwise the sub (`shifts.ultima.sub`), one row per qualifying metric (label, value,
direction word reusing `shifts.word.*`, and the mejor/peor/igual word via a literal `t(...)` call
per branch -- never `t("shifts.ultima.word." + veredicto)`, which would be a new, unlisted dynamic
prefix and trip `tests/test_i18n_paridad.py`'s dynamic-prefix guard, outside this slice's
`touches:`), and the recovery line. No card at all when `ultima_semana` is `None`.

**Wording** verbatim per the spec, in both `body/i18n/es.json` and `body/i18n/en.json`:
`shifts.ultima.title`, `shifts.ultima.sub`, `shifts.ultima.word.mejor/peor/igual`,
`shifts.ultima.recuperacion`, `shifts.ultima.faltan`. One deviation: the spec named only
`shifts.ultima.recuperacion` for the recovery line and described a second sentence (no figure yet
for the last block) without naming its key. Added `shifts.ultima.recuperacion_sin_dato` for that
case, verbatim text as given. A third, unnamed edge the spec did not enumerate -- the last block HAS
a recovery figure but none of its earlier blocks do (so there is nothing to take a median of) --
got its own `shifts.ultima.recuperacion_sin_anteriores` ("Volviste a tu normal en {d} días." / "You
were back to your normal in {d} days."), to stay honest rather than fabricate a comparison; not
reachable by this slice's own tests, since `MIN_BLOQUES_PREVIOS` already requires 3+ earlier blocks
before any row shows, and the fixtures that exercise the gap path never also claim a last-block
recovery figure.

**Tests** (`tests/test_turnos_ultima_semana.py` -- 10 new): `UltimaSemanaTest` calls the pure
`_ultima_semana()` directly (no conn, same style as `CostoBloqueTest`/`RecuperacionBloqueTest`) --
worse resting HR against three earlier blocks reads peor/mas, better sleep reads mejor/mas, HRV
under threshold reads igual, a metric with only two earlier blocks is left out, recovery with and
without a figure, zero metrics reaching the minimum is the gap, no completed block is `None`.
`ResumenUltimaSemanaTest` checks the wiring through `resumen()` on seeded blocks.
`WebUltimaSemanaTest` checks `/shifts` renders the section (and the gap text, and no section) in
Spanish and English. `tests/test_turnos_costo.py` (existing cost rows and hero) and
`tests/test_i18n_paridad.py` (the wording guard) stay green, unmodified.

**Merge policy A**: customer-facing bytes changed (the new `/shifts` card and its wording) --
**stops before merge**, per the approval reason's own words ("the slice stops AWAITING_APPROVAL for
the orchestrator's 375 px check"). No schema/migration change, no cross-repo contract change.

## BODY-AGENTE-DIA-FUTURO-1 -- one rule for a future day, across every write tool that records what already happened

Carries out BODY-REVISION-9B-1-INV's findings 4 and 3 (the minor asymmetry), per
`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`. Day handling was not one rule across the assistant's write
tools: `_marcar_habito` (body/agente/herramientas.py) refused a future `day` against the person's
own local today, but `_registrar_entreno` and `_registrar_medida` only checked the ISO format, so
"what I did" or a number the person measured could be proposed for a day that had not happened
yet. `_planear_entreno` rightly keeps accepting a future day -- a plan is for later -- and now
carries a one-line comment saying why, so the next reader does not "fix" it.

The habit tool's check (ISO parse + `fechas.fecha_real_valida` against
`fechas.hoy_local(db.person(conn, person_id))`, raising the same two `ToolError` texts) is now one
private helper, `_dia_no_futuro`, called from `_marcar_habito`, `_registrar_entreno` and
`_registrar_medida` (for the latter, after its default day is filled in). No other write tool in
the file records something that already happened without this check; `_proponer_meta` and
`_proponer_cambio_meta` take a `deadline`, and `_planear_entreno` a `day`, both plans that look
forward on purpose.

Separately, `_drift_aplicar`'s `registrar_entreno` branch (body/agente/propuestas.py) now compares
the watch set's weight unit (`garmin_weight_unit`, read off `db.exercise_sets`' own `garmin` dict)
alongside exercise, reps, weight value and category, so a unit-only change on the watch side
between proposal and apply is caught as drift like every other field. The `sets_antes` snapshot
built in `_registrar_entreno` now carries `garmin_weight_unit`; a stored proposal from before this
slice, whose snapshot lacks that key, is treated as "not compared" for that one field, so an
old-shape snapshot still applies.

Tests (tests/test_agente_entreno.py, tests/test_agente_medida.py, tests/test_agente_propuestas.py):
`registrar_entreno` and `registrar_medida` each accept the person's own local today and refuse a
day beyond `fechas.TOLERANCIA_DIAS`'s one-day tolerance, checked with an invented person in
`Pacific/Kiritimati` (UTC+14) at a mocked UTC instant where the UTC date and that zone's date
disagree -- proving the check reads the person's own local today, not the server's. `deviation`:
the spec's own text said "refuse tomorrow"; `fechas.fecha_real_valida`'s existing one-day tolerance
(shared with the habit tool, and itself covered by `tests/test_fecha_futura_1.py`'s
`test_tomorrow_accepted`) accepts a day that is literally tomorrow in the person's zone, so the
refused case tested is the day after tomorrow instead, with today as the accepted case -- changing
neither `fechas.py` nor the tolerance was in scope. `_planear_entreno` gained a test proposing a
day over six months out, still accepted. The habit tool's existing tests
(tests/test_agente_habito.py) are unchanged and stayed green; moving its future check to the top of
`_marcar_habito` (ahead of the habit lookup, now that both checks live in one helper call) does not
change any of their outcomes, since none of them combines an unknown/inactive/foreign habit with a
future day. The drift fix gained two tests: a weight-unit-only change on the watch side between
propose and apply is refused as drift; an old-shape snapshot with that key deleted still applies,
even when the watch's unit has since changed, proving the missing key is treated as "not compared"
rather than "unchanged".

A behaviour-preserving refactor, approved by ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1: the eight proposal
actions (`proponer_meta`, `proponer_cambio_meta`, `proponer_confirmar_turnos`, `proponer_idioma`,
`planear_entreno`, `registrar_entreno`, `registrar_medida`, `marcar_habito`) were each named in four
parallel `if accion == ...` chains in body/agente/propuestas.py (`_drift_aplicar`, `_drift_deshacer`,
`_escribir_aplicacion`, `_escribir_deshacer`) in a different order each time, plus a fifth chain in
body/rutas/asistente.py's `_tarjeta_propuesta` (8 branches) -- a ninth action would have meant
editing five places by hand, with nothing but a registry count to notice a missed one.

**Shape chosen**: a frozen dataclass, `_Accion` (propuestas.py), with four fields -- `drift_aplicar`,
`drift_deshacer`, `escribir_aplicacion`, `escribir_deshacer` -- each a callable `(conn, row) -> ...`,
plus a `tiene_deshacer` property. `TABLA: dict[str, _Accion]` keys one entry per action. A dataclass
over a plain dict-of-tuples because the property gives a named, typed answer to "can this be undone"
without a second lookup, and frozen because no code should ever reassign one action's writer onto
another's entry. "No drift" (the insert-shaped actions) and "no undo writer"
(`proponer_confirmar_turnos`) are explicit, named no-ops -- `_sin_drift`, `_sin_escritura_deshacer` --
never a missing branch; `tiene_deshacer` is an identity check against `_sin_escritura_deshacer`, so
"every entry has all four callables" stays literally true even for the one action with no real undo
writer. `SIN_DESHACER` is now `tuple(nombre for nombre, entrada in TABLA.items() if not
entrada.tiene_deshacer)` -- derived, not hand-maintained -- and still read by body/rutas/asistente.py
by that same name, unchanged. `aplicar`, `descartar` and `deshacer` keep their exact signatures,
return shapes and status codes; they now look up `TABLA[row["accion"]]` once instead of walking four
chains. `deviation`: for a truly unknown `accion` (never reachable in production -- every write path
creates its row through `crear` with one of the eight literal action strings, and the new guard test
below ties that set to the tool registry), the old chains fell through silently (no drift, no write,
`estado` still flipped to "aplicada"/"deshecha"); the table version raises `KeyError` instead. Spec
BODY-PROPUESTAS-TABLA-1 asked to keep aplicar/deshacer's behaviour "byte-for-byte" including "an
unknown action raises the same error it raises today"; reading the old code, no error was raised
today for that case -- the table's loud failure on a key the registry guard guarantees can never
occur was judged the correct trade, not the literal byte-for-byte match, and is recorded here as the
deviation it is.

body/rutas/asistente.py's `_tarjeta_propuesta` is reduced the same way: one small card-builder
function per action (`_tarjeta_meta_nueva`, `_tarjeta_cambio_meta`, `_tarjeta_confirmar_turnos`,
`_tarjeta_idioma`, `_tarjeta_planear_entreno`, `_tarjeta_registrar_entreno`,
`_tarjeta_registrar_medida`, `_tarjeta_marcar_habito`), each returning `(antes_txt, despues_txt,
series_tarjeta)`, in a `TARJETAS` dict keyed the same way as `TABLA`; `_tarjeta_propuesta` itself is
now the shared frame (title, antes/despues wrapping, series, buttons via `etiquetas`) plus one
dictionary lookup. The card dicts it returns are identical to before for every action and state --
proven by the untouched `tests/test_agente_propuestas.py`, `tests/test_agente_entreno.py`,
`tests/test_agente_habito.py`, `tests/test_agente_medida.py` and `tests/test_asistente_panel.py`
(below).

**New test** (tests/test_propuestas_tabla.py) is the guard that a ninth action cannot be half-added:
(a) `propuestas.TABLA`'s keys, `asistente.TARJETAS`'s keys and the `tipo == 'propuesta'` tool names in
`herramientas.HERRAMIENTAS` are the same set; (b) every `TABLA` entry's four fields are callables;
(c) the set of entries with `tiene_deshacer` False equals `propuestas.SIN_DESHACER` and equals exactly
`{"proponer_confirmar_turnos"}`, the old `SIN_DESHACER`.

**Existing tests touched**: none. Searched every proposal test file (test_agente_propuestas.py,
test_agente_entreno.py, test_agente_habito.py, test_agente_medida.py, test_asistente_panel.py,
test_agente_registro.py, test_persona_fuga.py, test_privacidad.py) for any reference to the removed
private chain functions or to `SIN_DESHACER`'s old shape -- none exists; every test reaches this
module only through `crear`, `aplicar`, `descartar`, `deshacer` and `PropuestaAjena`, which are
unchanged, so no edit was needed anywhere outside the new test file.

**Defects seen and left** (not this slice's place to fix, per spec step 1): none found. The review
that proposed this slice (BODY-REVISION-9B-1-INV finding 3) explicitly found no action whose drift or
undo logic was weaker than the others -- this was a structural defect only, and the refactor changed
no action's actual drift or write behaviour.

**Gate**: baseline run on main's tree before any change, foreground, `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m
unittest discover tests -t .` -> `Ran 1608 tests in 423.158s ... OK (skipped=1)`. Final run on the
branch after the change, same command -> `Ran 1612 tests in 361.009s ... OK (skipped=1)` (the four
new tests in test_propuestas_tabla.py).

## BODY-VIVO-REFRESCO-1 -- the live-tree refresh guard was tripping on its own import, since 350ac4e

**Cause, since when**: BODY-ERRORES-CENSO-2 (`350ac4e`) added `from . import errores` to the top of
`body/vivo.py`. `_modulos_body_inesperados()` flagged every `body*` module in `sys.modules` except
a hardcoded `("body", "body.vivo")`, so by the time `main()` called it, `body.errores` was already
loaded by vivo's own import line and the guard ALWAYS returned `['body.errores']`. `main()` then
always set `resultado = "sin_cambio:modulos_previos"` and never called `refrescar()` -- the
live-tree refresh has never run since that commit, in any process, on any task. The fail-safe design
(run the task anyway on whatever commit is checked out) meant this produced no error, only a stdout
line a scheduled task discards -- which is how 80+ commits of drift on the PC's live tree
(BODY-LIVE-CHECKOUT-1) went unflagged. `tests/test_vivo.py`'s existing coverage used a fake module
name inside the shared unittest process, where `body.vivo` had already settled its own imports
long before that test ran, so it could not see vivo's own import trip the guard -- only a fresh
process can.

**The fix** (`body/vivo.py`): `_modulos_body_inesperados()` now compares `sys.modules` against
`_MODULOS_AL_CARGAR`, a baseline captured once, right after vivo.py finishes its own imports
(itself plus whatever it pulled in -- today `body.config` and `body.errores`), instead of a
hardcoded exception list. A module a PREVIOUS task left cached in the same process still trips the
guard and blocks the refresh; the next import vivo adds joins the baseline automatically and cannot
reopen this bug.

**The status file**: `main()` now writes `BODY_HOME/vivo-estado.json` after every run (besides the
existing stdout line): `resultado` (`actualizado` | `ya_al_dia` | `sin_cambio:<motivo>`), `tarea`,
`sha` (the short sha now checked out), `sha_main` (main's short sha), and `marca_tiempo_utc`.
Nothing else, never a figure. A failure to write it (`OSError`) does not stop the task, matching
`refrescar()`'s own fail-safe. The expected follow-up reader is the sync-status text in
`body/rutas/comun.py` (a separate slice, not done here).

**New tests** (`tests/test_vivo.py`): `ProcesoFrescoTest.test_un_proceso_fresco_se_actualiza_a_la_nueva_main`
runs `python -m body.vivo subir_turnos --help` in an actual fresh interpreter (`sys.executable`,
which under this gate is `.venv/Scripts/python.exe`), `cwd` a temporary linked worktree one commit
behind its own throwaway `main`, `BODY_HOME` a temp dir passed via `env=` -- the case the existing
fake-module test could not reach. `subir_turnos` was picked because `--help` makes argparse exit
before `main()` reaches the shifts folder, the device link or the network, so it touches no data.
Asserts `resultado == 0`, stdout contains `actualizado`, HEAD moved to the new commit, and the
status file's fields match. Also added: `test_el_archivo_de_estado_tiene_exactamente_los_campos_esperados`
(exactly `resultado`, `tarea`, `sha`, `sha_main`, `marca_tiempo_utc`, for both `actualizado` and
`sin_cambio:*`) and `test_estado_no_escribible_no_impide_la_tarea` (an `OSError` from
`config.ensure_home()` still lets the task run). The existing fake-module test
(`test_modulos_body_previos_se_registran_pero_la_tarea_igual_corre`) is untouched and still passes.

**Gate**: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .` -> `Ran 1615 tests in
530.426s ... OK (skipped=1)`, run once on the branch tip.

**Merge**: `git checkout main` (tip `04650a0a37be108a28129644e79c0fe7c5ff69b5`), branch commit
`da926b9bf70abb10492aef796644980545875001`, `git merge --no-ff feat/body-vivo-refresco-1` ->
`8d9ecc3a660f333946f96678ed4a4d05ed721130`. Merge tree `3f38cfd103a58fedf3783b78d31db1a90f281636`
equals the branch tip's own tree (`git rev-parse feat/body-vivo-refresco-1^{tree}`) -- the merge
carried the branch content verbatim.

**Still needed, not done here**: Carlos's live tree on the PC (`C:\Duna\body\body-app-live`) still
runs its own on-disk copy of the OLD, buggy `body/vivo.py` -- this fix only reaches it once that
tree is moved onto this `main` by hand, which needs Carlos's own yes (it runs new migrations
against his real database) and is explicitly out of scope for this slice.

## BODY-DEMO-TURNOS-1 -- the demo's default seed shows both states of "Tu última semana de noches" honestly

BODY-TURNOS-REFERENCIA-NOCHE-1's new section (merged `a9e6942`) needs
`turnos_costo.MIN_BLOQUES_PREVIOS` (3) earlier night blocks before the last COMPLETE one to show a
verdict. `body/demo.py`'s `DIAS_DEFAULT` was 90 days -- about three night weeks of the demo's
4-week cycle (`_CYCLE`) -- so after the last completed block at most two earlier ones remained, one
short of the floor: the demo home could only ever render the section's gap state at 375 px,
whatever day it was run on, as the orchestrator's 2026-11-09 measurement found (it had to seed extra
blocks with a scratch script to see the other state).

**What changed**: `DIAS_DEFAULT` raised from 90 to **120**. `_seed_shifts` holds the last 7 seeded
days back as a proposed (unconfirmed) batch, never written into the `shift` table, so the usable
confirmed window is `dias - 7`, not `dias`. Measured by brute force over one full 28-day cycle of
anchor dates (the demo's night-week period, so every phase of the cycle is covered regardless of
which real day the demo is seeded on): 115 confirmed days is the minimum that always leaves
`MIN_BLOQUES_PREVIOS` earlier blocks before the last complete one; 120 clears it with a small margin
and stays `<= turnos_costo.RESUMEN_DIAS` (180), so `resumen()` still sees the whole seeded window.
Every other seeded object (the cycle, `SEED`, the recovery shaping, the goals/habits/household
seeding) is unchanged. A single seeding run went from ~1.3s to ~1.8s -- not a noticeable cost for the
tutorial/Growth workflow that calls this CLI.

The short-seed path (`--dias` with a window under the new floor) still shows the gap honestly --
confirmed by test, not by running the CLI against a real home.

**Tests (`tests/test_demo.py`)**: `UltimaSemanaReachableTest` seeds in-process (not through the CLI
subprocess the rest of the file uses) so a test can control "today" -- `body.demo`'s own `date` name
is patched to a fixed value per iteration, with no change to `_seed`'s own logic or signature. For
every anchor across one full 28-day cycle starting `2026-01-05`: the default seed (`DIAS_DEFAULT`)
gives `resumen(...)['ultima_semana']` with at least one metric carrying a verdict, and a 40-day seed
(well under the floor) gives either no completed block or the `pocos_bloques_previos` gap reason.
All values stay invented; `_forbidden_home` and the demo's other refusals are untouched. The existing
19 tests in the file (refusals, determinism, seeded content against an explicit `--dias 90`, which
nothing here depends on the default for) pass unchanged.

## BODY-VIDA-DIA-1 -- a second vida-v1 file: today's wake time, last night's sleep, readiness

Carlos, 2026-11-09, dictated to his Personal desk, relayed: a morning brief that knows
"approximately at which time I woke up, how was my night sleep, and what are my plans for the
day." Personal reads Body only through vida-v1 files on his PC (contract rule 2); this slice adds
a DAILY file beside the existing weekly one, built only from blocks the contract already defines
(Metric, Event) -- no contract change needed. Approved per ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1: a second
vida-v1 file, same rules as the weekly one (stays on the PC, visibility owner, Personal reads the
file, never the database); no screen changes, so not customer-facing.

**`body/vida_dia.py`** (`python -m body.vida_dia [--day YYYY-MM-DD]`, default today in the
person's own zone, `fechas.hoy_local`): writes `BODY_HOME/vida/body-day-<day>.json`:

    {"person", "day", "generated_at" (instant with offset),
     "metrics": [{"person", "day", "key", "value", "source", "visibility", "kind"}, ...],
     "events": [{"id", "person", "hogar_id", "kind", "starts_at", "ends_at", "all_day",
                 "timezone", "source", "ref", "data"}, ...],
     "missing": ["body.<key>", ...]}

`DAY_METRICS` (a module constant): `sleep_minutes`, `sleep_score`, `readiness`,
`body_battery_wake` -- each read straight from `daily_metric` (namespaced `body.<key>`), `source`
fixed to `"body"` for readiness and `"garmin"` for the other three (never the row's own stored
`source` column), `kind` from `metric_def` so readiness's `estimated` kind shows. A key with no
value yet for that day (the watch has not synced) is never invented and never zero: it goes in
`missing` instead of a metric row. One `body.sleep` Event is added when `sleep_session` has the
day's row, `starts_at`/`ends_at` taken verbatim from its `start_local`/`end_local`
(`body/db.py:161-167`), `id` a stable `uuid.uuid5(uuid.NAMESPACE_URL, "body.vida_dia:<person>:<day>:sleep")`
so the same day's file always carries the same event id, `timezone` from the person, `all_day:
false`, `source: "garmin"`. Hosted installs refuse, same as `vida_export`'s refusal (a per-person
API is a later slice -- open follow-up below). Reuses `vida_export.vida_person`/`PERSON_KEY`
rather than duplicating that lookup.

**`body/vivo.py`** gains two `TAREAS` entries: `vida_dia` (writes the file alone) and `manana`
(the scheduled morning run: the same pull `pull` uses, `--days 1`, then `vida_dia`). A new
`PASOS_PREVIOS` mapping runs that pull step, via `runpy.run_module`, immediately before the
task's own module; a non-zero exit (`SystemExit`) or a raised exception from it (no network,
Garmin down) is swallowed -- `vida_dia` always runs next and writes the file from whatever is
already stored, with its own `missing` telling the truth, instead of the scheduled run losing the
whole file to a pull failure. The in-process model and the stale-module guard
(BODY-VIVO-REFRESCO-1) are unchanged; `pull`, run alone, never triggers this pre-step.

**`scripts/install-daily-sync.ps1`** gains a new task **"Body app morning file"**, running
`-m body.vivo manana` from the live tree, triggered at every time in a new `-MorningAt` parameter
(`[string[]]`, **default `"04:40", "07:40", "12:40"`** -- one `New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily`
per time, since `Register-ScheduledTask -Trigger` takes an array). Each run rewrites the same
day's file. The header's "Remove with:" line and the task list now name it too; no other task's
registration changed. **Installing this task on Carlos's PC is a separate step needing his own
yes -- this slice does not run the installer.**

**Tests**: `tests/test_vida_dia.py` (8 tests) -- the full shape (all four metrics, the sleep
event, exact field names, `kind`/`source` per key), an unsynced day writing `missing` with no
metric rows (never 0), the same event id for the same person+day, a partial day mixing metrics
and `missing`, no event when `sleep_session` has no row, the hosted refusal, and the printed line
being the path only (no figure). `tests/test_vivo.py` gains `TareasVidaDiaTest` (both task names in
`TAREAS`), `MananaTest` (4 tests: `manana` still runs `vida_dia` after the pull step raises or
exits non-zero, the pull step's fixed `--days 1` argv, `pull` alone skips the pre-step), and
`InstallScriptMorningFileTest` (3 tests, reading the `.ps1` text only -- never executed: the new
task/parameter/default exist, every other task name and action line is unchanged, the removal
line names the new task).

**Open follow-ups**: a per-person API for the daily section (same gap `vida_export` already has
for the weekly one), for whenever Body serves more than one hosted person.

402.308s ... OK (skipped=1)`, run once on the branch tip.

## BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-CONSENTIMIENTO-1 -- the consent widens to v3: intraday heart rate and stress,
## experiments and logged moments, named before Wave 9 stores any of them

`BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-1-INV` (OBSERVED 2026-11-09) found two kinds of data Wave 9 will store that
`privacidad.consentimiento.que` does not name: the watch's heart rate and stress minute by minute
(on the days an experiment or a study needs them, not every day) and what the person adds
themself -- experiments and the moments they log. `ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1` carries out the
slice with wording approved verbatim, same precedent as `BODY-ENTRENO-PRIVACIDAD-1` (v1 -> v2): this
must land before any intraday figure is stored, since `BODY-MOMENTOS-PULL-1` depends on it.

**What changed.** `body/privacidad.py`'s `CONSENT_VERSION` moves from `"consentimiento-v2"` to
`"consentimiento-v3"`. Nothing else in that module changed -- `has_consented`/`record_consent`
already take `version` as a parameter, and `body/identity.py`'s gate already re-asks on any
version bump with no code of its own naming one.

**Text, verbatim, both catalogs** (`body/i18n/es.json`, `body/i18n/en.json`):
`privacidad.consentimiento.que` now names the heart rate and stress figures kept minute by minute
on the days an experiment or a study needs them, and -- "if you add them" -- experiments and the
moments logged (a cold shower, a breathing round), alongside the shift calendar, goals, habits and
self-recorded measures already named since v2. No other consent key changed. Neither string
tripped `tests/test_registro_tu.py`'s register guard (no usted marker, no new `su/sus/tiene/puede`
hit) or its link-punctuation guard, so no allow-list needed editing.

**Tests** (`tests/test_privacidad.py`): `test_v2_only_acceptance_is_sent_to_consent_and_accepting_adds_v3_keeping_v2`
mirrors the v1->v2 precedent -- a person carrying only a `consentimiento-v2` row is sent to
`/privacidad/consentimiento` on the next request same as a person with no row at all, and
accepting inserts a `consentimiento-v3` row while leaving the v2 row in place (both counted at 1
afterward). `test_v3_acceptance_is_not_sent_to_consent_again` checks the other direction: a person
already carrying the current version's row reaches `/` without a redirect. A new
`ConsentTextNamesTheNewDataTest` reads both catalogs' `consentimiento.que` string directly and
asserts "minuto a minuto"/"minute by minute", "experimento"/"experiment" and
"momentos"/"moments" each appear, in es and en respectively. The existing accept/decline/language
tests keep passing unchanged: none asserted the literal version string except through
`privacidad.CONSENT_VERSION` itself, which now reads v3 everywhere they use it.
